items.title: Ku dhowaad 2,800 qof oo hal Maalin gudaheed uga Barakacay Gobalka Blue Nile ee Suudaan
items.description: Ku dhowaad 2,800 qof ayaa hal maalin gudaheed ka barakacay 10 tuulo oo ku yaalla gobolka Blue Nile ee koonfur-bari Suudaan, kaddib markii ay sii xumaadeen xaaladaha amni ee deegaanka. Sida ay sheegtay Hay’adda Caalamiga ah ee Socdaalka (IOM), dadkaasi waxay ka carareen deegaannadooda, iyadoo amni-darrada sii kordheysa ay ku qasabtay qoysas badan inay raadsadaan goobo ay ku helaan badbaado. Barakaca cusub ayaa kusoo beegmaya xilli Suudaan uu weli wajahayo xaalad bani’aadannimo oo aad u adag, iyadoo colaadaha iyo amni-darradu ay sababeen in malaayiin qof ay ka qaxaan guryahooda. Gobolka Blue Nile ayaa ka mid ah deegaannada ay saameeyeen colaadaha iyo dhaq-dhaqaaqyada amni, waxaana barakaca cusub uu kordhin karaa baahida loo qabo gargaar bani’aadannimo, hoy iyo adeegyo aasaasi ah. IOM ayaa sheegtay in xaaladda amni ee sii xumaanaysa ay sababtay barakacan degdegga ah, iyadoo aan weli la ogeyn muddada ay dadkaasi ku maqnaan doonaan deegaannadooda. Mas’uuliyiinta iyo hay’adaha gargaarka ayaa wajahaya caqabado sii kordhaya oo ku saabsan sidii loo gaarsiin lahaa dadka barakacay adeegyada iyo taageerada ay u baahan yihiin.

items.title: R/W Xamza oo ka degay degmo ka tirsan Galmudug + ujeedka
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Xukuumadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, Xamza Cabdi Barre iyo wafdi uu hoggaaminayo ayaa goordhow gaaray degmada Balanballe ee gobolka Galgaduud ee bartamaha Soomaaliya, halkaas oo si weyn loogu soo dhaweeyay. Xamza ayaa waxaa garoonka diyaaradaha Balanballe kusoo dhaweeyay Madaxweynaha Galmudug, Axmed Cabdi Kaariye (Qoor Qoor), Taliyaha Hay’adda Sirdoonka iyo Nabadsugidda Qaranka ee NISA Mahad Maxamed Salaad iyo mas’uuliyiin kale. Ujeedka Ra’iisul wasaare Xamza ayaa ah inuu ka qayb-galo gogol nabadeed oo taalla Balanballe, taas oo lagu soo afjarayo colaad beeleed muddo ka taagneyd degmadaasi. Ra’iisul wasaaraha waxaa kaga sii horreeyay Balanballe mas’uuliyiin ka tirsan dowladda dhexe oo uu ugu horreeyo Taliye Mahad Salaad oo shalay booqday ciidamo ka tirsan NISA oo uu tababar uga socdo halkaasi, isagoo inta uu kormeerka ku jiray la kulmay ciidamada tababarka qaadanaya, wuxuuna kula dardaarmay inay ka dhabeeyaan ballanta ay u qaadeen difaaca dalka, dadka iyo diinta. Dhanka kale waxaa kulanka dib u heshiisiinta ah la filayaa inay ka qayb-galaan bulshada deegaanka oo ay ugu horreeyaan waxgaradka beelaha, si ay goobjoog ahaadaan heshiiska lagu gaarayo halkaasi. Horay dowladda Soomaaliya ayaa go’aanno adag uga soo saartay colaadihii ka taagnaa gobollada dhexe, kadib markii uu amarro la siiyay ciidamada dowladda ee ku sugan halkaasi, kuwaas oo ka hortegoay dagaal beeleedyada iyo dilalka la xiriira aanooyinka qabiil ee deegaanada Galmudug. Xaaladda guud ayaa hadda ah mid deggan, waxaana haatan qorshaha uu yahay in la guda galo dib-u-heshiisiin dhab ah oo lagu soo afjarayo colaadaha ka taagan gobollada dhexe. items.title: Ururka Bisha Cas ee Soomaaliya iyo ICRC oo u Diyaar garoobaya Fatahaadaha El Niño
items.description: Ururka Bisha Cas ee Soomaaliyeed (SRCS), oo taageero ka helaya Guddiga Caalamiga ah ee Laanqayrta Cas (ICRC), ayaa bilaabay diyaar-garow iyo tababarro loogu talagalay ka jawaabidda fatahaadaha laga cabsi qabo inay ka dhacaan Soomaaliya xilliga xaaladaha cimilada ee El Niño. Diyaargarowgan ayaa si gaar ah diiradda loogu saaray webiyada Jubba iyo Shabeelle, oo ka mid ah goobaha ay fatahaaduhu si joogto ah uga dhacaan xilliyada roobabka. SRCS ayaa tababarka ku diyaarisay 72 qof, kuwaas oo ay ku jiraan 60 mutadawiciin ah oo ka kala socda bulshada deegaanka. Tababarrada waxaa lagu qabtay qaar ka mid ah deegaannada inta badan ay fatahaaduhu saameeyaan, oo ay ka mid yihiin Baardheere, Jowhar, Beledweyne iyo Kismaayo. Tababarka ayaa isugu jiray casharro aragti ah iyo tababarro la xiriira hawlgalka doomaha, si mutadawiciintu u helaan xirfadaha looga baahan yahay gurmadka degdegga ah. Intii tababarku ka socday magaalada Jowhar iyo hareeraha Webiga Shabeelle, ka-qaybgalayaashu waxay barteen farsamooyin ay ka mid yihiin wadista doomaha, jeereysiinta iyo dib-u-wadista doonta si xakameysan. Waxaa sidoo kale la baray hababka isgaarsiinta ee loo isticmaalo xaaladaha ay matoorrada doomuhu sameynayaan sawaxan, iyadoo xoogga la saaray adeegsiga calaamadaha gacmaha. Tababarka ayaa sidoo kale lagu baray ka-qaybgalayaasha sida matoorka doonta si sax ah loogu rakibo, hubinta badqabka ka hor inta aan doonta la dhaqaaqin iyo diyaarinta shaqaalaha iyo qalabka gurmadka. Mid ka mid ah casharrada muhiimka ah ayaa ahaa adeegsiga xarigga badbaadada ee matoorka, kaas oo xaalad degdeg ah lagu jiidi karo si matoorka si dhaqso ah loo damiyo, taasoo muhiim u ah badbaadada shaqaalaha iyo dadka gurmadka u baahan. SRCS ayaa sheegtay in tababarradan ay qayb ka yihiin dadaallada lagu xoojinayo awoodda gurmadka fatahaadaha, gaar ahaan maadaama fatahaado hore oo Soomaaliya ka dhacay ay muujiyeen muhiimadda ay leeyihiin kooxaha doomaha iyo mutadawiciinta deegaanka. Sanadkii 2023, kooxaha doomaha ee Bisha Cas ayaa door ka qaatay hawlgallada badbaadinta dadka ay fatahaaduhu saameeyeen, waxaana hadda la doonayaa in khibradahaas lagu sii xoojiyo tababarrada iyo diyaar-garowga cusub. Guud ahaan, 72-ka qof ee tababarka qaatay ayaa la diyaariyey, halka SRCS ay haysato sagaal doon oo lagu kala meeleeyay goobaha ay fatahaaduhu inta badan ka dhacaan. Tallaabooyinkan ayaa loogu talagalay in bulshada si degdeg ah loogu gurmado haddii fatahaado ka dhashaan xaaladaha El Niño iyo roobabka xiga. Diyaargarowga Bisha Cas iyo ICRC ayaa ku soo beegmaya xilli Soomaaliya ay wajahdo khataro la xiriira fatahaado, abaaro iyo xaalado cimilo oo isbedbedelaya, taasoo sare u qaadaysa baahida loo qabo in hay’adaha gurmadka ay hore ugu sii diyaar garoobaan xaaladaha degdegga ah.

items.title: Somalia’s Parliament Kills the Merit Hiring Plan: An Analytical Perspective
items.description: By Farah Mire Somalia’s parliament has struck down one of the government’s key reforms. On Wednesday, 23 September, the House of the People voted to cancel Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre’s order requiring open competition for director posts across government. The vote wasn’t close. 136 MPs backed the annulment. Only two voted against it. Two more abstained. Deputy Speaker Abdullahi Omar Abshir chaired the session and announced the result. About 30 lawmakers had pushed for the debate in the first place. Their motion made it onto the agenda after hours of argument over what changing the system might mean for Somalia’s civil service law. The directive at the center of this fight was only six days old. Barre issued it on 17 September. It told the Civil Service Commission to start grading department directors on competence, knowledge, experience, leadership and performance — the first phase beginning 20 September. Barre grounded the order in Article 161(1) of the Constitution and Article 7 of the Civil Service Law. He called directors general the backbone of the state. Build a professional, permanent leadership layer, he said, and government policy actually gets implemented. Two days after the PM’s order, the National Civil Service Commission followed up with its own directive — reference XGG/NCSC/1488/09/2026, sent to every ministry and agency, copied to the Prime Minister’s office. It laid out three rules. Fill director general posts through internal merit-based competition first, giving current qualified staff priority. Fill future vacancies through open competition, open to any qualified Somali. And the Commission itself would set the timetable and conditions. Ministries were told to freeze any appointments that might disrupt the process. Pay had to keep flowing. And — a detail easy to miss — the directive specifically told agencies to prioritize and encourage qualified women to apply. Then parliament stepped in. The House Committee on Social Services Development, led by MP Nadra Salah Abdi, had already challenged the directive before the vote. Some lawmakers argued it threatened people currently holding director jobs — that competence testing could simply push sitting officials out. After the vote, the Deputy Speaker sent the matter back to the federal government. The Civil Service Commission, for its part, came out publicly defending merit-based hiring anyway. Step back, and this fight sits inside a much bigger story. In December 2023, Somalia hit the Completion Point under the IMF and World Bank’s HIPC debt relief programme. External debt fell from $5.3 billion — 64 percent of GDP — down to $0.6 billion, less than 6 percent of GDP. That wasn’t charity. It came with strings attached: An Extended Credit Facility arrangement running from December 2023 to December 2026, built on reforms to tax policy, debt management, PPP legislation, central bank operations, and — this is the part that matters here — payroll integration. Most of those benchmarks are met or on track, according to a Central Bank of Somalia policy brief. But the brief also names eight fault lines still threatening the country’s fiscal footing: weak revenue collection, bloated recurrent spending, heavy aid dependence, thin debt-management capacity, and more. The wage bill tells the story on its own. It climbed from 1.29 percent of GDP in 2013 to almost 6 percent by 2021, according to the World Bank. In that same year, wages alone ate up 53 percent of everything the Federal Government spent — a figure the Bank says puts Somalia in the same bracket as other fragile, conflict-affected states, where personnel costs routinely crowd out nearly everything else. Temporary workers sit at the center of this problem, and here, at least, there’s a genuine success story. The Finance Ministry’s own review, published in March 2026, found that non-formal wages — money paid to staff outside the official payroll system — dropped from 36.3 percent of total compensation in 2021 to just 0.03 percent by the end of 2025. The original target was full payroll integration by the end of 2024. It arrived a year late, but it arrived. That’s real progress, and it’s worth saying so plainly. Recruitment itself is the piece still stuck. A 2024 Heritage Institute report on the civil service didn’t mince words: hiring has run for years on nepotism, favouritism, clan affiliation and political patronage. Its fix was straightforward — move qualified temporary staff into permanent roles based on merit, not connections. Separately, an audit of 6,448 positions found 1,626 of them belonged to “ghost employees” — people drawing salaries for jobs that, in practice, don’t exist. Somalia’s Finance Minister puts the total civil service headcount somewhere between 10,000 and 11,000, and says the government is actively working to stop it from growing further. So why did this particular reform collapse so fast? Look at how it was built. The procedure behind it — the Habraaca Hirgelinta Hannaanka Tartanka Furan — was never meant to go through parliament at all. Its Article 15 let it take effect by executive decree: Cabinet approval, the PM’s signature, publication in the gazette. Nothing more. That’s a deliberate design choice. It’s also a fragile one. On Wednesday, 23 September, the House of the People voted to cancel Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre’s order requiring open competition for director posts across government. The vote wasn’t close. 136 MPs backed the annulment. Only two voted against it. Two more abstained. Deputy Speaker Abdullahi Omar Abshir chaired the session and announced the result. About 30 lawmakers had pushed for the debate in the first place. Their motion made it onto the agenda after hours of argument over what changing the system might mean for Somalia’s civil service law. The directive at the center of this fight was only six days old. Barre issued it on 17 September. It told the Civil Service Commission to start grading department directors on competence, knowledge, experience, leadership and performance — the first phase beginning 20 September. Fill future vacancies through open competition, open to any qualified Somali. And the Commission itself would set the timetable and conditions. Ministries were told to freeze any appointments that might disrupt the process. Pay had to keep flowing. And — a detail easy to miss — the directive specifically told agencies to prioritize and encourage qualified women to apply. Then parliament stepped in. The House Committee on Social Services Development, led by MP Nadra Salah Abdi, had already challenged the directive before the vote. Some lawmakers argued it threatened people currently holding director jobs — that competence testing could simply push sitting officials out. Recruitment itself is the piece still stuck. A 2024 Heritage Institute report on the civil service didn’t mince words: hiring has run for years on nepotism, favouritism, clan affiliation and political patronage. items.title: Turkiga, Sacuudiga iyo Pakistan oo Riyadh kaga wada hadlaya xoojinta heshiiska difaaca
items.description: Guddiga heshiiska difaaca ee Turkiga, Sacuudiga iyo Pakistan ayaa maanta oo Isniin ah kulan ku yeelanaya magaalada Riyadh, iyadoo mas’uuliyiin sare oo ka kala socda saddexda dal ay ka qeybgalayaan. Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda ee Turkiga ayaa sheegtay in kulanka looga hadli doono xaaladihii ugu dambeeyay ee gobolka , iyo heerka uu marayo dadaalka lagu dhisayo, laguna xoojinayo qaab-dhismeedka hay’adaha ee isbahaysiga saddexda dal. Kulanka ayaa kusoo beegmaya xilli xaaladda amni ee gobolka ay sii xasaasiyeynayso, gaar ahaan dagaalka Yemen iyo howlgallada militari ee ka dhanka ah kooxda Xuutiyiinta. Sida ay Reuters werisay, Wasiirka Arrimaha Dibadda Turkiga Hakan Fidan , Wasiirka Difaaca Yasar Guler iyo Taliyaha Guud ee Ciidamada Turkiga, General Selcuk Bayraktaroglu , ayaa ka qeybgalaya shirka, iyadoo sidoo kale ay joogaan mas’uuliyiin ka socda Sacuudiga iyo Pakistan. Kulanka ayaa sidoo kale lagu wadaa in lagu falanqeeyo soo jeedin la xiriirta in Xuutiyiinta Yemen lala yeesho wada-hadallo siyaasadeed, ayadoo Wasiirka Arrimaha Dibadda Pakistan uu hore u sheegay in Iran ay soo jeedisay in si siyaasadeed loola macaamilo Xuutiyiinta kaddib weerarradii ay geysteen. Dhinaca kale, hoggaamiyaha dowladda Yemen ee Sacuudigu taageero ayaa ku dhawaaqay bilowga howlgal militari oo ballaaran oo lagu doonayo in dib loogu qabsado dhul ay Xuutiyiintu gacanta ku hayaan. Heshiiskan saddex geesoodka ah ayaa muhiimad gaar ah yeelanaya xilli Turkiga, Sacuudiga iyo Pakistan ay doonayaan inay xoojiyaan iskaashigooda dhinacyada difaaca, amniga iyo siyaasadda , iyadoo xaaladda Bariga Dhexe iyo gaar ahaan Yemen ay weli tahay arrin si dhow loola socdo.

items.title: Turkey’s Growing Military Role Raises Alarm, Prompting Somaliland to Seek Israeli Air Defences
items.description: Hargeisa’s Wake-Up Call: Baidoa Fighting Raises Fears That Turkish Military Power Could Become Entangled in Somalia’s Political Conflicts HARGEISA (WDN) — For Somaliland, the lesson from Baidoa is no longer theoretical. As Turkish F-16s, drones and other military capabilities have become increasingly visible in Somalia, the violent confrontation surrounding Baidoa has given Hargeisa a powerful reason to reconsider its own air-defence needs and to look toward Israel for protection against a changing regional military balance. The warning from Hargeisa is becoming increasingly direct. Mohamed Osman Fadal, a senior foreign-affairs adviser to Somaliland President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi, told Middle East Eye that Somaliland wants Israeli air-defence systems because of Türkiye’s expanding military presence in Somalia. “We need air defence systems,” Fadal said, specifically citing Turkish F-16s in Mogadishu and Ankara’s growing drone capabilities. “We want Israel to support us against Turkey.” The statement does not establish that Israel has agreed to provide such systems. Nor does it demonstrate that Türkiye intends to attack Somaliland. But it reveals a significant change in how Somaliland officials are assessing the regional security environment. And that change has been shaped by what has happened in Baidoa. Baidoa Changed the Calculation Türkiye says its military partnership with Somalia is designed to strengthen Somali security institutions and fight terrorism. Ankara has repeatedly denied allegations that its forces are being used to influence Somalia’s internal political struggles. But the political controversy surrounding Türkiye’s military role has intensified as Somalia’s federal crisis has turned violent. In and around Baidoa, Turkish aircraft and drones have been reported during periods of intense fighting involving federal forces and forces aligned with former South West State President Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen. Laftagareen-aligned authorities have accused Türkiye of conducting F-16 strikes against their forces. Those allegations have not been independently verified, and Turkish authorities have not publicly accepted responsibility for the alleged attacks. Nevertheless, the controversy itself matters. For observers in Hargeisa, the question is no longer simply how many Turkish weapons or aircraft Somalia possesses. It is how those capabilities might be used if Somalia’s political disputes become military confrontations. That is the wake-up call Somaliland appears to have taken from Baidoa. From Counterterrorism to Political Risk Türkiye’s defence relationship with Somalia is substantial. The two countries signed a ten-year defence and economic cooperation framework in 2024 under which Türkiye committed to building, training and equipping the Somali navy. Türkiye has also maintained a major military training presence in Mogadishu, while its parliamentary authorization for military deployment in Somalia has been extended through July 2028. The deployment has now expanded to include advanced aircraft. Three Turkish F-16s have been publicly seen operating in Somalia, while Turkish helicopters , drones and other military assets have also been deployed. Reporting has increasingly linked Turkish aircraft to security operations in Somalia, although the circumstances and targets of particular air operations remain disputed. For Türkiye, these capabilities are part of its defence partnership with Mogadishu. For Somaliland, however, they represent a potential strategic vulnerability. Critics argue, if Turkish military assets are used or are perceived to be used in Somalia’s internal political conflicts, Hargeisa has reason to ask what safeguards exist to prevent the same capabilities from eventually becoming relevant to a confrontation involving Somaliland. A Growing Political Backlash The controversy is also beginning to affect Türkiye’s wider political standing among Somalis. There is no reliable nationwide polling establishing that a majority of Somalis now oppose Türkiye.  But criticism of Ankara’s role has become increasingly visible among opposition politicians, former officials and commentators who argue that Türkiye’s close relationship with President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud makes it difficult for Ankara to be viewed as a neutral actor in Somalia’s political disputes. That perception has become particularly important because Türkiye has simultaneously presented itself as a diplomatic partner capable of facilitating dialogue among Somali political actors. The contradiction is increasingly obvious to Türkiye’s critics: a country perceived by some political actors as closely aligned with the federal government may find it difficult to convince those same actors that it can serve as an impartial mediator. Türkiye rejects that characterization, saying its military presence is focused on counterterrorism, strengthening Somali institutions and respecting Somalia’s political process. But perceptions can have consequences even when allegations remain unproven. Could a Future Government Reconsider the Relationship? The political debate raises another question that is attracting increasing attention in Somalia: what happens to the Turkish partnership if a future federal government takes a different view of Ankara’s role? Some opposition figures and political commentators have argued that Somalia’s next government could review existing defence and security arrangements with Türkiye if Ankara is perceived to have abandoned neutrality in domestic political disputes. That is a political expectation, not an established government policy. The current defence framework remains in force, and Somalia continues to describe Türkiye as an important strategic security partner. But the Baidoa crisis has introduced a new variable. Military cooperation that is broadly welcomed when directed against Al-Shabaab can become politically contentious if the same military capabilities are perceived as being deployed during disputes between Somali political factions. That distinction could become increasingly important as Somalia approaches another political transition. Why Somaliland Is Looking to Israel This is the strategic calculation behind Hargeisa’s request. Somaliland has watched Türkiye build a sophisticated military relationship with Mogadishu while its own relationship with Israel has developed rapidly following Israel’s recognition of Somaliland in December 2025. Israel has already begun security cooperation with Somaliland. Somaliland Defence Minister Mohamed Yusuf Ali previously confirmed that Israel was providing training to Somaliland police and military personnel, while saying there were no discussions or plans for an Israeli military base. The request for air-defence systems would take that relationship into a considerably more sensitive area. For Somaliland, Israeli technology could provide a potential defensive counterweight to the growing military capabilities associated with Mogadishu. For Israel, however, supplying advanced air-defence systems would be a major strategic decision with implications for its relationship with Türkiye, Somalia and other regional actors. A New Security Equation in the Horn The emerging regional picture is striking. Türkiye has established a deep military relationship with Mogadishu. Israel has established diplomatic relations with Hargeisa and begun security cooperation. Somaliland is now publicly asking Israel for air-defence capabilities. Meanwhile, Somalia’s unresolved political divisions have demonstrated in Baidoa how quickly political disputes can become armed confrontations. The danger is not that a Turkish-Somaliland military confrontation is inevitable. There is no established evidence that Türkiye is preparing to attack Somaliland. The danger is that the expansion of foreign military capabilities could become entangled with Somalia’s unresolved political disputes, creating perceptions of threat even where governments insist that their objectives are defensive or counterterrorism-related. For Somaliland, Baidoa appears to have provided the clearest warning yet. Hargeisa is looking at what happened when advanced military capabilities entered a deeply divided Somali political environment—and it does not want to wait until a crisis reaches its own doorstep before developing an air-defence strategy. That is why the Israeli request matters. It is not simply about buying weapons. It is about Somaliland’s attempt to ensure that the rapidly changing military balance around Somalia does not leave it without options. And it raises a much larger question for Somalia’s next political chapter: can foreign military partnerships remain credible as neutral security arrangements when Somalia’s political actors increasingly disagree over who controls the state, its forces and its territory? For Türkiye, the answer will depend not only on what Ankara says about neutrality, but on how its military partnership is perceived by the Somali political actors who may govern the country in the future. For Somaliland, the lesson from Baidoa is already clear: air power changes political calculations—and Hargeisa does not intend to ignore the warning. items.title: Soomaaliya iyo Sacuudiga oo ka wada hadlay Xoojinta Xariirka iyo Amniga Badda Cas
items.description: Wasiiru-dowlaha Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda iyo Iskaashiga Caalamiga ah ee Soomaaliya, Cali Maxamed Cumar , ayaa kulan la yeeshay Safiirka Boqortooyada Sacuudiga u fadhiya Soomaaliya, Axmed Maxamed Al-Mould , kaas oo ka dhacay xarunta Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda ee Muqdisho. Kulanka ayaa diiradda lagu saaray sidii loo xoojin lahaa xariirka taariikhiga ah ee Soomaaliya iyo Boqortooyada Sacuudiga , iyadoo labada dhinac ay ka wada hadleen fursadaha lagu horumarin karo iskaashiga labada dal. Wada-hadallada ayaa si gaar ah loogu eegay dhinacyada ganacsiga iyo maalgashiga , iyadoo la adkeeyay muhiimadda ay leedahay in la kordhiyo iskaashiga dhaqaale ee labada dal iyo in la abuuro fursado cusub oo maalgashi. Sidoo kale, Wasiiru-dowlaha iyo Safiirka Sacuudiga ayaa ka wada hadlay amniga Badda Cas , oo ah marin muhiim u ah ganacsiga iyo isu-socodka gobolka iyo caalamkaba. Kulankan ayaa qeyb ka ah dadaallada lagu sii xoojinayo xiriirka diblomaasiyadeed iyo iskaashiga u dhexeeya Soomaaliya iyo Boqortooyada Sacuudiga, iyadoo labada dal ay leeyihiin xiriir muddo dheer soo jiray oo ku saleysan iskaashi iyo dano wadaag.

items.title: Hiiraan Community Power Struggle Threatens to Deepen Hirshabelle Crisis
items.description: Hawadle Demand for Hirshabelle Presidency Collides With Hassan Sheikh’s Backing of Abgaal President Ali Guudlaawe BELEDWEYNE (WDN) — The crisis in Hirshabelle is increasingly becoming a struggle over political power, with the Hawadle community demanding the presidency of the regional state while President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud has backed incumbent President Ali Abdullahi Hussein Guudlaawe, an Abgaal politician, for another term. The dispute has gone far beyond an ordinary election contest. Hawadle political leaders and elders say they were led to expect that the presidency would return to their community under an informal power-sharing understanding, but President Hassan Sheikh ultimately supported Guudlaawe instead. Hirshabelle Vice President Yusuf Hagar Dabageed has publicly accused the president of breaking that understanding. The confrontation has now spilled into the political and security environment of Hiiraan. Hawadle leaders have rejected the planned election without a prior political agreement, while elders have moved to prevent Hirshabelle officials and aircraft from operating through airports in Hiiraan until their grievances are addressed. Al-Shabaab also says it has reached an understanding with Hawadle elders in Maxaas to end years of fighting. The reported agreement has not been independently verified, and it is unclear whether the elders involved represent the wider Hawadle community. But its emergence at a time of intense political confrontation with Mogadishu gives the development far greater significance. Macawisly militia A Presidency Dispute with Wider Consequences The immediate dispute is about who should lead Hirshabelle. Hawadle leaders argue that political representation and power-sharing must be settled before an election can proceed. President Hassan Sheikh’s support for Guudlaawe has therefore been interpreted by opposing Hawadle figures as a departure from an earlier political understanding. At the same time, the Hawadle community is not politically united. A separate Hawadle political council led by former Hirshabelle President Ali Abdullahi Osoble has backed Guudlaawe and supported participation in the election. That division is important. The confrontation should not be presented as if every Hawadle leader holds the same position. But the scale of the opposition is significant. Hawadle elders and politicians have demanded a political settlement, and demonstrations in Beledweyne have rejected an election without an agreement on representation and power-sharing. The Al-Shabaab Factor Hawadle communities were among the most important local forces in the fight against Al-Shabaab during the 2022 Macawisley offensive. Local fighters, working alongside Somali government forces, helped drive Al-Shabaab from large areas of central Somalia. But the gains were not permanent. Al-Shabaab later regained territory, while prolonged fighting imposed heavy costs on communities that had participated in the war. The reported understanding in Maxaas therefore raises a serious question: what happens when a community that once fought Al-Shabaab begins looking for local arrangements with the group while simultaneously confronting the federal government over political representation? Al-Shabaab has previously sought agreements with local clans and sub-clans when such arrangements serve its interests. Similar understandings involving Hawadle subdivisions were reported in 2023. The latest development should therefore not automatically be interpreted as a Hawadle alliance with Al-Shabaab. It may instead reflect a combination of local security concerns, political frustration and war fatigue. A Political Crisis Becoming a Security Risk For Mogadishu, the danger is that a dispute over the Hirshabelle presidency could gradually become something much larger. The federal government faces an increasingly difficult choice: push ahead with an election that significant Hawadle figures reject, or reopen negotiations over the political settlement and power-sharing arrangements. The Al-Shabaab development adds urgency to that choice. The central question is no longer simply who will become president of Hirshabelle. It is whether the struggle over political power will deepen the alienation of a community that has already paid a heavy price fighting Al-Shabaab — and create new space for the militant group to exploit. If political disputes continue without a settlement, Al-Shabaab may not need to defeat its former opponents militarily. It may simply wait for political frustration, insecurity and exhaustion to do the work. items.title: Madaxda Soomaaliya,  Masar, Eritrea, iyo Suudaan oo ku baaqay xal Siyaasadeed
items.description: Mas’uuliyiinta ugu sarreeya ee Soomasliya, Masar, Eritrea, Masar, iyo Suudaan ayaa soo saaray bayaan wadajir ah oo ay ku baaqayaan in colaadaha ka socda gobolka lagu dhammeeyo wada-hadal iyo xalal siyaasadeed , xilli dagaalladu ka sii xoogeysanayaan Suudaan iyo Itoobiya. Madaxweynaha Masar Abdel Fattah el-Sisi, Madaxweynaha Eritrea Isaias Afwerki, Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud iyo Taliyaha Ciidanka Suudaan Abdel Fattah al-Burhan ayaa kulmay Axaddii magaalada New Alamein ee dalka Masar, halkaas oo ay ka soo saareen bayaanka wadajirka ah. Bayaanka ayaa si gaar ah u taageeray in colaadda Suudaan lagu dhammeeyo hannaan siyaasadeed oo ay hoggaaminayaan dhinacyada Suudaan, iyadoo dalkaasi uu dagaal kula jiray tan iyo Abriil 2023 ciidamada dowladda iyo ciidamada gurmadka degdegga ah ee RSF. Afarta dal ayaa sidoo kale sheegay in maamulka iyo amniga Badda Cas ay tahay inay door weyn ku yeeshaan dalalka xeebaha leh, arrintaas oo ku soo beegmaysa dadaallada Itoobiya ay ku doonayso inay ku hesho marin ganacsi iyo joogitaan badeed, maadaama Itoobiya ay tahay dal aan bad lahayn. Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud ayaa hore u sheegay in Soomaaliya aysan diiddanayn in Itoobiya hesho marin ganacsi oo ay isticmaasho dekedaha Soomaaliya, balse uu shardi yahay in arrintaasi lagu heshiiyo Soomaaliya. Bayaanka ayaa sidoo kale ka hadlay muranka ka dhashay Biyo-xireenka Weyn ee Itoobiya ee Renaissance Dam , iyadoo Masar iyo Suudaan ay ka digeen tallaabooyin hal dhinac ah oo ay sheegeen inay saameyn ku yeelan karaan dalalka ku teedsan webiga Nile. Kulanka afarta dal ayaa ku soo beegmay xilli dagaallo culus ay ka socdaan Itoobiya, gaar ahaan gobolka Tigray, halkaas oo ciidamada dowladda federaalka iyo isbahaysi hubeysan oo ka kooban dhowr kooxood ay isku hayaan dagaallo cusub. Ciidamada dowladda Itoobiya iyo kuwa xulafada la ah ayaa Axaddii dib ula wareegay magaalada Mekelle, caasimadda gobolka Tigray, kadib markii TPLF ay sheegtay inay si ku-meel-gaar ah uga baxday magaalada, ayna hawlgalladeeda ka sii wadi doonto meel kale. Mas’uuliyiinta Itoobiya ayaa sidoo kale Eritrea ku eedeeyay inay taageerayso isbahaysiga hubeysan ee dagaalka kula jira dowladda federaalka. Eritrea ayaa beenisay eedeymahaas, iyadoo wasiirka warfaafinta Eritrea uu sheegay in Addis Ababa ay isku dayayso inay abuurto marmarsiiyo ay Eritrea ku weerarto. Hoggaamiyeyaasha afarta dal ayaa, iyadoo xaaladdu sidaas tahay, xoogga saaray muhiimadda wada-hadalka, xasilloonida gobolka iyo xal siyaasadeed , xilli colaadaha Suudaan iyo Itoobiya ay saameyn ku yeelan karaan amniga guud ee Geeska Afrika iyo Badda Cas.

items.title: Mekelle Falls as Tigray War Explodes Into a Regional Crisis
items.description: TPLF Withdraws After 11 Days of Fighting as Ethiopia-Eritrea Relations Collapse and Regional Powers Move to Coordinate MEKELLE (WDN) — Ethiopia’s renewed Tigray war has moved with extraordinary speed from a major Tigrayan offensive to the fall of Mekelle, while a parallel diplomatic crisis between Ethiopia and Eritrea threatens to turn the conflict into a wider Horn of Africa confrontation. The current round of fighting began on September 23, when forces led by the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) launched a major offensive against Ethiopian federal forces. The Tigrayan side initially made advances, including taking control of Mekelle’s main airport. The federal government responded with a rapid counteroffensive. Over the following days, Ethiopian federal forces and allied fighters retook strategic positions and advanced toward Mekelle. By the end of September, fighting had intensified around the capital, while reports of drone strikes and disruptions to communications and commercial flights underscored the growing severity of the conflict. Then the crisis widened beyond the battlefield. On October 1 , Eritrea announced that it was severing diplomatic relations with Ethiopia after Addis Ababa accused Eritrea of supporting the TPLF-led opposition alliance. Eritrea rejected the accusation. Ethiopia had already closed its embassy in Asmara and expelled Eritrean diplomats. By October 2–3 , federal forces and their allies were closing in on Mekelle. The airport was retaken, and pro-government Tigray Peace Forces advanced into the city. On October 3 , the TPLF announced that it was withdrawing from Mekelle and that the regional government would temporarily operate from elsewhere. By October 4, Reuters confirmed that Ethiopian federal forces and allied militias had regained control of the Tigrayan capital. The entire sequence unfolded in just 11 days. That speed is what makes the latest crisis so dangerous. Mekelle has fallen, but there has been no declaration that the war is over. items.title: Weerarrada lagu Bartilmaameedsanayo Maraakiibta Shidaalka oo Ku Sii kordhaya Bariga Dhexe
items.description: Weerarrada lagu bartilmaameedsanayo maraakiibta qaadda shidaalka ayaa sii kordhaya, inkastoo dhoofinta saliidda cayriin ee gobolka Bariga Dhexe ay weli ku socoto heerar xooggan. Maraakiibta xamuulka shidaalka ayaa weli maraya qaar ka mid ah waddooyinka muhiimka ah ee badda, kuwaas oo laf-dhabar u ah ganacsiga iyo gaarsiinta tamarta ee suuqyada caalamka. Kororka khataraha amni ee ka jira marin-biyoodka muhiimka ah ayaa sare u qaaday walaaca laga qabo badqabka maraakiibta, hakad ku yimaada silsiladaha sahayda iyo saameynta ay tani ku yeelan karto suuqyada tamarta ee caalamka . Khubarada iyo shirkadaha ka shaqeeya gaadiidka badda ayaa si gaar ah isha ugu haya xaaladda, maadaama carqalad weyn oo ku timaadda isu-socodka maraakiibta shidaalka ay saameyn ku yeelan karto qiimaha iyo helitaanka saliidda ee suuqyada caalamka. Inkasta oo dhoofinta shidaalka Bariga Dhexe ay weli tahay mid xooggan, haddana sii kordhaya khataraha amni ayaa muujinaya caqabadda ka dhex jirta sii socoshada ganacsiga tamarta iyo ilaalinta amniga maraakiibta . Xaaladda ayaa weli u baahan in si dhow loola socdo, iyadoo marin-biyoodka Bariga Dhexe uu yahay mid muhiim u ah dhaq-dhaqaaqa saliidda iyo badeecooyinka tamarta ee suuqyada caalamka.

items.title: Madaxda Soomaaliya iyo Suudaan oo Kulan ku yeeshay Al-Alamein
items.description: Madaxweynaha Golaha Madaxbannaanida Ku-meelgaarka ah ee Suudaan, General Cabdifataax Al-Burhan , ayaa kulan la yeeshay Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, Dr. Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud , magaalada New Alamein ee dalka Masar. Kulanka ayaa ka dhacay xilli labada madaxweyne ay ka qeybgalayeen shir wadatashi oo ay isugu yimaadeen madaxda Masar, Suudaan, Soomaaliya iyo Eritrea , kaas oo looga hadlay xaaladaha siyaasadeed iyo amni ee Geeska Afrika iyo gobolka Badda Cas. Madaxda afarta dal ayaa kulanka ku adkeeyay muhiimadda ay leedahay in la ixtiraamo madaxbannaanida, midnimada iyo wadajirka dhuleed ee dalalka gobolka, iyadoo sidoo kale lagu baaqay in khilaafaadka lagu xalliyo waddooyin siyaasadeed iyo nabadeed. Arrimaha Suudaan ayaa si gaar ah uga mid ahaa qodobadii laga hadlay, iyadoo madaxdu taageereen midnimada iyo hay’adaha qaranka Suudaan, isla markaana ku baaqeen in dib loo bilaabo hannaan siyaasadeed ay hoggaaminayaan dhinacyada Suudaan. Kulanka Al-Alamein ayaa sidoo kale lagu isla meel dhigay in la xoojiyo wada-tashiga iyo iskaashiga u dhexeeya afarta dal, iyadoo la sameynayo hannaan dabagal ku sameeya natiijooyinka shirarka, kuwaas oo la qorsheeyay in si joogto ah loo qabto. Shirkan ayaa kusoo beegmaya xilli gobolka Geeska Afrika iyo Badda Cas ay wajahayaan caqabado siyaasadeed iyo amni oo isbiirsaday, taas oo sii kordhisay muhiimadda wada-shaqeynta iyo isku-duwidda dalalka gobolka.

items.title: Dagaalka Tigray oo Saameyn ku yeeshay Xiriirka dalalka Geeska Afrika
items.description: Xiisadda ka taagan gobolka Tigray ee waqooyiga Itoobiya ayaa mar kale dhalisay walaac ku saabsan xaaladda siyaasadeed iyo amni ee gudaha dalka Itoobiya, iyadoo saameynteedu ay gaareyso xiriirka Itoobiya ay la leedahay dalalka kale ee Geeska Afrika. Xiisadaha gudaha Itoobiya ayaa sidoo kale ku soo beegmaya xilli xiriirka dalalka Geeska Afrika ay wajahayaan caqabado siyaasadeed iyo diblomaasiyadeed. items.title: Guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka oo Kulan Muhiim ah la yeeshay Madaxweynaha Baarlamaanka Carabta
items.description: Guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka ee Baarlamaanka Federaalka Soomaaliya, Cabdulqaadir Maxamed Nuur (Jaamac) , ayaa magaalada Arusha ee dalka Tanzania kulan kula yeeshay Madaxweynaha Baarlamaanka Carabta, Mohamed Ahmed Al-Yamahi . Kulanka ayaa diiradda lagu saaray xoojinta xiriirka iyo iskaashiga baarlamaaniga ah ee u dhexeeya Soomaaliya iyo dalalka Carabta, iyadoo labada dhinac ay isla garteen muhiimadda ay leedahay in la joogteeyo wada-tashiyada iyo isku-duwidda mowqifyada laga yeesho arrimaha ay wadaagaan. Sidoo kale, waxaa kulanka looga hadlay sidii loo xoojin lahaa doorka Soomaaliya ee iskaashiga baarlamaaniga ah ee dunida Carabta, iyadoo la adkeeyay muhiimadda ay leedahay in la sii horumariyo xiriirka ka dhexeeya hay’adaha sharci-dejinta Soomaaliya iyo kuwa dalalka Carabta. Guddoomiye Cabdulqaadir Maxamed Nuur iyo Madaxweyne Mohamed Ahmed Al-Yamahi ayaa sidoo kale carrabka ku adkeeyay xiriirka taariikhiga ah ee ka dhexeeya Soomaaliya iyo dalalka Carabta, kaas oo ku saleysan is-ixtiraam, dano wadaag iyo iskaashi. Guddoomiyaha Golaha Shacabka ayaa sheegay in Soomaaliya ay muhiimad gaar ah siinayso xoojinta xiriirka baarlamaaniga ah ee ay la leedahay dalalka Carabta. Cabdulqaadir Maxamed Nuur ayaa sidoo kale uga mahadceliyay dowladaha Carabta taageerada ay Soomaaliya ka siiyaan ilaalinta midnimada, madax-bannaanida, qarannimada iyo wadajirka dhuleed ee dalka . Kulankan ayaa ka mid ahaa kulamada ka socda magaalada Arusha ee Tanzania, iyadoo mas’uuliyiinta Soomaaliya ay halkaasi kaga qaybgalayaan hawlo la xiriira iskaashiga iyo xiriirka baarlamaaniga ah.

items.title: Somaliland oo sheegtay in DF Soomaaliya ay qorsheyneyso duullaan ay ku qabsaneyso
items.description: Hargeysa (Caasimada Online) – Mas’uul sare oo ka tirsan maamulka Somaliland ayaa sheegay in Muqdisho ay ka fekereyso duullaan ka dhan ah Somaliland oo ku qabsato, isaga oo ku dooday in Turkey uu taageerayo tallaabadaas haddii ay dhacdo. Maxamed Cabdiraxmaan Xasan, agaasimaha guud ee wasaaradda arrimaha dibadda Somaliland, ayaa hadalkan ku sheegay wareysi uu siiyay warbaahinta Middle East Eye . “Muqdisho waxay ka fekereysaa duullaan, Turkey-na wuu taageeri lahaa,” ayuu yiri Maxamed, isaga oo intaas ku daray in Somaliland ay u baahan tahay inay “isu diyaariso mustaqbalka”. Sheegashadan si madax-bannaan looma xaqiijin, dowladda federaalka Soomaaliya-na ma shaacin wax qorshe ah oo ku saabsan howlgal militari oo ka dhan ah Somaliland. Hadallada Maxamed ayaa kusoo beegmaya xilli xiriirka Somaliland iyo Israel uu sii yeelanayo dhinac amni, iyadoo mas’uuliyiin kale oo Somaliland ah ay sheegeen inay doonayaan taageero militari oo Israel ay ka helaan si ay uga hortagaan waxa ay ku tilmaameen awoodda militari ee Turkey ee Soomaaliya ku sii kordheysa. Israel oo laga doonayo difaaca hawada Maxamed Cusmaan Fadal, oo ah la-taliye sare oo arrimaha dibadda u qaabilsan madaxweynaha Somaliland Cabdiraxmaan Maxamed Cabdullaahi, ayaa Middle East Eye u sheegay in Somaliland ay si gaar ah u dooneyso nidaamyada difaaca hawada ee Israel. “Waxaan u baahanahay nidaamyada difaaca hawada,” ayuu yiri Fadal. “Turkey wuxuu F-16 ku leeyahay Muqdisho, wuxuuna doonayaa inuu saldhig diyaaradaha aan duuliyaha lahayn ka sameeyo Soomaaliya,” ayuu raaciyay. Fadal ayaa kadib si toos ah u yiri: “Waxaan rabnaa in Israel ay naga taageerto Turkey.” Hadalladan ayaa muujinaya sida ay qaar ka mid ah mas’uuliyiinta Somaliland u arkaan xiriirka cusub ee Israel, iyadoo Israel ay bishii December 2025 noqotay dalkii ugu horreeyay ee Somaliland u aqoonsada dal madax-bannaan. Turkey ayaa ka mid ah saaxiibada istaraatiijiga ah ee ugu dhow dowladda Soomaaliya, wuxuuna sanadihii dambe si weyn u ballaariyay joogitaankiisa militari, dhaqaale iyo diblomaasiyadeed. Ankara ayaa Muqdisho ku leh xarunteeda militari ee ugu weyn ee dibadda, waxaana halkaas lagu tababaray kumannaan askari oo Soomaali ah. Soomaaliya iyo Turkey ayaa 2024 sidoo kale kala saxiixday heshiis difaac iyo iskaashi dhaqaale oo muddo 10 sano ah, kaas oo Ankara kaalin ka siinaya dhismaha iyo tababarka ciidamada badda Soomaaliya iyo ilaalinta xeebaha dalka. Turkey ayaa sanadkan sidoo kale Soomaaliya keenay diyaarado dagaal oo F-16 ah, kuwaas oo bishii April ka qeyb-galay dabaaldegga sanad-guurada ciidamada xoogga dalka ee Muqdisho. Joogitaankaas militari ayaa hadda u muuqda inuu yahay mid ka mid ah waxyaabaha ugu waaweyn ee ay Somaliland ku saleyneyso dalabkeeda taageerada amni ee Israel. items.title: Mareykanka oo deg deg uga baxay saldhig ku yaal UK kadib markii la ogaaday in Iran ay…
items.description: London (Caasimada Online) – Mareykanka ayaa si degdeg ah dhammaan 12-ka diyaaradood ee dagaalka ee B-1 uga saaray saldhigga RAF Fairford ee koonfurta Britain, kadib markii saraakiisha militariga ay heleen xog cusub oo ku saabsan qorshe weerar oo la tuhunsan yahay inuu xiriir la leeyahay Iran. Tallaabadan oo dhacday dhammaadkii toddobaadka ayaa ahayd mid aan caadi ahayn, maadaama Mareykanku uu si dhif ah diyaarado tiro intaas le’eg uga daadgureeyo saldhig ku yaalla waddan xulafo la ah oo kumannaan kiiloomitir u jira goobaha dagaalka. Laba sarkaal oo Mareykan ah ayaa New York Times u sheegay in xaaladda loo arkay mid aad u degdeg badan, taasoo keentay in qaar ka mid ah diyaaradaha iyo shaqaalahooda ay duulaan xilli diyaaradaha shidaalka hawada ku bixiya weli loo diyaarinayey inay taageeraan safarkooda dib ugu laabanaya Mareykanka. Ugu yaraan saddex ka mid ah diyaaradaha ayaa Axaddii gaaray saldhiggooda South Dakota, sida ay saraakiishu sheegeen. Taliska Mareykanka ee Yurub ayaa xaqiijiyey in dhammaan diyaaradaha laga saaray Britain, balse wuxuu ka gaabsaday inuu faahfaahin ka bixiyo hanjabaadaha cusub ee sababay go’aanka. “Waxaan hadda xaqiijin karnaa in dhammaan diyaaradaha wax duqeeya ee Mareykanka ee lagu geeyey RAF Fairford dib loogu celinayo saldhigyadooda gudaha Mareykanka,” ayuu talisku ku yiri bayaan. Wasaaradda Difaaca Britain ayaa iyaduna diiday inay ka hadasho dhaqdhaqaaqa hantida militariga Mareykanka. Saraakiisha Mareykanka ma aysan shaacin nooca xogta cusub ee keentay in diyaaradaha sida degdegga ah looga saaro saldhigga, balse hal sarkaal ayaa sheegay in xogtu ay la xiriirto digniino soo baxay saddex toddobaad ka hor, iyadoo faahfaahinta iyo heerka degdegga ahi ay si weyn u kordheen 24-kii saac ee ugu dambeeyey. Qaar ka mid ah B-1-yada la saaray ayaa saldhigga yimid toddobaadkii lasoo dhaafay oo keliya, iyagoo qayb ka ahaa wareeg caadi ah oo ciidamada Mareykanka ah. Go’aanka ayaa yimid toddobaad kadib markii booliska Britain ay xireen shan nin oo lagu arkay baabuurro cadcad meel u dhow RAF Fairford, oo ka mid ah saldhigyada ay diyaaradaha Mareykanku u adeegsadeen hawlgallada dagaalka ka dhanka ah Iran. Raggaas ayaa maalintii xigtay damiin lagu sii daayey kadib markii aan wax walxaha qarxa ah laga helin baabuurtooda, balse boolisku waxay sheegeen in baaritaankoodu weli socdo. Khamiistii, booliska la-dagaallanka argagixisada Britain ayaa sidoo kale xiray nin haysta dhalashada Britain iyo Iran, kaas oo looga shakisan yahay diyaarinta falal argagixiso oo la xiriira baaritaanka RAF Fairford. Ninkaas ayaa markii dambe damiin lagu sii daayey iyadoo baaritaanku sii socdo. Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Britain Andy Burnham ayaa toddobaadkii hore sheegay in dowladda Britain ay hayso xog muujinaysa in Iran ay door ku lahayd qorshaha la tuhunsan yahay. Saraakiil Mareykan iyo British ah ayaa sidoo kale baaraya suurtagalnimada in qorshuhu xiriir la leeyahay Ciidanka Ilaalada Kacaanka Islaamiga ah ee Iran, IRGC, ama xarun kale oo militari oo ku taal Tehran. Iran ayaa si adag u beenisay eedeymahaas. Booliska Britain ayaa sheegay inay baarayaan dhammaan jihooyinka suurtagalka ah, oo ay ku jirto ku lug lahaanshaha dowlad shisheeye. Xiisadda ku saabsan RAF Fairford ma ahan mid cusub. Bishii July, Ilaalada Kacaanka Iran ayaa si cad uga digtay Britain inay Mareykanka u oggolaato inuu saldhiggaas u isticmaalo weerarro ka dhan ah Iran. “Wax saldhig ah oo loo adeegsado weerarro lagu qaado dhulka Iran wuxuu bartilmaameed sharci ah u yahay ciidamadeenna,” ayaa lagu yiri digniinta Iran. Bishii September, saraakiisha militariga Mareykanka ayaa sidoo kale helay digniino sirdoon oo Mareykan iyo reer Galbeed ah oo sheegayey in RAF Fairford uu halis ugu jiro weerar ay Iran taageerto. Sida laga soo xigtay saraakiisha xogtaas lagu wargeliyey, hay’adaha sirdoonka ayaa sawir ka sameeyey qorshaha la tuhunsan yahay iyagoo adeegsanaya isgaarsiino la qabtay, xog ay bixiyeen ilo sirdoon iyo macluumaad kale. Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Israel Benjamin Netanyahu ayaa isna sheegay in sirdoonka dalkiisa uu Britain uga digay suurtagalnimada weerar ay Iran taageerto, inkastoo digniintaasi aysan magacaabin bartilmaameed gaar ah. Qiimeynaha sirdoonka ayaa sidoo kale ka digay in haddii weerar dhaco ay suurtagal tahay in weerarro kale oo daba socda loo adeegsado diyaaradaha aan duuliyaha lahayn. Digniinahaas ayaa sare u qaaday walaaca saldhigyada Mareykanka ee Yurub. Sida uu sheegay sarkaal sare oo Mareykan ah, Israel ayaa Jarmalka uga digtay in saldhigyada Mareykanka ee Spangdahlem iyo Ramstein ay iyaguna wajahaan halis sare. Ka saarista dhammaan B-1-yada RAF Fairford ayaa hadda muujineysa sida dhab ah ee Washington u qaadatay khatarta la tuhunsan yahay. Reuters iyo warbaahin kale ayaa Axaddii xaqiijiyey in diyaaradaha laga saaray saldhigga iyadoo baaritaanka Britain ee qorshaha argagixiso uu weli socdo. Haddii la xaqiijiyo in Tehran ay ka dambeysay qorshe lagu weerarayo saldhig militari oo ku yaalla Britain, waxay noqon doontaa sare-u-kac weyn oo ku yimaada xiisadda Iran iyo dalalka reer Galbeedka, xilli dagaalka Iran iyo xulafada Mareykanka uu sii kordhiyey halista ka dhalan karta saldhigyada ay ciidamada Mareykanku ku leeyihiin Yurub. Reuters iyo warbaahin kale ayaa Axaddii xaqiijiyey in diyaaradaha laga saaray saldhigga iyadoo baaritaanka Britain ee qorshaha argagixiso uu weli socdo. Haddii la xaqiijiyo in Tehran ay ka dambeysay qorshe lagu weerarayo saldhig militari oo ku yaalla Britain, waxay noqon doontaa sare-u-kac weyn oo ku yimaada xiisadda Iran iyo dalalka reer Galbeedka, xilli dagaalka Iran iyo xulafada Mareykanka uu sii kordhiyey halista ka dhalan karta saldhigyada ay ciidamada Mareykanku ku leeyihiin Yurub. items.title: Higher Education and Federalism in Somalia: What the Constitution and Higher Education Laws Actually provide
items.description: By Dr. Abdirazak Takar On 4 March 2026, Somalia adopted a new constitution in Mogadishu , ratified under President Hassan Sheikh Mohamed, replacing the Provisional Constitution that had governed the federal project since 2012.  For outside observers, Somali’s federal experiment is easy to misrepresentation as either a fragile arrangement barely holding the country together or a formality that changes little in practice. Neither view survives contact with the text. Among its articles and schedules is a clear answer to a question that has troubled Somali higher education policy for over a decade: does responsibility for universities, research institutes and technical colleges belong the Federal Government or to the Federal Member States? The new text is unambiguous about the multi-level character of higher education governance. Article 25(5) assigns the development of higher education to the different levels of government, and the Second Schedule places both higher education, technology and research institutions, and the development and quality of education more broadly, among the powers the Federal Government and Federal Member States hold concurrently. The constitutional framework envisions a system of shared and collaborative governance, rather than one in which either level of government administers exclusively    Article 29(5): A Deliberate Rewrite The old Provisional Constitution’s Article 30(7) read simply: “The State shall promote higher education, technical institutes, and technology and research institutions.” In Somali constitutional practice, “the State” (Dawladda) has generally been understood, rightly or wrongly, as shorthand for the Federal Government. The new constitution abandons that language. Article 29(5) now reads: “Heerarka kala duwan ee hay’adaha dawladda ee u xilsaaran waxbarashada waa in ay horumariyaan tacliinta sare, machadyada farsamo, tiknoolijiyada, cilmibaarista, hal-abuurka, cayaaraha, hiddaha iyo dhaqanka.”  (“The various levels of government institutions responsible for education shall develop higher education, technical institutes, technology, research, innovation, sport, heritage and culture.”) This is not a minor stylistic change. Replacing “the State” with “the various levels of government institutions” broadens the provision deliberately, recognising that federal, state and local institutions each carry this obligation. The 2012 text could reasonably be read as assigning higher education to Mogadishu alone. The 2026 text closes off that reading. The Schedule Confirms the Position If any doubt remained after Article 29(5), the Second Schedule settles it. The constitution distinguishes between Schedule Two (A), the exclusive powers of the Federal Government; Schedule Two (B), powers held concurrently by both levels of government; and Schedule Two (C), the exclusive powers of the Federal Member States. Item 8 of Schedule Two (B) lists “the development plan for education and the protection of its quality” among the concurrent powers. Item 41 of the same schedule, the final entry under its education heading, then adds: “Tacliinta sare, tiknoolijiyadda iyo hay’adaha cilmibaarista.”  (“Higher education, technology, and research institutions.”) Both provisions sit in Schedule Two (B). Neither appears in Schedule Two (C), which begins immediately afterwards with an entirely different list covering matters such as state constitutions and state budgets. Higher education and the development and quality of education generally are, in other words, companion entries within the same concurrent list, not powers split across separate federal and state schedules. The constitution treats them as a shared undertaking. A Deliberate Distinction, Not an Omission The drafters plainly understood the difference between functions that require a single national authority and those that do not, because they drew that line explicitly in the neighbouring schedule. Item 40 of Schedule Two (A), the exclusive federal list, gives the Federal Government sole authority over curriculum setting, teacher training, and national secondary school certification examinations. Those functions demand a single national standard, and the constitution says so without qualification. Higher education was not given the same treatment. It was placed instead in the concurrent schedule, alongside the general duty to develop education and protect its quality. The stronger constitutional inference is that curriculum, teacher training and national examinations were considered to need one national voice, while higher education, technology and research were considered to need shared national and state involvement rather than exclusive control by either level. Articles 64 and 68: How the Shared Power Operates The position becomes clearer still when the surrounding articles are read alongside Article 29(5) and Schedule Two (B). Article 64 sets out the constitution’s general principles of federalism, including the requirement that governmental power be distributed across all levels of government, that levels of government cooperate continuously with one another, and that responsibility for delivering services be assigned to whichever level of government has sufficient capacity to deliver them most effectively and is closest to the citizen being served. Article 68 then gives the concurrent powers listed in Schedule Two (B) a specific operating structure, rather than leaving them undifferentiated. It assigns responsibility for legislation, policy, regulation, standards and monitoring in concurrent areas to the Federal Government, while assigning implementation and execution of those same powers to the Federal Member States. Applied to higher education, this is a considered division of labour. The Federal Government’s role is to set national policy, standards and regulatory frameworks and to monitor their application. The Federal Member States’ role is to implement them, including through their own institutions such as state-level higher education commissions. Read together, Article 29(5), Article 64, Article 68 and Schedule Two (B) describe one coherent model: national standards set and monitored centrally, delivered through Federal Member State institutions on the ground. National Standards Without a Single Administrator This constitutional structure resolves a false choice that has shaped the debate for years: the assumption that credible national standards require a single national administrator. Somalia clearly needs coherence in higher education. Qualifications should carry the same weight whether earned in Mogadishu, Garowe or Kismayo. Quality assurance systems need to command the confidence of employers and international partners. Research institutions should be able to meet recognised benchmarks. None of this requires concentrating every regulatory decision in one federal office. A concurrent power, structured as Article 68 structures it, is built to deliver both outcomes at once: national standards, exercised in practice through Federal Member State institutions. What the Higher Education Laws Actually Provide The constitutional question becomes more concrete when the two higher education laws already in force are examined. The Federal Higher Education Law, enacted in December 2024, creates a substantial national regulatory architecture. It defines “Government” as the Federal Government, provides that the Minister leads national higher education policy after consultation with Federal Member State education authorities and the National Higher Education Commission, and establishes the National Commission with its headquarters in the capital and branches in the Federal Member States. The Commission is given broad functions, including setting standards for higher education institutions, inspecting and evaluating them, granting accreditation, determining qualification requirements, and recognising degrees and diplomas. (Federal Higher Education Law, Law No. 30, 4 December 2024, Articles 2, 4, 9 to 10 and 19 to 20.) The Federal law also recognises a Federal Member State role. Article 35 provides that a Federal Member State may establish a university and assumes responsibility for its facilities, with the university’s budget approved by the state parliament. The same provision, however, requires the state university to proceed through procedures set by the Federal law, while the law separately allows the Federal Government to establish higher education institutions elsewhere in the country. The statutory model is therefore mixed: it recognises state institutions while placing extensive licensing, accreditation and quality control functions within the federal framework. (Federal Higher Education Law, Articles 23 to 35.) Puntland’s amended Higher Education Law establishes a parallel state-level framework. Its scope extends throughout Puntland and applies to Puntland’s higher education institutions. It establishes the Puntland Higher Education Commission as a legally independent administrative body under the political supervision of the Ministry of Education, empowered to set standards for opening and operating higher education institutions, determine qualification requirements, inspect and evaluate institutions, grant accreditation, and develop higher education policy and strategy for Puntland. It also gives the Commission a direct role in establishing and accrediting universities and other institutions, and places responsibility for their facilities and budgets on the Puntland Government. (Puntland Higher Education Law, as amended in 2025, Articles 3 to 6, 19 to 20 and 23 to 30.) The comparison reveals a genuine overlap. The two statutes cover much of the same regulatory ground: standards, accreditation, inspection, recognition and institutional establishment. That overlap does not by itself show that either level possesses exclusive authority. It shows instead that the statutory framework developed with substantial regulatory roles at both levels, before the 2026 Constitution clarified how those roles should relate to one another. The Federal law predates the new constitution, and so do Puntland’s 2025 amendments. Both should now be read, and where necessary revised, in line with the allocation confirmed in Article 29(5), Schedule Two (B) and Article 68, rather than treated as settling the matter on their own terms. Read this way, the statutes reinforce the constitutional argument rather than complicate it. A national framework is plainly valuable, and the Federal law shows why. But a national framework does not require every accreditation, licensing, inspection or institutional decision to be administered from the centre. Puntland’s law shows that substantial regulatory capacity already exists at the Federal Member State level. The more coherent solution is a functional division consistent with Article 68: national standards and monitoring, exercised through Federal Member State implementation, with agreed mechanisms for mutual recognition. Two Commissions, One Constitutional Logic The coexistence of a National Higher Education Commission and a Puntland Higher Education Commission should be read in light of both the constitutional allocation of powers and the statutes enacted under it. Neither institution’s existence is, by itself, evidence that the other must yield. The precise legal task is to harmonise their statutory powers with the constitutional division set out above. That task is not to decide which commission should give way, but to identify which functions are genuinely national, which sit within Federal Member State authority, and which require cooperation. Common benchmarks, mutual recognition, compatible accreditation procedures, shared data and a standing federal and state dialogue on quality assurance can supply the connective structure. A National Higher Education Commission can perform national coordination and standard setting where constitutionally authorised, while a state-level commission regulates and supervises institutions within its own jurisdiction. The aim should be complementarity, not duplication or unilateral expansion by either side. Towards a Federal Higher Education Compact What Somalia needs now is not a further contest over jurisdiction, but a negotiated Federal Higher Education Compact that translates the constitutional allocation into workable administrative arrangements: agreed national quality benchmarks, clear accreditation and licensing pathways, mutual recognition between federal and state regulators, shared data systems, and a standing mechanism for resolving disputes through dialogue and constitutional procedure. Such a compact matters because the existing statutes predate the 2026 Constitution and were drafted against an earlier and less settled understanding of how federal and state authority over higher education should relate. The aim should not be to invalidate the legitimate regulatory objectives of either law, but to clarify institutional boundaries and build a coherent federal and state system consistent with what the constitution now provides. Why Adherence to the Text Matters Now The analysis above is not a merely academic exercise. It has direct bearing on how the Federal Ministry of Education, and Federal Member State authorities such as Puntland’s Ministry of Education and its Higher Education Commission, should conduct themselves in practice. Where the constitution assigns a function concurrently, as it does with higher education, technology, research institutions, and the development and protection of education quality, the Federal Government’s role under Article 68 is to set policy, standards and regulation and to monitor their application. It is not to administer Puntland’s universities directly, to bypass Puntland’s own statutory Higher Education Commission, or to treat implementation, which the constitution assigns to Federal Member States, as a federal prerogative. A Federal Government that exceeds this role, whether by asserting licensing or accreditation authority the constitution does not give it, by disregarding Puntland’s Higher Education Law, or by making appointments and decisions that displace rather than coordinate with Puntland’s Commission, is not exercising national leadership. It is departing from the constitutional text this article has set out. The remedy is not political improvisation on either side, but adherence to Article 29(5), Schedule Two (B) and Article 68 as written, and to the Federal Higher Education Law and Puntland’s Higher Education Law as they stand until lawfully harmonised through negotiation. This matters beyond the immediate dispute. Federal systems are judged internationally by whether their central governments observe the limits the constitution places on them, not only by whether subnational governments comply with the centre. A Federal Government that treats concurrent powers as an opening for administrative expansion, rather than a basis for cooperation, risks the same institutional distrust, duplicated structures and politicised disputes over academic quality that this article has warned against throughout. That outcome would serve neither Somalia’s national cohesion nor Puntland’s legitimate institutional interests. It would serve only the temporary convenience of whichever office in Mogadishu found it expedient to disregard the allocation of powers the constitution itself sets out. None of this is a case against federal involvement in higher education. Somalia needs the national standards, coordination and monitoring that Article 68 assigns to the Federal Government. It is a case against mistaking that concurrent role for exclusive control, and against any ministry, federal or state, substituting personal or factional discretion for the procedures the constitution and the existing statutes already provide. The Wider Lesson Somalia’s higher education debate is not simply about which institution holds regulatory authority. It is about whether the federal system can distinguish national leadership from centralised administration, and whether its institutions, federal and state alike, will be bound by the constitution they operate under rather than by convenience. The constitution, read together with the existing higher education laws, points to a system in which national standards and coordination coexist with meaningful Federal Member State implementation and institutional authority. Any departure from that allocation, in either direction, is a constitutional problem to be corrected, not a political victory to be defended. Somalia does not need a higher education system organised around which institution holds the pen. It needs one that is coherent, credible and cooperative: national where the constitution assigns a national standard, shared where the constitution assigns a concurrent responsibility, and implemented locally where the constitution assigns that role to the Federal Member States. That is the more sustainable way to reconcile national standards with federalism. items.title: Suudaan, Eritrea, Masar iyo Somaliya oo kala saxiixday heshiis wadajir ah
items.description: Hoggaamiyeyaasha Somaliya, Masar, Suudaan iyo Eritrea ayaa Axaddan Magaalada Alamein ku kala saxiixday heshiis afar geesood ah oo loogu magac-daray “Bayaanka wadajirka ah ee Alamein”. Heshiiskan ayaa waxa uu udub-dhexaad u yahay iskaashi cusub oo dhanka amniga, difaaca iyo siyaasadda oo dalalkan ay yeelanayaan, kaas oo si toos ah u taabanaya is bedelada iyo xiisadaha ka taagan Geeska Afrika iyo Badda Cas. Bayaanka oo la tarjumay, laguna daabacay bogga wararka ee Villa Somalia ayaa u qornaa:- 1.
