items.title: Misan Harriman: I won’t rest until there are no zero-dose children in Nigeria Written By :
items.description: Misan Harriman: I won’t rest until there are no zero-dose children in Nigeria Written By : Ijeoma Thomas-Odia Misan Harriman is a Nigerian-born photographer, filmmaker, entrepreneur and social activist who built a career around using his camera to document humanity, protest and social change. A self-taught photographer, he became the first Black photographer to shoot the cover of British Vogue’s September issue and has documented major social and cultural moments around the world. He is also Chair of the Southbank Centre in London and an ambassador for Save the Children. His work has taken him to communities affected by conflict, hunger and displacement, including Somalia, Somaliland and Egypt, where he has used photography and advocacy to amplify the voices and experiences of children. Currently in Nigeria supporting Save the Children’s efforts to reach children who have received no routine vaccinations, in this interview held at Federal Palace Resort, he discusses why immunisation became a cause he could not ignore, the barriers Nigerian families face, and why he believes Nigerians can mobilise their collective resources to protect vulnerable children. You have been involved in social activism for several years. What drew you to Save the Children’s work in Nigeria? For me, as a Nigerian with a platform, it is important to use it for good not just outside Nigeria but in Nigeria. Over the last few years, I have had numerous projects with Save the Children in Nigeria. My team has just returned from Borno State, and my focus is on the work we are doing to make sure there are no zero-dose children in Nigeria. By zero-dose, I mean children who have received no vaccinations. That means their early life can potentially become a death sentence from diseases such as diphtheria, pneumonia and measles. All of these can be fatal, and there is no reason why they should be. So, I am trying to make sure these children can go to the nearest primary healthcare facility and receive free vaccines. Any mother or father with a child within the appropriate age range should be able to give that child the same chance my children have the chance to live a healthy life and grow well. That is the very least I can do as someone with a platform and as someone who was born in Nigeria. How can I not help the vulnerable? Why did immunisation become such an important cause for you? There are many things wrong with all countries, but when you know the medicine exists and that children will die without it, how can you sit there knowing that children can live and that the medicine exists? That is why I chose it. The solution to the problem already exists. It is about distribution and resources. When you see that and ignore it, you have to live with that. I couldn’t live with myself knowing that I had the ability to do something about it. From your recent interactions with families, what do you see as some of the biggest barriers to accessing healthcare? There are a lot of cultural and economic issues. Some of the mothers I spoke to in Ikorodu, where I spent time recently, explained that sometimes their husbands do not want to spend money on transportation because the cost of living is so high. That money could become another meal for the whole family. People sometimes prioritise what seems immediately urgent without necessarily understanding that their child could become very sick without vaccination. Education is also important. We need to help mothers know where their nearest primary healthcare facility is. In some places, it is quite far, and even if you have transport, getting there can be difficult. One of the women who came had triplets. She came with her grandmother, and they walked. When you see that level of effort, you realise that these mothers want to protect their children. It is a natural instinct, so how can we not also help facilitate that and make it easier for them? What can Nigerians do to support the work? Save the Children Nigeria has channels through which people can donate directly to the projects we are doing. I would encourage people to support the work. You can go through Save the Children’s platforms and donate directly to the Nigerian projects. Every contribution helps because it goes towards supporting these children. You have described this as an ongoing project. What have you seen on the ground? This is ongoing. I happen to be here now, but this is not a one-off project. I came to oversee the work and make sure everything had been implemented, and I was really blown away. About 90 per cent of the people I met were home-grown Nigerians. They know the area and understand the cultural nuances. It is amazing to see how effective the work can be when people understand the context. We are not asking for somebody to come and save us. We are doing our own work, saving our own children, and it is really important to understand the context of this work. What are the biggest limitations? Resources. There are 2.1 million zero-dose children, so that is a huge challenge. The more resources we have, the more children we can reach and save. It is as simple as that. Vaccine hesitancy remains an issue in some communities. How do you approach those concerns? We speak to people respectfully and provide information. We show them historically how medicine has changed lives. Before penicillin was invented, people were scared of it. Imagine a world without penicillin. Medicine works. It is as simple as that, especially when children are far more vulnerable. As an adult, if you want to make decisions about your own healthcare, that is your choice. But when a child gets measles, can you ignore medicine? You have to ask yourself: are you going to sit and pray and hope your child gets better, or are you going to give that child the medicine that could save his or her life? To me, that is an easy choice. What has been the most rewarding part of this work for you? I am just really proud of everyone I have seen working in humanitarian and primary healthcare services in Nigeria. They are dedicated men and women. They care about children. We are dealing with children and, usually, mothers as well, and there are a lot of people dedicating their lives to this. Let’s support them and recruit more people like them in every state in Nigeria. Let’s expand the work. I won’t rest until there are no zero-dose children in this country. Do you see the government as an important partner in achieving that goal? If the government wants to participate, that is fine. Save the Children is a global humanitarian organisation, and I am its global ambassador. I look at many projects around the world. I was recently in Somaliland and in Cairo, helping Palestinian children in Egypt. There are many projects I get involved in, but as a Nigerian, I take particular pride in the work we do in Nigeria. So, if the government wants to participate, I am sure we can work with them. But I am focused on fundraising from Nigerians, both in the country and in the diaspora. We can do this ourselves. Having worked with children in different parts of the world, what has that experience taught you about Nigerians and our responsibility to one another? I think Nigerians are very aware of how we can make a difference. Before we were colonised, all the tribes and villages knew how to look after their sick and protect their children. It is actually in our bones. Something happened after colonisation, where we became more individualistic capitalism, protecting my own family and that is all I care about. But something is beginning to change. We are going back to a better way of living. Think of all the money we spend on Detty December and what that means in Lagos. Imagine if some of that was spent on children who have a chance of living or dying. Tell me what you would rather be doing. I think people are beginning to grow in what they see as their value system. At the end of the day, we all die. From the people I have met in their final days, they never talk about how much they have. They talk about who they helped and what they did in this life. So, let’s continue to move in that direction. Your photography is another powerful part of your activism. What role does it play in telling these stories? I photograph these stories, and I will be releasing some of the images soon. I have released work before, usually with magazines, newspapers or Save the Children. For me, photography is about truth. There is no small talk in black and white. If you look at history books and some of the most important photographs of all time, many of them are black and white for a reason. I love it. I was inspired by photographers I saw when I was a child, images of Martin Luther King Jr., Malcolm X and so many others. Those are the shoulders I stand on. Gordon Parks and his civil rights photography. Peter Magubane’s photography during the apartheid movement in South Africa. Much of that work was in black and white. I guess my eyes see things in monochrome. Your decision to remain committed to black-and-white photography has become part of your visual identity. What keeps you committed to it? My work is not about being accepted, it is about truth. If you’re a real artist, you don’t care about acceptance. You care about truth. That is why I do what I do. I have no interest in who accepts me. I have every interest in making people see the truth of the human condition through my lens. That is possibly why so many people around the world have responded to my work. Whether it is the #EndSARS protests I photographed, work in Johannesburg and Minnesota with George Floyd’s family, Black children, children with Down syndrome or my sister, people respond to the images. Sometimes people cry when they see my photographs. As a photographer, you have to search for truth. That is why I don’t use Photoshop. I don’t retouch. I don’t use lighting or flash. I have my camera. That’s it. I’m not a wedding photographer. I document the human condition. I have my camera, my eye and my heart. That’s all I need. What do you hope people see when they look at your photographs? I think humans are still humans. We can be good and bad. We can be kind, and people are simply trying to figure out life. The mothers I met just a few days ago are just the same as you and me. They are trying to figure out life. If my images can humanise them and remind everyone that we are all the same that no one is better than anyone else then that is important to me. Guardian Nigeria

You can go through Save the Children’s platforms and donate directly to the Nigerian projects. Every contribution helps because it goes towards supporting these children. You have described this as an ongoing project. What have you seen on the ground? This is ongoing. I happen to be here now, but this is not a one-off project. I came to oversee the work and make sure everything had been implemented, and I was really blown away. About 90 per cent of the people I met were home-grown Nigerians. They know the area and understand the cultural nuances. It is amazing to see how effective the work can be when people understand the context. We are not asking for somebody to come and save us. We are doing our own work, saving our own children, and it is really important to understand the context of this work. What are the biggest limitations? Resources. There are 2.1 million zero-dose children, so that is a huge challenge. The more resources we have, the more children we can reach and save. It is as simple as that. Vaccine hesitancy remains an issue in some communities. How do you approach those concerns? We speak to people respectfully and provide information. We show them historically how medicine has changed lives. Before penicillin was invented, people were scared of it. Imagine a world without penicillin. Medicine works. It is as simple as that, especially when children are far more vulnerable. As an adult, if you want to make decisions about your own healthcare, that is your choice. But when a child gets measles, can you ignore medicine? You have to ask yourself: are you going to sit and pray and hope your child gets better, or are you going to give that child the medicine that could save his or her life? To me, that is an easy choice. What has been the most rewarding part of this work for you? I am just really proud of everyone I have seen working in humanitarian and primary healthcare services in Nigeria. They are dedicated men and women. They care about children. We are dealing with children and, usually, mothers as well, and there are a lot of people dedicating their lives to this. Let’s support them and recruit more people like them in every state in Nigeria. Let’s expand the work. I won’t rest until there are no zero-dose children in this country. Do you see the government as an important partner in achieving that goal? If the government wants to participate, that is fine. Save the Children is a global humanitarian organisation, and I am its global ambassador. I look at many projects around the world. I was recently in Somaliland and in Cairo, helping Palestinian children in Egypt. There are many projects I get involved in, but as a Nigerian, I take particular pride in the work we do in Nigeria. So, if the government wants to participate, I am sure we can work with them. But I am focused on fundraising from Nigerians, both in the country and in the diaspora. We can do this ourselves. Having worked with children in different parts of the world, what has that experience taught you about Nigerians and our responsibility to one another? I think Nigerians are very aware of how we can make a difference. Before we were colonised, all the tribes and villages knew how to look after their sick and protect their children. It is actually in our bones. Something happened after colonisation, where we became more individualistic capitalism, protecting my own family and that is all I care about. But something is beginning to change. We are going back to a better way of living. Think of all the money we spend on Detty December and what that means in Lagos. Imagine if some of that was spent on children who have a chance of living or dying. Tell me what you would rather be doing. I think people are beginning to grow in what they see as their value system. At the end of the day, we all die. From the people I have met in their final days, they never talk about how much they have. They talk about who they helped and what they did in this life. So, let’s continue to move in that direction. Your photography is another powerful part of your activism. What role does it play in telling these stories? I photograph these stories, and I will be releasing some of the images soon. I have released work before, usually with magazines, newspapers or Save the Children. For me, photography is about truth. There is no small talk in black and white. If you look at history books and some of the most important photographs of all time, many of them are black and white for a reason. I love it. I was inspired by photographers I saw when I was a child, images of Martin Luther King Jr., Malcolm X and so many others. Those are the shoulders I stand on. Gordon Parks and his civil rights photography. Peter Magubane’s photography during the apartheid movement in South Africa. Much of that work was in black and white. I guess my eyes see things in monochrome. Your decision to remain committed to black-and-white photography has become part of your visual identity. What keeps you committed to it? My work is not about being accepted, it is about truth. If you’re a real artist, you don’t care about acceptance. You care about truth. That is why I do what I do. I have no interest in who accepts me. I have every interest in making people see the truth of the human condition through my lens. That is possibly why so many people around the world have responded to my work. Whether it is the #EndSARS protests I photographed, work in Johannesburg and Minnesota with George Floyd’s family, Black children, children with Down syndrome or my sister, people respond to the images. Sometimes people cry when they see my photographs. As a photographer, you have to search for truth. That is why I don’t use Photoshop. I don’t retouch. I don’t use lighting or flash. I have my camera. That’s it. I’m not a wedding photographer. I document the human condition. I have my camera, my eye and my heart. That’s all I need. What do you hope people see when they look at your photographs? I think humans are still humans. We can be good and bad. We can be kind, and people are simply trying to figure out life. The mothers I met just a few days ago are just the same as you and me. They are trying to figure out life. If my images can humanise them and remind everyone that we are all the same that no one is better than anyone else then that is important to me. Guardian Nigeria

items.title: Turkiga iyo Pakistan oo ku dhow in ay ku biiraan dagaalka…
items.description: Riyadh (Caasimada Online) – Turkiga iyo Pakistan ayaa taliyeyaashooda ugu sarreeya ciidamada u diraya Sacuudi Carabiya, kadib markii Riyadh ay codsatay kulan degdeg ah oo looga arrinsanayo hirgelinta heshiis difaac wadajir ah, xilli weerarrada gantaallada iyo diyaaradaha aan duuliyaha lahayn ee Xuutiyiinta Yemen ay sii kordhayaan. Wasaaradda Difaaca Turkiga ayaa Jimcihii xaqiijisay in taliyaha guud ee ciidamada, General Selcuk Bayraktaroglu, uu u safrayo Sacuudi Carabiya si uu uga qeyb galo kulanka taliyeyaasha ciidamada ee dalalka ku mideysan heshiiska difaaca. Taliyaha ciidamada Pakistan, Field Marshal Asim Munir, ayaa sidoo kale la filayaa inuu gaaro Riyadh, sida ay Al Jazeera sheegtay, inkastoo milatariga Pakistan uusan si rasmi ah u xaqiijin safarkiisa. Kulanka ayaa imanaya kadib toddobaadyo ay Xuutiyiintu kordhiyeen weerarrada ay ku qaadayaan gudaha Sacuudi Carabiya, taas oo Riyadh ku riixday inay taageero ka raadiso xulafadeeda cusub ee heshiiska difaaca. Khamiistii, Xuutiyiintu waxay sheegeen inay gantaallo iyo diyaarado drone ah ku weerareen bartilmaameedyo Sacuudi ah, oo ay ku jiraan xarumo ay leedahay shirkadda shidaalka ee Saudi Aramco ee Yanbu iyo goob ay ku tilmaameen “bartilmaameed xasaasi ah” oo ku yaalla Riyadh. Sacuudi Carabiya ayaa dhankeeda sheegtay inay soo ridday lix gantaal oo ballistic ah oo ku wajahnaa Taif iyo Yanbu. Digniino degdeg ah ayaa sidoo kale laga bixiyey dhowr magaalo, iyadoo colaadda Yemen ay si isa soo taraysa uga gudbeyso xadka. Heshiiska difaaca ee Maka Sacuudi Carabiya, Turkiga iyo Pakistan ayaa 7-dii August ku kala saxiixday magaalada Maka heshiiska Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, kaas oo dhigaya in weerar hubeysan oo lagu qaado mid ka mid ah saddexda dal loo aqoonsanayo weerar lagu qaaday dhammaantood. Heshiiska ayaa sidoo kale dhigaya in saddexda dal ay ballaariyaan iskaashiga difaaca iyo awooddooda wadajirka ah ee ka hortagga khataraha. Dhammaadkii August, wasiirrada arrimaha dibadda iyo difaaca iyo taliyeyaasha ciidamada saddexda dal ayaa Istanbul ku yeeshay kulankii ugu horreeyey ee guddiga siyaasadda iyo difaaca ee heshiiska. Waxay isku raaceen in Riyadh laga dhiso xoghayn joogto ah oo maamusha howlaha heshiiska, iyadoo xoghayaha guud ee ugu horreeya uu ka imaanayo Pakistan muddo saddex sano ah. Xiisadda cusub ee Yemen ayaa hadda noqoneysa tijaabadii ugu horreysay ee weyn ee muujin karta sida heshiiskaasi uga shaqeynayo xaalad dagaal oo dhab ah. Wasiirrada arrimaha dibadda Sacuudi Carabiya, Turkiga iyo Pakistan ayaa Khamiistii ku kulmay New York, iyagoo halkaas kaga arrinsaday qabanqaabada kulanka degdegga ah ee taliyeyaasha ciidamada. Sacuudi Carabiya waxay sheegtay in wadahadalladu ay ku saabsan yihiin sidii taageero loogu fidin lahaa boqortooyada iyadoo la adeegsanayo heshiiska difaaca. Saddexda dal ayaa sidoo kale cambaareeyey weerarrada lagu bartilmaameedsaday Maka iyo xarumaha rayidka iyo dhaqaalaha ee Sacuudiga, iyagoo xaqiijiyey xaqa Riyadh ay u leedahay inay is-difaacdo. Laakiin Ankara iyo Islamabad waxay muujiyeen hadal ka taxaddar badan kan Sacuudi Carabiya. Pakistan waxay sheegtay in kulanka looga hadlay horumarka laga sameeyey dhismaha hay’adaha heshiiska iyo xaaladda amni ee gobolka, halka ilo diblomaasiyadeed oo Turki ah ay sheegeen in wasiirradu dib u eegeen wada-xaajoodyada farsamo ee lagu hirgelinayo heshiiska. Kala duwanaanshahaas ayaa muujinaya in inkastoo saddexda dal ay leeyihiin waajibaad difaac oo wadajir ah, haddana aan weli la caddeyn nooca taageerada milateri ee Turkiga iyo Pakistan ay diyaar u yihiin inay siiyaan Sacuudi Carabiya. Xuutiyiinta oo digniin diray Xuutiyiinta oo taageero ka hela Iran ayaa dhankooda uga digay Ankara iyo Islamabad inay si toos ah ugu lug yeeshaan dagaalka Yemen. Mohammed al-Bukhaiti, oo ka tirsan hoggaanka siyaasadeed ee Xuutiyiinta, ayaa sheegay in Turkiga iyo Pakistan ay wajihi doonaan jawaab adag haddii ay dagaalka ku soo biiraan, sida ay Al Jazeera werisay. Kooxdu waxay toddobaadyadii ugu dambeeyey sidoo kale horumar ka sameysay gudaha Yemen, iyadoo qabsatay dekedda istaraatiijiga ah ee Mocha iyo goobo kale oo ku teedsan Badda Cas. Taasi waxay sare u qaaday walaaca laga qabo marinka Bab al-Mandab, oo ah marin muhiim u ah ganacsiga iyo dhoofinta tamarta caalamka. Dagaallada ayaa sidoo kale sababay barakac cusub. Hay’adda Qaxootiga Qaramada Midoobay ayaa sheegtay in in ka badan 230,000 qof ay guryahooda ka barakaceen tan iyo bilowgii September, iyadoo dagaalladu ku fidayaan dhowr jiho oo Yemen ah. Sacuudi Carabiya ayaa dhanka kale sii xoojinaysa difaaceeda. Faransiiska ayaa sheegay inuu ciidamo, raadaarro iyo nidaamyo difaac u dirayo Yanbu si loo ilaaliyo xarumaha muhiimka ah ee shidaalka, halka Britain ay taageero ka bixineyso howlgallada difaaca Sacuudiga. Kulanka taliyeyaasha ciidamada ee Riyadh ayaa sidaas darteed indhaha lagu hayaa, maadaama go’aannada kasoo baxa ay tilmaami karaan in heshiiska cusub ee difaaca uu ku ekaanayo taageero siyaasadeed iyo farsamo, ama inuu horseedi karo kaalin milateri oo toos ah oo Turkiga iyo Pakistan ay ka qaataan difaaca Sacuudi Carabiya. items.title: Soomaaliya oo wajahaysa cadaadis dhaqaale oo ka dhashay qalalaasaha Marinka Hormuz
items.description: Soomaaliya ayaa wajahaysa cadaadis dhaqaale oo sii kordhaya, kaddib markii khalkhalka ka jira Marinka Hormuz uu saameyn ku yeeshay isu-socodka ganacsiga iyo badeecadaha dalka, iyadoo Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud uu sheegay in xaaladdu ay qayb ka noqotay hoos u dhac lagu qiyaasay 40 boqolkiiba dakhliga kastamka Soomaaliya . Madaxweynaha ayaa arrintan ka sheegay khudbad uu ka jeediyay Kalfadhiga 81-aad ee Golaha Guud ee Qaramada Midoobay, isagoo tilmaamay in Soomaaliya ay si weyn ugu tiirsan tahay badeecooyin laga keeno Bariga Dhexe, gaar ahaan cunto iyo shidaal. Sida uu sheegay, qalalaasaha ka jira marinka muhiimka u ah ganacsiga caalamiga ah ayaa sare u qaaday qiimaha badeecadaha, sicir-bararka iyo kharashaadka gaadiidka iyo caymiska. Madaxweynaha ayaa sheegay in hoos u dhaca dakhliga kastamku uu saameyn ku yeelan karo il muhiim ah oo dowladda uga soo xaroota maalgelinta dib-u-habaynta dhaqaalaha, kobaca iyo dadaallada lagu dhimayo saboolnimada. xogta la heli karo waxay tilmaamaysaa in madaxweynuhu uusan caddeyn muddada uu hoos u dhaca 40-ka boqolkiiba dhacay ama soo bandhigin xogta faahfaahsan ee lagu saleeyay qiyaastaas. Saameyntan dhaqaale ayaa kusoo beegmaysa xilli Soomaaliya ay horey ugu tiirsanayd badeecooyin dibadda laga keeno, waxaana Wasaaradda Ganacsiga Soomaaliya ay dhawaan sheegtay in dalka uu sanadkii soo dejiyo badeecooyin ku dhow 9 bilyan oo doollar , taasoo muujinaysa heerka uu dhaqaalaha Soomaaliya ugu tiirsan yahay ganacsiga dibadda. Dhibaatada ayaa sidoo kale gaareysa ganacsatada iyo dekedaha Soomaaliya, ayadoo Ganacsatada Soomaaliyeed ay bilaabeen inay raadiyaan waddooyin kale oo ay badeecooyinka ku soo mariyaan, kaddib markii khalkhalka ka jira marinnada muhiimka ah ee gobolka uu kordhiyay kharashaadka iyo walaaca laga qabo dib-u-dhacyada shixnadaha. Maamulka Dekedda Muqdisho ayaa sheegay in ganacsatada lagala shaqeynayo sidii loo heli lahaa waddooyin kale oo sahaydu dalka ku soo gaarto. Marinka Hormuz ayaa ah marin muhiim u ah gaadiidka tamarta iyo ganacsiga caalamiga ah, waxaana warbixinno laga helay xaaladda maraakiibta ay muujinayaan hoos u dhac weyn oo ku yimid maraakiibta badeecadaha ee halkaas mara. Reuters ayaa 22-kii Sebtembar soo werisay in laba markab oo badeecooyin ah oo keliya ay maalintaas ka gudbeen marinka, halka celceliska ka hor colaadda lagu qiyaasay 125 markab oo waaweyn maalintii. Dhinaca kale, Soomaaliya waxay wajahaysaa xaalad bani’aadantinimo oo adag, iyadoo Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh uu sheegay in in ka badan lix milyan oo qof ay saameysay abaarta la xiriirta isbeddelka cimilada. Kororka qiimaha cuntada iyo shidaalka ayaa sidaas darteed kusoo beegmaya xilli qaybo badan oo bulshada Soomaaliyeed ah ay durba la tacaalayaan saameynta abaarta iyo baahiyaha bani’aadantinimo. Si kastaba ha ahaatee dowladda Soomaaliya waxay hadda wajahaysaa laba cadaadis oo isku mar socda: hoos u dhaca dakhliga gudaha iyo kororka kharashaadka soo dejinta , iyadoo dhinaca kale malaayiin qof ay u baahan yihiin gargaar iyo taageero ay kaga gudbaan saameynta abaarta.

Madaxweynaha ayaa sheegay in hoos u dhaca dakhliga kastamku uu saameyn ku yeelan karo il muhiim ah oo dowladda uga soo xaroota maalgelinta dib-u-habaynta dhaqaalaha, kobaca iyo dadaallada lagu dhimayo saboolnimada. xogta la heli karo waxay tilmaamaysaa in madaxweynuhu uusan caddeyn muddada uu hoos u dhaca 40-ka boqolkiiba dhacay ama soo bandhigin xogta faahfaahsan ee lagu saleeyay qiyaastaas. Saameyntan dhaqaale ayaa kusoo beegmaysa xilli Soomaaliya ay horey ugu tiirsanayd badeecooyin dibadda laga keeno, waxaana Wasaaradda Ganacsiga Soomaaliya ay dhawaan sheegtay in dalka uu sanadkii soo dejiyo badeecooyin ku dhow 9 bilyan oo doollar , taasoo muujinaysa heerka uu dhaqaalaha Soomaaliya ugu tiirsan yahay ganacsiga dibadda. Dhibaatada ayaa sidoo kale gaareysa ganacsatada iyo dekedaha Soomaaliya, ayadoo Ganacsatada Soomaaliyeed ay bilaabeen inay raadiyaan waddooyin kale oo ay badeecooyinka ku soo mariyaan, kaddib markii khalkhalka ka jira marinnada muhiimka ah ee gobolka uu kordhiyay kharashaadka iyo walaaca laga qabo dib-u-dhacyada shixnadaha. Maamulka Dekedda Muqdisho ayaa sheegay in ganacsatada lagala shaqeynayo sidii loo heli lahaa waddooyin kale oo sahaydu dalka ku soo gaarto. Marinka Hormuz ayaa ah marin muhiim u ah gaadiidka tamarta iyo ganacsiga caalamiga ah, waxaana warbixinno laga helay xaaladda maraakiibta ay muujinayaan hoos u dhac weyn oo ku yimid maraakiibta badeecadaha ee halkaas mara. Reuters ayaa 22-kii Sebtembar soo werisay in laba markab oo badeecooyin ah oo keliya ay maalintaas ka gudbeen marinka, halka celceliska ka hor colaadda lagu qiyaasay 125 markab oo waaweyn maalintii. Dhinaca kale, Soomaaliya waxay wajahaysaa xaalad bani’aadantinimo oo adag, iyadoo Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh uu sheegay in in ka badan lix milyan oo qof ay saameysay abaarta la xiriirta isbeddelka cimilada. Kororka qiimaha cuntada iyo shidaalka ayaa sidaas darteed kusoo beegmaya xilli qaybo badan oo bulshada Soomaaliyeed ah ay durba la tacaalayaan saameynta abaarta iyo baahiyaha bani’aadantinimo. Si kastaba ha ahaatee dowladda Soomaaliya waxay hadda wajahaysaa laba cadaadis oo isku mar socda: hoos u dhaca dakhliga gudaha iyo kororka kharashaadka soo dejinta , iyadoo dhinaca kale malaayiin qof ay u baahan yihiin gargaar iyo taageero ay kaga gudbaan saameynta abaarta.

items.title: Afrika oo dalbanaysa kuraas joogto ah Golaha Ammaanka ah, balse dib-u-habayntu weli caqabad ku tahay
items.description: Dalalka Afrika ayaa mar kale xoogga saaray baahida loo qabo in dib-u-habayn lagu sameeyo Golaha Ammaanka ee Qaramada Midoobay, iyagoo dalbanaya in qaaradda la siiyo ugu yaraan laba kursi oo joogto ah iyo shan kursi oo aan joogto ahayn. Baaqan ayaa kusoo beegmaya xilli uu socdo Kalfadhiga 81-aad ee Golaha Guud ee Qaramada Midoobay, iyadoo dalalka Afrika ay ku doodayaan in qaab-dhismeedka Golaha Ammaanka uusan si ku filan uga tarjumaynin xaqiiqada siyaasadeed iyo juqraafiyeed ee dunida maanta. Xoghayaha Guud ee Qaramada Midoobay António Guterres ayaa isna mar kale ku baaqay in Golaha Ammaanka dib loo habeeyo si uu u noqdo mid matalaad ahaan ka tarjumaya xaaladda maanta jirta. Golaha Ammaanka wuxuu ka kooban yahay 15 xubnood, kuwaas oo shan ka mid ahi yihiin xubno joogto ah oo kala ah Maraykanka, Ruushka, Shiinaha, Faransiiska iyo Boqortooyada Midowday. Shantan dal waxay leeyihiin awoodda veto-ga, taas oo u oggolaanaysa mid kasta inuu hor istaago qaraar muhiim ah oo Golaha Ammaanku doonayo inuu ansixiyo. Afrika ayaa muddo dheer ka cabanaysay in iyadoo qaaraddu si weyn uga dhex muuqato ajandayaasha Golaha Ammaanka, haddana aysan lahayn wax kursi joogto ah. Sanadkii 2025, Golaha Ammaanku wuxuu ansixiyay 44 qaraar, waxaana 24 ka mid ah lagu saleeyay Cutubka VII ee Axdiga Qaramada Midoobay, kaas oo la xiriira cunaqabateyn iyo tallaabooyin lagu qaado xaaladaha khatarta ku ah nabadda iyo amniga caalamka. 18 ka mid ah 24-kaas qaraar waxay khuseeyeen Afrika, taasoo muujinaysa sida weyn ee qaaraddu uga dhex muuqato shaqada Golaha Ammaanka. Madaxweyne Bola Tinubu oo hadalkiisa Golaha Guud uu jeediyay Madaxweyne-ku-xigeenka Nigeria Kashim Shettima ayaa sheegay in Afrika ay u baahan tahay ugu yaraan laba kursi oo joogto ah oo leh dhammaan xuquuqda iyo waajibaadka xubinnimada joogtada ah, oo ay ku jirto awoodda veto-ga inta awooddaasi weli jirto. Nigeria waxay sidoo kale dalbatay shan kursi oo aan joogto ahayn oo Afrika loogu kordhiyo Golaha Ammaanka. Madaxweynaha Ghana John Mahama ayaa isna taageeray baaqa Afrika, isagoo sheegay in dib-u-habaynta Golaha Ammaanku aysan ahayn arrin Afrika loogu samafalayo, balse ay muhiim u tahay sharciyadda, kalsoonida iyo sii jiritaanka Qaramada Midoobay. Dib-u-habaynta Golaha Ammaanka ayaa muddo dheer socotay, balse heshiis laga gaaro qodobada ugu muhiimsan ayaa weli adkaaday, ayadoo golaha Guud uu sanadkii 2008 bilaabay wada-hadallada u dhexeeya dowladaha xubnaha ka ah Qaramada Midoobay, kuwaas oo diiradda saaraya tirada xubnaha Golaha, qaybinta kuraasta joogtada ah iyo kuwa aan joogtada ahayn, matalaadda gobollada iyo mustaqbalka awoodda veto-ga. Si kastaba ha ahaatee, wada-hadalladaasi weli ma aysan dhalin heshiis wax ka beddela qaab-dhismeedka Golaha. Caqabadda ugu  weyn ayaa ah in wax ka beddelka xubinnimada joogtada ah uu u baahan yahay in wax laga beddelo Axdiga Qaramada Midoobay, Sida ku cad Qodobka 108, wax-ka-beddelka wuxuu u baahan yahay ansixinta laba-meelood saddex meel Golaha Guud. Haddaba shanta dal ee hadda haysta kuraasta joogtada ah waxay door rasmi ah ku leeyihiin go’aan kasta oo lagu beddelayo nidaamka Golaha. Nigeria ayaa si gaar ah u doonaysa in ay ka mid noqoto dalalka Afrika ee heli kara kursi joogto ah haddii dib-u-habayntu hirgasho, ayadoo Masar iyo Koonfur Afrika ay sidoo kale hore u muujiyeen danayn ku saabsan matalaad joogto ah. Midowga Afrika weli ma magacaabin dalal gaar ah oo qaadanaya kuraasta la doonayo, waxaana Mowqifka guud ee Midowga Afrika uu yahay in qaaraddu hesho ugu yaraan laba kursi oo joogto ah iyo shan kursi oo aan joogto ahayn, iyadoo Midowga Afrika uu go’aaminayo dalalka matalaya qaaradda. Arrinta ugu adag ayaa sidoo kale ah awoodda veto-ga, ayadoo mowqifka loo yaqaan Ezulwini Consensus ee Midowga Afrika uu dhigayo in haddii Afrika hesho kuraas joogto ah, xubnaha Afrika ay yeeshaan xuquuq iyo awood la mid ah kuwa xubnaha joogtada ah ee hadda jira, oo ay ku jirto veto-ga inta nidaamka veto-gu sii jiro. Dalalka Afrika waxay ku doodaan in haddii kuraas joogto ah la siiyo balse aan la siin awood la mid ah tan shanta xubnood ee hadda jira, aysan si buuxda u saxaynaynin farqiga ay ka cabanayaan. Professor Ibrahim Gambari, oo horey u ahaa wasiirka arrimaha dibadda Nigeria iyo wakiilkii joogtada ahaa ee Nigeria u fadhiyay Qaramada Midoobay, ayaa sheegay in xaaladda hadda jirta ay adkeynayso in Afrika ay si buuxda uga qaybqaadato go’aamada caalamiga ah ee saameeya qaaradda. Wuxuu sidoo kale tilmaamay in hawlgallada nabad-ilaalinta ee Qaramada Midoobay ee Afrika ay ku shaqeeyaan mandaatyo uu Golaha Ammaanku ansixiyo, taasoo sii xoojinaysa doodda ah in Afrika ay u baahan tahay cod joogto ah oo awood leh. Doodda ayaa sidoo kale taageero ka heshay qaar kamid ah dhalinyarada Afrika, ayadoo Favour Aniezi, oo ah Nigerian u dooda arrimaha dhalinyarada, ay sheegtay in arrintu aysan ku koobnayn in Afrika lagu casuumo miiska wada-hadalka, balse ay muhiim tahay in qaaraddu yeelato awood ay ku saameyso go’aamada laga gaarayo arrimaha sida tooska ah u saameeya. Inkasta oo dalalka Afrika ay si joogto ah ugu baaqayaan dib-u-habayn, haddana su’aalaha ugu muhiimsan ayaa weli jawaab la’aan ah, waxaana weli la isku hayaa tirada kuraasta cusub, dalalka Afrika ee qaadan doona kuraastaas, awoodda veto-ga iyo in shanta xubnood ee hadda joogtada ah ay oggolaan doonaan isbeddelka.

items.title: Hassan Sheikh draws line on UN role in Somalia elections
items.description: New York, USA — Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud urged the United Nations and international partners to support the country’s move towards direct elections, while insisting Somalia retain ownership of the process amid a deepening political dispute. Addressing the UN General Assembly on Thursday, Mohamud said constitutional reforms were laying the foundations for universal suffrage, accountable institutions and a multiparty political system. “We invite the United Nations and our international partners to support this transition by helping to strengthen democratic institutions, but always respecting our ownership of Somali democracy,” he said. His remarks came as the Somali Future Council has urged the UN Security Council to mediate the country’s election dispute and provide international oversight of the electoral process. In a September 11 letter to the council, the opposition alliance called for international backing for an agreed electoral model. It proposed a mediation and guarantee mechanism involving Security Council members and countries contributing troops to the African Union mission in Somalia. The two positions reflect differing views over the extent of international involvement in resolving Somalia’s political deadlock. Mohamud welcomed international support for democratic institutions but framed the transition as a Somali-led process. “Our aim is to become an effective democracy where differences are resolved through dialogue, law and elections, not violence,” he told the General Assembly. Mohamud said his government had engaged Somali political leaders, federal member states, civil society, women’s groups, young people and the diaspora in the constitutional reform process. Opposition leaders dispute the government’s handling of the transition and say previous attempts to negotiate an election settlement have failed. Election deadlock Further talks between the federal government and opposition groups ended without agreement in July after the two sides failed to bridge differences over the voting system and management of the next national elections. Both sides support moving towards direct voting but remain sharply divided over how to conduct the elections. The federal government favours elections through registered political parties under a national electoral commission. The Future Council has proposed a transitional system that allows citizens to vote directly while retaining the 4.5-clan formula for allocating parliamentary seats. At the heart of the standoff are constitutional amendments that parliament approved in March , increasing presidential and parliamentary terms from four to five years. The Future Council has asked the Security Council to back an “inclusive and attainable election model” covering federal and regional institutions, as well as a mechanism to mediate and guarantee any political settlement. Mohamud told the General Assembly that Somalia was entering what he described as a new democratic chapter in which citizens determine political power under the constitution and rule of law. “This is a new progressive chapter where political power is determined by citizens, guided by constitutional law and safeguarded by the rule of law,” he said. This version is tighter and more naturally wire-style while keeping the central contrast and all the useful election context. items.title: Crisis Group warns Somali towns at risk as AU mission shrinks
items.description: Mogadishu, Somalia — Several Somali towns face heightened vulnerability to Al-Shabaab as African Union troops scale back and UN logistical support winds down, the International Crisis Group warned , saying some territorial losses may be difficult to avoid. The Brussels-based conflict-monitoring organisation singled out Qoryoley in Lower Shabelle and Jalalaqsi in Hirshabelle as locations that could come under intense pressure if foreign forces withdraw without adequate replacements. The warning comes as Somalia and its international partners prepare for a major overhaul of the security architecture that has sustained the campaign against Al-Shabaab for nearly two decades. The United States agreed this month to extend support for the UN Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) by an additional 12 months rather than ending it on December 31. The drawdown is now expected to begin in January 2027 , giving Somalia, the African Union and international partners more time to prepare for the transition. UNSOS provides food, water, fuel, transport and other logistical support that enable the African Union Support and Stabilisation Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM) to maintain 49 locations across southern and central Somalia. Crisis Group warned the AU mission would struggle to operate in anything resembling its current form without that logistical network. Vulnerable towns In Lower Shabelle, Uganda maintains more than a dozen bases that could become difficult to sustain once UN logistical support ends. Crisis Group said smaller towns surrounded by Al-Shabaab positions, including Qoryoley, “could be at risk of falling to the insurgents” if AU contingents withdraw. Parts of Hirshabelle face similar pressure because Al-Shabaab has concentrated more forces in the region since 2025, threatening towns along major transport routes, including Jalalaqsi. The report cautioned that even localised territorial losses could give Al-Shabaab renewed momentum, while control of roads and economic centres could provide additional revenue for the group. Crisis Group stopped short of predicting the collapse of Somalia’s federal government or the loss of major cities. It said Somali troops working alongside bilateral foreign partners could protect key population centres, infrastructure and supply routes, although some withdrawal from current AU-held positions appeared likely. Bilateral forces Somalia’s future security architecture is likely to rely increasingly on bilateral defence arrangements with regional partners, particularly Uganda, Kenya and Ethiopia, Crisis Group said. Mogadishu has established agreements with all three countries that could allow their troops to remain deployed even if the broader AU mission contracts or eventually ends. Kenya and Ethiopia are likely to consolidate forces closer to their borders, where they have longstanding security interests linked to Al-Shabaab, while Uganda could focus more heavily on Mogadishu and surrounding areas, according to the report. Smaller troop contributors such as Burundi and Djibouti may find it harder to maintain deployments without additional financial and logistical support. Türkiye is expected to remain central to Somalia’s security structure through training and military deployments, while the United States intends to maintain bilateral counter-terrorism operations. Crisis Group described such partnerships as the most realistic short-term alternative to the multilateral system, but urged the Somali government to establish a regular forum with foreign partners to coordinate responsibility for protecting towns, major roads and strategic infrastructure. Hold ground first The organisation urged Mogadishu to prioritise holding existing territory rather than launching major new offensives while the transition remains unsettled. Mogadishu said in August that about 14,000 Somali troops were available for military operations, and Crisis Group suggested some could deploy to positions expected to be vacated by AU forces. However, it cautioned that Somali units generally have less equipment and support than foreign contingents, making a direct one-for-one substitution a “hazardous proposition”. Several positions previously transferred from AU contingents to Somali forces later fell to Al-Shabaab, while national operations continue to rely heavily on foreign intelligence, air power, transport and logistics. The report also linked the security transition to Somalia’s political disputes , saying tensions between the federal government and the federal member states of Puntland and Jubaland have hindered efforts to build a unified national security structure. At the same time, the dispute over upcoming national elections risks further complicating preparations for the drawdown. items.fullContent: Mogadishu, Somalia — Several Somali towns face heightened vulnerability to Al-Shabaab as African Union troops scale back and UN logistical support winds down, the International Crisis Group warned , saying some territorial losses may be difficult to avoid. The Brussels-based conflict-monitoring organisation singled out Qoryoley in Lower Shabelle and Jalalaqsi in Hirshabelle as locations that could come under intense pressure if foreign forces withdraw without adequate replacements. The warning comes as Somalia and its international partners prepare for a major overhaul of the security architecture that has sustained the campaign against Al-Shabaab for nearly two decades. The United States agreed this month to extend support for the UN Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) by an additional 12 months rather than ending it on December 31. The drawdown is now expected to begin in January 2027 , giving Somalia, the African Union and international partners more time to prepare for the transition. UNSOS provides food, water, fuel, transport and other logistical support that enable the African Union Support and Stabilisation Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM) to maintain 49 locations across southern and central Somalia. Crisis Group warned the AU mission would struggle to operate in anything resembling its current form without that logistical network. Vulnerable towns In Lower Shabelle, Uganda maintains more than a dozen bases that could become difficult to sustain once UN logistical support ends. Crisis Group said smaller towns surrounded by Al-Shabaab positions, including Qoryoley, “could be at risk of falling to the insurgents” if AU contingents withdraw. Parts of Hirshabelle face similar pressure because Al-Shabaab has concentrated more forces in the region since 2025, threatening towns along major transport routes, including Jalalaqsi. The report cautioned that even localised territorial losses could give Al-Shabaab renewed momentum, while control of roads and economic centres could provide additional revenue for the group. Crisis Group stopped short of predicting the collapse of Somalia’s federal government or the loss of major cities. It said Somali troops working alongside bilateral foreign partners could protect key population centres, infrastructure and supply routes, although some withdrawal from current AU-held positions appeared likely. Bilateral forces Somalia’s future security architecture is likely to rely increasingly on bilateral defence arrangements with regional partners, particularly Uganda, Kenya and Ethiopia, Crisis Group said. Mogadishu has established agreements with all three countries that could allow their troops to remain deployed even if the broader AU mission contracts or eventually ends. Kenya and Ethiopia are likely to consolidate forces closer to their borders, where they have longstanding security interests linked to Al-Shabaab, while Uganda could focus more heavily on Mogadishu and surrounding areas, according to the report. Smaller troop contributors such as Burundi and Djibouti may find it harder to maintain deployments without additional financial and logistical support. Türkiye is expected to remain central to Somalia’s security structure through training and military deployments, while the United States intends to maintain bilateral counter-terrorism operations. Crisis Group described such partnerships as the most realistic short-term alternative to the multilateral system, but urged the Somali government to establish a regular forum with foreign partners to coordinate responsibility for protecting towns, major roads and strategic infrastructure. Hold ground first The organisation urged Mogadishu to prioritise holding existing territory rather than launching major new offensives while the transition remains unsettled. Mogadishu said in August that about 14,000 Somali troops were available for military operations, and Crisis Group suggested some could deploy to positions expected to be vacated by AU forces. However, it cautioned that Somali units generally have less equipment and support than foreign contingents, making a direct one-for-one substitution a “hazardous proposition”. Several positions previously transferred from AU contingents to Somali forces later fell to Al-Shabaab, while national operations continue to rely heavily on foreign intelligence, air power, transport and logistics. The report also linked the security transition to Somalia’s political disputes , saying tensions between the federal government and the federal member states of Puntland and Jubaland have hindered efforts to build a unified national security structure. At the same time, the dispute over upcoming national elections risks further complicating preparations for the drawdown. Crisis Group urged political leaders to resolve the electoral dispute and include federal member states in discussions over future security arrangements. It said the additional year of UN support allows Somalia and its partners to develop a replacement system that could begin operating as early as the second half of 2027. But the extension postpones rather than eliminates the challenge, Crisis Group warned, saying a poorly managed transition could leave security gaps for Al-Shabaab to exploit as the multilateral system contracts. items.title: Soomaaliya oo EALA kala hadashay ka-qaybgalka Isbahaysiga Siyaasadeed ee Bariga Afrika
items.description: Muqdisho, 25 Sebtembar 2026 – Dowladda Soomaaliya ayaa soo gabagabeysay wadatashiyo muddo saddex maalmood ah socday oo ay la yeelatay Golaha Sharci-dejinta Bulshada Bariga Afrika (EALA), kuwaas oo diiradda lagu saaray ka-qaybgalka Soomaaliya ee geeddi-socodka isdhexgalka siyaasadeed ee gobolka. Wadatashiyada oo ka dhacay magaalada Muqdisho ayaa lagu falanqeeyay horumarka laga sameeyay qorshaha Isbahaysiga Siyaasadeed ee Bariga Afrika (East African Political Confederation), iyo diyaar-garowga hay’adaha dowladda, shuruucda iyo dastuurka Soomaaliya ee ku aaddan ka-qaybgalka qorshahaasi. Kulanka waxaa ka qaybgalay xubno ka tirsan EALA, wakiillo ka socday Xoghaynta Bulshada Bariga Afrika (EAC), hay’adaha dowladda Soomaaliya, xildhibaanno, khubaro dhanka dastuurka iyo sharciga ah, bulshada rayidka ah, aqoonyahanno iyo ganacsato. Intii ay wadatashiyadu socdeen, waxaa si gaar ah looga hadlay hababka isku-duwidda hay’adaha qaranka, diyaar-garowga hay’adaha dowladda iyo arrimaha sharci iyo dastuuri ah ee la xiriira ka-qaybgalka Soomaaliya ee isbahaysiga siyaasadeed ee la qorsheynayo. Soomaaliya ayaa xubin buuxda ka noqotay Bulshada Bariga Afrika bishii Maarso 2024, kaddib markii ay dhigatay dukumentiga ansixinta xubinnimada. Tan iyo xilligaas, dalka ayaa ku guda jira hannaan uu hay’adihiisa ugu waafajinayo qaab-dhismeedka iyo waajibaadka ururka. Maalintii ugu dambeysay ee wadatashiyada, Agaasimaha Guud ee Arrimaha Bulshada Bariga Afrika ee Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda iyo Iskaashiga Caalamiga ah ayaa carrabka ku adkeeyay muhiimadda ay leedahay xoojinta wada-shaqeynta hay’adaha qaranka iyo waafajinta shuruucda iyo nidaamyada dalka ee waajibaadka sii kordhaya ee Soomaaliya ka saaran EAC. Isbahaysiga Siyaasadeed ee Bariga Afrika ayaa loo qorsheeyay inuu noqdo marxalad ku-meel-gaar ah oo loo maro dhismaha mustaqbalka ee federaal siyaasadeed oo ay ku mideysan yihiin dalalka xubnaha ka ah ururka. Dowladda Soomaaliya ayaa sheegtay in wadatashiyadan ay qayb ka yihiin dadaallada joogtada ah ee ay kula shaqeyneyso EALA iyo Xoghaynta EAC, si loo sii ambaqaado wadahadallada ku saabsan isdhexgalka siyaasadeed ee dalalka Bariga Afrika.

items.title: Puntland Is Not One Man — and Somalia’s Presidency Requires a National Mandate
items.description: By Abdiqani Haji Abdi President Said Abdullahi Deni is not only the president of Puntland. He is also among the political figures seeking a role in Somalia’s national leadership, making his recent position on Puntland’s relationship with Mogadishu particularly consequential. That creates a fundamental political contradiction. A politician seeking to lead Somalia nationally must explain how his national ambitions fit with a position that now openly raises the possibility of Puntland permanently severing its relationship with the Federal Government. In his September 13 letter to the United Nations, Deni’s administration said Puntland was facing pressure from what it described as “huge masses” of citizens favouring full independence and warned that Puntland might eventually consider permanently severing ties with Mogadishu. The letter did not provide polling, a referendum or another representative process establishing that such a position reflects the collective will of Puntland’s population. That does not automatically establish that Deni has adopted a formal policy of secession. The same political record is more complicated: as recently as June, Deni said Puntland had “never abandoned the federal system of Somalia” and described its position as seeking a consensus-based federal government. But the September letter has nevertheless changed the political question. If Deni wants to become president of Somalia, Somali voters and political stakeholders are entitled to ask what political future he is seeking to lead. Is he campaigning to become president of a united federal Somalia? Or is he simultaneously presenting Puntland’s possible separation from Somalia as an option? Those are fundamentally different political propositions. The National Presidency Requires a National Political Vision Deni’s candidacy places his Puntland position under a much broader national spotlight. A presidential candidate is asking Somalis across the country to entrust him with the country’s political destiny. That requires a clearly articulated national vision for the future of Somalia, including the relationship between the Federal Government and the federal member states. The independence language therefore creates an obvious political vulnerability for Deni. His opponents can reasonably ask how a candidate can seek the presidency of Somalia while his administration is simultaneously telling the United Nations that Puntland could consider permanently severing ties with Mogadishu. That question cannot be dismissed simply as another disagreement between Garowe and Mogadishu. It goes directly to the political identity of a presidential candidate. Puntland’s Future Cannot Be Decided by One President There is also a separate question of mandate. Puntland was established in 1998 through a broad community-based political process involving traditional elders, political representatives, businesspeople, intellectuals and civil-society participants. Its original political project was built around regional autonomy within a future federal Somalia, rather than a declaration of sovereign independence. That history matters because Puntland is not synonymous with whoever occupies the presidency. Deni has a mandate to lead Puntland’s administration and articulate its government’s position. But a decision as consequential as permanently separating Puntland from Somalia would raise a much larger question of popular and constitutional consent. The September letter itself provides no evidence of a referendum or other formal process through which Puntland’s population has collectively authorized such a change. Indeed, Somalia Today reported that federal officials rejected the suggestion that the letter represented the views of Puntland’s population, while political analysts disputed the claim that secession enjoys broad support. Those are contested political assessments and should not be treated as independently established facts. The Political Cost of Ambiguity This is where Deni’s national presidential ambitions encounter their greatest political difficulty. He can argue that Puntland is being pushed toward separation by what his administration describes as persistent federal interference and political exclusion. He can also argue that his reference to possible separation is a warning intended to pressure Mogadishu into reaching a negotiated settlement. But once the possibility of separation has been placed formally before the United Nations, the issue can no longer be treated simply as rhetoric. For a politician seeking Somalia’s presidency, the central question becomes whether his ultimate political project is the reconstruction of a functioning federal Somalia or the possibility of a different political future for Puntland. That ambiguity could become a defining issue in any national presidential contest. Puntland Is Bigger Than the Presidency None of this means that Puntland’s grievances should be ignored. The disputes over constitutional reform, elections, federal authority and the relationship between Mogadishu and the federal member states are substantive political questions. Puntland has repeatedly argued that Somalia’s political order must be negotiated rather than imposed unilaterally. Those positions can be debated without assuming that Puntland’s people have chosen independence. But the political destiny of Puntland cannot be reduced to a dispute between Deni and Hassan Sheikh Mohamud. Neither president owns Puntland. Neither president owns Somalia. And neither should be presumed to possess the authority to determine the ultimate constitutional future of millions of people without a legitimate political process. The Question Deni Must Answer For Deni, therefore, the central political challenge is no longer simply whether Puntland has legitimate grievances against Mogadishu. It is this:  If you are asking Somalis to trust you with the presidency of Somalia, what Somalia are you asking them to trust you to lead? A united federal Somalia? A radically restructured federation? Or a Somalia in which Puntland ultimately considers a separate political destiny? Deni has the right to articulate his position. Somali voters have the right to examine the consequences and consistency of that position. The issue is not whether Puntland has the right to complain about Mogadishu. It plainly has a political voice. The issue is whether a presidential candidate seeking to lead the entire Somali Republic can simultaneously leave open the possibility that the territory and population from which his political career is rooted may permanently separate from that republic. That is a question that cannot be answered by political rhetoric alone. Ultimately, Puntland’s future belongs to its people, just as Somalia’s future belongs to the Somali people. If the political future of Puntland is ever to be fundamentally reconsidered, the decisive question should therefore be neither what Deni wants nor what Hassan Sheikh wants. It should be what Puntland’s people, through a legitimate and representative political process, decide for themselves. Abdiqani Haji Abdi Email: Hajiabdi0128@gmail.com The post Puntland Is Not One Man — and Somalia’s Presidency Requires a National Mandate appeared first on WardheerNews .

items.title: Aadan Madoobe oo culeys ku haya laamaha amniga, kiiska Ikhlaas Ibraahim awgiis
items.description: Wararka ka imanaya Magaalada Baydhabo ayaa sheegaya in Hoggaamiyaha Dowlad Goboleedka Koonfur Galbeed, Aadan Maxamed Nuur (Aadan Madoobe) uu hay’adaha ammaanka faray inaysan ka seexan, sidii qoyska Ikhlaas Ibraahim Amiin ay caddaalad u heli lahaayeen. Ikhlaas Ibraahim oo shan jir ahayd ayaa galabta meydkeeda laga helay xaafadda Xaqsoor ee Magaalada Baydhabo, ka dib markii qoyskeeda ay Arbacadii ku kadsoomeen maqnaanshaheeda. Wararka ayaa sheegaya in gabadhaasi meydkeeda laga helay goob caafimaad ama MCH ku dhegan hoygooda, iyadoo ay ka muuqdaan calaamado muujinaya in xarig lagu ceejiyay. Wararka ayaa intaasi ku daraya in Booliska Baydhabo ay saddex qof u soo xireen kiiskeeda, kuwaas oo laba ka mid ah ay gabdho yihiin iyo nin dhallinyaro ah, oo sida la sheegay waardiye ka ahaa goobta laga helay meydka gabadhaasi. Ilo wareedyo ayaa sheegaya in Hoggaamiyaha Koonfur Galbeed uu culeys ku saarayo Taliyeyaasha iyo Saraakiisha Ciidamada Booliska iyo Nabad Sugidda inay soo afjaraan baaritaanka caddeymaha la xiriira dilka la tuhunsan yahay in loo gaystay Ikhlaas Ibraahim. Sarkaal ka tirsan Xarunta Madaxtooyada Koonfur Galbeed ee Baydhabo ayaa Universaltv u sheegay in Aadan Madoobe uu doonayo in si degdeg ah loo helo xog dhab ah iyo haddii ay jiraan cid falkaasi gaysatay, si aanu baaritaanka u jiitamin. Sarkaal kale oo ka tirsan Booliska Baydhabo ayaa sheegay in Madaxtooyadu ay riixeyso in maxkamad la horkeeno dadkii ka dambeeyay falka, si qoyska iyo ehelada dhibanaha ay u helaan qanaaco sharci. Qoyska Ikhlaas waxay ka mid ahaayeen qoysas barakacayaal ah oo bishii July dib-u-dejin loogu sameeyay guryo cusub oo laga dhisay xaafadda Xaqsoor. Ibraahim Maxamed Amiin oo adeerkii uu dhalay gabadhaasi ayaa sheegay inay maamulka ka doonayaan caddaalad. Waa dhacdo xanuun badan, waxayna shacabka Baydhabo iyo guud ahaan dadkii baraha bulshada kala socday raadinta Ikhlaas ay ku reebtay naxdin iyo tiiraanyo, markii la xaqiijiyay geerideeda.

items.title: Puntland Forces Free Hijacked Vessel in Major Anti-Piracy Operation
items.description: PMPF Says MTT SIBU 1 and Its Crew Were Rescued From Somali Pirates Off Mudug Coast Garowe (WDN) — Puntland’s maritime security forces have carried out a major anti-piracy operation off the Mudug coast, rescuing a vessel and its crew after Somali pirates reportedly held them captive for weeks. The Puntland Maritime Police Force (PMPF) said its forces stormed the MTT SIBU 1 and brought the hijacking to an end after targeting the pirate group responsible for the seizure. Puntland said the operation secured the vessel and its crew and reported that members of the pirate group were killed or wounded during the confrontation. No casualty figures were provided, and the administration has not released detailed information about the crew’s condition or identities. PMPF Intensifies Coastal Security The operation comes amid increased PMPF activity along Puntland’s coastline, where the force has maintained a longstanding role in combating piracy and other maritime threats. Puntland said PMPF units had intensified patrols and operations in recent days to disrupt pirate networks and prevent further attacks on commercial shipping. The successful intervention highlights the role of Somali-led maritime forces in responding directly to threats along the country’s coastline. Puntland has also called for stronger international cooperation on maritime security, arguing that piracy in Somali waters can threaten commercial shipping along major routes linking Asia, the Middle East, Africa and Europe. items.title: Farmaajo Warns Somalia Could Drift Toward Political Fragmentation
items.description: Former President Says Election Disputes, Constitutional Deadlock and Federal Tensions Risk Creating Competing Centres of Power Mogadishu (WDN) — Somalia is facing a deepening political crisis that could leave the country increasingly divided into competing centres of power, former President Mohamed Abdullahi Mohamed “Farmaajo” has warned, urging President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud to reopen national dialogue and reach agreement on the rules for the next election. Farmaajo’s intervention comes as Mogadishu remains locked in disputes with opposition groups and several federal member states over constitutional reforms, federalism, political mandates and the electoral system. Puntland and the Somali Future Council have separately taken their concerns to the United Nations, highlighting the widening political divide. The Crisis Is Bigger Than an Election Farmaajo argues that Somalia’s political stability depends on four pillars: a broadly agreed constitution, completion of the federal system, timely and inclusive elections, and dialogue and compromise. All four are under pressure. Negotiations over the next electoral framework have yet to produce an agreement acceptable to all major political actors, while relations between Mogadishu and several federal member states have deteriorated. The dispute is therefore no longer simply about an election date. It is increasingly about who sets the rules, who controls political institutions and who determines Somalia’s political order. If the deadlock continues, federal institutions and regional administrations could increasingly operate according to competing political mandates, leaving Somalia formally united but increasingly divided in practice. The Human Cost The political crisis is unfolding alongside a severe displacement and housing crisis in Mogadishu. EUAA reporting, based on UN and other humanitarian data, estimated that more than 1.1 million people were living in verified IDP sites in the capital as of July 2025. Forced evictions added to the pressure, with 143,548 evictions reported during 2025, including 63,132 people removed from government properties. Opposition figures and rights groups have also alleged that some properties cleared through evictions were subsequently transferred or sold without adequate legal process or transparency. Those allegations remain contested, but the scale of displacement is documented. The political crisis is therefore being felt beyond government institutions — it is affecting families whose access to land and shelter remains uncertain. Farmaajo’s intervention comes with the experience of Somalia’s previous electoral crisis still fresh.His presidential term expired in February 2021 without an agreed election. Parliament subsequently approved a two-year extension, triggering intense opposition and armed clashes in Mogadishu before the extension was abandoned and political leaders returned to negotiations. That episode remains a reminder of how disputes over political mandates can escalate when dialogue breaks down. Farmaajo’s Three Demands Farmaajo is calling for three immediate steps. First, he wants Hassan Sheikh to lead a genuine national dialogue involving the country’s principal political stakeholders. Second, he calls for agreement on the electoral framework before the next election. Third, he wants an inclusive election held within a short timeframe to end Somalia’s prolonged political uncertainty. He also argues that Somalia’s political disputes should ultimately be resolved through a Somali-led process rather than determined by external actors. The Central Question The Federal Government maintains that its constitutional and electoral reforms are intended to strengthen Somalia’s democratic institutions. Its opponents argue that fundamental changes require broader political agreement. That disagreement lies at the heart of the current crisis. The question is no longer simply who will contest the next election. It is who will agree on the rules under which that election takes place — and whether those rules will be accepted by Somalia’s principal political actors. Without such an agreement, the country risks deeper institutional confrontation and increasingly competing centres of political authority. Farmaajo’s warning comes at a critical moment. Somalia’s political leaders face the challenge of restoring a negotiated process before disputes over elections, constitutional authority and federalism become even more deeply entrenched. For a country already confronting insecurity, displacement and institutional fragility, the stakes extend far beyond the next presidential contest. items.title: Jaamacadda Hope University oo qabatay kulan ay isugu yimaadeen ardaydii hore uga qalin-jabisay
items.description: Muqdisho – Jaamacadda Hope University ayaa maanta si guul leh u qabatay kulanka Aluumi-ga (Alumni), kaas oo ay ka qeyb galeen qaar ka mid ah ardaydii hore uga qalin-jabisay jaamacadda, kuwaas oo maanta haya xilal sare iyo masuuliyado muhiim ah. Kulanka ayaa diiradda lagu saaray xoojinta xiriirka ka dhexeeya jaamacadda iyo ardaydii hore uga qalin-jabisay, kor u qaadista wada-shaqeynta labada dhinac iyo ballaarinta kaalinta ay jaamacaddu ku leedahay adeegga iyo horumarinta bulshada. Munaasabadda ayaa waxaa ugu horreyn daahfurtay Haawo Ibraahim Cali, oo ka mid ah ardaydii hore uga qalin-jabisay Jaamacadda Hope University. Intii uu kulanku socday, qaar ka mid ah ardaydii hore ayaa halkaas ka jeediyay hadallo ay ku cabbireen dareenkooda ku aaddan waxbarashadii ay ku qaateen jaamacadda, iyagoo sidoo kale ka hadlay doorka ay Hope University ku lahayd kobcinta aqoontooda iyo horumarkooda shaqsiyeed iyo mid xirfadeed. Ugu dambeyn, munaasabadda ayaa waxaa soo xiray Madaxweyne Ku-xigeenka Jaamacadda Hope University, Eng. Maxamed Cilmi, kaas oo ardaydii hore kula dardaarmay inay sii wadaan dadaalkooda, aqoontooda uga faa’iideeyaan bulshada, isla markaana ay door muuqda ka qaataan horumarka dalka. Kulankan ayaa qeyb ka ah dadaallada lagu xoojinayo xiriirka jaamacadda iyo ardaydii hore uga qalin-jabisay, si loo kobciyo wada-shaqeynta, is-weydaarsiga aqoonta iyo doorka ay ku leeyihiin horumarinta bulshada Soomaaliyeed.

items.title: NISA oo dharbaaxo culus ku dhufatay Al-Shabaab – Maxaa dhacay maanta?
items.description: Jowhar (Caasimada Online) – Ciidanka Hay’adda Sirdoonka iyo Nabadsugidda Qaranka (NISA) oo kaashanaya saaxiibada caalamka ayaa howlgal qorsheysan ka fuliyay tuulada Bur Saruur ee gobolka Shabeellaha Dhexe. Howlgalka ayaa ka dhacay tuulada oo qiyaastii 2 KM koonfur-bari kaga beegan deegaanka Cali-Gaduud, waxaana lagu bartilmaameedsaday goob ay ku sugnaayeen maleeshiyaad ka tirsan kooxda Al-Shabaab. Ciidamada NISA ayaa dilay 12 xubnood oo ka tirsan Al-Shabaab, iyadoo sidoo kale la burburiyay agab ciidan oo ay kooxdaasi adeegsanaysay, sida lagu sheegay bayaan kasoo baxay hay’adda. Intii uu socday howlgalka, ciidamada ayaa sidoo kale burburiyay goobihii ay maleeshiyaadku gabbaadka ka dhiganayeen, taas oo qayb ka ahayd howlgallada lagu wiiqayo awoodda kooxda ee gobolka. Howlgalka ayaa la sheegay inuu ahaa mid qorsheysan, waxaana ciidamada iyo saaxiibada caalamka ay si gaar ah u bartilmaameedsadeen goobta ay maleeshiyaadku isku uruursanayeen. Howlgalka ayaa u dhacay sidii loo qorsheeyay, iyadoo ciidamada ay sii wadaan raadraaca xubnihii ka firxaday goobta. Ciidamada NISA ayaa sidoo kale wada howlgallo ka dhan ah dagaalyahannada Al-Shabaab ee ku sugan deegaanno ka tirsan gobolka Shabeellaha Dhexe, iyadoo la isku dayayo in laga hortago dhaq-dhaqaaqyada kooxda. Howlgalkan ayaa kusoo aadaya xilli ciidamada dowladda Soomaaliya iyo saaxiibada caalamka ay wadaan howlgallo lagu beegsanayo fariisimaha iyo goobaha ay ku dhuumaaleysanayaan maleeshiyaadka Al-Shabaab. items.title: Gabar maalmo la la’aa oo meydkeeda laga helay Baydhabo
items.description: Gabadhan oo da’deeda lagu sheegay shan jir ayaa galabta meydkeeda laga helay Magaalada Baydhabo, ka dib muddo 48 saacadood ah oo qoyskeeda ay weysanaayeen. Gabadhan oo lagu magacabayay Ikhlaas Ibraahim Amiin ayaa meydkeeda laga helay xaafadda Xaqsoor ama Xaqsoor Village, oo ah xaafad cusub oo horaantii sanadkan dhismaheeda laga bilaabay Baydhabo. Wararka ayaa sheegaya in ciidamada amniga ay gaareen goobta, isla-markaana ay meydka Ikhlaas u gudbiyeen Isbitaal Goboleedka Baay, si baaritaan loogu sameeyo sababta ay u geeriyootay. Ibraahim Maxamed Amiin oo adeerkii uu dhalay gabadhaasi ayaa inoo sheegay “Gabadhan waxaa la waayay 2-dii duhurnimo ee maalintii Arbacada, waxaana galabta casirkii meydkeeda laga helay meel MCH ah ama goob caafimaad oo ku dhegan gurigooda. Qoyskeeda waxay ka mid ahaayeen qoysaska barakacayaasha ee degan Magaalada Baydhabo ee bishii July la dejiyay guryaha cusub ee laga dhisay laanta Xaqsoor Village oo ka tirsan xaafadda Wadajir.” Ibraahim Maxamed ayaa sheegay inay jiraan calaamado muujinaya in gabadhaasi ay u geeriyootay jirdil iyo xarig cunaha looga ceejiyay. Sarkaal ka tirsan Booliska Baydhabo ayaa Universaltv u sheegay in labadii maalmood ee u dambeysay ay ku howlanaayeen baadigoobka gabadhaasi, ka dib markii qoyskeeda ay la soo wadaageen maqnaanshaheeda. Sarkaalkan oo codsaday inaanan magaciisa la soo xigan ayaa xusay in falkaasi ay u soo xireen wiil iyo laba gabar, isagoo intaasi ku daray in wiilku uu waardiye ka ahaa goobta laga helay meydka gabadha. Dhacdadan naxdinta leh ayaa saamayn qoto dheer ku yeelatay dareenka dadka deegaanka, kuwaas oo si weyn u hadal haya.

items.title: Xog: Villa Soomaaliya oo dooratay shaqsiga ku-xigeen u noqonaya Cali Guudlaawe
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Madaxtooyada Soomaaliya ayaa u garatay Cabdifataax Xasan Afrax inuu noqdo ku-xigeenka Madaxweynaha Hirshabeelle, Cali Guudlaawe Xuseen, sida ay ogaatay Caasimada Online. Arrintan ayaa lagu go’aamiyay kulan galabta ka dhacay xarunta ururka Madaxweyne Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud ee JSP, halkaas oo Cabdifataax Afrax loogu xushay inuu noqdo ku-xigeenka Guudlaawe, xilli doorashada maamulka la qorsheeyay inay HirShabelle ka dhacdo 30-ka September. Go’aanka Villa Soomaaliya ayaa kusoo aadaya iyadoo ay jireen siyaasiyiin kala duwan oo kasoo jeeda gobolka Hiiraan, kuwaas oo doonayay inay qabtaan xilka ku-xigeenka Madaxweynaha HirShabelle, balse ugu dambeyn waxaa laga dhex xushay Afrax. Sida xogtu tilmaamayso, xulashada Cabdifataax Afrax ayaa lagu saleeyay dhowr arrimood, oo ay kamid yihiin saamiga beeleed ee uu matalo, waayo-aragnimadiisa maamul iyo xiriirka uu la leeyahay deegaanka Hiiraan. Afrax ayaa hore dhowr jeer u soo maamulay Hiiraan, taas oo la rumeysan yahay inay kamid tahay qodobbada Villa Soomaaliya ku tixgelisay markii ay qiimeynaysay shaqsiga ku habboon inuu Guudlaawe ku weheliyo hoggaanka HirShabelle. Xogta ayaa sidoo kale sheegeysa in Madaxtooyada Soomaaliya ay u aragto Afrax shaqsi awood u yeelan kara inuu wajaho xaaladda siyaasadeed ee ka taagan Hiiraan, gaar ahaan kacdoonka iyo diidmada HirShabelle ee ay beeshiisu ka waddo magaalada Beledweyne. Doorashada ku-xigeenka ayaa muhiimad gaar ah yeelanaysa xilli HirShabelle ay isu diyaarineyso doorasho, iyadoo ay weli jiraan khilaafaad siyaasadeed iyo aragtiyo kala duwan oo ku saabsan maamulka iyo mustaqbalka siyaasadeed ee gobolka Hiiraan. Si kastaba, Cabdifataax Afrax ayaa noqonaya shaqsiga ku wehelinaya Cali Guudlaawe doorashada iyo hoggaanka HirShabelle, iyadoo indhaha lagu hayo sida xulashadiisu uga falcelin doonto xaaladda siyaasadeed ee Beledweyne iyo guud ahaan gobolka Hiiraan. Sida xogtu tilmaamayso, xulashada Cabdifataax Afrax ayaa lagu saleeyay dhowr arrimood, oo ay kamid yihiin saamiga beeleed ee uu matalo, waayo-aragnimadiisa maamul iyo xiriirka uu la leeyahay deegaanka Hiiraan. Afrax ayaa hore dhowr jeer u soo maamulay Hiiraan, taas oo la rumeysan yahay inay kamid tahay qodobbada Villa Soomaaliya ku tixgelisay markii ay qiimeynaysay shaqsiga ku habboon inuu Guudlaawe ku weheliyo hoggaanka HirShabelle. Xogta ayaa sidoo kale sheegeysa in Madaxtooyada Soomaaliya ay u aragto Afrax shaqsi awood u yeelan kara inuu wajaho xaaladda siyaasadeed ee ka taagan Hiiraan, gaar ahaan kacdoonka iyo diidmada HirShabelle ee ay beeshiisu ka waddo magaalada Beledweyne. Doorashada ku-xigeenka ayaa muhiimad gaar ah yeelanaysa xilli HirShabelle ay isu diyaarineyso doorasho, iyadoo ay weli jiraan khilaafaad siyaasadeed iyo aragtiyo kala duwan oo ku saabsan maamulka iyo mustaqbalka siyaasadeed ee gobolka Hiiraan. Si kastaba, Cabdifataax Afrax ayaa noqonaya shaqsiga ku wehelinaya Cali Guudlaawe doorashada iyo hoggaanka HirShabelle, iyadoo indhaha lagu hayo sida xulashadiisu uga falcelin doonto xaaladda siyaasadeed ee Beledweyne iyo guud ahaan gobolka Hiiraan. items.title: Wada jirkeenu waa guusha Wasiir Yoonis Axmed Yoonis
items.description: Qore : Wasiir Yoonis Axmed Yoonis. Muddo dhowr toddobaad ah ayuu Madaxweynaha Jamhuuriyadda Somaliland Mudane, Dr. Cabdiraxmaan Maxamed Cabdillaahi(Cirro), safar shaqo ku joogay dalka Mareykanka, isaga oo codka Somaliland gaadhsiiyey fagaareyaal muhiim u ah siyaasadda iyo diblomaasiyadda caalamka. Intii Madaxweynahu uu safarka ku jiray wuxu kulamo la yeeshay mas’uuliyiin, xildibbaano, siyaasiyiin, aqoonyahanno iyo qeybaha kala duwan ee bulshada Mareykanka, isaga oo si cad u soo bandhigay danaha Somaliland, xaqa ay u lee dahay aqoonsi caalami ah iyo muhiimadda istaraatijiyaddeed ee ay ku lee dahay gobalka. Safarkani, wuxu ahaa tallaabo muhiim u ah ballaadhinta xidhiidhka caalamiga ah iyo kor u qaadista doorka Somaliland. Waxa uu dunida xasuusiyey jiritaanka dal leh hay’ado dawladnimo oo dhisan, nidaam dimuqraadi ah, nabad, iyo xasilooni, diyaar na u ah iskaashi ku dhisan dano wadaag. Dedaalka uu maanta hoggaaminayo Madaxweyne Cirro, wuxu saldhig u yahay fursadaha berri. Guusha laga rajeynayo siyaasadda dibaddu se waxay ku xidhan tahay oo u baahan tahay taageero gudaha ah, wadajir qaran iyo in danta guud laga hormariyo kala duwanaanshaha siyaasaddeed. Ugu dambayn, waxa aan boggaadinayaa shacabka Somaliland ee garab istaagay Madaxweynaha iyo safarkiisa shaqo. Waxaanan lee yahay dawlad haday tahay iyo weli ba muxaafad iyo mucaarad ba, ururada bulshada iyo shacabba waxa ina saaran mas’uuliyad ah inaynu ilaalino nabadda iyo xasiloonida, isla markaana dunida tusno inaynu nahay qaran isku kalsoon oo u taagan mustaqbalkiisa. Midnimadeenu waa awoodeena, Wada-jirkeenu na waa jidka guusha. Guul Somaliland.

items.title: Sidii uu ku bilaabmay xasuuqii shalay loo gaystay qoys Fuqashini ah
items.description: Sidee u dhacay dagaalka Fiqishini iyo Dhulbahante shalay? Nin Fiqishini oo reer miyi ah isla markaana ka guuray aaga Adhicadeeye ayaa degey meel u dhow Jidbaale oo roob helay, waxaa u yimid nin Dhulbahante ah wuxuu yidhi: “halkan ma degi kartid ee ka guur” is af dhaafkaas ayaa sababay in la dilo ninka Dhulbahante, ninka Fiqishini ee wax dilay aabihiis ayaa hore loogu dilay Madax lagu xoor bilo ka hor iyada oo dhulka uu deganaa loo diidan yahay. Ka dib Ciidamo Dhulbahante ah ayaa duulay waxaanay weerareen rag meesha wax ka dhaceen ka fog oo geel la joogay isla markaasna oo hal qoys u badan waxaanay ku bilaabeen inay qoryo saaran tikniko la dhacaan raga Fiqishini ee goobtaas ku dhintay waxaa ku jira afar nin oo isku qoys ah oo kala ah: Dalab Yuusuf Cawad iyo Mukhtaar Yuusuf cawad oo walaalo ah, wiil uu Dalab dhalay iyo wiil ay Dalab iyo Mukhtaar abti u yihiin.
