items.title: Wararkii ugu dambeeyey dagaalka gobolka Tigray ee Itoobiya iyo TPLF oo maanta…
items.description: Mekelle (Caasimada Online) – Adeegyada internet-ka iyo taleefannada ayaa Jimcaha maanta ah si weyn uga go’ay gobolka Tigray ee waqooyiga Itoobiya, xilli dagaal culus uu toddobaadkan dib uga qarxay ciidamada dowladda federaalka iyo xoogagga Tigray. Dagaalladan ayaa ah kuwii ugu xooganaa ee gobolka ka dhaca tan iyo markii heshiis nabadeed lagu soo afjaray dagaalkii dhiigga badan ku daatay ee Itoobiya ka socday intii u dhaxeysay 2020 iyo 2022. Afar ilo-wareed oo arrintan xog-ogaal u ah, oo uu ku jiro diblomaasi, ayaa Reuters u sheegay in xisbiga talada Tigray haya ee Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) uu shirkadaha Ethio Telecom iyo Safaricom ku amray inay joojiyaan adeegyada internet-ka iyo taleefannada ee gobolka. Mid ka mid ah ilaha ayaa sheegay in tallaabadaasi ay suuragal tahay inay qeyb ka tahay isku day ay xoogagga Tigray ku doonayaan inay ku yareeyaan faa’iidada ay ciidamada federaalku ka helaan diyaaradaha aan duuliyaha lahayn. Joojinta shabakadaha telefoonka ayaa adkeyn karta in ciidamada dowladda ay drones-ka qaarkood ku xiraan ama uga faa’iideystaan shabakadaha isgaarsiinta ee goobaha dagaalka. TPLF kama jawaabin codsi Reuters ay u dirtay oo ku saabsan arrintan. Hase yeeshee, ilo ku dhow kooxda oo magaciisa qariyey ayaa beeniyey inay TPLF ka dambeyso go’itaanka isgaarsiinta, isaga oo eedda dusha ka saaray dowladda federaalka. Wicitaanno iyo farriimo ay weriyeyaasha Reuters u direen taleefannada isticmaala shabakadda Ethio Telecom ma aysan shaqeyn Jimcihii, halka macaamiisha Safaricom ay meelo kooban ka heli kareen adeeg. Hay’adda NetBlocks, oo la socota xaaladda internet-ka caalamka, ayaa sidoo kale xaqiijisay in carqalad weyn ay ka jirto internet-ka waqooyiga Itoobiya. Xafiiska Ra’iisul Wasaare Abiy Ahmed, Ethio Telecom iyo Safaricom Ethiopia kama aysan jawaabin codsiyo faallo ah oo loo diray. Cabsi laga qabo xaaladdii dagaalkii hore Go’itaanka isgaarsiinta ayaa sare u qaaday walaaca laga qabo in dadka Tigray ay mar kale wajahaan xaalad la mid ah tii dagaalkii 2020-2022. Intii uu dagaalkaasi socday, dowladda federaalka ayaa muddo dheer jartay adeegyada isgaarsiinta ee Tigray, halka helitaanka raashinka, lacagta iyo dawooyinkuba si weyn u adkaadeen. Xaaladdaas ayaa boqolaal kun oo qof gelisay duruufo ay hay’adaha gargaarku ku tilmaameen kuwo u dhow macluul. Dagaalka toddobaadkan dib u qarxay ayaa durba dadka ku nool Tigray ku qasbay inay si degdeg ah u iibsadaan raashin iyo agab kale oo muhiim ah, isla markaana bankiyada kala baxaan lacag caddaan ah. Dadka deegaanka ayaa Reuters u sheegay in bakhaarro iyo dukaamo badan ay alaabtu ka dhammaaneyso sababo la xiriira dadweynaha oo cabsi darteed wax badan iibsanaya. Dadka ku nool caasimadda Tigray ee Mekelle ayaa sheegay in adeegga Ethio Telecom uu istaagay fiidnimadii Khamiista, taasoo sidoo kale saameysay adeegyada lacagaha lagu kala diro taleefannada. “Xitaa Safaricom meel walba kama shaqeyneyso. Waa inaad meelba meel u guurtaa si aad shabakad u hesho,” ayuu yiri qof ku nool Mekelle oo la hadlay Reuters. Dagaalka oo sii fidaya Xoogagga Tigray iyo xulafadooda ayaa toddobaadkan la wareegay saddex garoon diyaaradeed, waxayna weerarro ku qaadeen ciidamada federaalka ee gobollada deriska la ah Tigray ee Afar iyo Amxaaro. TPLF ayaa dagaalka ku tilmaantay mid difaac ah oo looga hortagayo waxa ay ugu yeertay gardarro uga imaaneysa dowladda Abiy Ahmed. Dowladda federaalka Itoobiya ayaa dhankeeda Eritrea ku eedeysay inay dhaqaale ku taageereyso TPLF iyo xulafadeeda, eedeyntaasi oo dowladda Eritrea ay beenisay. Qaar ka mid ah dadka Tigray ayaa sidoo kale sheegay inay arkeen dhalinyaro lagu qasbayo inay ku biiraan dagaalka. “Dagaalyahannada TPLF waxay hadda guri guri u raadinayaan dhalinyarada. Guriga ayaan ku dhuumanayaa, shaqadana ma aadin,” ayuu Reuters u sheegay qof ku nool magaalada Maichew. Warbixin dhinaca khatarta ah oo bishan lala wadaagay diblomaasiyiin, Reuters-na ay aragtay, ayaa sheegtay in TPLF ay horey tallaabooyin ugu qaaday carqaladeynta adeegyada isgaarsiinta, oo ay ku jirto ka saarista qalab ay leedahay Ethio Telecom magaalooyin dhowr ah. Ciidamada Itoobiya ayaa dagaalladii hore si weyn ugu tiirsanaa diyaaradaha aan duuliyaha lahayn, waxaana la rumeysan yahay inay haystaan tiro badan oo drones ah oo dibadda laga keenay iyo kuwo gudaha dalka lagu sameeyo. Hay’adda Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project (ACLED) ayaa sheegtay in ciidamada federaalka ay drones u adeegsanayeen weerarro ka dhan ah bartilmaameedyo ku yaalla Tigray tan iyo bishii hore. Dib u soo laabashada dagaal weyn oo Tigray ka dhaca ayaa sidoo kale sii murjin karta xaaladda Geeska Afrika, xilli xiriirka Itoobiya iyo Eritrea uu sii xumaanayo, dagaalka Sudan uu weli socdo, isla markaana muranka Itoobiya ee marin-u-helidda Badda Cas uu taagan yahay. Qaramada Midoobay iyo Midowga Yurub ayaa dhinacyada ugu baaqay inay is xakameeyaan oo ay dib ugu laabtaan geeddi-socodkii nabadda ee Midowga Afrika fududeeyey, kaas oo soo afjaray dagaalkii hore ee ay ku dhinteen boqolaal kun oo qof. Dhanka kale, waxaa sii kordhaya walaaca laga qabo kaniisadaha qadiimiga ah ee dhagaxa laga qoday ee magaalada Lalibela ee gobolka Amxaaro, kuwaas oo UNESCO u aqoonsan tahay goob dhaxal caalami ah. Duulimaadyadii garoonka Lalibela ayaa Khamiistii la hakiyey kaddib markii dagaallo ay ka dhaceen deegaanno u dhow magaalada. items.title: Hawlgal qorsheysan oo la sheegay in lagu dilay xubno ka tirsan Al Shabaab
items.description: Hay’adda Nabad Sugidda & Sirdoonka Qaranka (NISA) ayaa Jimcahan sheegtay in ciidankeeda oo kaashanaya kuwa saaxiibada caalamka ay fuliyeen hawlgal qorsheysan, kaas oo ay sheegtay in lagu bartilmaameedsaday maleeshiyada Al Shabaab. NISA ayaa sheegtay in hawlgalkan oo laga fuliyay tuulada Bur Saruur oo qiyaastii 2km koonfur bari kaga beegan deegaanka Cali Gaduud ee Gobolka Shabellaha Dhexe lagu dilay 12 xubnood oo ka tirsanaa Al Shabaab. “Ciidanka Hay’adda Sirdoonka iyo Nabad Sugidda Qaranka (NISA) oo kaashanaya saaxiibada caalamka ayaa tuulada Bur Saruur, oo qiyaastii 2 KM koonfur bari kaga beegan deegaanka Cali Gaduud ee Gobolka Shabellaha Dhexe ka fuliyay hawlgal qorsheysan oo lagu dilay 12 dhagarqabe oo ka tirsanaa Khawaarijta.” Ayay NISA ku sheegtay war qoraal ah. Warka ayaa lagu sheegay in hawlgalka si gaar ah loogu beegsaday goob ay isku uruursanayeen maleeshiyada Al Shabaab oo Dowladda Somaliya ay u taqaano (Khawaarijta), laguna burburiyay agab ciidan iyo goobihii gabaadka u ahaa maleeshiyadaasi. “Hawlgalka ayaa si gaar ah loogu bartilmaameedsaday goob ay isku uruursanayeen maleeshiyaadka Khawaarijta, waxaana lagu burburiyay agab ciidan iyo goobihii ay gabaadka ka dhiganayeen.” Ayaa lagu yiri warka. NISA waxay sheegtay in hawlgalku uu u dhacay sidii loo qorsheeyay, isla-markaana uu socdo baadigoobka iyo dabagalka haraadiga kuwii ka baxsaday goobta. “Hawlgalka ayaa u dhacay sidii loo qorsheeyay, iyada oo weli lagu raad-joogo firxadka haraadiga Khawaarijta.” Ayaa lagu soo geba-gabeeyay warka. NISA ayaa soo uruurisa xogaha maleeshiyada iyo horjoogeyaasha Al Shabaab, ka hor inta aan hawlgalada hawada la qaadin, waana isha ugu weyn, uguna muhiimsan ee laga raadraaco xubnaha khatarta ku ah nolosha bulshada.

items.title: UK-backed climate initiative lays groundwork for water resilience in Horn of Africa
items.description: UK-backed climate initiative lays groundwork for water resilience in Horn of Africa 25 September 2026 Consultancy.africa A UK government programme is on its way to unlock groundwater resilience for the Horn of Africa. That is according to a Midline Evaluation of the Regional Climate and Nature (ARCAN) Programme, carried out in partnership with international consulting firm Ecorys. Announced at COP26 in Glasgow, the ARCAN Programme supports the World Bank’s Sustainable Renewables Risk Mitigation Initiative (SRMI) to help regions around the world adopt renewable energy technologies and storage scale, and seeks to boost sustainable energy generation by pairing battery storage alongside solar, wind, and other technologies. It has been funded by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO). The ARCAN programme as a whole has received over £100 million in funding from International Climate Finance (ICF) aims to boost several different climate and nature-related efforts across Africa, covering things like renewable energy, forest protection, and water management. The Ecorys evaluation looks more specifically at the Cooperation in International Waters in Africa (CIWA) programme, a multi‑donor trust fund managed by the World Bank, a part of the larger ARCAN programme that focuses on water resilience in the Horn of Africa, specifically. The Horn of Africa is home to over 140 million people spread across the countries of Ethiopia, Djibouti, Eritrea, Somalia, and the partially recognised country of Somaliland. The region is geographically diverse, but in large part is dominated by arid and semi-arid landscapes, which have been impacted by climate change. Much of the region has suffered under severe drought conditions since 2023, especially in Somalia, a war-torn country lacking basic infrastructure. Tens of millions of people are currently affected by, or at risk of famine. This is the backdrop for international development project and the Ecorys evaluation of its progress so far. Some of the main recommendation are to develop regionally aligned national standards for groundwater projects, apply lessons from other groundwater interventions, and to engage graduate students to consolidate technical data and research. Mixed progress on the ground The evaluation, which focused on a UK-backed effort called Cooperation in International Waters in Africa (CIWA) found a mixed picture. On one hand, researchers found real signs that the programme is helping countries in the region talk to each other about shared water resources for the first time in a meaningful way. On the other hand, the actual work of building wells and water systems on the ground in places like Turkana County in northern Kenya is running into serious problems. For example, evaluators visited four planned well sites in Turkana and found that, none of the local contractors had even begun construction yet. The report warns that unless the programme changes its approach, it risks failing. Money is not the primary issue The report makes clear that funding a well is the easy part. The harder problem is keeping it running for years afterward. Researchers found that communities in the borderlands, many of whom have never had to pay cash for water, often cannot or will not pay enough to cover repairs. New sources of water can also, in some cases, become a catalyst for conflict. The report describes a case where a newly drilled well meant to serve two rival communities was vandalised after a dispute broke out over who controlled it. Researchers found that the programme has started factoring in strategies for managing these disputes, but it is not yet clear whether those measures are strong enough. “Boreholes may create resentment between communities that are not served, leading to vandalism of new infrastructure while water tariffs may create perverse incentives to partake in illicit activities, such as charcoal production, to generate cash,” notes a press release from ARCAN. Positive steps in cooperation Despite these struggles, the report found genuine progress at a higher level. Government officials in the region increasingly see groundwater, rather than rivers, as an easier starting point for cooperation, since it is less politically sensitive than shared rivers like the Juba and Shebelle. Somalia, Kenya, and Ethiopia are now working together through the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) and are beginning to build the kind of trust needed to eventually share data on their water resources. Lessons for the road ahead The evaluators offered several recommendations, including working more closely with organisations like Oxfam that have already tested different ways of running local water systems, and making sure lessons learned in one country are not lost when staff move on to other jobs. They also suggested that groundwater projects alone cannot solve the water crisis in the region and that broader government policy, such as programmes that let wealthier communities subsidise poorer ones, will likely be needed for lasting change. Overall, the report concludes it is still too early to say whether the current phase of the programme, known as Groundwater for Resilience, will succeed where past efforts have failed. But it credits UK-backed funding with helping lay the groundwork for a level of regional cooperation that did not exist before. “Evidence of mutual benefits and a shift in mindset within government agencies from competition to collaboration supported by CIWA activities is leading to tangible progress on data sharing and transboundary aquifer management, which could contribute to future collaboration on other issues,” notes ARCAN.     Source Consultancy.africa

items.title: Cabdiraxmaan Cirro: Aragtida Soomaali-weyn waxay sababi doonta burbur iyo dagaal
items.description: New York (Caasimada Online) – Madaxweynaha Somaliland, Cabdiraxmaan Maxamed Cabdillaahi (Cirro) ayaa sheegay in isku dayga lagu mideynayo dhammaan dhulalka ay Soomaalidu ku nool yihiin uu horseedi karo dagaal iyo burbur, isagoo soo bandhigay aragtidiisa ku aaddan waxa uu ku tilmaamay mashruuca Soomaali-weyn. Cirro ayaa hadalkan ka sheegay kulan iyo dood uu shalay uga qeyb-galay Golaha Xidhiidhka Dibadda ee Mareykanka (Council on Foreign Relations – CFR) ee magaalada New York, halkaas oo uu kaga hadlay taariikhda Somaliland iyo Soomaaliya, midowgii labada dhinac iyo doodda Somaliland ee ku saabsan madaxbannaanida. Madaxweynaha ayaa sheegay in Soomaalidu ay yihiin hal bulsho oo wadaagta luuqad iyo diin, balse aysan taasi khasab ka dhignayn inay ku wada noolaadaan hal dal. Wuxuu tusaale u soo qaatay dalalka Carabta oo uu sheegay inay yihiin 22 dal oo wadaaga luuqad iyo diin, iyo dalalka Afrikaanka ah ee ku hadla afka Sawaaxiliga oo uu sheegay inay yihiin 12 dal. Isagoo ka hadlayay taariikhda labada dhinac, Cirro wuxuu xusay in Somaliland iyo Soomaaliya ay hore u ahaayeen laba dhul oo ay kala maamulayeen gumaystayaal kala duwan. “Somaliland waxay xornimadeeda ka qaadatay Boqortooyada Ingiriiska sannadkii 1960, halka Soomaaliya ay xornimada ka qaadatay Talyaaniga. Labada dhinac ayaa markii dambe midoobay, iyadoo ujeeddadu ahayd in la dhiso hal dal oo ay ku midoobaan dhammaan dadka Soomaalida ah ee ku nool Geeska Afrika,” ayuu yiri Cirro. Sidoo kale wuxuu sheegay in himiladaasi aysan dhab noqon, maadaama Soomaalida Jabuuti ay ku nool yihiin dal madax-bannaan, halka Soomaalida Itoobiya ay weli ka tirsan yihiin Itoobiya, qaybta Soomaalida ee Kenya-na ay ku jirto Kenya. Marka laga hadlayo mustaqbalka Soomaalida, Cirro wuxuu su’aal ka keenay in xal loogu raadiyo in dhammaan dhulalka Soomaalidu ku nool yihiin lagu mideeyo hal dal iyo in la aqbalo in bulshooyinkaasi ay ku kala noolaadaan dalalka ay hadda ka tirsan yihiin, iyadoo la ilaalinayo nabadda iyo xasilloonida gobolka. Wuxuu ku dooday in haddii la isku dayo mideynta dhulalkaas ay taasi keeni karto dagaal iyo burbur. Si kastaba, kulanka CFR ayaa sidoo kale diiradda lagu saaray dalabka Somaliland ee aqoonsi caalami ah iyo xaaladda amni ee Geeska Afrika, iyadoo hadallada Cirro ay qayb ka yihiin dadaallada diblomaasiyadeed ee Somaliland ka waddo Mareykanka. Madaxweynaha Somaliland ayaa intii uu New York ku sugnaa xoogga saarayay soo bandhigista mowqifka maamulka Somaliland ee raadinta aqoonsi caalami ah, taas oo si adag u diidan tahay Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya. The post Cabdiraxmaan Cirro: Aragtida Soomaali-weyn waxay sababi doonta burbur iyo dagaal appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: The Somaliland President Addresses Council On Foreign Relations In New York
items.description: New York The Somaliland President, Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi addressed the Council For Foreign Relations In New York. The President spoke at length about Somaliland’s historical journey and it’s ability to create lasting peace and democracy within the country. The forum which was invitees only, also discussed the prospective relationship between Somaliland and the United States of America. During the forum, the President took questions from the floor from some of the distinguished guests that were present. Qarannews.

items.title: Israa’iil oo askar ku weyday qarax diyaarad oo maanta…
items.description: Gaza (Caasimada Online) – Laba askari oo ka tirsan ciidamada Israa’iil ayaa lagu dilay waqooyiga Gaza kadib markii ay qaraxday diyaarad aan duuliye lahayn (drone) oo ay ciidamadu adeegsanayeen, sida uu sheegay milatariga Israa’iil. Milatariga ayaa sheegay in drone-ka uu shalay gudaha saldhig milatari ugu dhacay sababo aan weli la shaacin, iyadoo ciidamada ay markii dambe soo qaadeen diyaaradda. Sida lagu sheegay warbixinta milatariga, drone-ka ayaa qarxay daqiiqado kadib markii askartu ay soo qaadeen, taas oo sababtay dhimashada labada askari. Dhacdadan ayaa ka dhacday waqooyiga Gaza, iyadoo milatariga Israa’iil uu sheegay in baaritaan lagu sameynayo sababta keentay in drone-ku uu qarxo. Dhacdadan ayaa sidoo kale dhalisay walaac la xiriira badqabka diyaaradaha yaryar ee aan duuliyaha lahayn ee ay ciidamada Israa’iil u adeegsadaan hawlgallada milatari. Sababo la xiriira dhacdadan, milatariga Israa’iil ayaa si ku-meel-gaar ah u hakiyay duullimaadyada dhammaan diyaaradaha yaryar ee aan duuliyaha lahayn ee sida walxaha qarxa, iyadoo tallaabadan la sheegay inay dhaqan-geli doonto inta lagu guda jiro baaritaanka. Joojinta ayaa sii socon doonta inta milatarigu qiimeynayo khataraha ka dhalan kara adeegsiga diyaaradaha noocaas ah iyo tallaabooyinka loo baahan yahay si looga hortago in dhacdo la mid ah ay mar kale dhacdo. Sida lagu sheegay warbixinta milatariga, drone-ka ayaa qarxay daqiiqado kadib markii askartu ay soo qaadeen, taas oo sababtay dhimashada labada askari. Dhacdadan ayaa ka dhacday waqooyiga Gaza, iyadoo milatariga Israa’iil uu sheegay in baaritaan lagu sameynayo sababta keentay in drone-ku uu qarxo. Dhacdadan ayaa sidoo kale dhalisay walaac la xiriira badqabka diyaaradaha yaryar ee aan duuliyaha lahayn ee ay ciidamada Israa’iil u adeegsadaan hawlgallada milatari. Sababo la xiriira dhacdadan, milatariga Israa’iil ayaa si ku-meel-gaar ah u hakiyay duullimaadyada dhammaan diyaaradaha yaryar ee aan duuliyaha lahayn ee sida walxaha qarxa, iyadoo tallaabadan la sheegay inay dhaqan-geli doonto inta lagu guda jiro baaritaanka. Joojinta ayaa sii socon doonta inta milatarigu qiimeynayo khataraha ka dhalan kara adeegsiga diyaaradaha noocaas ah iyo tallaabooyinka loo baahan yahay si looga hortago in dhacdo la mid ah ay mar kale dhacdo. items.title: DF Soomaaliya iyo WFP oo gaaray heshiis cusub oo ku saabsan…
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Guddoomiyaha Hay’adda Maareynta Musiibooyinka Soomaaliyeed (SoDMA), Maxamuud Macallin Cabdulle iyo Madaxa Hay’adda Cunnada Adduunka ee Qaramada Midoobay (WFP) Soomaaliya, Hameed Nuru ayaa kala saxiixday heshiis cusub oo iskaashi. Heshiiska ayaa qeexaya qaabka ay SoDMA iyo WFP uga wada shaqeyn doonaan arrimaha la xiriira maareynta musiibooyinka iyo gurmadka bani’aadannimo labada sano ee soo socota. Wada-shaqeynta labada dhinac ayaa diiradda lagu saaray xoojinta awoodda Soomaaliya ee saadaalinta khataraha iyo diyaar-garowga xaaladaha musiibooyinka. Sidoo kale, heshiiska ayaa lagu xoojinayaa nidaamyada digniinta hore iyo tallaabada hore, si loo suurageliyo in si degdeg ah looga jawaabo xaaladaha degdegga ah ee dalka ka dhaca. Labada hay’adood ayaa sidoo kale ka wada shaqeyn doona sidii loo heli lahaa gurmad bani’aadannimo oo wax-ku-ool ah, gaar ahaan xilliyada ay bulshada Soomaaliyeed la kulmaan xaalado degdeg ah iyo musiibooyin. Heshiiska ayaa sidoo kale taageeraya xoojinta nidaamka maareynta khataraha musiibooyinka, sugnaanta cunnada, taageerada bani’aadannimada iyo kobcinta awoodda bulshada. Ujeeddada wada-shaqeyntan ayaa ah in la yareeyo saameynta ay musiibooyinku ku yeeshaan bulshada, lana ilaaliyo nolosha iyo nolol-maalmeedka dadka Soomaaliyeed, iyadoo la xoojinayo awoodda dalka ee ka hortagga iyo wax-ka-qabashada musiibooyinka. The post DF Soomaaliya iyo WFP oo gaaray heshiis cusub oo ku saabsan… appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Cumar Cabdirisaaq oo soo hadlay, sheegayna in aan laga eryin Isbaheysiga ee…
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Cumar Cabdirisaaq Xuseen oo xalay Guddoomiyaha Isbaheysiga Xaqsoor iyo Haybad Qaran, Danjire Cabdiraxmaan Caynte uu sheegay inuu ka qaaday xilkii Xoghayaha Guud ee Isbaheysiga ayaa sheegay in aan laga eryin Isbaheysiga ee uu is-casilay. Cumar ayaa qoraal uu soo saaray ku sheegay inuu si ikhtiyaari ah iskaga casilay xilkii Xoghayaha Guud ee Isbaheysiga Arbacadii oo ay taariikhdu aheyd 23 September 2026. Sidoo kale waxa uu sheegay in is-casilaadiisu timid kaddib markii uu diiday jihada maamulka iyo siyaasadda ee Isbaheysiga Xaqsoor iyo Haybad Qaran uu qaatay. “Go’aankaygu wuxuu ku salaysan yahay: In Isbaheysiga siyaasadeed loo weeciyay hannaan NGO, taas oo ka fog jihadii iyo ujeeddadii loo aas-aasay. Arrintii ugu dambeysay waxay ahayd in kulan siyaasadeed loo beddelo bandhig warbixin sannadeedka Heritage, taas oo aan si cad uga biyo diiday,” ayuu yiri. Cumar ayaa hoggaanka Isbaheysiga ku eedeeyay in uu gudan waayay waajibaadkiisa iyo mas’uuliyad aan si hufan looga warqabin xaaladda gudaha ee Isbaheysiga. “Isbaheysi siyaasadeed ma aha mashruuc shaqsiyeed, NGO ama madal dano gaar ah lagu maamulo. Waa inuu yeeshaa jiho siyaasadeed oo cad, hoggaan masuul ah iyo hannaan isla xisaabtan oo hufan.” Hoos ka aqriso qoraalka oo dhameystiran: Bismillaahi Raxmaani Raxiim, Mahad oo dhan Alle ayay u sugnaatay. Waxaan si cad u xaqiijinayaa in aan si ikhtiyaari ah iskaga casilay xilkii Xoghayaha Guud ee Isbaheysiga, Arbacadii oo ay taariikhdu aheyd 23 September 2026 kaddib markii aan diiday jihada maamulka iyo siyaasadda ee Isbaheysigu qaatay. Go’aankaygu wuxuu ku salaysan yahay: In Isbaheysiga siyaasadeed loo weeciyay hannaan NGO, taas oo ka fog jihadii iyo ujeeddadii loo aas-aasay. Arrintii ugu dambeysay waxay ahayd in kulan siyaasadeed loo beddelo bandhig warbixin sannadeedka Heritage, taas oo aan si cad uga biyo diiday. Faragelin iyo khilaafaad gudaha ah, oo ay ku jiraan kala aragti duwanaansho aan la yeeshay qaar ka mid ah masuuliyiinta. Hoggaan siyaasadeed oo aan gudan waajibaadkiisa, iyo masuuliyad aan si hufan looga warqabin xaaladda gudaha ee Isbaheysiga. Hannaanka warbixinta iyo maamulka oo aan u arkay in uu dhaawacayo madax-bannaanida xubnaha iyo isla xisaabtanka siyaasadeed. Isbaheysi siyaasadeed ma aha mashruuc shaqsiyeed, NGO ama madal dano gaar ah lagu maamulo. Waa inuu yeeshaa jiho siyaasadeed oo cad, hoggaan masuul ah iyo hannaan isla xisaabtan oo hufan. Gabagabadii, waxaan xaqiijinayaa in aan si madax-bannaan uga baxay Isbaheysiga ka dib xaaladihii aan u arkayay in ay ka hor imaanayaan mabaadi’dayda iyo himiladayda siyaasadeed. Waxaan doorbidayaa in aan ilaashado sharaftayda, mabda’ayga iyo aragtideyda siyaasadeed. items.title: Magaalooyin waa weyn oo la shaaciyey in ay u gacan geli karaan kooxda Al-Shabaab
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) — Soomaaliya waxay wajihi kartaa inay Al-Shabaab dib ugu lumiso deegaanno ay dowladdu maamusho, xilli ciidamada Midowga Afrika ay isu diyaarinayaan inay yareeyaan joogitaankooda, taageerada saadka ee Qaramada Midoobayna ay sii dhammaaneyso, waxaa sidaas ka digtay hay’adda International Crisis Group. Hay’adda ayaa si gaar ah farta ugu fiiqday magaalooyinka Qoryooley ee gobolka Shabeellaha Hoose iyo Jalalaqsi ee Hiiraan, kuwaas oo ay sheegtay inay halis weyn wajihi karaan haddii ciidamada shisheeye ay ka baxaan iyadoo aan la helin ciidamo Soomaali ah oo awood u leh inay boosaskooda la wareegaan. Qoryooley ayaa ka mid ah magaalooyinka ay hareeraha kaga sugan yihiin Al-Shabaab, iyadoo Crisis Group ay sheegtay inay “halis ugu jirto inay gacanta u gasho fallaagada” marka ciidamada Midowga Afrika ay ka baxaan. Jalalaqsi ayaa iyaduna wajahaysa cadaadis sii kordhaya, kadib markii Al-Shabaab ay tan iyo 2025 ciidamo badan ku uruurisay qeybo ka mid ah Hirshabelle, gaar ahaan agagaarka waddooyinka muhiimka ah. Crisis Group waxay ka digtay in xitaa luminta deegaanno kooban ay Al-Shabaab siin karto dardar cusub, halka qabsashada waddooyinka iyo xarumaha dhaqaale ay kooxda u abuuri karto ilo dhaqaale oo dheeraad ah. Isbeddel weyn oo amni Digniintan ayaa kusoo aadeysa xilli Soomaaliya iyo saaxiibadeeda caalamka ay isku diyaarinayaan isbeddel weyn oo ku yimaada nidaamka amni ee dalka taageerayay ku dhowaad labaatan sano. Mareykanka ayaa bishan ogolaaday in taageerada Xafiiska Qaramada Midoobay ee Soomaaliya ee UNSOS la sii wado 12 bilood oo dheeraad ah, halkii si toos ah loo joojin lahaa dhammaadka December 2026. UNSOS ayaa ciidamada AUSSOM siisa adeegyo muhiim ah oo ay ka mid yihiin cunto, biyo, shidaal, gaadiid iyo adeegyo kale oo saadka ah, kuwaas oo u suurtageliya ciidamada Midowga Afrika inay joogaan tobannaan saldhig oo ku yaalla koonfurta iyo bartamaha Soomaaliya. Crisis Group waxay sheegtay in AUSSOM ay aad ugu adkaan doonto inay qaabkeeda hadda ku sii shaqeyso haddii taageeradaas meesha ka baxdo. Uganda ayaa, tusaale ahaan, in ka badan toban saldhig ku leh Shabeellaha Hoose, kuwaas oo hay’addu sheegtay inay adkaan karto in la sii hayo marka taageerada saadka ee Qaramada Midoobay dhammaato. Hay’addu ma saadaalineyso burbur ku yimaada dowladda federaalka ama in Al-Shabaab ay la wareegto magaalooyinka waaweyn, balse waxay sheegtay in dib-u-gurasho kooban oo laga sameeyo qaar ka mid ah goobaha hadda ay joogaan ciidamada AU-da ay u muuqato mid ay adag tahay in laga fogaado. Ciidamo laba-geesood ah Crisis Group waxay sheegtay in nidaamka amni ee soo socda uu si weyn ugu tiirsanaan karo heshiisyada tooska ah ee Soomaaliya la leedahay dalalka Uganda, Kenya iyo Itoobiya. Dalalkan ayaa sii haysan kara ciidamo gudaha Soomaaliya jooga xitaa haddii howlgalka AUSSOM la dhimo ama mustaqbalka la soo afjaro. Kenya iyo Itoobiya ayaa la filayaa inay xoogga saaraan deegaannada u dhow xuduudahooda, halka Uganda ay mudnaan siin karto Muqdisho iyo hareeraheeda. Türkiye ayaa sidoo kale door weyn ku sii yeelan doonta tababarka iyo taageerada ciidamada Soomaaliya, halka Mareykanka uu sii wadi karo howlgallada ka dhanka ah argagixisada, gaar ahaan taageerada dhinaca cirka. Crisis Group waxay sheegtay in iskaashiyadan laba-geesoodka ahi ay yihiin beddelka ugu macquulsan muddada dhow, balse waxay ku baaqday in la sameeyo hannaan joogto ah oo lagu kala caddeeyo cidda ilaalineysa magaalooyinka, waddooyinka waaweyn iyo goobaha istiraatiijiga ah. Dhulka la haysto ha la difaaco Hay’addu waxay sidoo kale dowladda Soomaaliya kula talisay inay mudnaanta siiso difaaca deegaannada ay hadda maamusho, halkii ay xilligan bilaabi lahayd howlgallo cusub oo ballaaran oo ka dhan ah Al-Shabaab. Dowladda Soomaaliya ayaa bishii August sheegtay inay haysato ku dhowaad 14,000 oo askari oo diyaar u ah howlgallo militari. Crisis Group waxay soo jeedisay in qaar ka mid ah ciidamadaas lagu beddelo ciidamada AU-da ee ka baxaya saldhigyada muhiimka ah. Hase yeeshee, waxay ka digtay in ciidamada Soomaaliya guud ahaan aysan haysan qalab iyo taageero la mid ah kuwa ciidamada Midowga Afrika, taas oo beddel toos ah ka dhigaysa mid khatar badan. Qaar ka mid ah goobihii horay ciidamada AU-da loogu wareejiyay ciidamada Soomaaliya ayaa dib ugu dhacay gacanta Al-Shabaab, halka howlgallada ciidamada dowladda ay weli si weyn ugu tiirsan yihiin sirdoon, diyaarado, gaadiid iyo saad ay bixiyaan saaxiibada caalamka. Crisis Group waxay sidoo kale sheegtay in khilaafaadka siyaasadeed ee u dhexeeya dowladda federaalka iyo maamulada Puntland iyo Jubaland ay caqabad ku noqdeen dhismaha nidaam amni oo mideysan. Waxay ugu baaqday madaxda Soomaalida inay xalliyaan khilaafaadka doorashooyinka, isla markaana maamul-goboleedyada lagu daro qorsheynta nidaamka amni ee beddeli doona kan hadda jira. Hay’addu waxay ka digtay in haddii waqtiga dheeraadka ah ee la helay aan si wanaagsan looga faa’iideysan, meelaha ay ka baxaan ciidamada shisheeye ay abuuri karaan firaaq amni oo Al-Shabaab ay ka faa’iideysato. Dhulka la haysto ha la difaaco Hay’addu waxay sidoo kale dowladda Soomaaliya kula talisay inay mudnaanta siiso difaaca deegaannada ay hadda maamusho, halkii ay xilligan bilaabi lahayd howlgallo cusub oo ballaaran oo ka dhan ah Al-Shabaab. Dowladda Soomaaliya ayaa bishii August sheegtay inay haysato ku dhowaad 14,000 oo askari oo diyaar u ah howlgallo militari. Crisis Group waxay soo jeedisay in qaar ka mid ah ciidamadaas lagu beddelo ciidamada AU-da ee ka baxaya saldhigyada muhiimka ah. Hase yeeshee, waxay ka digtay in ciidamada Soomaaliya guud ahaan aysan haysan qalab iyo taageero la mid ah kuwa ciidamada Midowga Afrika, taas oo beddel toos ah ka dhigaysa mid khatar badan. Qaar ka mid ah goobihii horay ciidamada AU-da loogu wareejiyay ciidamada Soomaaliya ayaa dib ugu dhacay gacanta Al-Shabaab, halka howlgallada ciidamada dowladda ay weli si weyn ugu tiirsan yihiin sirdoon, diyaarado, gaadiid iyo saad ay bixiyaan saaxiibada caalamka. Crisis Group waxay sidoo kale sheegtay in khilaafaadka siyaasadeed ee u dhexeeya dowladda federaalka iyo maamulada Puntland iyo Jubaland ay caqabad ku noqdeen dhismaha nidaam amni oo mideysan. Waxay ugu baaqday madaxda Soomaalida inay xalliyaan khilaafaadka doorashooyinka, isla markaana maamul-goboleedyada lagu daro qorsheynta nidaamka amni ee beddeli doona kan hadda jira. Hay’addu waxay ka digtay in haddii waqtiga dheeraadka ah ee la helay aan si wanaagsan looga faa’iideysan, meelaha ay ka baxaan ciidamada shisheeye ay abuuri karaan firaaq amni oo Al-Shabaab ay ka faa’iideysato. items.title: Somalia president pledges democracy at UN amid term extension row
items.description: MOGADISHU (Somaliguardian) – Somalia’s President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud said on Thursday his government was laying the foundations of universal suffrage, addressing the United Nations General Assembly as opposition leaders at home said he had left unresolved a dispute over his term extension and changes to the constitution. Mohamud, speaking at the 81st session of the General Assembly in New York, said Somalia was moving toward a multi-party democracy and away from the clan-based power-sharing system that has underpinned its politics for decades. “Through constitutional reform, we’re laying the foundations of universal suffrage, accountable institutions and a multi-party system that allows every Somali citizen to have a voice. Our aim is to become an effective democracy where differences are resolved through dialogue, law and elections, not violence,” president Mohamud said. He added that the United Nations and international partners should support the transition “while respecting Somali ownership of Somali democracy.” Opposition Faults Timing Former President Mohamed Abdullahi Farmajo and other opposition leaders said Mohamud should have resolved Somalia’s political crisis before traveling to New York. Farmajo has accused Mohamud for months of pushing through constitutional changes without consensus and of using a planned shift to one-person-one-vote elections to extend his own time in office. The dispute dates to March 2026, when parliament passed, and Mohamud signed, amendments extending presidential and parliamentary terms to five years from four and pushing national elections back to 2027. Opposition figures, including Farmajo, former President Sharif Sheikh Ahmed, several former prime ministers, and the Puntland and Jubaland state administrations, said the vote fell short of the consensus required for constitutional change and that some opposition lawmakers were barred from the session. Mohamud’s original mandate expired on May 15, 2026. The government declared what it called a “transition period” after no agreement was reached with the opposition by that date. The standoff has at times turned violent, with clashes reported in Mogadishu and federal forces entering Baidoa amid a related crisis in Southwest State. The political crisis has coincided with strain on Somalia’s security partnerships. The African Union’s stabilization mission in the country has faced a funding shortfall this year, and Ethiopian troops withdrew from the town of Burhakaba, developments that have added to international concern about Somalia’s stability. Wider UN Address Mohamud also called for reform of the UN Security Council, saying Africa’s absence from permanent membership was “a historical injustice” affecting 54 countries. He reaffirmed Somalia’s support for Palestinian statehood along 1967 borders and said instability in the Strait of Hormuz had driven up fuel and food prices at home, adding to economic pressure that has cut customs revenue and pushed up inflation this year. The government has cast the UN appearance as a chance to secure continued international support for Somalia’s institutions. Opposition figures say that support means little without an agreed, consensus-based path to elections at home. Contact us: info@somaliguardian.com

items.title: Itoobiya, Jabuuti iyo Dangote oo dhisaya dhuun shidaal oo $660 milyan ah
items.description: Itoobiya, Jabuuti iyo shirkadda Dangote Group ee uu leeyahay ganacsadaha reer Nigeria Aliko Dangote ayaa qorsheynaya in ay si wadajir ah u dhisaan dhuun shidaal oo qiimaheedu gaarayo 660 milyan oo doollar, taas oo isku xiri doonta labada dal, iyadoo mashruucan lagu doonayo in lagu xoojiyo sahayda shidaalka, lana yareeyo kharashaadka iyo dib-u-dhacyada ka dhasha gaadiidka shidaalka ee mara marinka ganacsi ee Itoobiya iyo Jabuuti. Sida ay sheegtay Reuters, mashruuca ayaa ka koobnaan doona dhuun dhererkeedu yahay ku dhowaad 120 kiiloomitir, taas oo qaadi doonta shidaalka la sifeeyey ee u kala gudbaya Jabuuti iyo Itoobiya. Waxaa sidoo kale la dhisi doonaa xarumo waaweyn oo lagu kaydiyo shidaalka. Jabuuti, gaar ahaan deegaanka Damerjog, waxaa laga qorsheeyay xarun kaydin oo qaadi karta ku dhowaad 375,000 mitir kuyuubik oo shidaal ah, halka Dewele ee Itoobiya laga dhisayo xarun kale oo awooddeedu gaareyso 800,000 mitir kuyuubik. Mas’uul ka tirsan xafiiska Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Itoobiya Abiy Ahmed ayaa sheegay in mashruucan la filayo in uu shaqo bilaabo muddo ku dhow 18 bilood gudahood. Abiy Ahmed ayaa sheegay in mashruuca ay iska kaashanayaan Ethiopian Investment Holdings iyo Dangote Group, isaga oo tilmaamay in ujeeddada ugu weyn ay tahay in la yareeyo kharashaadka saadka iyo dib-u-dhacyada ka dhasha gaadiidka shidaalka ee u dhexeeya Itoobiya iyo Jabuuti. Itoobiya oo aan lahayn xeeb ayaa si weyn ugu tiirsan Jabuuti, gaar ahaan dekedaha dalkaas, si ay u hesho badeecooyin muhiim ah oo dibadda laga keeno. Shidaalka ayaa ka mid ah badeecooyinka ugu muhiimsan ee mara marinka Itoobiya iyo Jabuuti, sidaas darteed dhuun shidaal oo si toos ah labada dal u xiriirisa ayaa wax ka beddeli karta habka shidaalka loogu gudbiyo gudaha Itoobiya. Dowladaha labada dal ayaa sidoo kale aaminsan in kaabayaasha cusub ay xoojin karaan ammaanka tamarta, isla markaana ay sare u qaadi karaan adkeysiga silsiladda sahayda. Haddii mashruucu hirgalo, waxaa la filayaa in qayb ka mid ah gaadiidka shidaalka ee hadda ku tiirsan gaadiidka waddooyinka loo wareejiyo dhuunta, taas oo yareyn karta kharashaadka iyo waqtiga loo baahan yahay in shidaalka lagu gaarsiiyo suuqyada Itoobiya. Mashruucan ayaa sidoo kale muujinaya sida uu Dangote Group u sii ballaarinayo maalgashigiisa Bariga Afrika, ayadoo Shirkadda ay horey Itoobiya uga wadday mashaariic kale oo waaweyn oo ku kacaya qiyaastii 4 bilyan oo doollar, kuwaas oo ay ka mid yihiin dhuun loogu talagalay warshad bacrimin ah, xarun koronto iyo xarun soo saarta baakadaha polypropylene. Dhanka Kenya, Dangote iyo dowladda dalkaas ayaa sidoo kale lagu wadaa in ay toddobaadka soo socda dhagax-dhigaan mashruuc cusub oo ah warshad sifeysa saliidda ceyriinka ah, taas oo la qorsheeyay in laga dhiso Lamu, iyadoo awooddeedu noqon doonto 700,000 foosto maalintii. Ra’iisul Wasaare Abiy Ahmed ayaa ku dhawaaqay mashruuca dhuunta shidaalka xilli uu booqasho ku joogay Jabuuti, waxaana uu arrinta kala hadlay Madaxweynaha Jabuuti Ismaaciil Cumar Geelle iyo Aliko Dangote. Mashruuca ayaa haddii uu hirgalo noqon kara mid muhiim u ah xiriirka dhaqaale iyo ganacsi ee Itoobiya iyo Jabuuti, gaar ahaan dhinaca tamarta, iyadoo Jabuuti ay sii xoojinayso doorkeeda ah marinka ugu muhiimsan ee Itoobiya u adeegsato ganacsiga iyo soo dejinta badeecooyinka. Dhuuntan shidaalka ee 660-ka milyan ee doollar ah ayaa sidaas darteed noqonaysa mashruuc isku keenaya danaha saddex dhinac: Itoobiya oo raadineysa sahay shidaal oo la isku halleyn karo iyo kharashyo gaadiid oo hooseeya, Jabuuti oo doonaysa in ay sii xoojiso doorkeeda kaabayaasha iyo ganacsiga gobolka, iyo Dangote Group oo sii ballaarinaysa maalgashigeeda dhinacyada tamarta iyo warshadaha Afrika.

items.title: Muxuu wasiirkii arrimaha dibedda Maxamed C/risaaq ka yiri warqadda Puntland
items.description: Waxaan akhriyey warqaddii Madaxweyne Deni uu u diray Xoghayaha Guud ee Qaramada Midoobay iyo Golaha Ammaanka. Qeybo qoraalka ka mid ah aad bay ii dhibeen—taas macnaheedu ma aha in cabashooyinka Puntland aysan ahayn kuwo jira, balse Deni wuxuu sheeganayaa wax ka baxsan awoodihiisa iyo waajibaadkiisa. Qoraalkiisa wuxuu leeyahay – “Puntland waxay hadda wajahaysaa cadaadis kaga imanaya shacab aad u tiro badan oo doonaya inay si buuxda uga go’aan Soomaaliya.” Meeday caddaynta? Afti miyaa la qaaday? La-tashi dadweyne miyaa dhacay? Afkaarta dadka miyaa la ururiyay? Halkuu mandate-ka ka haystaa? Waxaa kale oo uu leeyahay: “Puntland waxay ugu dambayn ka fiirsan kartaa inay si joogto ah xiriirka uga jarto Muqdisho.” Yaa Deni u siiyey awooddaas uu Puntland kaga jarayo dalka? Puntland ma aha Deni, Deni-na ma aha Puntland. Sannadkii 1998-kii, shacabka Puntland waxay shirkii dastuuriga ahaa ee Garoowe si ku talogal ah ugu go’aansadeen inay qayb ka ahaadaan Soomaaliya ku dhisan nidaam federaal ah. Taariikhdaas hal hoggaamiye siyaasadeed maanta iskama beddeli karo. Tankale, Deni ma iska baxshay galoofisyadii dagaalka oo ma ka tanaasulay hammigiisii ahaa inuu noqdo Madaxweynaha ama Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Soomaaliya? Waayo, warqaddiisu waxay u muuqataa inay leedahay: “ Hadaanan helin heshiiska siyaasadeed ee aan doonayo, Puntland way ka go’aysaa Soomaaliya. ” Taasi waxay ka dhigan tahay ninkii yiri: “Cadyahow ku cunay ama ku ciideeyay.” Maya, taas lagaa diid. Mahadsanid. Waa run, Xasan Sheekh wuxuu galay xadgudubyo culus oo dastuuri ah iyo kuwo siyaasadeedba. Muddadii dastuuriga ahayd ee xil-heyntiisu wey dhammaatay. Xukuumaddiisu waxay awood ciidan u adeegsatay Jubaland iyo Koonfur Galbeed, waxaana ku dhintay dhalinyaro Soomaaliyeed. Kumannaan qof ayaa guryahooda laga barakiciyey, hay’adihii dowladdana waa la wiiqay, musuqmaasuqa iyo eexduna waxay gaareen heerkii ugu darnaa. Cabashooyinkaas ma aha kuwo u gaar ah hal qabiil, hal gobol ama hal dhinac siyaasadeed. Soomaali inteeda badan oo ka kala socota dalka oo dhan—oo ay ku jiraan reer Puntland—iyo qurbo-joogtu way wada qabaan aragtidaas. Haddaba maxaad Xasan Sheekh u siinaysaa meel uu ka baxsado, adigoo leh Puntland waxay ka go’i kartaa Soomaaliya? Maxaad u oggolaanaysaa inuu doodda ka leexiyo xadgudubyadiisa dastuuriga ah, oo uu u beddelo dood ku saabsan difaaca midnimada iyo wadajirka dhuleed ee Soomaaliya? Maxaad u oggolaanaysaa inuu u muuqdo mid ka macquulsan dadka siyaasadda kaga soo horjeeda, arrin ay ahayd inaan dhammaanteen ka mideysnaano? Maxaad ugu oggolaanaysaa inuu caalamka ugu muuqdo qof ka macquulsan mucaaradkiisa marka ay noqoto midnimada Soomaaliya? Kulama dagaalami karo shakhsi inuu ku-takri-fallay awood, anagoo isla markaana u ogolaanayna inuu midkale sheegto magac iyo awood shacbi uusan ogolaasho u haysan. Soomaaliya waxaa leh dhammaan dadka Soomaaliyeed oo dhan, Puntland-na dadkeeda. Ma jiri karo hoggaamiye siyaasadeed oo xaq u leh inuu magaca Soomaaliya ama Puntland iyo midnimada iyo wadajirka dhuleed ee Soomaaliya ku bedesho dano gaar ah, ama uu iska sameysto awood uu ku sheegto in dadku doonayaan gooni-isu-taag. Waxaa qoray Maxamed Cabdirisaaq, wasiirkii hore ee arrimaha dibedda Soomaaliya oo reer Puntland ah. Ma jiri karo hoggaamiye siyaasadeed oo xaq u leh inuu magaca Soomaaliya ama Puntland iyo midnimada iyo wadajirka dhuleed ee Soomaaliya ku bedesho dano gaar ah, ama uu iska sameysto awood uu ku sheegto in dadku doonayaan gooni-isu-taag. Waxaa qoray Maxamed Cabdirisaaq, wasiirkii hore ee arrimaha dibedda Soomaaliya oo reer Puntland ah. items.title: Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya oo Qaramada Midoobay ka dalbaday xabbad-joojin degdeg ah oo Gaza ka dhaqan-gasha
items.description: Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud ayaa Qaramada Midoobay ka jeediyay baaq ku aaddan in si degdeg ah oo waarta loo joojiyo colaadda Gaza, iyadoo sidoo kale loo oggolaado in gargaarka bani’aadannimo uu si aan xannibaad lahayn u gaaro shacabka Falastiiniyiinta. Khudbaddiisa uu ka jeediyay Golaha Guud ee Qaramada Midoobay, Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya wuxuu sheegay in rabshadaha, barakaca iyo xaaladda bani’aadannimo ee ka jirta dhulka Falastiiniyiinta, gaar ahaan Gaza, ay u baahan yihiin tallaabo degdeg ah oo caalami ah. Wuxuu ku celiyay baaqa Soomaaliya ee ku aaddan xabbad-joojin degdeg ah oo waarta , iyo in la fududeeyo gaarsiinta gargaarka bani’aadannimo dadka u baahan. Madaxweynaha ayaa sidoo kale carrabka ku adkeeyay muhiimadda ay leedahay  in dib loogu laabto dadaallada siyaasadeed ee lagu doonayo in lagu gaaro xalka labada dowladood , isaga oo ku tilmaamay waddada keliya ee lagu gaari karo nabad caddaalad ah oo waarta oo ka dhalata Bariga Dhexe. Mawqifkan ayaa sidoo kale ka mid ahaa hadalkii Xasan Sheekh ee Golaha Guud ee Qaramada Midoobay, kaas oo lagu sheegay in Soomaaliya ay si qoto dheer uga walaacsan tahay dhibaatada shacabka Falastiiniyiinta. Baaqan ayaa ku soo beegmaya xilli xaaladda Gaza iyo arrinta Falastiin ay ka mid yihiin qodobada ugu waaweyn ee looga hadlayo kalfadhiga 81-aad ee Golaha Guud ee Qaramada Midoobay. Qaramada Midoobay ayaa iyaduna si gaar ah u adkaysay muhiimadda xalka labada dowladood, iyadoo Xoghayaha Guud António Guterres uu sheegay in xal waara uu ku salaysnaado dowlad Falastiini ah oo madax-bannaan iyo Israel oo si nabad iyo amni ah u wada nool. Mowqifka Soomaaliya wuxuu sidoo kale la jaanqaadayaa siyaasadda ay Muqdisho muddo dheer ka taagnayd arrinta Falastiin, iyadoo Soomaaliya ay taageerto xaqa shacabka Falastiiniyiinta u leeyihiin dowlad madax-bannaan iyo xal siyaasadeed oo ku dhisan xeerarka iyo qawaaniinta caalamiga ah. Khudbadda Madaxweynaha ayaa muujisay in Soomaaliya ay doonayso in dadaallada caalamiga ah lagu saleeyo joojinta colaadda, ilaalinta shacabka, gaarsiinta gargaarka bani’aadannimo iyo dib u soo nooleynta geeddi-socod siyaasadeed oo horseeda xal waara oo u dhexeeya Falastiin iyo Israa’iil.

items.title: Safiirka cusub ee Turkiga ee Soomaaliya oo soo saaray farriin culus kadib markii uu…
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Danjiraha cusub ee Turkiga u fadhiya Soomaaliya, Ferhat Alkan, oo soo gaaray Muqdisho, ayaa sheegay in Ankara ay sii wadi doonto taageerada ay siiso Soomaaliya, gaar ahaan dhinacyada amniga, horumarinta iyo xoojinta awoodda hay’adaha dowladda. Alkan ayaa hadalkan ku sheegay farriintiisii ugu horreysay ee uu u diray shacabka Soomaaliyeed kaddib markii uu si rasmi ah u bilaabay shaqadiisa safiirnimo ee Muqdisho. Waxa uu sheegay inuu sharaf iyo farxad weyn u yahay inuu xilka la wareego xilli Soomaaliya iyo Turkiga ay xusayaan 60 sano oo ka soo wareegtay markii ay labada dal yeesheen xiriir diblomaasiyadeed. Xilligan ayaa sidoo kale ku beegan 15 sano guuradii ka soo wareegtay booqashadii taariikhiga ahayd ee madaxweynaha Turkiga Recep Tayyip Erdoğan uu ku yimid Soomaaliya sanadkii 2011, xilli uu ahaa ra’iisul wasaare. “Waxaan sharaf iyo farxad weyn u arkaa inaan xilka safiirka Jamhuuriyadda Turkiga ee Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya bilaabo xilligan muhiimka ah,” ayuu yiri Alkan. Danjiraha ayaa sidoo kale sheegay inuu shalay Muqdisho kula kulmay dhalinyaro Soomaaliyeed goob lagu qaxweeyo, isaga oo kala hadlay xaaladda dalka iyo aragtidooda ku saabsan isbeddellada ka jira caasimadda. Sida uu sheegay Alkan, dhalinyarada uu la kulmay ayaa muujiyey inay ku faraxsan yihiin xaaladda amni iyo degganaansho ee sanadihii ugu dambeeyey laga dareemayey Muqdisho iyo nawaaxigeeda. Waxa uu intaas ku daray in Turkigu uu si buuxda u taageerayo dadaallada Soomaaliya ee lagu xoojinayo amniga, horumarka iyo awoodda hay’adaha dowladda. Alkan ayaa sheegay in Ankara ay doonayso in xiriirka labada dal lagu sii horumariyo ixtiraam, kalsooni iyo dano wadajir ah, iyadoo mudnaanta la siinayo horumarka iyo danta labada shacab. “Ujeeddadeenna ugu weyn waa inaan xiriirka Turkiga iyo Soomaaliya sii gaarsiino heer sare, annagoo ku dhiseyna ixtiraam, kalsooni iyo dano wadajir ah,” ayuu yiri. Waxa uu sidoo kale sheegay in safaaradda Turkiga ee Muqdisho ay diyaar u tahay inay dhageysato fikradaha iyo talooyinka muwaadiniinta Turkiga iyo shacabka Soomaaliyeed. “Albaabada safaaraddeennu mar walba way idiin furnaan doonaan,” ayuu yiri. Ferhat Alkan ayaa xilka kala wareegay Alper Aktaş, iyadoo xiriirka Soomaaliya iyo Turkiga uu sanadihii la soo dhaafay si weyn ugu fiday dhinacyada amniga, tababarka ciidamada, horumarinta, gargaarka bani’aadannimo, ganacsiga iyo iskaashiga istiraatiijiga ah. items.title: Ugu yaraan 41 qof oo ku dhintay doon ku degtay harada Tanganyika ee dalka DRC Congo
items.description: Ugu yaraan 41 qof ayaa ku dhintay, halka 49 kalena la soo badbaadiyey, kaddib markii doon ay saarnaayeen ku dhowaad 100 qof oo rakaab iyo xamuul ah ay ku rogmatay harada Tanganyika ee Jamhuuriyadda Dimuqraadiga ah ee Congo (DRC). Doontan ayaa ka ambabaxday dekedda Kigoma ee dalka Tanzania, iyadoo ku sii jeedday magaalada Kalemie ee DRC, waxaana ay ku degtay meel u dhow tuulada Mapera habeenkii Khamiista. Mas’uuliyiinta gobolka Tanganyika ayaa sheegay in hawlgallada baadigoobka iyo samatabbixinta ay weli socdaan, iyadoo kooxaha gurmadku ay raadinayaan rakaab kale oo laga yaabo inay ku jireen doonta markii ay rogmatay. Ilaa hadda lama xaqiijin tirada saxda ah ee dadka la la’yahay, sidaas darteed waxaa suuragal ah in tirada dhimashada ay isbeddesho marka hawlgallada gurmadku sii socdaan. Mid ka mid ah dadka ka badbaaday shilkan, Annie Moyoni, ayaa Radio Okapi u sheegtay in rakaabka laga kiciyey hurdada abbaaraha 1:00 habeenimo, kaddib markii ay ogaadeen in doontu hal dhinac u janjeertay. Shilkan ayaa mar kale soo bandhigay khatarta ka jirta gaadiidka biyaha ee Jamhuuriyadda Dimuqraadiga ah ee Congo, halkaas oo doonyuhu ay door muhiim ah ka ciyaaraan isku socodka dadka iyo badeecadaha. Dad badan oo ku nool dalka ayaa doonyaha u isticmaala safarrada maadaama ay yihiin habka ugu jaban ee gaadiid, gaar ahaan meelaha ay ka liitaan waddooyinka iyo kaabayaasha kale ee gaadiidka. doonyaha qaarkood ayaa la sheegay inay qaadaan rakaab iyo xamuul ka badan awooddooda, iyadoo qalabka badbaadada sida jaakadaha dabaasha aanu mar walba ku filnayn dadka saaran. Musiibadan ayaa sidoo kale dhacday xilli wax ka yar hal bil uu ka soo wareegay shil kale oo ka dhacay isla marinka Kigoma iyo Kalemie, waxaana 28-kii Agoosto, markabka MV Pacifique uu dab qabsaday kadibna ku qarxay dekedda Kigoma xilli shidaal lagu shubayey. Sida uu sheegay Radio Okapi, lix shaqaale ah ayaa ku dhintay dhacdadaas, halka qof toddobaad ahna la sheegay inuu weli maqan yahay. Sidoo kale, bishii Luulyo, ugu yaraan 20 qof ayaa ku dhintay bartamaha DRC kaddib markii doon alwaax ah oo ay saarnaayeen arday ka soo laabanayey imtixaannada dowladda ay degtay. Dhacdooyinkan isdaba jooga ah ayaa sare u qaaday walaaca laga qabo badbaadada gaadiidka biyaha ee dalka. Harada Tanganyika, oo ah mid ka mid ah harooyinka waaweyn ee Afrika, waxay muhiim u tahay isku socodka iyo ganacsiga dadka ku nool gobollada ku hareeraysan.

items.title: Somalia reaffirms support for Palestinian statehood at UN General Assembly
items.description: Somalia called for a resolution to the plight of the Palestinian people on Thursday, while saying the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz poses a threat not only to itself but the rest of the region. Speaking at the UN General Assembly in New York, Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud warned that the world faces uncertainty amid escalating political, military and climate crises, calling on the organization to reform and improve to better serve the needs of the world’s most vulnerable. “For millions of vulnerable people, global development can sometimes appear to be moving from one framework to another framework,” he said. “Trust in the UN won’t be restored through declarations alone. It will be restored when institutions act constituently, uphold international law and produce results that people can see and experience.” On the issue of Palestine, Mohamud was clear: “Somalia stands firmly with the Palestinian people and their legitimate right to self-determination and statehood. “We reaffirm our support for a just and lasting peace based on a two-state solution with an independent and viable Palestinian state along the 1967 borders. “A just resolution of the Palestinian question remains essential to lasting peace and stability in the Middle East and beyond.” He added: “Respect for international law is becoming increasingly selective. Multilateral cooperation is weakening; conflict, geopolitical rivalry and mistrust are becoming the defining features of our time. Uncertainty, unfortunately, has become the new norm.” Mohamud warned that it is not just conflict that poses a threat to humanity, raising climate change as a profound concern of his government and others. “Humanitarian needs are rising while the resources available to meet them are rapidly declining. “Nationalism, intolerance and political polarization are weakening the spirit of international cooperation.” He added: “The climate crisis continues to destroy lives, livelihoods and public infrastructure, particularly across the developing world. “According the UN, over 40 percent of the global population are vulnerable to the destructive effects of climate change, and governments in developing countries spend over 10 percent of their GDP (gross domestic product) to respond to this. “This painful fiscal trade off comes at the expense of investment in education and health, which should never be the case.” The escalation of the conflict in the Gulf, and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, have placed great strain on Somalia, he said. “For Somalia, disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz have serious economic and humanitarian consequences. “As an import-dependent country reliant on the Middle East for much of our food, fuel, trade, Somalia is already facing rising prices, inflation.” He added: “Ensuring free and fair navigation through the strait is therefore essential to protecting vulnerable economies like Somalia, and sustaining stability, advancing development and delivering basic services.” As a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council, Mohamud called for reform of a body that has failed with African representation despite the continent’s various conflicts over the years. The UNSC “must become more representative, transparent and effective,” he said. “Africa remains unrepresented in the permanent category … This historical injustice against 54 sovereign states can’t be postponed indefinitely. “Somalia supports the common African position and meaningful representation in both categories of the council. “Given that many of the discussions directly concern African states, they have the right to full representation on equal par with all other permanent Security Council members.” His country, Mohamud said, has played an outsized role in maintaining international security in its fight against organized terrorist groups in East Africa. “Somalia continues to confront international terrorism with determination and with the support of our international partners. “We’re strengthening our national security institutions, improving force generation, developing intelligence capabilities and expanding security cooperation with our neighbors and the rest of the world,” he said. “But the fight against terrorism in Somalia mustn’t be understood as Somalia’s responsibility alone. “We stand on the frontline for a struggle that directly effects regional and international security. “We therefore call for predictable, sustainable support for Somalia’s security transition, including adequate financing for an African Union mission in Somalia.” He noted that negative effects of international intervention in African states has affected Somalia in particular, saying: “Respect for national sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity isn’t an abstract principle for Somalia only. “It’s a foundation for peace and stability in our country, our region and the wider international community. “Therefore, Somalia firmly rejects unilateral actions that undermine its sovereign, unity and internationally recognized borders.” Mohamud also focused on the need for UN assistance in his country to be better organized and coordinated to allow the government to lead its own development. “The majority of UN assistance continues to be delivered through parallel structures, fragmented projects and off-budget arrangements in Somalia. “This makes it difficult for the government to plan, coordinate resources, measure results and build institutions required for long-term stability. “Let us be clear here, Somalia isn’t calling for the UN to withdraw, we’re simply calling for a more accountable, strategic and result-oriented partnership where Somali institutions are in the lead when it comes to implementation.” Political progress and reform, he said, are of paramount importance for Somalia’s development. “Our people have dreamed of choosing their leaders through their vote. The last democratic election that took place in Somalia was held in 1969. items.fullContent: Somalia called for a resolution to the plight of the Palestinian people on Thursday, while saying the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz poses a threat not only to itself but the rest of the region. Speaking at the UN General Assembly in New York, Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud warned that the world faces uncertainty amid escalating political, military and climate crises, calling on the organization to reform and improve to better serve the needs of the world’s most vulnerable. “For millions of vulnerable people, global development can sometimes appear to be moving from one framework to another framework,” he said. “Trust in the UN won’t be restored through declarations alone. It will be restored when institutions act constituently, uphold international law and produce results that people can see and experience.” On the issue of Palestine, Mohamud was clear: “Somalia stands firmly with the Palestinian people and their legitimate right to self-determination and statehood. “We reaffirm our support for a just and lasting peace based on a two-state solution with an independent and viable Palestinian state along the 1967 borders. “A just resolution of the Palestinian question remains essential to lasting peace and stability in the Middle East and beyond.” He added: “Respect for international law is becoming increasingly selective. Multilateral cooperation is weakening; conflict, geopolitical rivalry and mistrust are becoming the defining features of our time. Uncertainty, unfortunately, has become the new norm.” Mohamud warned that it is not just conflict that poses a threat to humanity, raising climate change as a profound concern of his government and others. “Humanitarian needs are rising while the resources available to meet them are rapidly declining. “Nationalism, intolerance and political polarization are weakening the spirit of international cooperation.” He added: “The climate crisis continues to destroy lives, livelihoods and public infrastructure, particularly across the developing world. “According the UN, over 40 percent of the global population are vulnerable to the destructive effects of climate change, and governments in developing countries spend over 10 percent of their GDP (gross domestic product) to respond to this. “This painful fiscal trade off comes at the expense of investment in education and health, which should never be the case.” The escalation of the conflict in the Gulf, and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, have placed great strain on Somalia, he said. “For Somalia, disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz have serious economic and humanitarian consequences. “As an import-dependent country reliant on the Middle East for much of our food, fuel, trade, Somalia is already facing rising prices, inflation.” He added: “Ensuring free and fair navigation through the strait is therefore essential to protecting vulnerable economies like Somalia, and sustaining stability, advancing development and delivering basic services.” As a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council, Mohamud called for reform of a body that has failed with African representation despite the continent’s various conflicts over the years. The UNSC “must become more representative, transparent and effective,” he said. “Africa remains unrepresented in the permanent category … This historical injustice against 54 sovereign states can’t be postponed indefinitely. “Somalia supports the common African position and meaningful representation in both categories of the council. “Given that many of the discussions directly concern African states, they have the right to full representation on equal par with all other permanent Security Council members.” His country, Mohamud said, has played an outsized role in maintaining international security in its fight against organized terrorist groups in East Africa. “Somalia continues to confront international terrorism with determination and with the support of our international partners. “We’re strengthening our national security institutions, improving force generation, developing intelligence capabilities and expanding security cooperation with our neighbors and the rest of the world,” he said. “But the fight against terrorism in Somalia mustn’t be understood as Somalia’s responsibility alone. “We stand on the frontline for a struggle that directly effects regional and international security. “We therefore call for predictable, sustainable support for Somalia’s security transition, including adequate financing for an African Union mission in Somalia.” He noted that negative effects of international intervention in African states has affected Somalia in particular, saying: “Respect for national sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity isn’t an abstract principle for Somalia only. “It’s a foundation for peace and stability in our country, our region and the wider international community. “Therefore, Somalia firmly rejects unilateral actions that undermine its sovereign, unity and internationally recognized borders.” Mohamud also focused on the need for UN assistance in his country to be better organized and coordinated to allow the government to lead its own development. “The majority of UN assistance continues to be delivered through parallel structures, fragmented projects and off-budget arrangements in Somalia. “This makes it difficult for the government to plan, coordinate resources, measure results and build institutions required for long-term stability. “Let us be clear here, Somalia isn’t calling for the UN to withdraw, we’re simply calling for a more accountable, strategic and result-oriented partnership where Somali institutions are in the lead when it comes to implementation.” Political progress and reform, he said, are of paramount importance for Somalia’s development. “Our people have dreamed of choosing their leaders through their vote. items.title: Somalia’s Federal System Frays as Election Crisis Reaches Hirshabelle and Galmudug
items.description: Future Council Takes Somalia’s Electoral Crisis to the UN as Political Rupture Spreads Across the Federal States Mogadishu (WDN) — Somalia’s political crisis is no longer confined to a confrontation between Mogadishu and its most outspoken opponents. It is now spreading into the heart of the federal system, with Hirshabelle and Galmudug increasingly drawn into the same electoral and constitutional disputes that have already fractured relations with Puntland, Jubaland and South West State. The warning could hardly be more stark. The Somali Future Council has taken the country’s political crisis directly to the United Nations Security Council, arguing that repeated attempts to negotiate an electoral settlement have failed and that Somalia is approaching a dangerous constitutional and political confrontation. In a letter addressed to Security Council President Jérôme Bonnafont, the opposition coalition called for international mediation, independent monitoring and an inclusive political agreement covering elections, constitutional arrangements and relations between the Federal Government and the federal member states. The letter was dated September 11, according to reporting on its contents. The significance goes beyond the opposition’s immediate demands. It exposes a federal system increasingly divided over who controls the electoral process, who determines the rules and whether regional governments can legitimately be elected through a process designed or heavily influenced by Mogadishu. The Crisis Moves Into Hirshabelle The most immediate flashpoint is now Hirshabelle.Political leaders and traditional figures in Hiiraan have rejected the planned regional election unless a prior political agreement is reached. Hirshabelle Vice President Yusuf Hagar Dabageed has warned that an election cannot proceed in Hiiraan without broad political consensus. The confrontation intensified after President Ali Abdullahi Hussein Guudlaawe was selected as the ruling Justice and Unity Party’s candidate for another term. Opponents in Hiiraan argue that the next Hirshabelle presidency should be determined through a political agreement involving the region’s principal constituencies. Dabageed has separately accused President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud of abandoning an alleged understanding that the Hawadle community would be considered for the Hirshabelle presidency. That allegation has been reported by Somali media but remains a claim by Dabageed rather than an independently established fact. The result is a potentially explosive contradiction: Mogadishu is pressing ahead with a regional electoral timetable while a significant political constituency in one of Hirshabelle’s two constituent regions says the process lacks the necessary agreement. Galmudug Is Also Under Pressure Hirshabelle is not the only federal state facing political uncertainty. Galmudug has also been drawn into the national electoral dispute, with disagreements over its forthcoming leadership election and competing political interests surrounding the process. Earlier this year, reports described a serious political dispute over the future leadership of Galmudug and tensions involving figures close to the federal government. President Hassan Sheikh has reportedly maintained that national electoral discussions should follow regional elections in Galmudug and Hirshabelle, a position that places enormous political importance on the outcome of those two state-level contests. That sequencing is contested by the opposition, which argues that the national electoral framework itself must first be negotiated among the major political actors. The dispute therefore becomes circular: Mogadishu wants regional elections to move forward before a broader national settlement, while its opponents want a national political agreement before the regional electoral process becomes irreversible. Puntland and Jubaland Already Outside the Political Centre The Future Council’s appeal comes against a backdrop of an increasingly fractured relationship between Mogadishu and Puntland and Jubaland, whose leaders have been among the strongest opponents of the Federal Government’s approach to elections, constitutional reform and federal power-sharing. The two administrations have been outside normal political cooperation with Mogadishu for an extended period, while their leaders participate in the Future Council. Puntland separately submitted its own letter to the Security Council this month, calling for greater international engagement with the federal member states and an inclusive political dialogue. The combined effect is striking: the dispute is no longer simply between a federal government and a conventional opposition bloc. It increasingly involves competing centres of political authority across Somalia’s federal map. South West State Shows How Quickly the Crisis Can Turn Violent South West State provides an even more alarming precedent. The political confrontation between Mogadishu and Baidoa has already produced a severe rupture, with the federal government and South West authorities becoming locked in a dispute over political control and the electoral process. The experience has become a warning for other federal states: an argument that begins over electoral rules can quickly become a confrontation over security forces, territorial authority and control of government institutions. That is precisely why the developing disputes in Hirshabelle and Galmudug are attracting such attention. The Bigger Problem: One Election, Multiple Political Systems At the centre of Somalia’s crisis is a deceptively simple question: Who gets to decide the rules of the next election? The Federal Government has pursued constitutional and electoral changes that it presents as part of a transition toward a new political system. Its opponents argue that fundamental changes to the electoral framework require agreement among the federal government, federal member states and other major political stakeholders. The Future Council says it has proposed a transitional model combining direct elections with the 4.5 power-sharing formula as a compromise intended to bring competing camps back to the negotiating table. The government has a different position. The disagreement has already contributed to failed rounds of political talks, while international mediation efforts involving Turkey and other international partners have yet to produce a comprehensive settlement. A Country Divided Over the Rules of Politics The danger is therefore larger than any individual presidential contest. If elections in different federal states are perceived as being determined by competing political centres rather than by negotiated rules accepted by the principal stakeholders, Somalia could end up with multiple governments claiming democratic legitimacy at the same time. That is the deeper fear now hanging over Hirshabelle and Galmudug. The political rupture with Puntland and Jubaland has not been resolved. South West State has experienced its own confrontation with Mogadishu. Now Hirshabelle is entering an increasingly bitter dispute, while Galmudug faces its own contested electoral process. The result is a federal system under extraordinary pressure. The UN Is Being Asked to Step In The Future Council is now asking the Security Council to intervene before the political dispute becomes even more deeply entrenched. Its proposals include an inclusive political dialogue, international mediation and guarantees for any agreement reached, as well as independent monitoring of political and security developments. The timing is significant. The UN Transitional Assistance Mission in Somalia is scheduled to complete its transition on October 31, 2026, while international support for Somalia’s security architecture is itself being recalibrated. The United States recently agreed to extend the period for ending UN support to AUSSOM, underscoring the continuing international concern over Somalia’s political and security fragility. The most unsettling feature of Somalia’s current crisis is that the country is not facing one political dispute. It is facing several disputes that are beginning to overlap — elections, constitutional reform, federal authority, regional leadership, security forces and political legitimacy. Puntland and Jubaland remain locked in confrontation with Mogadishu. South West State has experienced a dramatic rupture. Hirshabelle is now approaching its own electoral crisis. Galmudug faces growing political pressure. The Future Council’s appeal to the Security Council is therefore more than another opposition complaint. It is a warning that Somalia’s federal political bargain is beginning to fray across multiple fronts at once. Whether that fragmentation remains political or develops into further security confrontation may depend on one unresolved question: Can Somalia agree on the rules of the next election before competing authorities begin treating their own electoral processes as the only legitimate path forward? items.title: Puntland oo shaacisay inay soo furatay markab shidaal oo afduub loo haystay
items.description: Garoowe (Caasimada Online) – Puntland ayaa sheegtay inay howlgal ku soo furtay markab ay kooxo burcad-badeed ku haysteen xeebaha Mudug, iyadoo maamulka ay xaqiijiyay in markabka iyo shaqaalihii saarnaa lasoo badbaadiyay. Howlgalka ayaa sababay dhimasho iyo dhaawac, iyadoo Puntland ay sheegtay in saddex qof ay ku dhinteen dagaalka, halka dhowr kalena ay ku dhaawacmeen. Markabka oo lagu magacaabo MTT-SIBU 1 ayaa lagu qabtay meel u dhexeysa xeebaha Garacad iyo Hobyo, sida ay sheegeen laamaha ammaanka Puntland. Markabkan ayaa siday shidaal, wuxuuna ku safrayay calanka dalka Eritrea. Ciidamada Badda Puntland ee PMPF ayaa fuliyay howlgalka lagu soo furtay markabka, xilli ciidamadu ay maalmihii lasoo dhaafay howlgallo ka dhan ah kooxaha burcad-badeedda ka wadeen xeebaha Puntland. War kasoo baxay maamulka Puntland ayaa lagu sheegay in howlgalka lagu badbaadiyay markabka iyo shaqaalihii saarnaa, iyadoo ciidamada ammaanku ay gacanta ku dhigeen markabka kaddib iska horimaad ay la galeen kooxdii haysatay. Markabka SIBU 1 ayaa 21-kii August laga afduubtay xeebaha dalka Yemen, ka hor inta aysan kooxihii qabsaday u soo jiheysan xeebaha Soomaaliya. Furashada markabka ayaa kusoo beegmaysa iyadoo xeebaha Mudug iyo deegaanno kale oo Puntland ah ay ciidamada badda ka wadaan howlgallo lagu beegsanayo kooxaha ku lugta leh afduubka iyo qabsashada maraakiibta. Puntland ayaa sheegtay in howlgalka uu kusoo dhammaaday si guul leh, laguna soo furashada markabka iyo shaqaalihii saarnaa, iyadoo laamaha ammaanku ay sii wadaan howlgalladooda ka dhanka ah kooxaha burcad-badeedda. items.title: Puntland Appeals to UN Security Council Over Somalia’s Political and Security Crisis
items.description: Puntland Calls for Inclusive Dialogue, Greater International Engagement with Federal States and Continued UN Role Garowe (WDN) — Puntland has appealed to the United Nations Security Council for renewed international engagement in Somalia, warning of deepening political, security and economic tensions between the Federal Government and federal member states. In a letter dated September 13, 2026, addressed to UN Secretary-General António Guterres and the Security Council president for September, French Ambassador Jérôme Bonnafont, Puntland called for an inclusive Somali political dialogue to address disputes over the constitution, elections and the division of powers between Mogadishu and the federal states. Puntland said its relations with the Federal Government have deteriorated significantly since 2023, accusing Mogadishu of interfering in its internal affairs and supporting rival political and armed actors. The allegations represent Puntland’s position and have not been independently established. The Federal Government has previously rejected accusations that it seeks to undermine federal member states. Puntland administration also highlighted its ongoing military campaign against Islamic State militants in the Cal Miskaad mountains, arguing that Puntland forces have not received sufficient federal military, financial or logistical support. Puntland further cited the August confrontation in Gaalkacyo, claiming that weapons and equipment were being transported toward northern Gaalkacyo. It said its forces detained 101 people and seized weapons, vehicles and other equipment. The account has not been independently verified. The letter also raised concerns about maritime security and what Puntland described as signs of a possible resurgence of Somali piracy. It urged renewed international cooperation to protect Somalia’s coastline and commercial shipping. Puntland separately alleged that Turkish forces carried out strikes near Garmaal and Jiifle on August 18 and 20, claiming that 14 Somalis were killed and fishing boats destroyed. The allegations have not been independently verified. The administration also called for an investigation into a September 3 drone strike in Doolow, arguing that modern military capabilities provided for counterterrorism operations should not be used in Somalia’s internal political disputes. Six Requests to the Security Council Puntland outlined six principal requests: 1. Inclusive political dialogue involving the Federal Government, federal member states and other major political stakeholders. 2. Greater direct international engagement with federal member states, particularly on security, humanitarian assistance and development. 3. Restoration of the UN Panel of Experts’ monitoring powers over arms flows, organized crime and militant networks. 4. A review of Somalia’s arms restrictions, amid concerns that military equipment could be diverted to domestic political confrontations. 5. Extension of the UN Transitional Assistance Mission in Somalia (UNTMIS), which is currently scheduled to complete its transition on October 31, 2026. 6. Greater international scrutiny of resource management and government transparency, including agreements and contracts involving Somalia’s national resources. 7. That Puntland is currently facing pressures from huge masses of its citizens, “who are in favor of full independence from the Center. Puntland also urged the Security Council to support a political process capable of resolving disputes between Mogadishu and the federal member states rather than allowing disagreements to escalate into security confrontations. The administration warned that continued political deadlock could deepen divisions between Somalia’s political authorities and potentially lead to the emergence of competing political centres. Puntland nevertheless reaffirmed its support for a stable, peaceful, democratic and federal Somalia. The letter comes as Somalia faces unresolved disputes over constitutional reforms, elections and federal relations, while international partners prepare for further discussions on the country’s political and security situation. Puntland’s appeal is expected to add to growing international attention on whether Somalia’s political leaders can reach a negotiated settlement before existing disagreements further strain relations between Mogadishu and the federal member states. Puntland also urged the Security Council to support a political process capable of resolving disputes between Mogadishu and the federal member states rather than allowing disagreements to escalate into security confrontations. The administration warned that continued political deadlock could deepen divisions between Somalia’s political authorities and potentially lead to the emergence of competing political centres. Puntland nevertheless reaffirmed its support for a stable, peaceful, democratic and federal Somalia. The letter comes as Somalia faces unresolved disputes over constitutional reforms, elections and federal relations, while international partners prepare for further discussions on the country’s political and security situation. Puntland’s appeal is expected to add to growing international attention on whether Somalia’s political leaders can reach a negotiated settlement before existing disagreements further strain relations between Mogadishu and the federal member states.
