items.title: The Dual Framework of Somali Moral Psychology
items.description: Dr. Ahmed Hassan, LPCC Recent discussions about Somalia’s ongoing political issues often blame the failures on immoral traits of Somali leaders , such as corruption, nepotism, and resource theft . While I agree, I believe the conversation should also include broader societal moral struggles. Politicians mirror their society, and a major root of these moral problems is Somalis’ difficulty extending empathy beyond their immediate group. The tribal divide, characterized by an us-versus-them mentality, plays a significant role in both moral decline and political instability. To understand Somalia’s persistent instability and why individual morals fail, we must examine not only politicians’ actions but also the cultural factors shaping societal values. One central problem with Somali morality is its dual nature. The same cultural values that foster remarkable solidarity and cooperation within clans also systematically justify exclusion and violence against outsiders. This is not a failure of morality but its distortion: the very mechanisms that foster trust and cooperation among clan members become weapons against minorities and rivals when the state collapses and resources become scarce. During the 1991 civil war, the country’s collapse revealed previously managed clan divisions. Clan militias protected their members and targeted others, driven by a moral logic of in-group loyalty that served as both motivation and justification. This behavior was not mere tribalism, but a survival response; extreme resource shortages and the breakdown of institutions pushed individuals to revert to primal instincts, emphasizing clan loyalty and punishing rival clans, reopening old wounds and grievances. While the Somali “clan conscience” fostered remarkable mutual aid and self-sacrifice, its intense solidarity also made it challenging to extend the same empathy to members of rival clans. To analyze Somali moral psychology, I will examine how emotions and reason influence moral decisions. For example, in conflicts, Somalis often use emotions like Shame ( ceeb ), a potent form of social regulator, which can have destructive effects. Shame promotes social conformity by instilling fear of public disgrace and losing face, prompting individuals to act honorably. However, when collective honor is involved, shame may lead to mob mentality and increased violence in inter-clan disputes. A recent incident illustrates this: people were killed along clan lines in Hirshabelle , often to avenge a clan member and defend group honor. Although killing an innocent is morally wrong and contradicts human conscience, cultural values may take precedence. People might justify it, viewing the other person’s clan as a threat because of past incidents. If someone responsible for avenging clan members does not do so, they risk shame from their clan; therefore, exclusion anxiety motivates them to act in ways that shut down conscience ( damiir ) voices.  Even empathy ( naxariis ), the virtue Somali tradition places at the foundation of all others, has limits. In the case of the man recently killed and widely circulated on social media, his plea for empathy, addressed to the people he called uncle on his mother’s side, went ignored. The killer’s lack of empathy can be explained by research showing that oxytocin, the bonding hormone, strengthens prosocial behavior within groups while simultaneously enhancing defensive aggression toward outsiders. In his case, the captors considered him an outsider despite his claim that they were related. This biological mechanism means that intense in-group solidarity can inadvertently justify hostility toward those outside the lineage who are perceived as a threat. The result is a “moral dualism” in which the same emotional bonds that sustain communities become barriers to universal justice. During the civil war, individuals with consciences ( damiir ) often engage in harmful acts they would usually avoid by using “moral disengagement” strategies. These involve justifying violence as necessary or insignificant, dehumanizing out-group members, blaming leaders, and framing violence as “protecting the community.” This process bypasses personal moral standards, allowing typically peaceful young men to commit extraordinary violence, especially under intense stress, charismatic warlords, and when legitimate state authority is absent. Although many human actions are driven by emotions, the key is to restore reason as a check against emotion-led morality. Reason allows careful assessment that can surpass impulsive emotional reactions rooted in self-interest or group loyalty, helping to confront clan biases that empathy alone can’t resolve. It promotes a concept called “responsible interdependence,” a balanced virtue that opposes both extreme tribalism and authoritarian nationalism, fostering personal responsibility while maintaining the advantages of cooperation among diverse groups. Reason also broadens moral concern beyond the clan. Guided by principles of individual dignity and universal rights, reason argues that if I have rights to justice and fairness, I should extend those rights to others. It helps prevent sacrificing individuals for leaders’ gain. Although I argue that reason is needed to address the moral challenges Somalis are struggling with, emotions such as empathy still play an important role in morality. Therefore, the way forward involves “moral pluralism,” acknowledging that different situations demand different ethical approaches; for example, emotions like empathy can be more suitable during crises like famine and drought, but always with a rational check to avoid sacrificing individual rights and to evaluate moral choices using reason. Practical wisdom is essential. The Somali proverb, sidee xeero lagu xagtaa ilkana ku nabad qabaan “How can one scrape the bowl and still keep their teeth safe?” captures the tension between short-term gains such as self-enrichment and long-term collective well-being. Reason enables reflection on this relationship, helping individuals choose restraint over impulsive reaction, whether in overgrazing, corruption, or clan conflict. Moral education, then, is less about transmitting rules and more about cultivating moral perception, the ability to see clearly the stakes and appropriate responses in complex situations. Somali morality isn’t broken but incomplete. Its ability to promote group unity and empathy is a strength, yet it becomes a weakness without universal constraints. To improve, it should be complemented by rational, universal values that expand moral concern beyond family ties. This involves early lessons in self-reflection and moral evaluation, as well as institutions that serve all, whether they are Laandheere or Laangaab , equally. Education must foster practical wisdom, and culture should shift toward embracing responsible interdependence. The real question isn’t if Somali morality can evolve, but if Somalis will prioritize reason over impulse, universal justice over clan loyalty, and long-term prosperity over immediate gains. The way forward is challenging yet straightforward: the moral principles that upheld communities during the war need reform to foster peace, not just through emotional appeals, but through thoughtful, rational engagement with what justice demands for all Somalis. Dr. Ahmed Hassan, LPCC Email: ahmedhassan01@yahoo.com The post The Dual Framework of Somali Moral Psychology appeared first on WardheerNews .

Shir looga hadlay amniga Koonfur Galbeed oo lagu qabtay Baydhabo
items.description: Baydhabo (Raxanreeb Hoggaamiyaha Koonfur Galbeed, Sheekh Aadan Maxamed Nuur (Madoobe) ayaa guddoomiyey shir looga hadlay xaaladda amniga guud ee deegaannada Koonfur Galbeed, gaar ahaan amniga iyo xasilloonida magaalada Baydhabo. Shirka ayaa diiradda lagu saaray qiimeynta xaaladda amni ee magaalada Baydhabo iyo guud ahaan deegaannada Koonfur Galbeed, iyadoo warbixinno laga dhageystay mas’uuliyiinta iyo saraakiisha amniga ee ka qeybgalay shirka. Hoggaamiyaha ayaa faray hay’adaha amniga in la xoojiyo wada-shaqeynta, feejignaanta iyo howlaha lagu sugayo amniga shacabka, iyadoo mudnaan gaar ah la siinayo ilaalinta nabadgelyada iyo badqabka bulshada. Sidoo kale waxaa shirka lagu adkeeyey muhiimadda ay leedahay in ciidamada amniga ay si dhow ula shaqeeyaan bulshada, si loo xaqiijiyo xasilloonida iyo amniga Magaalada Baydhabo iyo guud ahaan deegaannada Koonfur Galbeed. Hoggaamiyaha oonfur Galbeed ayaa ku boorriyey hay’adaha amniga in ay sii laba-jibaaraan dadaallada lagu xaqiijinayo amniga iyo xasilloonida, isla markaana shacabka ay si dhow ula shaqeeyaan ciidamada amniga. Kulanka waxaa ka qeybgalay Wasiirka Amniga, Wasiiru-Dowlaha Madaxtooyada, Agaasimaha Madaxtooyada, Taliyaha Ciidanka Dhulka XDS iyo saraakiisha kala duwan hay’adda amniga ee ka howlgala deeganada Koonfur Galbeed Soomaaliya. items.title: Hoggaamiyaha Koonfur Galbeed oo shir amni la yeeshay  taliyaasha ciidamada
items.description: Hoggaamiyaha Maamulka Koonfur Galbeed, Sheekh Aadan Maxamed Nuur (Madoobe) , ayaa guddoomiyey shir looga hadlay xaaladda amniga iyo xasilloonida deegaannada Koonfur Galbeed, iyadoo si gaar ah diiradda loo saaray amniga magaalada Baydhabo . Shirka ayaa lagu qiimeeyay xaaladda guud ee amni ee Baydhabo iyo deegaanada kale ee maamulka, waxaana warbixinno ku saabsan xaaladda amniga laga dhageystay mas’uuliyiinta iyo saraakiisha hay’adaha amniga ee ka qeybgalay kulanka. Intii uu shirku socday ayaa la falanqeeyay xaaladaha amni ee jira iyo howlaha socda ee lagu ilaalinayo nabadgelyada shacabka, iyadoo la isku raacay muhiimadda ay leedahay in hay’adaha amnigu yeeshaan wada-shaqeyn iyo isku-duwid dheeraad ah. Hoggaamiyaha Koonfur Galbeed ayaa faray hay’adaha amniga in ay xoojiyaan wada-shaqeynta, feejignaanta iyo howlaha lagu sugayo amniga , isagoo mudnaan gaar ah siiyay ilaalinta nabadgelyada iyo badqabka shacabka. Kulanka ayaa kusoo dhammaaday iyadoo la adkeeyay muhiimadda ay leedahay in la sii xoojiyo dadaallada lagu ilaalinayo amniga Baydhabo iyo guud ahaan deegaannada Koonfur Galbeed.

items.title: Puntland iyo Mareykanka oo sheegay inay burburiyeen bakhaar hub oo Al-Shabaab leedahay
items.description: Maamulka Puntland iyo Mareykanka ayaa sheegay in si guul leh loo fuliyay howlgal ka dhan ah Al-Shabaab oo ka dhacay buuraha Al-Madow-Golis , gaar ahaan deegaanka Markad , halkaas oo lagu bartilmaameedsaday goob lagu keydinayay hub iyo saanad ciidan. Sida lagu sheegay war kasoo baxay dhinacyada howlgalka, ciidamada ayaa weeraray goob ay sheegeen in Al-Shabaab u adeegsanaysay kaydinta hubka iyo rasaasta , kuwaas oo loogu talagalay taageeridda howlgallada kooxda iyo weerarrada ay ka fuliso Soomaaliya. Howlgalka ayaa la sheegay inuu dhacay iyadoo la kaashanayo oo lala xiriirinayo hay’adaha amniga Puntland , waxaana Mareykanka iyo Puntland ay ku tilmaameen tallaabadan qayb ka mid ah howlgallo ballaaran oo lagu wiiqayo awoodda Al-Shabaab ee waqooyiga Soomaaliya. Labada dhinac ayaa sheegay in bartilmaameedsiga goobaha lagu kaydiyo hubka iyo kaabayaasha kale ee taageera shabakadaha hubeysan uu yareynayo awoodda kooxda ee qorsheynta iyo fulinta weerarrada . Puntland iyo Mareykanka ayaa sidoo kale sheegay in howlgalka uu qayb ka yahay dadaal joogto ah oo lagu wiiqayo awoodda Al-Shabaab, looga hortagayo in kooxda ay hesho goobo ay ku dhuumato, isla markaana lagu taageerayo xasilloonida iyo nabadda muddada dheer ee waqooyiga iyo bariga Soomaaliya.

items.title: In ka badan 3,000 oo Yemeni ah oo qaxooti ah ayaa gaaray xeebaha Jabuuti
items.description: In ka badan 3,000 oo qaxooti Yemeni ah , oo u badan haween iyo carruur, ayaa gaaray xeebaha waqooyi ee dalka Jabuuti, gaar ahaan nawaaxiga Obock , kadib markii ay ka gudbeen marin-biyoodka Bab al-Mandab iyagoo raadinaya badbaado iyo meel ay uga cararaan xaaladaha adag ee ka jira Yemen. Qaxootigan ayaa ka mid ah dadka Yemeniyiinta ah ee ka tallaaba marin-biyoodka Bab al-Mandab, kaas oo isku xira Badda Cas iyo Gacanka Cadmeed, iyagoo u gudbaya dhanka Geeska Afrika. Hay’adda Qatar Charity ayaa bilowday gurmad bani’aadamnimo oo degdeg ah oo loogu talagalay qaxootiga cusub ee gaaray Jabuuti. Hay’addu waxay sheegtay inay hal milyan oo doollar ($1 milyan) u qoondeysay marxaladda hore ee gurmadka, iyadoo lacagtaas lagu bixinayo baahiyaha aasaasiga ah ee qaxootiga. Gargaarka waxaa ka mid ah hoy degdeg ah, bustayaal iyo dhar, cunto , iyo sidoo kale biyo nadiif ah oo la cabbo iyo adeegyada fayadhowrka. Waxaa sidoo kale la qorsheeyay in qaxootiga la gaarsiiyo daryeel caafimaad oo aasaasi ah iyo taageero dhinaca nafaqada ah , gaar ahaan hooyooyinka iyo carruurta oo ka mid ah dadka sida weyn ugu nugul xaaladaha bani’aadamnimo.

items.title: Aadan Madoobe oo la kulmay Saraakiisha Militariga iyo kuwa Koonfur Galbeed (SAWIRRO)
items.description: Hoggaamiyaha Dowlad Goboleedka Koonfur Galbeed, Aadan Maxamed Nuur (Aadan Madoobe) ayaa Madaxtooyada Magaalada Baydhabo ku qaabilay Saraakiisha Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka iyo kuwa laamaha amniga ee maamulkiisa. Shirka ayaa waxaa ka qaybgalay Taliyaha Ciidanka Dhulka ee Xoogga Dalka, General Sahal Cabdullaahi Cumar, Taliyaha Qaybta 60aad, G/dhexe Isaaq Aadan Berdaale, Wasiirka Amniga Koonfur Galbeed, Isaaq Maxamed Isaaq (Koosaar), Taliyaha Qaybta Booliska Gobolka Baay, Korneyl Mukhtaar Maxamed Dugudow iyo xubno kale. War Khamiistan ka soo baxay Madaxtooyada Koonfur Galbeed ayaa lagu sheegay in Aadan Madoobe uu shir guddoomiyay shir looga hadlayay amniga deegaanada Koonfur Galbeed, gaar ahaan Magaalada Baydhabo. “Shirka ayaa diiradda lagu saaray qiimeynta xaaladda amni ee Magaalada Baydhabo iyo guud ahaan deegaanada Koonfur Galbeed, iyadoo warbixinno laga dhageystay masuuliyiinta iyo saraakiisha amniga ee ka qaybgalay shirka.” Ayaa lagu yiri warka. “Hoggaamiyaha ayaa faray hay’adaha amniga in la xoojiyo wada-shaqaynta, feejignaanta iyo howlaha lagu sugayo amniga shacabka, iyadoo mudnaan gaar ah la siinayo ilaalinta nabadgelyada iyo badqabka bulshada.” Ayaa lagu sheegay warka. Warka ayaa intaasi ku daray “Sidoo kale waxaa shirka lagu adkeeyay muhiimadda ay leedahay in ciidamada amniga ay si dhow ula shaqeeyaan bulshada, si loo xaqiijiyo xasilloonida iyo amniga Magaalada Baydhabo iyo guud ahaan deegaanada Koonfur Galbeed.” Shirka ayaa imanaya, iyadoo uu socdo diyaargarow ku aaddan abaabulka cutubyo ka tirsan Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka iyo kuwa Koonfur Galbeed, oo la doonayo in ay hawlgal sifayn ah ka bilaabaan deegaanada hoostaga Baydhabo. Aadan Madoobe ayaa dadaal ugu jira in ciidamada taabacsan Madaxweynihii hore ee Koonfur Galbeed, Cabdicasiis Xasan Maxamed Laftagareen) iyo maleeshiyada Al Shabaab laga fogeeyo nawaaxiga magaaladaasi.

items.title: IGAD Iyo AUSSOM Oo Ka Digay Maalgelin-Yari Carqaladeyn Karta Howlgalka Soomaaliya
items.description: IGAD iyo hoggaanka Howlgalka Taageerada iyo Xasilinta Midowga Afrika ee Soomaaliya AUSSOM ayaa walaac ka muujiyey caqabadaha dhaqaale iyo kuwa saadka ee horyaalla howlgalka. IGAD waxay Qaramada Midoobay iyo saaxiibbada caalamiga ah ka dalbatay maalgelin joogto ah, la saadaalin karo oo waarta. Taliyaha ciidamada AUSSOM, Jeneraal Sam Kavuma, ayaa sheegay in Xafiiska Qaramada Midoobay ee Taageerada Soomaaliya—UNSOS—uu bixiyo qiyaastii 85% taageerada saadka ee howlgalka. Wuxuu ka digay in yareynta taageeradaas, iyadoo aan la helin ilo kale, ay saameyn karto howlgallada iyo ilaalinta goobaha muhiimka ah. Kavuma ayaa sidoo kale sheegay in wareejinta mas’uuliyadda amniga aysan ku koobnaan karin bixitaanka ciidamada Midowga Afrika. Wuxuu tilmaamay baahida loo qabo ciidamo Soomaaliyeed oo lugta ah oo tababaran, awood sahan iyo taageero cirka ah iyo ciidan badeed awood u leh ilaalinta xeebaha dalka. Qiyaasta 85%-ka ah waxay ku salaysan tahay hadalka taliyaha AUSSOM, halka aan weli la shaacin qorshe maaliyadeed oo kama-dambays ah oo daboolaya howlgalka. Hubanti la’aanta maalgelinta ayaa dhalinaysa walaac ku saabsan sii wadidda howlgallada ka dhanka ah Al-Shabaab iyo hirgelinta qorshaha kala-guurka amniga.

Warsaxaafadeed kasoo baxay Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda Soomaaliya ayaa si adag loogu cambaareeyay weerarkan oo loo adeegsaday diyaaradaha aan duuliyaha lahayn, kaas oo ay ka hortageen ciidamada difaaca dalka Sacuudiga “Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya waxay si adag u cambaareyneysaa isku dayga weerarkii diyaaradda aan duuliyaha lahayn ee lagu qaaday magaalada barakeysan ee Makkah Al-Mukarramah, kaas oo ay Ciidamada Difaaca Cirka ee Boqortooyada Sacuudi Carabiya ku qabteen kuna burburiyeen ka hor inta uusan gaarin magaalada Makkah,” ayaa lagu yiri bayaanka. Sidoo kale, Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa si adag u cambaareysay weerarradii dhowaan lagu qaaday goobaha rayidka ah ee ku yaalla Boqortooyada Sacuudi Carabiya, iyadoo muujisay garab istaag buuxa oo ay la garab taagan tahay dowladda iyo shacabka Sacuudiga. “Dowladda Soomaaliyeed waxay muujineysaa garab istaag buuxa oo ay la garab taagan tahay Boqortooyada walaalaha ah ee Sacuudi Carabiya, oo uu hoggaamiyo Khadiimka Labada Masjid ee Barakeysan, waxayna sidoo kale xaqiijineysaa xaqa ay Boqortooyada Sacuudi Carabiya u leedahay inay difaacdo dhulkeeda, dadkeeda iyo goobaha barakeysan ee Islaamkam,” ayaa mar kale lagu yiri warsaxaafadeedka. Si kastaba, Riyadh ayaa dhankeeda dhacdadan ku tilmaantay mid ka gudubtay “khad cas”, maadaama ay khatar gelin karto goobaha barakeysan ee Muslimiinta. Xuutiyiinta ayaa beeniyay inay Makka bartilmaameedsadeen, iyagoo ku eedeeyay Sacuudiga inuu arrintaas u adeegsanayo dacaayad dagaal Arrimahan ayaa kusoo aadayo, iyada oo uu sii xoogeysanayo d agaalka u dhaxeeya Sacuudiga iyo Xuutiyiinta, waxaana haatan diyaaradaha dagaalka Sacuudiga ay duqeymo culus ka wadaan gudaha Yemen, halka Xuutiyiintuna ay gantaallo iyo diyaarado aan duuliye lahayn ku weerareen bartilmaameedyo ku yaalla gudaha Sacuudiga. Xiisadda cusub ayaa sidoo kale timid kadib markii Xuutiyiinta oo ay taageerto Iran ay toddobaadkii lasoo dhaafay horumar degdeg ah ka sameeyeen xeebaha Badda Cas ee dalka Yemen, iyagoo la wareegay magaalooyin iyo jasiirado muhiim ah oo ku dhow marin-biyoodka Bab al-Mandab. Wasiirka Arrimaha Gudaha Jabuuti, Cumar Cabdi Saciid, ayaa sheegay in in ka badan 2,500 oo qof oo Yemeni ah ay dalka soo gaareen tan iyo Khamiistii toddobaadkii hore. “Waxaan filaynaa in tirada dadka barakacay ay toddobaadyada soo socda gaarto ku dhowaad 10,000,” ayuu Saciid sheegay Arbacadii. Wasiirka ayaa sheegay in qulqulka dadka soo galaya Jabuuti uu cadaadis weyn saarayo adeegyada iyo awoodda dalka, xilli ay sidoo kale sii yaraaneyso maalgelinta caalamiga ah ee loogu talagalay arrimaha bani’aadannimada. “Qulqulka muhaajiriinta wuxuu durba ka sarre maray awooddeena qaran, waxaana wajahaynaa cadaadis sii kordhaya iyadoo maalgelinta caalamiga ah ay hoos u dhacayso,” ayuu yiri. “Waxaan ugu baaqeynaa Qaramada Midoobay iyo saaxiibada caalamiga ah inay si degdeg ah u abaabulaan dhaqaale u dhigma baaxadda dhibaatada.” Dadkan ayaa ka soo cararaya dagaallo culus oo ka socda galbeedka Yemen, kuwaas oo u dhaxeeya Xuutiyiinta ay Iran taageerto iyo dowladda Yemen ee caalamku aqoonsan yahay, oo taageero ka heleysa Sacuudi Carabiya. Jabuuti ayaa si toos ah uga soo horjeedda Yemen, iyadoo labada dal ay kala qeybiso Badda Cas, taas oo ka dhigeysa dalka mid ka mid ah meelaha ugu dhow ee ay gaari karaan dadka ka baxsanaya dagaallada. Xiisadda cusub ayaa sii xumeyneysa xaaladda bani’aadannimo ee Yemen, oo horey uga mid ahayd dalalka ugu saboolsan Bariga Dhexe. In ka badan 4.5 milyan oo qof ayaa gudaha Yemen ku barakacay tan iyo markii isbahaysiga uu hoggaamiyo Sacuudi Carabiya uu sanadkii 2015 ku biiray dagaalka sokeeye ee dalkaas. Dagaallada cusub ayaa hadda dhalinaya cabsi laga qabo barakac hor leh oo gudaha Yemen ah, iyo in dad badan ay isku dayaan inay dalka ka baxaan. Xafiiska Hay’adda Caalamiga ah ee Socdaalka ee IOM ee Jabuuti ayaa sheegay in shaqaalaheeda iyo mas’uuliyiinta maxalliga ah ay ku sugan yihiin goobaha ay dadka Yemeniyiinta ahi ka soo degayaan, iyagoo siinaya cunto iyo biyo. Isuduwaha gurmadka IOM ee Jabuuti, Safiya Ibraahim, ayaa sheegtay in maalin kasta ay dalka soo gaarayaan haween, carruur, dhallaanka iyo dad xanuunsan. Waxay sheegtay in hay’addu u baahan tahay taageero dhaqaale oo dheeraad ah si ay u sii waddo howlaha gargaarka ee dadka soo galaya dalka. Jabuuti, oo ka mid ah dalalka ugu yar qaaradda Afrika, ayaa waxaa ku nool dad ka yar 1.2 milyan, taas oo sii kordhineysa walaaca laga qabo awoodda dalka uu ku qaabili karo kumannaan qof oo dheeraad ah haddii dagaallada Yemen ay sii socdaan. items.title: Mareykanka oo kordhiyay xayiraadda fiisaha madaxda Falastiin
items.description: Dowladda Mareykanka ayaa muddo kordhisay cunaqabateynta dhanka fiisaha ah ee lagu soo rogay mas’uuliyiinta Maamulka Falastiin (PA) iyo xubno ka tirsan Ururka Xoreynta Falastiin (PLO), taas oo ka hor istaageysa qaar ka mid ah madaxda Falastiin inay u safraan magaalada New York xilli uu soo dhowaanayo shirka Golaha Guud ee Qaramada Midoobay. Go’aanka ayaa si gaar ah u saameynaya Madaxweynaha Falastiin Mahmoud Abbas , kaas oo sannadkii labaad oo xiriir ah laga hor istaagayo inuu dalka Mareykanka u safro si uu uga qeyb galo kalfadhiga Golaha Guud ee Qaramada Midoobay ee toddobaadka soo socda. Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda Mareykanka ayaa sheegtay in tallaabadan loo sababeeyay waxa ay ku tilmaantay dib-u-habeyn la’aanta Maamulka Falastiin , iyadoo sidoo kale ku eedeysay PA iyo PLO inay qaadeen tallaabooyin Washington u aragto kuwo wiiqaya fursadaha nabadda. Mareykanka ayaa si gaar ah u sheegay in Maamulka Falastiin uu ku xadgudbay shuruucda Mareykanka isagoo raadinaya aqoonsi caalami ah oo loo sameeyo dowlad Falastiin ah oo aan ku imaan wada-hadallo toos ah oo lala yeesho Israa’iil. Washinton  waxay sidoo kale ku eedeysay PA inay murannadeeda Israa’iil u gudbisay maxkamadaha caalamiga ah iyo inay bixiso lacago ay Mareykanka iyo Israel ku tilmaamaan kuwo la siiyo dad loo xukumay weerarro iyo qoysaskooda. Si kastaba ha ahaatee, xafiiska wakiillada Falastiin ee Qaramada Midoobay ayaa weli loo oggolaaday inuu sii shaqeeyo , iyadoo shaqaalaha caadiga ah ee xafiiska ay haystaan ka-dhaafitaan ku saleysan heshiiska xarunta Qaramada Midoobay, inkastoo mas’uuliyiin gaar ah laga mamnuucay inay galaan Mareykanka. Mahmoud Abbas ayaa la filayay inuu khudbaddiisa Golaha Guud ee Qaramada Midoobay xoogga ku saaro dadaallada lagu doonayo aqoonsi caalami ah oo loo sameeyo dowlad Falastiin ah , iyo dib u soo nooleynta xalka labada dowladood. Arrintan ayaa ku soo beegmaysa xilli dhowr dowladood oo reer Galbeed ah, oo ay ku jiraan Boqortooyada Midowday, Faransiiska iyo Kanada , ay bishan qaadeen tallaabooyin ku saabsan aqoonsiga dowladnimada Falastiin.

items.title: Muxuu u kala duwan yahay qiimaha shidaalka dalalka kale ee Afrika?
items.description: Dhammaan dalalka qaaradda Afrika ma aha kuwo hodan ku ah saliidda, waxa ay kasoo dhoofsadaan qaaradaha kale. Qaar ka mid ah dalalka ayaa ku tiirsan inay shidaalka la sifeeyey ka soo dhoofiyaan dalal kale, halka qaar kalena ay haystaan kayd badan oo saliid ceeriin ah, aysan lahayn warshado sifeeya oo ku filan baahida gudaha. Dalalka ay ka mid yihiin Nigeria, Koonfur Afrika, Liibiya iyo Suudaan ayaa hodan ku ah saliidda, inkastoo qaar ka mid ah ay wajahaan caqabado waaweyn oo dhanka shidaalka ah. Haysashada khayraadka saliidda macnaheedu ma aha in muwaadiniinta dalkaasi ay heli doonaan shidaal jaban. Inkasta oo saliidda ceeriin lagu kala iibsado doollarka Maraykanka suuqyada caalamka, haddana qiimaha shidaalka laga iibiyo dadweynaha aad ayuu ugu kala duwan yahay dalalka. Arrintan waxaa la xiriiriyaa dhowr arrimood, oo ay ka mid yihiin kabista dowladda, canshuuraha, awoodda lacagta dalka, kharashka shidaalka la soo dhoofiyo iyo wax-soo-saarka gudaha. Hadda, qiimaha saliidda ceeriin ee suuqyada caalamka ayaa ka sarreeya 100 doollar foostadii, taas oo ay sabab u tahay colaadda Bariga Dhexe iyo caqabadaha ku yimid marinnada badda ee fududeyn jiray dhoofinta shidaalka, waana sababta ugu weyn ee keenta kala duwanaanta qiimaha shidaalka waddamada Afrika.

items.title: IGAD Oo Ka Digtay Cunno-Yari Saameysay 49 Milyan
items.description: Warbixin ay soo saartay IGAD ayaa sheegtay in ku dhowaad 49 milyan oo qof oo ku nool Bariga Afrika ay wajahayaan cunno-yari ba’an. Abaaraha soo noqnoqday, isbeddelka cimilada iyo colaadaha ayaa lagu tilmaamay sababaha ugu waaweyn, halka in ka badan 19 milyan oo qof ay ku barakacsan yihiin gudaha dalalkooda. Ra’iisul Wasaarihii hore ee Soomaaliya, Xasan Cali Khayre, ayaa dhanka kale dowladda federaalka ku eedeeyey inay ku guuldarreysatay inay mudnaan ku filan siiso xaaladda bani’aadannimo iyo dadka barakacayaasha ah. Wuxuu ku baaqay in la kordhiyo taageerada la gaarsiinayo qoysaska ay saameeyeen colaadaha iyo masiibooyinka dabiiciga ah. Khayre ayaa soo xigtay xog sheegaysa in Soomaaliya ay ku nool yihiin ku dhowaad 4.8 milyan oo qof oo gargaar u baahan, halka 30.7% oo keliya laga helay dhaqaalihii loo baahnaa. Tirada 49-ka milyan waa wadarta dalalka ay warbixintu daboolayso, mana aha tiro Soomaaliya u gaar ah, balse waxaa la wadaaga dalalka kale ee gobolka.

items.title: Sacuudi Carabiya oo bixisay jawaab culus iyo dagaalka Xuutiyiinta oo xoogeystay
items.description: Jabuuti (Caasimada Online) – Dagaalka u dhaxeeya Sacuudiga iyo Xuutiyiinta Yemen ayaa si weyn u sii xoogeysanaya, iyadoo diyaaradaha dagaalka Sacuudiga ay duqeymo culus ka fuliyeen gudaha Yemen, halka Xuutiyiintuna ay gantaallo iyo diyaarado aan duuliye lahayn ku weerareen bartilmaameedyo ku yaalla gudaha Sacuudiga. Xiisadda cusub ayaa timid kadib markii Xuutiyiinta oo ay taageerto Iran ay toddobaadkii lasoo dhaafay horumar degdeg ah ka sameeyeen xeebaha Badda Cas ee Yemen, iyagoo la wareegay magaalooyin iyo jasiirado muhiim ah oo ku dhow marin-biyoodka Bab al-Mandab. Kooxda ayaa sidoo kale baahisay muuqaallo laga soo duubay goobaha dagaalka oo muujinaya dagaalyahannadeeda oo gacanta ku dhigaya gaadiid gaashaaman oo ay lahaayeen ciidamada Yemen ee uu Sacuudigu taageero. Muuqaallada ayaa sidoo kale muujinayay diyaarado dagaal oo dul heehaabaya iyo qaraxyo waaweyn oo ka dhacaya dhulka saxaraha ah. Afhayeenka militariga Xuutiyiinta, Yahya Saree, ayaa Arbacadii sheegay in kooxdu ay weerarro cusub oo gantaallo iyo diyaarado drone ah ku qaaday magaalada dekedda leh ee Yanbu, oo xarun muhiim u ah dhoofinta shidaalka Sacuudiga, iyo saldhigga cirka ee Khamis Mushait ee koonfurta dalka. Saree ma sheegin waqtiga ay weerarradaasi dhaceen. Sacuudiga ayaa Talaadadii digniino amni ka soo saaray magaalooyin badan oo dalkaas ah, oo ay ku jireen goobaha ay Xuutiyiintu sheegeen inay bartilmaameedsadeen. Mas’uuliyiinta Sacuudiga iyo shirkadda shidaalka ee Aramco ayaan markiiba ka jawaabin codsiyo loo diray oo ku saabsanaa weerarrada. Xuutiyiinta ayaa sidoo kale sheegay inay soo rideen diyaarad dagaal oo Sacuudigu leeyahay oo nooca F-15 ah, hase yeeshee ma aysan soo bandhigin caddeyn degdeg ah oo xaqiijineysa sheegashadaas. Saree ayaa sheegay in ciidamada Sacuudigu toddobaadkan Yemen ka fuliyeen illaa 450 duqeyn. Mas’uuliyiinta dowladda Yemen ee uu Sacuudigu taageero, taas oo maamusha koonfurta dalka, ayaa qiray in ciidamadooda iyo kuwa Sacuudiga ay duqeynayaan fariisimaha Xuutiyiinta, inkastoo Riyadh aysan si rasmi ah u xaqiijin tirada duqeymaha. Xuutiyiinta ayaa maalmihii lasoo dhaafay dhowr jeer weerarro ku qaaday gudaha Sacuudiga, taas oo digniino hawada ah ka dhalisay magaalooyin ku yaalla koonfurta iyo galbeedka boqortooyada. Sacuudiga ayaa Talaadadii sheegay in difaaciisa cirka uu soo riday diyaarad drone ah oo Xuutiyiintu leeyihiin xilli ay ku sii jeedday dhanka magaalada barakeysan ee Makka, ka hor inta aysan gelin hawada mamnuuca ah ee magaalada. Riyadh ayaa dhacdadaas ku tilmaantay mid ka gudubtay “khad cas”, maadaama ay khatar gelin karto goobaha barakeysan ee Muslimiinta. Xuutiyiinta ayaa beeniyay inay Makka bartilmaameedsadeen, iyagoo ku eedeeyay Sacuudiga inuu arrintaas u adeegsanayo dacaayad dagaal. Xiisadda ayaa sidoo kale ku sii fideysa kaabayaasha tamarta ee Sacuudiga. Weerar todobaadkii hore lagu eedeeyay kooxo Iran taageerto oo ka howlgala Ciraaq ayaa hakad geliyay dhuumaha shidaalka ee Bariga-Galbeed ee Sacuudiga, kuwaas oo muhiim u ah in shidaalka looga wareejiyo marin-biyoodka Hormuz marka uu khalkhal galo. Hakadka ku yimid dhuumahaas ayaa sii kordhiyay walaaca laga qabo sahayda shidaalka caalamka, xilli dagaalka gobolka uu horey u carqaladeeyay isu socodka maraakiibta ee marin-biyoodka Hormuz. Ganacsatada shidaalka ayaa sheegay in haddii dhuumaha Sacuudiga ay muddo dheer xirnaadaan, ay saameyn karaan sahay u dhiganta ilaa afar boqolkiiba shidaalka caalamka. Sacuudiga wali ma shaacin waqtiga ay dhuumahaasi dib ugu soo laaban doonaan shaqada caadiga ah, hase yeeshee Xoghayaha Tamarta Mareykanka Chris Wright ayaa Talaadadii sheegay inuu filayo in shidaalku uu mar kale dhex maro dhuumaha maalmo gudahood. Kulanka Mareykanka iyo Xuutiyiinta Dagaalka cusub ayaa sidoo kale Mareykanka ku qasbaya inuu si taxaddar leh uga fiirsado doorkiisa gobolka. Washington ayaa adkeysay digniinteeda safarka ee Sacuudiga, iyadoo shaqaalaha dowladda Mareykanka laga mamnuucay inay u safraan meel 20 mayl u jirta xadka Yemen. Ilo xog-ogaal ah ayaa Reuters u sheegay in mas’uuliyiin Mareykan ah ay dhammaadkii toddobaadka kulan qarsoodi ah kula yeesheen wakiillo ka socda Xuutiyiinta magaalada Muscat ee dalka Cumaan. Xuutiyiinta ayaa kulankaas ku sheegay inaysan damacsaneyn inay weeraraan maraakiibta Mareykanka, isla markaana ay weli ku dheggan yihiin heshiiskii xabbad-joojinta ee ay Washington la galeen sanadkii hore. Xiisadda cusub ayaa timid kadib markii Xuutiyiinta oo ay taageerto Iran ay toddobaadkii lasoo dhaafay horumar degdeg ah ka sameeyeen xeebaha Badda Cas ee Yemen, iyagoo la wareegay magaalooyin iyo jasiirado muhiim ah oo ku dhow marin-biyoodka Bab al-Mandab. Kooxda ayaa sidoo kale baahisay muuqaallo laga soo duubay goobaha dagaalka oo muujinaya dagaalyahannadeeda oo gacanta ku dhigaya gaadiid gaashaaman oo ay lahaayeen ciidamada Yemen ee uu Sacuudigu taageero. Muuqaallada ayaa sidoo kale muujinayay diyaarado dagaal oo dul heehaabaya iyo qaraxyo waaweyn oo ka dhacaya dhulka saxaraha ah. Afhayeenka militariga Xuutiyiinta, Yahya Saree, ayaa Arbacadii sheegay in kooxdu ay weerarro cusub oo gantaallo iyo diyaarado drone ah ku qaaday magaalada dekedda leh ee Yanbu, oo xarun muhiim u ah dhoofinta shidaalka Sacuudiga, iyo saldhigga cirka ee Khamis Mushait ee koonfurta dalka. Saree ma sheegin waqtiga ay weerarradaasi dhaceen. items.title: Ciidanka Danab oo qabtay rag waday qaraxyo culus
items.description: Leego (Caasimada Online) – Faah-faahinno kala duwan ayaa kasoo baxaya howlgal qorsheysan oo maanta ciidamada kumaandooska Danab ee Xoogga Dalka, gaar ahaan ururka 161-aad, ay ka sameeeyeen deegaanka Leego ee gobolka Shabeellaha Hoose, kaas oo lagu beegsaday kooxda Al-Shabaab. Ciidamada ayaa fashiliyey qorshe ay Khawaarijtu doonayeen in ay miinooyin ku aasaan waddooyinka ay isticmaalaan shacabka gaar ahaan jidadka isku xira gobollada Shabeellaha Hoose iyo Baay ee Koonfur Galbeed Soomaaliya. War-saxaafadeed kasoo baxay Taliska Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka ayaa lagu sheegay in sidoo kale ciidamada ay nolosha ku qabteen qaar kamid ah raggii qaraxyada ku aasayay halkaasi, kuwaas oo haatan baaritaano ay ku socdaan. “Intii uu socday howlgalka, Ciidanka Danab ayaa sidoo kale qabtay xubno ka tirsan shabakad ku howlanayd abaabulka iyo diyaarinta qaraxyada, kuwaas oo qorsheynayey in ay waxyeello u geystaan shacabka Soomaaliyeed iyo dadka isticmaala waddooyinka,” ayaa lagu yiri qoraalka. Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka Soomaaliyeed ayaa sidoo kale weli sii wada howlgallada lagu xaqiijinayo amniga, laguna burburinayo shabakadaha kooxda Al-Shabaab ee khatarta ku haya shacabka. Dhanka kale ma jiro illaa iyo hadda wax hadal ah oo kasoo baxay dhinaca Al-Shabaab oo ku aadan howlgalladaas ee ay guulaha ka sheegatay dowladda Soomaaliya, welina kasii socda gobolka Shabeellaha Hoose. Gobolkan waxaa weli ku xoogan Al-Shabaab oo weeraro culus kasoo abaabula halkaasi, kuwaas inta badan ay ku beegsadaan xarumaha ciidamada. The post Ciidanka Danab oo qabtay rag waday qaraxyo culus appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Waxgaradka Beesha Xawaadle Oo Dalbaday Hakinta Doorashada HirShabeelle iyo IGAD oo Ku Baaqday Wada-Hadal Qaran
items.description: Waxgarad, odayaal dhaqameed iyo siyaasiyiin ka tirsan beesha Xawaadle ayaa kulan ballaaran oo ay ku yeesheen Beledweyne kaga dalbaday in la hakiyo howlaha doorashada HirShabeelle, waxayna sheegeen in hakinta loo baahan yahay inta xal siyaasadeed laga gaarayo tabashooyinka ka jira gobolka Hiiraan. Ka qayb-galayaasha kulanka ayaa ku dooday in hannaanka doorashada ee hadda socda uusan si buuxda uga tarjumin rabitaanka bulshada deegaanka. Waxay ku baaqeen hannaan ku dhisan caddaalad, matalaad dhab ah iyo awood-qaybsi ay ku qanci karaan dhammaan dhinacyada wadaaga maamulka HirShabeelle. Dhanka kale, IGAD ayaa madaxda Dowladda Federaalka, dowlad-goboleedyada iyo saamileyda siyaasadda Soomaaliya ugu baaqday wada-hadal qaran oo loo dhan yahay. Baaqa ururka wuxuu khuseeyaa xaaladda siyaasadeed iyo doorashooyinka Soomaaliya guud ahaan, mana ahayn hindise si gaar ah loogu dhex-dhexaadinayo muranka HirShabeelle. Baaqa waxgaradka Xawaadle ayaa imaanaya xilli dhowaan  ururka JSP uu shaaciyay in madaxweyne Cali Guudlaawe uu yahay murashaxooda doorashada Hirshabeelle, islamarkaana siyaasiyiinta iyo waxgaradka Hiiraan ay arrintaas ka biya diideen.

items.title: Dowladda Oo Sheegtay In Dakhliga Gudaha Laba Jibaarmay Afar Sano Gudahood
items.description: Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa sheegtay in dakhliga gudaha uu laba jibaarmay afartii sano ee u dambeysay. Wasiirka Maaliyadda, Biixi Iimaan Cige, ayaa kororka u sababeeyey hirgelinta nidaamka canshuuraha SOMCAS, adeegyada canshuuraha dhijitaalka ah iyo dib-u-habeynta maamulka maaliyadda guud. Ra’iisul Wasaare Xamse Cabdi Barre ayaa sheegay in dowlad-goboleedyadu heleen taageeradii maaliyadeed ee ugu badnayd intii lagu jiray sannadkii 2025. Wuxuu tilmaamay in dowladda federaalku ay doonayso in dakhliga iyo kheyraadka qaranka loo adeegsado xoojinta adeegyada bulshada ee gobollada dalka. Dowladda ayaa sidoo kale sheegtay inaysan qaadan deyn cusub tan iyo markii Soomaaliya loo dhammeystiray barnaamijka deyn-cafinta. Wasaaradda Maaliyadda ayaa sheegtay inay diyaarinayso istiraatiijiyad iyo sharciyo lagu nidaaminayo amaah kasta oo mustaqbalka loo qaato horumarinta kaabayaasha dhaqaalaha. xogta la shaaciyey kuma jirin jadwal muujinaya dakhliga sannad kasta, ilaha kororka ama lacagaha la gaarsiiyey dowlad-goboleed kasta.

items.title: US counterterrorism officials are replicating their Pakistan mistakes in Somaliland
items.description: The idea that supporting Somaliland means sacrificing Somalia’s cooperation rests on foolish assumptions and inherently highlights how poor the partnership with Mogadishu is. By Michael Rubin, Middle East Forum President Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi (“Irro”) continues his visit to the United States, with a heavy schedule of government and think tank meetings in Washington.Still, the drive for U.S. recognition of Somaliland appears to be stalled. While the Trump administration remains tight-lipped, insiders place the blame on two offices: One is Deputy Secretary of State Chris Landau, who, short of being told otherwise, is unwilling to buck a Mogadishu-centric policy that dates to Secretary of State Hillary Clinton. The other block reportedly is the National Security Council’s counterterrorism office. Officials there worry that recognition of Somaliland will undercut ongoing U.S. counterterrorism cooperation with Somalia. The U.S. military long has deployed trainers and special operators to Somalia to bolster that country’s fight against Al Shabaab and to help support African Union peacekeepers. While President Donald Trump withdrew U.S. forces from Somalia during his first term, President Joe Biden returned them after he took office. There reportedly are small contingents of U.S. troops at the Baledogle airfield, an old Italian base, inland from Mogadishu, and some U.S. personnel reportedly operate in the Halane compound area they share with the United Nations and African Union missions. There also reportedly are some Navy SEALS and other special operators in Bosaso and Kismayo. There have been, at least temporarily, U.S. personnel in Baidoa, Dhusamareb, and Jowhar. Inaddition, U.S. military and intelligence officials increasingly support the counterterrorism mission from Camp Lemonier in Djibouti, Kenya, and Somaliland itself. There have been two main targets for U.S. action: the Islamic State encampment in the Golis Mountains in Puntland, near Bosaso, and the broader fight against Al Shabaab. The idea that supporting Somaliland means sacrificing Somalia’s cooperation rests on foolish assumptions and inherently highlights how poor the partnership with Mogadishu is. First, consider Puntland and the fight against the Islamic State. Puntland resents the federal government in Mogadishu because Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud—selected, rather than elected, and now past his constitutional term—rejects the federal rights of states like Puntland. Although Puntland and Somaliland are rivals and have a border dispute, they also cooperate. While Puntland remains in the federal government for now, Mogadishu’s centralization drive is as likely to force Puntland to follow Somaliland’s path as it is to bring Puntland to heel. Nor does it make sense that Puntland would stop assistance containing and countering the Islamic State. While some Somali officials and the Turkish intelligence officials who support them dream they can leverage the Islamic State against Somaliland, Puntland is unlikely to stop counterterrorism cooperation. Its capital, Garowe, is a sleepy, inland town, ironically dependent on Somaliland trade; Puntland’s broader economic future rests with its Bosaso port, located just 44 miles from the Islamic State Somaliland’s mountain headquarters. Somalia’s cooperation with Al Shabaab is trickier. While Al Shabaab threatens President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s appointed government, the president’s corruption ensures that even the U.S.-trained Danab Special Forces cannot win. Meanwhile, the Turkish-trained Gorgor unit is as likely to support Al Shabaab as to fight its members. Repeatedly, Hassan Sheikh Mohamud has shown himself more willing to deploy Somali forces against his political competitors or federal state challengers than to defeat the Islamists. Today, it is impossible to run a business or construct a building in Mogadishu without an Al Shabaab permit. Somalis are more willing to trust Al Shabaab justice than state courts due to the speed of operation and perceived lack of corruption. In effect, the pattern in Somalia now is akin to what the United States experiences in Pakistan. As Washington shelled out billions of dollars to support Pakistani counterterror efforts, it created a moral hazard in which continuation of lucrative military assistance required that Pakistani forces never completely defeat the Taliban, Al Qaeda, or other radial Deobandi groups. If the National Security Council believes defeating Al Shabaab requires sacrificing the aspirations of democratic, pro-West, and secure Somaliland and winning the good graces of a Mogadishu government that repeatedly has shown itself to be little more than a Chinese puppet and a Turkish satrapy, Americans will die. Counterterrorism cooperation and extortion are not synonymous. The only way to truly secure the Gulf of Aden and, eventually, roll back Al Shabaab’s gains in Somalia will be to recognize and partner with Somaliland, then to consolidate security in Puntland and Jubaland, and finally to extricate and then deal with Al Shabaab, despite Mogadishu rather than necessarily in partnership with it. Source Worldisraelnews

There reportedly are small contingents of U.S. troops at the Baledogle airfield, an old Italian base, inland from Mogadishu, and some U.S. personnel reportedly operate in the Halane compound area they share with the United Nations and African Union missions. There also reportedly are some Navy SEALS and other special operators in Bosaso and Kismayo. There have been, at least temporarily, U.S. personnel in Baidoa, Dhusamareb, and Jowhar. Inaddition, U.S. military and intelligence officials increasingly support the counterterrorism mission from Camp Lemonier in Djibouti, Kenya, and Somaliland itself. There have been two main targets for U.S. action: the Islamic State encampment in the Golis Mountains in Puntland, near Bosaso, and the broader fight against Al Shabaab. The idea that supporting Somaliland means sacrificing Somalia’s cooperation rests on foolish assumptions and inherently highlights how poor the partnership with Mogadishu is. First, consider Puntland and the fight against the Islamic State. Puntland resents the federal government in Mogadishu because Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud—selected, rather than elected, and now past his constitutional term—rejects the federal rights of states like Puntland. Although Puntland and Somaliland are rivals and have a border dispute, they also cooperate. While Puntland remains in the federal government for now, Mogadishu’s centralization drive is as likely to force Puntland to follow Somaliland’s path as it is to bring Puntland to heel. Nor does it make sense that Puntland would stop assistance containing and countering the Islamic State. While some Somali officials and the Turkish intelligence officials who support them dream they can leverage the Islamic State against Somaliland, Puntland is unlikely to stop counterterrorism cooperation. Its capital, Garowe, is a sleepy, inland town, ironically dependent on Somaliland trade; Puntland’s broader economic future rests with its Bosaso port, located just 44 miles from the Islamic State Somaliland’s mountain headquarters. Somalia’s cooperation with Al Shabaab is trickier. While Al Shabaab threatens President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s appointed government, the president’s corruption ensures that even the U.S.-trained Danab Special Forces cannot win. Meanwhile, the Turkish-trained Gorgor unit is as likely to support Al Shabaab as to fight its members. Repeatedly, Hassan Sheikh Mohamud has shown himself more willing to deploy Somali forces against his political competitors or federal state challengers than to defeat the Islamists. Today, it is impossible to run a business or construct a building in Mogadishu without an Al Shabaab permit. Somalis are more willing to trust Al Shabaab justice than state courts due to the speed of operation and perceived lack of corruption. In effect, the pattern in Somalia now is akin to what the United States experiences in Pakistan. As Washington shelled out billions of dollars to support Pakistani counterterror efforts, it created a moral hazard in which continuation of lucrative military assistance required that Pakistani forces never completely defeat the Taliban, Al Qaeda, or other radial Deobandi groups. If the National Security Council believes defeating Al Shabaab requires sacrificing the aspirations of democratic, pro-West, and secure Somaliland and winning the good graces of a Mogadishu government that repeatedly has shown itself to be little more than a Chinese puppet and a Turkish satrapy, Americans will die. Counterterrorism cooperation and extortion are not synonymous. The only way to truly secure the Gulf of Aden and, eventually, roll back Al Shabaab’s gains in Somalia will be to recognize and partner with Somaliland, then to consolidate security in Puntland and Jubaland, and finally to extricate and then deal with Al Shabaab, despite Mogadishu rather than necessarily in partnership with it. items.title: How Somalia’s Flag Was Sold to Turkey
items.description: By Isha Qarsoon On the night of September 9, 2026, drones struck a tugboat named TEDY near Odesa, Ukraine . The vessel was hit again as it tried to reach Constanta. Two Azerbaijani crew members were killed and two suffered burns. Its ten-person crew included Azerbaijani, Turkish, German and Ukrainian nationals. Mert Marine Corporation, a Turkish company, owned the tug. TEDY sailed under the Somali flag. No Somali was aboard. [1] Ukraine’s government blamed Russia and described the attack as part of a wider campaign against civilian shipping. Russia’s Defence Ministry said it had struck two cargo vessels and a tugboat near Odesa, alleging that the ships were carrying military supplies. It did not identify TEDY, and the connection between its statement and the attack has not been independently confirmed. Azerbaijan did not attribute responsibility. The competing accounts do not change the point. A Turkish-owned vessel with an entirely foreign crew carried Somali nationality into a European war. The attack does not prove that the registry was inappropriate. A ship under any flag can be attacked in a war. Also, a ship crew does not have to include nationals of the flag it is sailing under. The attack exposes, however, the scale of the risk Somalia accepted: within months of reviving its ship registry, Somali nationality appeared on a foreign-owned ship with a foreign crew operating in a European conflict. Somalia acquired the flag state’s legal duties and reputational exposure without acquiring control of the voyage. The Turkish ownership was not incidental: Turkish interests already run Somalia’s main port and airport, train and help command its military, hold rights to its offshore oil and fish stocks, and now operate the very registry that flagged TEDY in the first place. TEDY is the trigger for examining what happens when that system is abused. What a flag of convenience is The term flag of convenience entered common use in the 1950s. American owners had used Panama between the two world wars to avoid domestic taxes, labour rules and crewing requirements. Liberia opened its international registry in 1948, and Honduras later joined the historical group known as PanLibHon. A flag of convenience generally describes a vessel registered in a country other than the country of its beneficial ownership or commercial control, often to reduce costs or avoid stricter regulation. A 1970 British government inquiry identified six common features of flag of convenience: foreign ownership or control, easy registration and withdrawal, low taxation, a registry maintained mainly for fee income rather than national shipping needs, unrestricted foreign crews, and limited capacity or willingness to enforce shipping rules.[3] These are descriptive indicators, not a binding legal test. Somalia’s new registry displays several of those features. On March 30, 2026, Abdulkadir Mohamed Nur, then minister of ports and marine transport, signed a memorandum with Somali Ship Register Limited, represented by Turkish national Cagdas Oykun Saltas. On April 2, 2026, the government announced GUNEY as the first vessel admitted under the revived flag. It was foreign-owned or controlled, had just left the Honduran flag, and was registered while in Turkey.[2] The memorandum was signed on March 30, 2026, and Guney entered the register three days later, on April 2. That interval is too short for an owner unfamiliar with a newly created registry to locate it, complete a flag change out of Honduras, and clear administrative review. It indicates the vessel’s move to the Somali flag was arranged before the memorandum was signed, not decided afterward, which means the registry and its first customer were not two separate developments but one planned transaction presented as two. The September attack revealed that TEDY, another Turkish-owned vessel, was flying the Somali flag.[1] The public record establishes that Somalia opened its nationality to foreign shipping through a foreign private operator before publishing how that operator would be supervised. Private administration is not automatically disreputable. Liberia and the Marshall Islands show that an overseas administrator can coexist with effective state regulation. Somalia’s problem is the political setting. The registry entered a relationship in which Turkey and Turkish-linked bodies already occupy Somalia’s airport, port, military and maritime security, petroleum, fisheries licensing and prospective minerals.[8] In that setting, abuse cannot be treated as a remote possibility to be considered after the first scandal. It is the working risk that should govern the registry. The burden belongs on the government to prove that Somali officials can refuse, suspend and deregister a ship against Turkish commercial or political pressure. The duties stay with Somalia Article 91 of the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea requires a genuine link between a ship and the state whose flag it flies. Article 94 requires the flag state to exercise effective jurisdiction and control over administrative, technical and social matters. Those duties include maintaining a register, enforcing safety and crewing standards, and investigating serious casualties.[4] A private registrar may process applications, collect fees and arrange surveys. It cannot take Somalia’s international responsibility with it. UNCLOS’s genuine-link rule offers less protection than its wording suggests. In M/V Saiga, the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea held that the absence of an effective link does not, by itself, allow another state to refuse recognition of a vessel’s nationality. Coastal and port states retain enforcement powers under other rules, but they cannot erase the Somali flag simply because Somalia fails to control the ship. UNCLOS therefore leaves the main burden where Somalia placed it: on Somalia. What abuse would cost Somalia The first cost is damage to the flag’s reputation. A poorly maintained vessel may be detained because of its own deficiencies. The Paris Memorandum of Understanding on Port State Control coordinates inspections of foreign ships entering participating European and North Atlantic ports. It classifies flags according to their inspection and detention records over a rolling three-year period. A flag enters the white, grey or black list only after at least thirty inspections. Once that threshold is met, repeated deficiencies and detentions can push the flag into a worse category and subject other vessels flying it to greater scrutiny.[5] Reputable owners then face higher inspection, insurance and chartering costs merely for carrying the same flag. The fastest customers to leave are often the ones Somalia should want to keep. The second cost is loss of control over who claims Somali nationality. The International Maritime Organization has documented fraudulent registrations and unauthorized use of flags, including several African flags targeted by vessels seeking a permissive or unverifiable identity.[6] A new international registry with opaque records is attractive to operators fleeing another flag, concealing ownership, manipulating vessel identities or avoiding scrutiny. If Somalia cannot publish and verify its register in real time, foreign authorities and commercial databases will struggle to distinguish a valid Somali ship from a fraudulent one. Both damage the same name. The third cost is sanctions exposure. The US Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control administers sanctions in support of United States foreign policy and national security. A Somali flag provides no immunity when a vessel, owner, manager, or service provider is subject to a US sanctions program. OFAC has warned that helping a blocked carrier reflag its vessels may constitute providing services to a blocked person and may itself support designation.[7] Misconduct by one vessel would not automatically subject Somalia or its registry to sanctions. It could nevertheless associate the Somali flag with weak screening, increase scrutiny of other vessels flying it, and discourage reputable owners from using the registry. The remaining costs are practical and political. Unsafe ships injure crews. Uninsured ships leave pollution and wreck-removal claims behind. Deceptive ships switch off tracking, falsify cargo papers or move sanctioned oil and weapons. Ships trading near wars pull the flag state into disputes it did not create. Each event demands records, investigation, cooperation and enforcement from Mogadishu. If the Somali government cannot or will not act against a vessel admitted by a Turkish operator, Somalia carries the liability while foreign owners and managers keep the commercial benefit. The control question The registry memorandum has not been published. The public therefore cannot see who has final authority over admission, beneficial-ownership checks, sanctions screening, surveyors, casualty investigations, suspension, deregistration, data and audits. Even if there is no public evidence that Ankara formally directs Somali Ship Register Limited, formal instructions are not the only measure of control. When a government already depends on the same foreign partner across its principal gateways, security and resources, the registrar’s independence cannot simply be presumed. Nur, who signed the registry memorandum and invited international owners to use the flag, later became Speaker of the House of the People. The issue is larger than one official. Somalia has built a structure in which the state must police ships brought to it through a relationship it may be politically unable to challenge. That conflict is exactly how a flag of convenience becomes dangerous: enforcement against a ship can also become a confrontation with the power behind the registry. Conclusion TEDY is a warning of potential misconduct. It shows how quickly Somalia’s legal identity can travel far beyond Somali commerce, territory or control. The next case may involve sanctions evasion, pollution, crew abuse, false registration or a voyage that serves a foreign war. By the time that case arrives, the cost will already carry Somalia’s name. The government licensed use of its flag through a Turkish-run company inside a relationship already marked by extreme dependence. Before more ships are admitted, Somalia should publish the memorandum and the live register, keep final registration and deregistration authority in accountable Somali hands, require independent ownership and sanctions screening, audit the operator, and fund the investigations and enforcement required by UNCLOS. Without those safeguards, Somalia will collect registration fees while assuming legal, diplomatic and reputational risks it cannot control. That is the harm an abused flag of convenience can do. items.title: The Battle for Marib Could Echo Across the Red Sea and Horn of Africa
items.description: Adan, Yemen (WDN) — Marib is a strategically and geopolitically important city in Yemen and a key part of the conflict-affected Red Sea region; if Marib were to fall, the consequences could extend well beyond Yemen’s borders, with wider implications for regional security and stability A Houthi breakthrough in this strategic oil- and gas-producing region could send a new shockwave across the Red Sea, placing Djibouti, Eritrea and Somalia directly in the path of a rapidly changing security threat. What begins as a battle for one Yemeni governorate could ultimately become a battle over the security of an entire maritime region. Marib is far more than another battlefield in Yemen’s seemingly endless war. The governorate remains one of the most important strongholds of Yemen’s internationally recognized government and contains significant oil and natural-gas resources. Whoever controls Marib gains territory, economic resources, military depth and considerable political leverage. That is precisely why the battle for Marib matters beyond Yemen. The Houthis already control Yemen’s capital, Sana’a, as well as large parts of the country’s north and west. A major Houthi advance into Marib would strengthen their position considerably, potentially giving them greater access to resources while consolidating their control over much of northern Yemen. But the strategic consequences would not necessarily stop at Yemen’s borders. Yemen sits across the water from the Horn of Africa, separated from Djibouti, Eritrea and Somalia by some of the world’s most strategically important maritime routes. As the military balance inside Yemen changes, so too can the security calculations surrounding the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden. The connection begins with geography. From Marib, a strengthened Houthi movement could consolidate its military position across northern Yemen and maintain greater pressure toward the country’s western coastline. Along that coastline lies the Red Sea, and beyond it the narrow maritime passage of Bab el-Mandeb, the gateway connecting the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and the wider Indian Ocean. Marib therefore does not need to be physically close to Bab el-Mandeb to matter to its security. What matters is what control of Marib could do to the overall military balance inside Yemen. The stronger the Houthis become, the greater their potential ability to influence developments along Yemen’s western coast. And the more militarized that coastline becomes, the greater the pressure on one of the world’s most important shipping corridors. That is where the concerns of neighboring African countries become particularly acute. For Djibouti, Yemen is not a distant conflict. The two countries sit almost face-to-face across the Red Sea. Djibouti has built much of its economy around ports, shipping and logistics and hosts military facilities belonging to several international powers. Its prosperity and strategic importance depend heavily on the security of the surrounding maritime environment. A worsening conflict in Yemen could therefore impose new security costs on Djibouti, from increased maritime surveillance to greater protection of ports and commercial vessels. Eritrea faces a different but equally important exposure. Its long Red Sea coastline places it directly within the broader strategic environment created by the conflict in Yemen. Greater military activity along Yemen’s western coast could increase concerns about weapons trafficking, maritime crime and the security of commercial shipping. For Asmara, what happens across the water can quickly become a matter of national security. Then there is Somalia. Somalia’s coastline stretches along the Gulf of Aden, directly connecting the country to the maritime consequences of instability in Yemen. items.title: Baidoa War Deepens as Former South West President Laftagareen Accuses Hassan Sheikh, Aden Madoobe and Turkey of Targeting the Region
items.description: Baidoa (WDN) — Somalia’s political crisis has increasingly taken on the character of an armed confrontation in and around Baidoa, with forces aligned with former South West State President Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen accusing the Federal Government of using national security forces and Turkish military support to consolidate control over the regional capital. The latest accusations came from Ugaas Hassan Mohamed, spokesperson for Laftagareen-aligned forces, who launched a strong attack on President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, South West State President Aden Mohamed Nur (Aden Madoobe) and Turkey over their roles in the unfolding conflict. Ugaas Hassan accused the Federal Government and the current South West State leadership of treating communities that support Laftagareen as adversaries, alleging that military operations and reported airstrikes have increasingly affected communities around Baidoa. He also claimed that authorities were pressuring residents to support Turkey and alleged that President Hassan Sheikh intends to expand the Turkish military presence in Baidoa, including the use of F-16 aircraft and drones. The allegations have not been independently verified, and neither the Federal Government nor Turkey has publicly confirmed the specific claims concerning air operations against civilian areas. The dispute itself, however, reflects a much deeper struggle over the political future of South West State. Laftagareen lost control of the South West presidency following the political and military developments that brought Aden Madoobe to power. Since then, Laftagareen has remained a powerful opposition figure, with his supporters rejecting the legitimacy of the current regional administration and resisting what they describe as federal interference in South West State affairs. The confrontation has therefore evolved beyond a conventional dispute between rival politicians. It has become a struggle between the Federal Government and its allies in Baidoa on one side, and Laftagareen’s political and armed supporters on the other. For residents caught in the middle, the distinction between political rivalry and military confrontation has become increasingly difficult to ignore. Growing Allegations Over Turkish Military Support The most controversial element of the conflict is the alleged role of Turkey. Laftagareen’s supporters accuse Ankara of providing military assistance to federal and South West forces operating against them, including alleged air support. Turkish involvement has become particularly contentious because Ankara has traditionally presented its security partnership with Somalia as support for national institutions and the fight against Al-Shabaab. If foreign military capabilities are perceived by local communities as being used in an internal political confrontation, the consequences could extend well beyond Baidoa. It could deepen resentment toward both the Federal Government and Turkey while making an already complicated political settlement considerably more difficult. “We Will Resist” Ugaas Hassan said forces aligned with Laftagareen would continue resisting what he described as an externally supported military campaign. “As long as our South West Darawiish forces remain capable and ready to confront the forces that have invaded our territory—with Aden Madoobe and Hassan Sheikh leading them and Turkey providing air support—we will, God willing, drive them out,” he said. He also described Turkey as a company allegedly “hired” by President Hassan Sheikh and warned residents of South West State against what he characterized as Ankara’s growing involvement. The comments demonstrate how sharply the political narrative has shifted. A dispute that initially centered on regional leadership and federal authority has increasingly become intertwined with military power and foreign security assistance. Civilians Caught in the Middle For ordinary residents around Baidoa, the political arguments between Mogadishu, the Aden Madoobe administration and Laftagareen’s camp are increasingly being experienced through insecurity, displacement and disruption to daily life. The central question is no longer simply who has the stronger political claim to South West State. It is whether the dispute can be resolved politically before the confrontation causes further damage to civilians and institutions. For the Federal Government, the challenge is to demonstrate that its military presence is directed toward legitimate national security objectives rather than political consolidation. For Laftagareen and his supporters, the challenge is to translate their opposition into a credible political strategy capable of competing for legitimacy without further destabilizing the region. Until that happens, Baidoa is likely to remain at the center of one of Somalia’s most dangerous political confrontations—one in which the struggle for regional power increasingly carries consequences far beyond the political arena. items.title: Somaliland’s president puts everything on the table for Trump
items.description: Somaliland’s president is putting almost everything on the table in his campaign to win US recognition for the breakaway territory of Somalia, offering US investors access to a strategically located port and mineral resources while leaving open the possibility of expanded military access.ĺ “We are not giving anything for free,” Abdirahman Mohamed Abdullahi “Irro” said in an interview with Semafor in Washington. “We have to offer something. And we expect the other partner [to have] the same or equal opportunities.” Recognition is the prize, but economic cooperation, trade and investment can proceed in parallel. Somaliland can offer “our facilities and our minerals,” he said. The US already has a military relationship with Somaliland, including training and security cooperation, but no military base there. The head of US Africa Command visited Hargeisa and Berbera last year as Washington continued to assess the territory’s strategic importance. Irro is signaling that the relationship could go further. Military access for the US, Israel or other countries, he said, “is a negotiation.” “I will not rule out,” he said of a future base agreement, arguing that any deal would depend on what Somaliland receives in return, including greater security and support for its forces. Israel’s recognition in December changed the diplomatic equation on Somaliland’s status. It gave the breakaway territory its first recognition from a UN member state and, more importantly, demonstrated that the decades-old consensus against recognizing the territory could be broken. Irro is now trying to turn that breakthrough into momentum. He is spending this week in Washington pressing his case at the White House and on Capitol Hill before heading to New York, where he hopes to meet other world leaders during the UN General Assembly and make the case for recognition. The US is the next prize. Irro described America as the “big fish” Somaliland wants to pursue. “The earlier, the better is always better,” he said. His appeal is also tailored to Trump. Somaliland could name Berbera’s airport after him, Irro suggested, or welcome him to build a Trump Tower in Hargeisa. The message underneath the flattery is more consequential since Somaliland is no longer simply making a historical or moral case for recognition. Irro is trying to show Washington what recognition could buy. Room for Disagreement Somalia sees the proposition very differently. Mogadishu rejects Somaliland’s claim to sovereignty and considers Berbera, its coastline and its resources part of Somalia. That makes Irro’s offer of strategic and commercial access politically contested before any foreign government or company accepts it. Israel’s recognition has sharpened that dispute, turning Somaliland’s push for wider recognition into a more consequential challenge to Somalia’s territorial claims. Know More Geography is central to Irro’s proposition. Berbera sits on the Gulf of Aden, close to the Bab el-Mandeb, the narrow maritime gateway between the Red Sea and the Indian Ocean. As conflict and disruption have put renewed pressure on the region’s sea lanes, Somaliland sees an opportunity to turn its location into diplomatic leverage. Diego Garcia, the US military facility in the central Indian Ocean, lies thousands of kilometers away from the Red Sea theater. Berbera offers a far closer location for logistics, resupply or other military operations around the Gulf of Aden and Bab el-Mandab, even if it would not simply replace the much larger US presence on Diego Garcia. Irro argued that American officials understand that strategic case. “They know that,” he said, pointing to US training and security cooperation already taking place in Somaliland. His offer is deliberately open-ended. Somaliland is not announcing a new US base; it is signaling that greater access could be negotiated. “We are not giving anything for free,” Irro said, returning to the transactional logic behind his recognition campaign. Step Back Irro is also trying to sell Somaliland as an economic opportunity rather than simply a strategic outpost. He points to Berbera’s port and free zone, an 850-kilometer coastline, fisheries and potentially significant oil, gas and mineral resources. Somaliland’s government budget has risen from less than $50 million when he became parliament speaker in 2005 to about $500 million today, he said. The ambition is considerably bigger. Irro said Somaliland could be “very rich” within a decade and claimed its budget could eventually reach $3 billion-$4 billion a year if its marine economy and other resources are developed. Recognition, in his view, would help unlock that potential by making it easier for US and other international investors to treat Somaliland as a conventional investment destination rather than an unrecognized territory. The View From China Irro’s push for US recognition does not mean he wants Somaliland locked into a single geopolitical camp. Taiwan’s representative office will remain in Hargeisa despite Beijing’s opposition. “We have decided Taiwan to remain,” Irro said, noting that Taiwan was already present when he took office. China is still welcome to invest. “If China is coming without condition, we will welcome China,” he said. Chinese companies already operate in Somaliland, he added. The line Irro draws is political saying no foreign power will decide Somaliland’s diplomatic relationships. “Nobody can dictate to us,” he said. SEMAFOR

items.title: Soomaaliya oo si adag u cambaareysay weerar diyaaradeed oo la isku dayay in lagu qaado Makkah
items.description: Muqdisho, 16 Sebtembar 2026 — Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa si adag u cambaareysay isku day weerar loo adeegsaday diyaarad aan duuliye lahayn (drone), kaas oo lagu beegsaday magaalada barakeysan ee Makkah Al-Mukarramah ee Boqortooyada Sacuudiga. Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda iyo Iskaashiga Caalamiga ah ee Soomaaliya ayaa sheegtay in Ciidamada Difaaca Cirka ee Boqortooyada Sacuudiga ay ku guuleysteen inay dhexda u galaan oo ay qabtaan diyaaraddii aan duuliyaha lahayn ka hor inta aysan gaarin magaalada Makkah. Soomaaliya ayaa sidoo kale cambaareysay weerarradii dhowaan lagu qaaday goobaha rayidka ah ee gudaha Boqortooyada Sacuudiga. War-saxaafadeedka Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda ayaa lagu sheegay in Soomaaliya ay muujineyso garab istaag buuxa oo ay la garab taagan tahay Boqortooyada Sacuudiga, iyadoo xaqiijisay xaqa Boqortooyada ay u leedahay inay ilaaliso dhulkeeda, dadkeeda iyo goobaha barakeysan ee Islaamka.

items.title: Baidoa’s Pro-Türkiye Rally Raises Questions as Ankara’s Image in Somalia Comes Under Strain
items.description: Baidoa (WDN) — Three days after reports of alleged Turkish airstrikes around Baidoa—and less than two weeks after anti-Türkiye protests erupted elsewhere in Somalia—a crowd gathered in the city on Tuesday, September 15, waving Turkish flags and praising Ankara. The timing could hardly be more striking. Hundreds of people gathered at Dr. Ayuub Stadium, carrying Turkish and Somali flags and expressing support for the longstanding relationship between Somalia and Türkiye. Organizers described the event as a demonstration of gratitude for Turkish assistance in security, development and humanitarian affairs. But the rally took place against a dramatically changed political backdrop. On September 12, reports emerged of alleged Turkish airstrikes around Baidoa, including claims of casualties and damage. The reports have not been independently verified, and neither Türkiye nor the Federal Government has publicly confirmed responsibility. The demonstration also came less than two weeks after the September 3–4 Doolow incident, when Jubaland officials accused Turkish aircraft of striking the residence of former Somali security commander General Mahad Abdirahman “Taliye Shub.” The allegations triggered protests in several parts of Somalia, including demonstrations in which Turkish flags were reportedly burned. The Federal Government disputed elements of the account, while Türkiye has not publicly acknowledged responsibility for the alleged strike. Critics question whether Tuesday’s gathering represented spontaneous public enthusiasm or a politically organized effort to demonstrate that Ankara still enjoys popular support. Some political opponents allege that former Speaker Sheikh Aden Mohamed Nur “Aden Madoobe” and political allies associated with the current South West administration helped organize or finance the rally. The allegation is politically significant because Turkish military assistance has become increasingly entangled with the confrontation surrounding Baidoa and the forces aligned with the Federal Government. There is, however, no independent evidence publicly establishing that Aden Madoobe personally financed the demonstration. The claim should therefore be treated as an allegation rather than an established fact. A Relationship Under Pressure For years, Türkiye enjoyed an unusually positive image in Somalia. Erdoğan’s visits, Turkish humanitarian assistance, infrastructure projects, scholarships, health services and military cooperation helped establish Ankara as one of Somalia’s most prominent international partners. The Turkish flag was widely associated with friendship and solidarity. That image is now under pressure. Protests and flag-burning incidents reported in recent weeks suggest that Türkiye’s military role has become increasingly controversial among sections of the Somali public. The dispute is no longer simply about development assistance or diplomatic relations. It is increasingly about whether Ankara has become involved in Somalia’s internal political and security conflicts. That distinction matters. Türkiye has trained Somali forces, provided military equipment and developed an extensive defense relationship with the Federal Government. Turkish armed drones have also been associated with Somalia’s counterterrorism campaign. But when Turkish aircraft or drones are alleged to have been used in operations connected to domestic political confrontations, the perception of Ankara’s role changes. A security partnership can quickly become a political liability if communities begin to associate it with controversial military operations. Why Baidoa Is Different Baidoa is at the center of that controversy. The city has become a major arena in the confrontation between the Federal Government and forces associated with former South West President Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen. As a result, Turkish military involvement in or around the region is being interpreted through an increasingly political lens. For Federal Government supporters, Ankara remains a strategic partner helping rebuild Somalia’s security institutions and combat Al-Shabaab. For opponents, the same military relationship has become evidence of foreign involvement in Somalia’s internal political struggle. The September 15 rally therefore carries significance beyond the crowd gathered at the stadium. Its timing raises questions about whether the demonstration was intended, at least in part, to counter the growing backlash against Türkiye and reinforce the image of a continuing Somalia–Türkiye partnership. The Bigger Question for Ankara A single demonstration cannot determine public opinion across Somalia. Nor can photographs of people waving Turkish flags erase the anger expressed in other parts of the country. The more consequential question is whether Türkiye can maintain its longstanding relationship with Somalia while avoiding the perception that it has become aligned with one side of the country’s increasingly polarized political landscape. That challenge is particularly acute because Türkiye’s influence in Somalia has been built on two pillars: development and security. The first created goodwill. The second now risks becoming the source of controversy. For Ankara, the distinction between supporting Somalia’s national security institutions and becoming involved in Somalia’s internal political disputes will therefore be increasingly important. For Mogadishu, the issue is equally sensitive. Foreign military assistance may strengthen the government’s capabilities, but if that assistance becomes identified with one faction in a domestic confrontation, it can deepen political divisions rather than resolve them. And for ordinary Somalis, the contrast is increasingly difficult to miss. In Baidoa, Turkish flags were raised on September 15. Elsewhere, they were burned. That is not simply a contradiction between two demonstrations. It is evidence of a relationship undergoing a profound political test. The Somalia–Türkiye friendship that once appeared almost unquestionable is now being debated in the streets—and its future may depend less on official speeches than on how Somalis perceive Ankara’s actions on the ground. Hundreds of people gathered at Dr. Ayuub Stadium, carrying Turkish and Somali flags and expressing support for the longstanding relationship between Somalia and Türkiye. Organizers described the event as a demonstration of gratitude for Turkish assistance in security, development and humanitarian affairs. items.title: Dhuumaha shidaalka Sacuudiga oo qaarkood waxyeello la gaarsiiyay
items.description: Riyadh (Caasimada Online) – Laba xarumood oo ku yaalla dhuumaha shidaalka ee isku xira bariga iyo galbeedka Sacuudiga ayaa waxyeello kasoo gaartay weerar toddobaadkii hore lagu qaaday, sida ay sheegtay Reuters oo soo xigatay ilo-wareedyo ka tirsan dhinacyada shidaalka iyo amniga. Dhuumahaasi oo dhererkoodu ku dhow yahay 1,200 oo kilomitir ayaa mara guud ahaan Jasiiradda Carabta, waxaana maamusha shirkadda Sacuudiga ee Aramco. Dhuumahan ayaa muhiimad gaar ah u leh dhoofinta iyo gaadiidka shidaalka Sacuudiga, maadaama ay shidaalka ka gudbiyaan bariga dalka, oo ah halka ugu weyn ee wax-soo-saarka, una gudbiyaan dhanka galbeed, si looga fogaado in maraakiibtu maraan Marinka Hormuz. Saddex ilo-wareed oo Reuters la hadashay ayaa sheegay in labada xarumood ay waxyeello kasoo gaartay weerarka, inkastoo aan si rasmi ah loo shaacin heerka uu gaarsiisan yahay khasaaraha soo gaaray kaabayaasha. Mas’uuliyiin Sacuudi ah ayaa horey u sheegay in shaqada dhuumaha si ku-meel-gaar ah loo hakiyay Jimcihii, kadib markii weerar loo adeegsaday diyaarad aan duuliye lahayn laga soo qaaday dhulka Ciraaq. Hakinta shaqada dhuumaha ayaa kusoo aadeysa xilli kaabayaasha shidaalka ee gobolka ay wajahayaan khataro amni oo sii kordhaya, gaar ahaan iyadoo ay socdaan xiisado saameynaya maraakiibta iyo isu-socodka shidaalka ee gobolka. Dhuumaha isku xira bariga iyo galbeedka Sacuudiga ayaa ah marin istiraatiiji ah oo dalka u saamaxaya inuu qayb ka mid ah shidaalkiisa u gudbiyo xeebaha Badda Cas, taas oo muhiim u ah yareynta ku-tiirsanaanta marinnada maraakiibta ee dhinaca Gacanka. Dhanka kale, Aramco iyo xafiiska warbaahinta dowladda Sacuudiga ayaan weli ka jawaabin codsi lagu weydiiyay baaxadda khasaaraha iyo muddada ay qaadan karto dayactirka xarumaha waxyeelloobay. Weerarkan ayaa kusoo aadaya xilli milatariga Sacuudiga uu la tacaalayo weerarro ay fulinayaan diyaarado aan duuliye lahayn oo ay Xuutiyiintu soo direen, iyadoo xiisadda u dhexeysa labada dhinac ay kasii dareyso.
