items.title: Jubaland Protests; Put Turkey’s Longstanding Somalia Partnership Under New Political Strain
items.description: Kismaayo (WDN) — Streets in Kismaayo and Doolow have become the latest stage for Somalia’s deepening political confrontation, as protesters rallied against the Federal Government and expressed anger toward Turkey, a country that has spent more than a decade building one of Somalia’s closest and most consequential foreign partnerships. Demonstrations were held in Kismaayo on Friday in an event reportedly organized with the involvement of the Jubaland administration. Similar protests were also reported in Doolow and Garbahaarey, following the attack two nights earlier on the residence of General Mahad Abdirahman “Shub.” The demonstrations reflected growing anger over the Doolow incident, which has become politically charged amid competing claims about who was responsible. The Federal Government has denied that the attack was carried out by an aerial strike. However, protesters in Jubaland reportedly expressed the belief that Turkey was involved, a view that appears to have been reinforced by statements from political figures aligned with Jubaland. The anger directed at Turkey is particularly striking because Ankara has developed an unusually deep relationship with Somalia since opening its major diplomatic mission in Mogadishu in 2011. Over the years, Turkey has become a major partner in Somalia’s humanitarian assistance, infrastructure development, education, health services and security sector. Turkish institutions have built schools and hospitals, provided humanitarian assistance and trained Somali security personnel. Turkey has also become one of the Federal Government’s most important security partners, making its military relationship with Mogadishu particularly sensitive whenever Somalia’s internal political disputes become intertwined with security operations. That is what makes the scenes in Kismaayo, Garbaharey and Doolow so significant. A country that once became one of Somalia’s most warmly received international partners is now seeing its national flag publicly rejected in Jubaland. From Friendship to Political Controversy The demonstrations demonstrate how quickly Somalia’s internal political divisions can spill over into attitudes toward foreign partners. For years, Turkey’s presence in Somalia was widely associated with development, humanitarian assistance and reconstruction. Its growing military role, however, has increasingly placed Ankara closer to the center of Somalia’s political and security disputes. The Doolow incident has brought that tension sharply into view. Protesters believe Turkey was connected to the attack, but those allegations have not been independently verified. The Federal Government has rejected claims that the incident involved an aerial bombardment. The competing narratives have nevertheless created a politically explosive environment in which Turkey’s role is becoming part of the wider dispute between Mogadishu and Jubaland. Perhaps the most unusual feature of the demonstrations was also the reported appearance—and burning—of the Egyptian flag, despite Egypt not being directly identified in the dispute described by the protesters. The unexpected symbolism has prompted speculation among political observers about whether outside actors could be attempting to influence or exploit the demonstrations. Some analysts have raised suspicions about possible Ethiopian involvement in the organization of the protests. There is, however, no independently verified evidence presented here establishing that Ethiopia organized or directed the demonstrations. The presence of an Egyptian flag therefore raises questions rather than providing answers. A Wider Regional Rivalry The episode is unfolding against a broader regional landscape in which Somalia has become an arena for competing strategic interests involving Turkey, Ethiopia, Egypt and other regional and international powers. Somalia’s location along the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden gives its political stability and security relationships importance far beyond its borders. For Turkey, Somalia represents one of Ankara’s most important footholds in Africa. For Ethiopia, developments inside Somalia have direct implications for border security and regional influence. Egypt, meanwhile, has its own strategic interests in the Horn of Africa and its long-running rivalry with Ethiopia. That makes any visible sign of foreign influence in a Somali political protest particularly sensitive. The protests in Kismaayo and Doolow should therefore not be viewed simply as isolated demonstrations over one security incident. They reflect a deeper question about how Somalia’s foreign partnerships are being perceived by different political constituencies inside the country. Turkey’s relationship with Somalia has survived governments, crises and changing political circumstances. But its increasingly visible security role means that Ankara can no longer easily remain outside Somalia’s political controversies. The irony is striking. Turkey built much of its influence in Somalia through an image of friendship, development and solidarity at a time when few other countries were visibly engaging with the country. Today, that same relationship is becoming entangled in Somalia’s increasingly bitter political and security disputes. The Doolow attack remains surrounded by competing accounts, and allegations of Turkish involvement require credible independent evidence. But the political symbolism of the protests is already clear. When Somali citizens begin burning the flag of a country that has spent years presenting itself as one of Somalia’s closest friends, the issue is no longer simply about one attack. It is a warning that even the deepest foreign partnership can become politically vulnerable when it is perceived as taking sides in Somalia’s internal struggles. items.title: Fahad Yasin Launches Explosive Attack on Somalia’s New Parliament Speaker
items.description: Mogadishu (WDN) — Former Somali intelligence chief Fahad Yasin has launched a pointed political attack on the newly elected Speaker of Somalia’s House of the People, Abdulqadir Mohamed Nur (Jaamac), accusing him—without naming him directly of being linked to two high-profile security operations separated by years of political upheaval. In a brief statement posted on Facebook, Fahad used pointed language and political insinuation that appeared to target the new parliamentary speaker. His remarks referenced the 2017 raid on the residence of opposition politician Abdirahman Abdishakur Warsame during the administration of former President Mohamed Abdullahi Farmaajo, as well as the recent drone attack in Doolow, which reportedly targeted the residence of General Mahad Abdirahman “Shub.” Fahad alleged that the same individual had played a leadership role in both incidents while serving in different positions of authority. “At one point, he served as acting intelligence chief and led the raid on Abdirahman Abdishakur’s residence. Later, he became acting president in a government that exceeded its mandate, and now he has led the drone attack in Doolow in which Commander Mahad Abdirahman (Shub) was targeted,” Fahad wrote. Although Fahad did not explicitly identify the person in his statement, the wording and references were widely interpreted as pointing toward Speaker Abdulqadir Mohamed Nur. The accusation is striking because it connects two politically sensitive moments in Somalia’s recent history with the current confrontation in Doolow. The 2017 raid on Abdishakur’s residence became one of the most controversial security operations of the Farmaajo era, while the Doolow incident has emerged amid a much deeper political confrontation involving the Federal Government, opposition figures and forces aligned with different political interests in South West State. Speaker Abdulkadir M Nur Fahad’s intervention therefore carries significance beyond a personal political dispute. His comments constitute an accusation, not evidence establishing that the Speaker directed or participated in either operation. The allegations would require independent verification and supporting evidence. A Remark Laden with Political Implications The remarks come shortly after Abdulqadir Mohamed Nur assumed the speakership of Somalia’s lower house, placing him at the center of the country’s increasingly polarized political environment. The Speaker now faces scrutiny from both supporters and opponents of the Federal Government as parliament becomes increasingly important in disputes over elections, constitutional changes and the balance of power between Mogadishu and Somalia’s federal states. Fahad’s statement adds another layer to that confrontation, raising questions about the Speaker’s past political and security roles and whether those experiences could influence his conduct in his new position. The extraordinary nature of the accusation lies in its timing. Rather than simply criticizing the Speaker’s political decisions, Fahad has sought to connect him symbolically to some of Somalia’s most contentious security episodes—turning the new parliamentary leadership into another battleground in the country’s widening political conflict. The allegations remain unproven. But the message is unmistakable: Somalia’s political war is no longer confined to parliament, elections or constitutional negotiations. The country’s past security battles are being pulled directly into today’s struggle for political power. items.title: Kulan Caawa Dhuusamareeb Ku Dhexmaray Musharraxa Xisbiga JSP Liibaan Axmed Xasan iyo Haweenka Caasimadda Galmudug
items.description: DHUUSAMAREEB (Goobjoog News) — Musharraxa u tartamaya doorashada ku-celiska ah ee Galmudug , Liibaan Axmed Xasan, ayaa caawa magaalada Dhuusamareeb ee caasimadda Galmudug kulan ballaaran kula yeeshay qaybaha kala duwan ee haweenka deegaanka. Kulanka ayaa si qoto dheer loogu lafa-guray xaaladda siyaasadeed ee maamulka, doorashada ku-celiska ah ee la filayo inay Galmudug ka dhacdo, iyo doorka lama-huraanka ah ee haweenku ku leeyihiin geeddi-socodka siyaasadda iyo dib-u-dhiska dowladnimada Galmudug. Liibaan Axmed Xasan ayaa bogaadiyay doorka muuqda ee haweenka Galmudug ay mar walba ka qaataan nabadeynta, dib-u-heshiisiinta bulshada, iyo horumarinta deegaanka, maadaama ay yihiin laf-dhabarta qoyska iyo bulshada. Musharraxa ayaa sidoo kale si dhow u dhageystay talooyinka, aragtiyaha, iyo baahiyaha aasaasiga ah ee ay haweenku mudnaanta siinayeen. Haweenka Caasimadda Dhuusamareeb ee madasha joogay ayaa dhankooda si cad u muujiyay taageerada buuxda ee ay u hayaan musharraxnimada Liibaan Axmed Xasan iyo barnaamijka siyaasadeed ee Xisbiga JSP, iyagoo soo bandhigay ajandaha iyo mudnaanta gaarka ah ee ay rabaan in hoggaanka cusub uu wax ka qabto. Ugu dambeyntii, Musharrax Liibaan Axmed Xasan ayaa hoosta ka xariiqay in ka-qaybgalka haweenku uu yahay tiirka koowaad ee dhismaha Galmudug nabdoon, horumarsan, oo loo dhan yahay, isagoo ballanqaaday in haddii uu guuleysto uu codkooda iyo doorkooda ku xoojin doono hoggaanka sare iyo go’aan-qaadashada maamulka.

items.title: Ra’iisul Wasaare Xamse oo Xafiiskiisa Ku Qaabilay Wafdi Ka Socday Ururka Iskaashiga Islaamka (OIC)
items.description: MUQDISHO (Goobjoog News) — Ra’iisul Wasaaraha Xukuumadda Federaalka Soomaaliya, Mudane Xamsa Cabdi Barre, ayaa magaalada Muqdisho ku qaabilay wafdi ballaaran oo ka socday Ururka Iskaashiga Islaamka (OIC), kaas oo uu hoggaaminayay Agaasimaha Guud ee Xafiiska OIC ee Soomaaliya, Danjire Maxamed Bamba M. Boba. Kulankan ayaa diiradda lagu saaray xoojinta xiriirka iyo iskaashiga labada dhinac, iyadoo la falanqeeyay qaababka ururku u kordhin karo taageerada uu siiyo dowlad-dhiska Soomaaliya. Intii uu kulanku socday, Ra’iisul Wasaaraha ayaa wafdiga siiyay warbixin faahfaahsan oo ku saabsan xaaladda guud ee dalka iyo tallaabooyinka wax-ku-oolka ah ee laga gaaray dhinacyada amniga, dib-u-dhiska dowladnimada, xasiloonida siyaasadda, iyo horumarinta dhaqaalaha qaranka. Waxa uu sidoo kale iftiimiyay sida xukuumaddu ay uga go’an tahay dardargelinta qorshe-hawleedka lagu hirgelinayo nidaamka doorashooyinka qof iyo cod ah oo ka bilaawday qeybo ka mid ah dalka. Dhinaca kale, Ra’iisul Wasaare Xamsa Cabdi Barre ayaa uga mahadceliyay Ururka Iskaashiga Islaamka taageerada joogtada ah iyo garab-istaagga walaalnimo ee ay mar walba la garab taagan yihiin ummadda Soomaaliyeed. Wuxuu si gaar ah u bogaadiyay dadaallada baaxadda leh ee OIC ay ku bixiso taabbagelinta dadaallada nabadda, dhismaha hay’adaha dowliga ah, iyo kobcinta adeegyada horumarineed ee dalka ka socda. Wafdiga OIC ayaa dhankooda caddeeyay inay sii wadi doonaan wada-shaqeynta dhow ee ay la leeyihiin Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya, iyagoo xusay muhiimadda ay leedahay in la xoojiyo barnaamijyada wax looga qabanayo baahiyaha aasaasiga ah iyo taageeridda dadaallada lagu gaarayo xasilooni waarta oo ka dhalata guud ahaan gobolka.

items.title: Sheekh Aadan Madoobe oo sameeyay xilka qaadis iyo magacaabis
items.description: Baydhaba Caasimada Online) – Madaxweynaha Dowladd-goboleedka Koonfur Galbeed Soomaaliya, Mudane Sheekh Aadan Maxamed Nuur (Aadan Madoobe) ayaa maanta sameeyay xilka qaadis iyo magacaabis kadib wareegto uu soo saaray oo la xiriirta maamulka Gobolka Shabeellaha Hoose. Aadan Madoobe ayaa xilkii guddoomiye ku-xigeenka qorshaynta iyo dib-u-dhiska Gobolka Shabeellaha Hoose ka qaaday Mudane Bashiir Maxamed Yuusuf, isaga oo xilkaas u magacaabay Mudane Xuseen Jilacow Maxamuud. Sababta isbeddelka loo sameeyay ayaa lagu sheegay in la dardar-geliyo howlaha qorshaynta iyo dib-u-dhiska Gobolka Shabeellaha Hoose oo haatan ay ka jiraan xaalado adag. Maamulka Koonfur Galbeed ayaa mas’uulka cusub ugu baaqay inuu si hufan uga shaqeeyo waajibaadka loo igmaday, isla markaana uu dardargeliyo howlaha horumarineed ee loogu adeegayo shacabka gobolka. Magacaabistan cusub ayaa qeyb ka noqonaysa isbeddellada Koonfur Galbeed uu ku sameynayo hay’adaha iyo maamulka gobollada, iyadoo xilalka qaar loo magacaabayo mas’uuliyiin cusub. Si kastaba ha’ahaatee, Gobolka Shabeellaha Hoose ayaa kamid ah meelaha muhiimka ah ee Koonfur Galbeed, waxaana muddooyinkii dambe ka jiray arrimo la xiriira amniga, maamulka iyo dib-u-dhiska, kuwaas oo u baahan isku-duwid iyo qorsheyn joogto ah. Waxaa kale oo gobolkan ka jira dhaq-dhaqaaqyo ay dowladda Soomaaliya ka waddo halkaasi, kuwaas oo ka dhan ah maleeshiyaadka kooxda Al-Shaaab. The post Sheekh Aadan Madoobe oo sameeyay xilka qaadis iyo magacaabis appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Sawirro: Macallin Mahdi oo fuliyay ballan uu horey u qaaday
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Taliyaha qaybta guud ee Booliska Gobolka Banaadir Gaashaanle Sare Mahdi Cumar Mumin oo loo yaqaano (Macallin Mahdi) ayaa maanta fuliyay ballan-qaadkii uu horay ugu sameeyay ardayda kaalmaha hore ka galay Imtixaanka Qaranka ee sannad dugsiyeedka 2025-2026 oo dhowaan natiijadiisa ay shaacisay wasaaradda waxbarashada Soomaaliya. Macallin Mahdi ayaa ka dhabeeyay ballan-qaadkiisii ahaa in la maamuuso ardeyda, laguna dhiirrigeliyo in la geeyo goobaha muhiimka ah ee dalka. Sidoo kale wuxuu horay usoo jeediyay in ardeyda guuleysatay lagu qaado diyaarado, wuxuuna kuwa galay kaalmaha hore uu maanta diyaarad ku geeyay magaalada Jowhar, si ay ugu soo dalxiisaan. Taliyaha iyo wafdiga ardayda ayaa si heer sare ah loogu soo dhaweeyay HirShabelle, waxaana sidoo kale loo sameeyay soo dhaweyn iyo martigelin wanaagsan, sida uu sheegay Macallin Mahdi oo qoraal soo saaray. “Aniga oo ay I wehliyaan qaar ka mid ah agaasinka waxbarashada, waxaan ardayda u qaadnay safar dalxiis oo ay ku tageen magaalada Jowhar, iyadoo shirkadda STARSKY AVIATION ay door muhiim ah ka qaadatay dhiirrigelinta iyo fududeynta safarka ardayda,” ayuu yiri Macallin Mahdi. Waxaa kale oo uu kusii daray “Waxbarashadu waa furaha mustaqbalka dalka, Waxaan sii wadi doonnaa dhiirrigelinta iyo garab istaagga jiilka Soomaaliyeed ee wax baranaya”. Tallaabadan ayaa qayb ka ah dadaallada uu taliyaha Booliska Gobolka Banaadir ku xoojinayo dhiirrigelinta waxbarashada, si dalka ay uga soo baxaan jiilal aqoon leh oo mustaqbalka anfaca dalkooda iyo dadkooda. The post Sawirro: Macallin Mahdi oo fuliyay ballan uu horey u qaaday appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Taliyaha Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka oo Kormeer Shaqo Ku Tegay Taliska Kumaandooska Gorgor
items.description: MUQDISHO (Goobjoog News) — Taliyaha Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka Soomaaliyeed, Sarreeye Guuto Ibraahim Maxamed Maxamuud, ayaa maanta booqasho shaqo ku tegay Taliska Qaybta 1-aad ee Kumaandooska Gorgor ee magaalada Muqdisho, halkaas oo uu kormeer ugu kuurgalayey xaaladda ciidamada iyo howlaha amni ee horyaalla. Markii uu halkaas gaaray, Taliyaha Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka waxaa si diirran ugu soo dhaweeyay Taliyaha Qaybta 1-aad ee Gorgor, Gaashaanle Sare Saahid Jaamac Faarax (Jarrare), iyadoo taliyuhu uu salaan sharaf ka qaatay cutubyo ka tirsan ciidanka kumaandooska. Taliye Ibraahim Maxamed Maxamuud ayaa khudbad dhiirrigelin iyo dardaaran ah u jeediyay saraakiisha iyo ciidanka Guutada 21-aad ee Gorgor. Wuxuu ciidanka si adag ugu boorriyay inay si daacadnimo iyo hufnaan leh u gutaan waajibaadkooda qaran, isla markaana ay dhowraan anshaxa ciidanimo iyo isku-duubnida guud. Taliyaha ayaa sidoo kale ku adkeeyay askarta iyo saraakiisha inay mar kasta joogteeyaan heeganka sare iyo diyaargarowga ciidan, si ay si buuxda oo degdeg ah uga jawaabaan waajibaadka qaran ee loo xilsaaray, gaar ahaan hawlgallada socda ee dalka lagu xorraynayo. Kormeerka kadib, Taliyaha Xoogga Dalka ayaa kulan gaar ah oo xasaasi ah la qaatay saraakiisha hoggaanka ee Gorgor. Kulamadaas ayaa si qoto dheer looga hadlay xaaladda guud ee ciidanka, xoojinta hoggaanka, tayeynta isku-xirka howlaha, taakulaynta ciidamada, iyo sidii loo kobcin lahaa awoodda hawlgal ee Kumaandooska Gorgor si loo dardargeliyo hawlgallada qaran.

Taliye Ibraahim Maxamed Maxamuud ayaa khudbad dhiirrigelin iyo dardaaran ah u jeediyay saraakiisha iyo ciidanka Guutada 21-aad ee Gorgor. Wuxuu ciidanka si adag ugu boorriyay inay si daacadnimo iyo hufnaan leh u gutaan waajibaadkooda qaran, isla markaana ay dhowraan anshaxa ciidanimo iyo isku-duubnida guud. Taliyaha ayaa sidoo kale ku adkeeyay askarta iyo saraakiisha inay mar kasta joogteeyaan heeganka sare iyo diyaargarowga ciidan, si ay si buuxda oo degdeg ah uga jawaabaan waajibaadka qaran ee loo xilsaaray, gaar ahaan hawlgallada socda ee dalka lagu xorraynayo. Kormeerka kadib, Taliyaha Xoogga Dalka ayaa kulan gaar ah oo xasaasi ah la qaatay saraakiisha hoggaanka ee Gorgor. Kulamadaas ayaa si qoto dheer looga hadlay xaaladda guud ee ciidanka, xoojinta hoggaanka, tayeynta isku-xirka howlaha, taakulaynta ciidamada, iyo sidii loo kobcin lahaa awoodda hawlgal ee Kumaandooska Gorgor si loo dardargeliyo hawlgallada qaran.

items.title: Puntland oo jawaab siisay DF Soomaaliya: Annagaa mas’uul ka ah khayraadkeenna
items.description: Garoowe (Caasimada Online) – Wasiirka Warfaafinta Puntland, Mudane Farxaan Cali Xirsi, ayaa maanta si adag uga hadlay xaaladda amni iyo mida siyaasadeed ee Soomaaliya, isaga oo sheegay in aysan jirin dowlad Soomaaliyeed oo haysata oggolaansho ay ku fulin karto hawlgallo gudaha Puntland. Farxaan oo qoraal soo saaray ayaa shaaca ka qaaday in waxa ka jira dalka ay yihiin kooxo uu ku tilmaamay “qawlaysato” oo beegsanaya haldoorka Soomaaliyeed, sida uu hadalka u dhigay. Wasiirka ayaa sidoo kale sheegay in Puntland ay si joogto ah ula dagaallanto burcad-badeedda iyo cid kasta oo wax u dhimaysa amniga deegaannadeeda, isaga oo xusay in gudaha Puntland aysan xilligan ku sugnayn ciidamo aan ka tirsanayn kuweeda. ‎”Puntland waxay si joogta ula dagaalantaa burcad badeedda iyo cid kasta oo wax u dhimaysa amnigeda bad iyo berriba, Mana jiraan ciidan aan ahayn ciidamada Dawladda Puntland oo ku sugan gudaha puntland wixii hawlgalana iyagaa u xilsaaran,” ayuu yiri wasiir Farxaan Cali Xirsi. Waxaa kale oo uu intaas in Puntland ay mas’uul ka tahay khayraadkeeda, isla-markaana aysan waxba ka waydiin doonin cid kale, wuxuuna xusay in Dastuurka 2012 uu qeexayo, sida loo maamulayo khayraadka dalka. Wasiirka Warfaafinta Puntland ayaa sidoo kale xusay in dalka uu u baahan yahay in laga badbaadiyo xaaladda adag ee uu ku jiro, maadaama ay soo kordhayaan xaalado saameyn ku yeelan kara amniga iyo siyaasadda dalka. ‎”Dawladda Puntland khayraadkeeda iyadaa masuul ka ah waxna ka waydiin mayso cid aan haysan sharciyad, Dastuurka ayaana qeexaya sida loo maamulayo(2012). Dalku wuxuu u baahan yahay in laga badbaadiyo saddexdan burcad, burcad dawladeed, burcad diimeed iyo burcad badeedba,” ayuu sii raaciyay wasiirku. Ugu dambeyn, wuxuu farriin u diray madaxda dowladda, isaga oo ugu baaqay inay ka shaqeeyaan arrimaha qaran, sida doorashooyinka dalka. “Meelkasta yaan dhaqaale laga raadin ee doorasho hala raadsho,” ayuu kusoo gabagabeeyay qoraalkiisa. Hadalkan kasoo yeeray Puntland ayaa kusoo aadaya, iyada oo warsaxaafadeed kasoo baxay dowladda Soomaaliya looga hadlay kooxaha burcad-badeedda ee kusii xoogeysanaya deegaannada maamulkaasi, waxaana dowladdu walaac ka muujisay soo noqoshada burcad-badeedda oo weerarro ka bilaabay xeebaha Soomaaliya. Dowladda dhexe ayaa sidoo kale sheegtay in ciidamada Soomaaliyeed ay tallaabooyin ka qaadayaan shabakadaha burcad-badeedda, kuwaas oo ka hawlgala badda iyo dhulkaba, sida lagu caddeeyay bayaanka oo kasoo baxay Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda Soomaaliya The post Puntland oo jawaab siisay DF Soomaaliya: Annagaa mas’uul ka ah khayraadkeenna appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Somali cleric Ali Wajis endorses killing of government critics
items.description: MOGADISHU (Somaliguardian) – A prominent pro-government religious scholar told a gathering of senior Somali officials, including the defense minister, on Sunday that people who oppose the administration of President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud should be treated as terrorists and killed – a statement that has alarmed opposition figures already on edge after a drone strike wounded a former security chief turned government critic on Thursday. Sheikh Ali Wajis, a cleric known for his consistent public backing of the Federal Government, made the remarks at a meeting attended by government officials, including the Minister of Defense. “Anyone who fights Somalia’s current government should face the same punishment as terrorists and should be killed,” Wajis told the gathering. Neither Wajis nor the Ministry of Defense could be reached for comment. Villa Somalia had not issued a statement responding to the remarks as of publication, and no official who attended Sunday’s meeting has publicly distanced the government from them. Coming on the heels of an attack on an opposition figure Wajis’s remarks land just days after a strike on the residence of Gen. Mahad Abdirahman Aden , widely known as “Taliye Shub,” in the border town of Doolow, in the Gedo region. Gen. Mahad, Somalia’s former Custodial Corps commander, was wounded in the attack along with his wife and several others; at least one person, reported to be an Ethiopian domestic worker, was killed. He was evacuated for treatment across the border in Ethiopia. Gen. Mahad, who was removed from his post earlier this year and briefly placed under house arrest, has since emerged as a vocal critic of the Federal Government and is aligned with the political camp of former Southwest State President Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed “Laftagareen.” Authorities in Jubaland have accused Turkish military aircraft of carrying out the strike, calling it a deliberate, politically motivated attack tied to Gen. Mahad’s opposition to Mogadishu. In a statement, Jubaland said two missiles were fired, with one also striking the residence of Doolow’s district commissioner. The Federal Government has denied any involvement in an airstrike, offering a different account of what caused the damage to the house. Turkey, which has become one of Somalia’s most significant military partners, providing training, equipment and air support, has not publicly responded to the accusation. The disputed strike triggered protests in Doolow, with residents demanding an independent investigation into who was responsible and why Gen. Mahad’s residence was targeted. A cleric with a history of hardline rhetoric This is not the first time Wajis, who has served as an adviser to successive Somali administrations, has taken a hardline public stance in defense of the government. In April, as Somali National Army desertions mounted during Al-Shabab’s offensive in the Shabelle regions, Wajis publicly branded soldiers who fled their posts as apostates and called for their arrest – remarks that were echoed at the time by a senior Custodial Corps commander, who warned that deserters and their families could face arrest or execution. His latest comments arrive at a moment of unusually sharp strain between Mogadishu and Somalia’s federal member states. Jubaland, Puntland and ousted Southwest administration have all rejected constitutional amendments extending federal institutions’ mandates, and have formally suspended ties with the Federal Government, accusing it of interference in their political and security affairs. Why it matters Coming so soon after an unresolved and contested attack on a prominent opposition-aligned general, a call from a cleric closely associated with the presidency – delivered in front of the defense minister – for opponents of the government to be killed is likely to deepen fears among opposition figures and federal member states that political dissent in Somalia is being conflated with terrorism. Independent verification of the strike’s origin, and any government response to Wajis’s remarks, remained pending as of publication. Contact us: info@somaliguardian.com

items.title: Taliyaha Militariga oo booqday guutada cusub Gorgor ee 21aad (SAWIRRO)
items.description: Taliyaha Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka, General Ibraahim Maxamed Maxamuud ayaa maanta booqday Xarunta Taliska Qaybta 1aad ee Ciidanka Kumaandooska Gorgor. Taliska Qaybta 1aad ee Kumaandooska Gorgor ayaa ah qayb ka tirsan Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka, taas oo talskeedu uu yahay Magaalada Muqdisho. Taliyaha Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka oo booqasho shaqo ku tegay taliska ayaa halkaasi kula hadlay Saraakiisha iyo Ciidanka Guutada 21aad, iyadoo guutadan ay tahay mid cusub oo bishii August tababar heer sare ah loogu soo xiray dalkaasi Turkiga. “Taliyuhu wuxuu ciidanka kula dardaarmay inay si hufan u gutaan waajibaadkooda qaran, ilaashadaan anshaxa iyo isku-duubnida ciidanka, isla-markaana ay joogteeyaan heeganka iyo diyaargarowga ciidan, si loo xaqiijiyo gudashada waajibaadka loo igmaday.” Ayaa lagu yiri war lagu daabacay bogga Taliska Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka. “Intii uu booqashada ku guda jiray, Taliyuhu wuxuu kulan gaar ah la qaatay Saraakiisha Hoggaanka, waxaana looga hadlay xaaladda guud ee ciidanka, xoojinta howlaha loo igmaday iyo sidii loo horumarin lahaa diyaargarowga iyo hufnaanta ciidanka.” Ayuu warka intaasi ku daray. General Ibraahim Maxamed Maxamuud ayaa waxaa booqashadan ku wehlinayay Taliyaha Taliska Taakuleynta ee Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka, General Maxamed Maxamuud Xasan (Garabey). Booqashadan ayaa ku soo beegmeysa, iyadoo Taliska Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka uu xoojinayo isku xirka ciidamada iyo awoodda hawlgal ee ciidamada, waana xilli maalmihii u dambeeyay ay caqabad ka haysatay dhameystirka hawlgalka ay ciidamadu 26-kii August ka bilaabeen deegaanka Basra.

items.title: Xildhibaanno ka tirsan BF oo Turkiga ku eedeeyay qaraxii guriga taliye Shub + Video
items.description: Nairobi (Caasimada Online) – Xildhibaanno ka tirsan labada Aqal ee Baarlamaanka Soomaaliya, lagana soo doorto Koonfur Galbeed iyo Jubbaland oo shir ku yeeshay Nairobi ayaa si kulul uga hadlay qaraxii ka dhacay guriga Jeneraal Mahad Cabdiraxmaan Shub ee degmada Doolow ee gobolka Gedo, iyaga oo dowladda Turkiga ku eedeeyay inay ku lug lahayd weerarkaasi. Xildhibaan Xasan Cabdinuur oo akhriyay warsaxaafadeed laga soo saaray kulanka ayaa sheegay inay cambaareynayaan waxa uu ku tilmaamay “isku day dil siyaasadeed” oo lagu qaaday taliyihii hore ee ciidanka Asluubta Soomaaliya oo hadda garab u ah madaxweynihii hore ee Koonfur Galbeed. Bayaanka ayaa si toos ah dowladda Turkiga loogu eedeeyay weerarka, iyadoo xildhibaannadu shaaciyeen in duqeynta lagu qaaday guriga Jeneraal Mahad Cabdiraxmaan ay fuliyeen diyaaradaha dagaalka ee F-16 ee Turkiga. “Waxaan ka walaacsanahay aadna u cambaareyneynaa isku daygii dil siyaasadeedka ahaa ee Jeneral Mahad Cabdiraxmaan gurigiisa Doolow lagu duqeeyay diyaaradaha Turkiga F-16, kaas oo ahaa weerar sharci darro ah oo amarkiisa uu bixiyay madaxweynaha muddo xileedkiisa dhammaaday Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud,” ayuu yiri Xildhibaan Xasan Cabdinuur Xildhibaannada ayaa sidoo kale dowladda Turkiga ugu baaqay inay si deg-deg ah u joojiso duqeymaha ay diyaaradaheeda ka fulinayaan deegaannada Koonfur Galbeed iyo Jubbaland. “Shirku wuxuu diiradda saaray xaaladaha ka taagan Koonfur Galbeed dood dheer iyo falanqeyn kadib waxaa laga soo saaray in dowladda Turkiga ay si deg-deg ah u joojiso duqeymaha ay diyaaradaheeda F-16 ka fulinayeen deegaannada Koonfur Galbeed iyo Jubbaland,” ayaa lasii raaciyay bayaanka. Dhanka kale, xildhibaannada ayaa soo jeediyay in la difaaco xuquuqda iyo sharafta ciidamada Daraawiishta Koonfur Galbeed, iyaga oo sheegay in ciidamadaasi aan lagu tilmaamin karin Al-Shabaab, ayna yihiin ciidan kamid hay’adaha amniga ee Koonfur Galbeed Soomaaliya. “Ciidanka Daraawiishta Koonfur Galbeed waa ciidamo ka tirsan hay’adaha amniga hay’adaha amniga sumadeynta ciidan dowladeed ama xubnihiisa ay yiihiin argagixisana waa eedeyn aad u culus oo u baahan caddeyn la xaqiijiyay,” ayuu yiri Xidhibaan Xasan Cabdinuur. Ugu dambeyn, xildhibaannada ayaa ku baaqay in la ixtiraamo nidaamka federaalka Soomaaliya, lana ilaaliyo awoodaha iyo xuquuqda dowlad-goboleedyada. Xildhibaan Xasan Cabdinuur oo akhriyay warsaxaafadeed laga soo saaray kulanka ayaa sheegay inay cambaareynayaan waxa uu ku tilmaamay “isku day dil siyaasadeed” oo lagu qaaday taliyihii hore ee ciidanka Asluubta Soomaaliya oo hadda garab u ah madaxweynihii hore ee Koonfur Galbeed. Bayaanka ayaa si toos ah dowladda Turkiga loogu eedeeyay weerarka, iyadoo xildhibaannadu shaaciyeen in duqeynta lagu qaaday guriga Jeneraal Mahad Cabdiraxmaan ay fuliyeen diyaaradaha dagaalka ee F-16 ee Turkiga. “Waxaan ka walaacsanahay aadna u cambaareyneynaa isku daygii dil siyaasadeedka ahaa ee Jeneral Mahad Cabdiraxmaan gurigiisa Doolow lagu duqeeyay diyaaradaha Turkiga F-16, kaas oo ahaa weerar sharci darro ah oo amarkiisa uu bixiyay madaxweynaha muddo xileedkiisa dhammaaday Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud,” ayuu yiri Xildhibaan Xasan Cabdinuur Xildhibaannada ayaa sidoo kale dowladda Turkiga ugu baaqay inay si deg-deg ah u joojiso duqeymaha ay diyaaradaheeda ka fulinayaan deegaannada Koonfur Galbeed iyo Jubbaland. “Shirku wuxuu diiradda saaray xaaladaha ka taagan Koonfur Galbeed dood dheer iyo falanqeyn kadib waxaa laga soo saaray in dowladda Turkiga ay si deg-deg ah u joojiso duqeymaha ay diyaaradaheeda F-16 ka fulinayeen deegaannada Koonfur Galbeed iyo Jubbaland,” ayaa lasii raaciyay bayaanka. Dhanka kale, xildhibaannada ayaa soo jeediyay in la difaaco xuquuqda iyo sharafta ciidamada Daraawiishta Koonfur Galbeed, iyaga oo sheegay in ciidamadaasi aan lagu tilmaamin karin Al-Shabaab, ayna yihiin ciidan kamid hay’adaha amniga ee Koonfur Galbeed Soomaaliya. “Ciidanka Daraawiishta Koonfur Galbeed waa ciidamo ka tirsan hay’adaha amniga hay’adaha amniga sumadeynta ciidan dowladeed ama xubnihiisa ay yiihiin argagixisana waa eedeyn aad u culus oo u baahan caddeyn la xaqiijiyay,” ayuu yiri Xidhibaan Xasan Cabdinuur. Ugu dambeyn, xildhibaannada ayaa ku baaqay in la ixtiraamo nidaamka federaalka Soomaaliya, lana ilaaliyo awoodaha iyo xuquuqda dowlad-goboleedyada. items.title: Puntland’s Road Advantage: Why Deni Can Reach His People by Road While Other Somali Presidents Cannot
items.description: Garowe (WDN) — Puntland’s Road Advantage: Why Deni Can Reach His People by Road While Other Somali Presidents CannotDeni of Puntland is demonstrating something increasingly rare: the ability to travel by road, day or night, across his territory and reach even some of its most remote communities. At the time of writing, President Deni is touring districts across Bari region, including areas far beyond the main paved road network. On Friday night, Deni and his delegation spent the night in Ufeyn after travelling through districts and settlements along roads outside the main highway. The journey is part of a wider tour intended to assess conditions in Bari and strengthen security, particularly following military operations against militant groups in the Cal Miskaad area. Deni is expected to continue travelling through districts including Balidhidhin, Iskushuban and Hafun, accompanied by senior parliamentary officials, government representatives, presidential advisers, members of the presidential administration and military officers. The significance of the journey extends well beyond the itinerary. Nevertheless, this comes amid growing frustration among many Puntlanders over government neglect and failure to fulfill its responsibilities. Citizens are facing severe economic and livelihood hardships, while even government employees have reportedly gone nearly a year without receiving their salaries. A Rare Political Freedom in Somalia Puntland’s relative security gives its president an advantage that leaders of most other Somali Federal Member States simply do not enjoy. Deni can leave Garowe, travel hundreds of kilometres over paved and unpaved roads, stop in towns and rural communities, meet local residents and government officials, and continue his journey without being confined to an aircraft or a heavily restricted security corridor. For much of Somalia, that kind of presidential outreach remains largely a dream. The presidents of South West, Jubaland, Hirshabelle and Galmudug face vastly greater security constraints. Travelling overland between major population centers can involve serious risks because of militant activity, contested territory, road insecurity and the limited reach of government security forces. President Hassan travelling from Mogadishu to Marka or Jowhar by air, for example, cannot take for granted the freedom of movement that Deni currently enjoys across much of Puntland. In practice, senior political leaders in several Federal Member States are heavily dependent on air travel to move between major locations. The ability to travel by road is not simply a matter of convenience. It is a measure of territorial control, security, state presence and political access. A president who can drive through his territory has an opportunity to see conditions firsthand rather than relying entirely on reports from officials. He can meet communities that rarely receive high-level government visitors. President Deni’s journey through Bari is taking him into areas that are geographically distant and, in some cases, far removed from Puntland’s main urban centres. Puntland is not the only Somali territory where senior leaders can travel overland. Somaliland also provides its president with significant freedom of movement across much of its territory. But among Somalia’s Federal Member States, Puntland’s current level of presidential road access stands out. The contrast is particularly striking when measured against the security environment facing the federal states in south-central Somalia. A president who cannot safely travel between his own major towns by road is inevitably more dependent on air transport, security escorts and tightly controlled schedules. That limits political outreach. It also creates distance between government and citizens. Deni’s Journey Sends a Political Message The current tour also carries an important political message. By travelling beyond Garowe and visiting remote districts personally, Deni is reinforcing the image of a government that can physically reach its population. The delegation includes senior political, administrative and security officials, suggesting that the journey is intended not merely as a presidential visit but as an exercise in government outreach. The stated focus is security and the conditions of communities in Bari. But the symbolism is broader. A government that can travel its roads can see its territory. A government that can see its territory can better understand its people. That connection is difficult to establish when political leaders are confined to capitals or forced to move almost exclusively by air. Puntland’s relative security should therefore be understood not only as a security achievement but also as a political asset. Road access creates opportunities for governance. It allows officials to reach communities, communities to see their leaders, and leaders to gather information directly from the population. It also gives the administration greater visibility across its territory. The contrast with much of southern and central Somalia is stark. In areas where Al-Shabaab remains capable of threatening major roads and where government authority is contested, presidential travel becomes a security operation rather than ordinary governance. The result is a state that can be physically present in one location while remaining largely inaccessible elsewhere. The Larger Somali Paradox Somalia has invested heavily in rebuilding national security institutions, yet large parts of the country remain difficult or dangerous for political leaders to traverse by road. That creates a fundamental paradox: How can a government claim effective territorial governance when its own president cannot freely travel across the territory he is supposed to govern? Puntland offers a different picture.Deni’s current journey—from established urban centres into remote districts and communities—demonstrates the practical value of security. It shows that roads can become instruments of governance rather than simply transport routes. And it highlights what other Somali leaders could achieve if they enjoyed comparable freedom of movement. The Real Measure of Security. Security is often measured in statistics: territory recovered, militants eliminated, weapons seized or operations conducted. But there is another, more tangible measure. Can a president get into a vehicle and travel through his own territory? Can he leave the capital at night? Can he travel on paved and unpaved roads? Can he reach remote districts without having to fly? Can ordinary citizens see their president arrive by road and speak directly to him? In much of Somalia, the answer remains uncertain or negative. In Puntland, Deni’s current tour offers a strikingly different reality. That does not mean Puntland has eliminated every security challenge, nor does road access by itself prove effective governance. But it demonstrates something fundamental: security creates political space. And at a time when many Somali leaders remain largely dependent on aircraft to move between their own territories, Puntland’s ability to move its president by road—across both highways and remote tracks—has become one of its most visible advantages. For Deni, the road is not merely a route between districts. It is a demonstration that his administration can reach the people it governs. However, the question on everyone’s mind is whether President Deni will return ready to address the people’s growing hardships—or simply return with another round of photo opportunities and political promises. items.title: Somalia’s Endless Search for a Political Deal
items.description: Mogadishu (WDN) — Somalia’s Federal Government and representatives of the political opposition are expected to sign a new political agreement in the coming days aimed at establishing a Democratic Transition Task Force (DTT), a body expected to play a role in shaping the country’s democratic transition and electoral process. In a post on X Mohamed Abdirizak Mohamud, a member of the Nabad iyo Nolol political group, said the negotiating parties are close to finalizing the agreement. He added, the talks were progressing positively, but he did not disclose the details of the proposed agreement, the issues that remain unresolved, or the exact date on which the deal is expected to be signed. That lack of detail is likely to fuel both interest and caution. The proposed agreement comes after years of political dialogue, reconciliation initiatives and mediation efforts that have repeatedly raised hopes of a breakthrough but failed to produce lasting political settlements. That history explains why many Somalis are likely to judge the new agreement not by the language of the signing ceremony, but by what happens afterward. Somalia has seen numerous political understandings announced with optimism, only for disagreements over elections, constitutional reform, federal-state relations and the distribution of political power to resurface.  The proposed DTT therefore faces a simple but difficult test: can this agreement turn political dialogue into an enforceable and broadly accepted process? The planned Democratic Transition Task Force is expected to contribute to Somalia’s democratic transition and preparations for elections. However, important details remain unclear. The names of its members, its precise mandate, the duration of its work and the mechanisms through which its decisions will be implemented have yet to be formally announced. Those details could ultimately determine whether the body becomes a meaningful instrument for political compromise or another temporary mechanism that fails to resolve the underlying dispute. A Deal Under Political Pressure The anticipated agreement comes as Somalia continues to face deep political disagreements and security concerns. The country remains divided over the direction of the electoral process, the constitutional framework and the balance of authority between the Federal Government and political and regional actors. Mohamed Abdirizak has urged political actors to reject violence and protect the ongoing dialogue, stressing the importance of ensuring that the negotiations produce an outcome acceptable to all sides. His comments came following the reported attack on the residence of General Mahad Abdirahman “Shub” in Doolow, in which five civilians were reportedly wounded. Mohamed Abdirizak questioned whether the Doolow incident could be connected to attempts to disrupt the political negotiations and efforts to reach an agreement. The Federal Government has previously denied involvement in the incident. Those allegations remain unproven and require independent investigation. For ordinary Somalis, the significance of the proposed agreement goes beyond the creation of another political committee. People have watched successive reconciliation efforts promise an end to political confrontation, only to see disagreements return. That experience has produced understandable skepticism. The question now is whether the latest initiative can break that cycle. If the Federal Government and opposition succeed in signing an agreement that is genuinely inclusive, clearly defined and supported by credible implementation mechanisms, it could provide an important opening for reducing political tensions and creating a more predictable path toward elections. But if the agreement merely postpones the underlying disputes without resolving them, public confidence could deteriorate further. Somalia does not lack political agreements. What it has lacked is an agreement capable of surviving the political pressures that follow its signing. That is why the coming days will be watched closely. The signing of the DTT agreement may generate another moment of optimism—but for a public that has seen too many reconciliation efforts fail to produce lasting results, the real test will begin the day after the signatures are placed on the paper. items.title: Ethiopia’s Growing Security Anxiety: U.S. Funding Cut Raises Fears Over Somalia Operations
items.description: Addis Ababa (WDN) — Ethiopia is facing growing security concerns, particularly along its eastern border, following plans to end U.S. logistical funding for the United Nations Support Office in Somalia (UNSOS) on December 31, 2026, according to a Somali lawmaker and regional security experts. The implications of the planned funding cutoff were discussed on September 3 during a security forum hosted in Addis Ababa by the Institute for Security Studies (ISS), where experts examined emerging threats across the Horn of Africa and their potential impact on regional stability. Experts warned that the loss of U.N.-backed transportation, aviation and logistical support could create a significant operational gap for the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM), particularly in areas near the Somalia-Ethiopia-Kenya border region. The logistical system supporting international and Somali forces is critical to troop movements, the delivery of supplies and the ability to conduct sustained security operations in remote and contested areas. Without an effective replacement mechanism, experts cautioned, forces deployed far from major population centers could face serious constraints on mobility and resupply. During the discussion, Somali MP Ahmed Abdi, secretary of the Federal Parliament’s Defence Committee, highlighted the role of the Ethiopian National Defence Force (ENDF) in Somalia’s security architecture. Ahmed said Ethiopian forces play an important role in stabilizing nine strategically important districts in South West State, where Ethiopian and Somali forces operate jointly against security threats. He argued that Ethiopia’s military presence in Somalia extends beyond the fight against Al-Shabaab. It is also closely linked to Ethiopia’s own border security, preventing armed groups from moving across the frontier and containing threats that could potentially spread from Somalia into Ethiopian territory. That makes any deterioration in Somalia’s security environment a direct concern for Addis Ababa. AUSSOM’s Logistics Problem Security experts therefore warn that any reduction in AUSSOM’s operational capacity could have consequences well beyond Somalia. The planned end of U.S. funding for UNSOS raises a critical question: who will replace the logistical support that currently enables international forces to move personnel, deliver supplies and sustain operations across difficult terrain? If adequate alternative financing and logistical arrangements are not secured, AUSSOM could face reduced capacity in transportation, aviation and supply operations. That, in turn, could create opportunities for Al-Shabaab to exploit gaps in areas where Somali government and international forces are attempting to maintain pressure on the militant group. The concern is particularly significant because logistics are often the unseen foundation of military operations. A force may have troops, weapons and political authority, but without reliable transportation, fuel, aviation and resupply, its ability to sustain operations in remote areas can deteriorate rapidly. The Ethiopia-Kenya Dimension The consequences could also extend to Kenya, which, like Ethiopia, shares a long and strategically sensitive border with Somalia. A weakening of Somalia’s security capacity could increase the security burden on both neighboring countries, potentially requiring them to devote additional resources to border surveillance, counterterrorism operations and the prevention of cross-border militant activity. For Ethiopia, the concern is especially acute because instability in Somalia can have direct implications for its eastern border.Regional security experts argue that changes to AUSSOM’s financing and logistical capabilities should therefore be viewed as a Horn of Africa security issue rather than simply an administrative or budgetary matter concerning an international mission. The Addis Ababa discussion highlighted a broader reality: the future of AUSSOM will depend not only on the number of troops deployed but also on whether those troops can be effectively supplied, transported and supported. The end of U.S. funding for UNSOS could therefore become a critical test of the international community’s commitment to sustaining Somalia’s security architecture. If replacement funding is delayed or inadequate, the consequences could extend from the battlefield in Somalia to the borders of Ethiopia and Kenya.The debate in Addis Ababa suggests that the logistics question surrounding AUSSOM may ultimately become a question of regional security. Somalia, Ethiopia and Kenya share interconnected security interests, and a significant decline in Somalia’s operational capacity could create new vulnerabilities across the wider Horn of Africa. For Ethiopia in particular, the issue is difficult to separate from its own national security calculations. As long as armed groups remain active in Somalia and capable of exploiting weakly governed or poorly secured areas, instability south of Ethiopia’s border remains a potential threat to Ethiopian territory. The December 31 deadline is therefore more than a funding date. It could mark a turning point for Somalia’s security operations—and potentially for the security balance of the wider Horn of Africa. items.title: DF oo qaylo dhaan u dirtay caalamka kadib soo noqoshada…
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Dowladda Soomaaliya oo soo saartay bayaan culus ayaa si adag kaga hadashay soo noqoshada kooxaha burcad-badeeda oo weerarro ku qaaday maraakiib ganacsi, xilli ay marayeen aagga xeebaha Puntland. Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda Soomaaliya oo qoraalka soo saartay ayaa walaac xooggan ka muujisay falalka haatan soo kordhay, kuwaas oo dib usoo nooleeyay khatarta burcad-badeednimada ee xeebaha dalka. “Dowladda Soomaaliya ma oggolaan doonto in biyaha dalkeedu noqdaan meel ay gabaad ka dhigtaan kuwa gala dambiyada baddaha,” ayaa lagu yiri bayaanka. Soomaaliya ayaa sidoo kale shaaca ka qaaday inay u baahan tahay taageero caalami ah, iyadoo ku baaqday in iskaasho laga yeesho ka hortegga burcad-badeedda. Hoos ka akhriso warsaxaafadeedka;- Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya waxay si adag u cambaaraynaysaa soo noqoshada falalka burcad-badeednimada ee ka dhacaya xeebaha Puntland ee Soomaaliya. Tan iyo bishii Abriil 2026, waxaa dhacay weerarro iyo afduub loo geystay maraakiib ganacsi, iyadoo qaar ka mid ah dhacdooyinkaas ay ku fidiyeen Gacanka Cadmeed. Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa sheegtay inay garab taagan tahay shaqaalaha maraakiibta ay saameeyeen falalkaan iyo qoysaskooda, waxayna ku baaqday in si degdeg ah oo shuruud la’aan ah loo sii daayo dhammaan badmaaxiinta weli gacanta ku hayaan kooxaha burcad-badeedda. Ciidamada Soomaaliyeed waxay tallaabooyin ka qaadayaan shabakadaha burcad-badeedka, kuwaas oo ka hawlgala badda iyo dhulkaba. Tallaabadii ugu dambeysay ayaa ahayd hawlgalkii lagu soo furtay markabka xamuulka ah ee MV Lutuf, kaas oo burcad-badeeddu afduubteen, waxaana markabka la soo furtay 29-kii Agoosto, Hawlgallo intaasi dheerna way sii socon doonaan. Iskaashiga amniga badda ee Soomaaliya waxaa lagu fuliyaa iyadoo lala kaashanaayo Dowladda Federaalka, waxaana lagu wadaa isku duubni ay la leeyihiin Dowlad goboleedyada xubnaha ka ah Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya, iyadoo lagu shaqeynaayo hannaan qaran oo amni ah isla markaana mideysan oo leh isla xisaabtan cad. Saaxiibbada Soomaaliya waxay Dowladda Soomaaliya ku soo dhaweynaysaa inay taageeraan ciidamada Soomaaliyeed ee ilaalada iyo amniga badda, iyagoo adeegsanaya hannaankaan. Kheyraadka badda Soomaaliya waxaa lagu maamulaa sharciga Soomaaliyeed, halka kalluumeysiga sharci darrada ah, aan la soo sheegin iyo kan aan nidaamsanayn (IUU Fishing) uu xadgudub ku yahay xuquuqda madaxbannaanida Soomaaliya ee ku cad Heshiiska Qaramada Midoobay ee Sharciga Badda (UNCLOS). Sida ku cad Qodobka 100-aad ee Heshiiska, dhammaan dowladuhu waxaa waajib ku ah inay iska kaashadaan la dagaallanka iyo ciribtirka burcad-badeednimada. Iyadoo Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ay hadda tahay xubin ka tirsan Golaha Ammaanka ee Qaramada Midoobay, waxay arrintaan khatarta ah horgeyn doontaa Golaha Ammaanka, waxayna si dhow ula shaqeyn doontaa saaxiibbadeeda laba geesoodka ah, kuwa gobolka iyo kuwa caalamiga ah, oo ay ku jiraan iskaashiga lagu sameeyo Xeerka Anshaxa Jabuuti (Djibouti Code of Conduct) iyo Wax ka beddelka Jeddah (Jeddah Amendment), si loo sii daayo badmaaxiinta ay saameeyeen falalkaan loona burburiyo shabakadaha burcad-badeedka ah. Dowladda Soomaaliya ma oggolaan doonto in biyaha dalkeedu noqdaan meel ay gabaad ka dhigtaan kuwa gala dambiyada baddaha. items.title: General Sahal Cabdullaahi Cumar oo gaaray Degmada Baardheere (SAWIRRO)
items.description: Taliyaha Ciidanka Dhulka ee Xoogga Dalka, General Sahal Cabdullaahi Cumar iyo wafdi Saraakiil ah oo uu hoggaaminayo ayaa Axaddan gaaray Degmada Baardheere ee Gobolka Gedo. “Taliyaha Guutada 36aad, Qaybta 43aad ee Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka Soomaaliyeed, G/sare Cismaan Sheekh Cabdi Qorax iyo Saraakiil ka tirsan Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka ayaa Garoonka Diyaaradaha ee Magaalada Baardheere ku soo dhaweeyay Taliyaha iyo Saraakiisha socdaalka ku wehlinayay.” Ayaa lagu yiri war ka soo baxay Taliska Militariga. Socdaalka Taliyaha Ciidanka Dhulka ee Baardheere ayaa la xiriira u kuurgelidda xaaladda amni ee gobolka, kormeerka howlaha Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka, dardargelinta hawlgalada ka dhanka ah kooxaha argagixisada iyo arrimo kale oo muhiim u ah howlaha ciidanka, sida lagu sheegay warka. Taliyaha ayaa kulan la qaatay Saraakiisha Ciidamada, isagoona ka dhageystay warbixino ku saabsan xaaladda guud ee amniga degmadaasi iyo hawlgalada ay ciidamadu ka wadaan deegaanada hoostaga. General Sahal Cabdullaahi Cumar, Taliyaha Ciidanka Dhulka ayaa waxaa safarka ku wehliya Taliyaha Taliska Tababarada iyo Doctrine-ka Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka, General Axmed Ciise Axmed, Madaxa Hoggaanka War-isgaarsiinta iyo Technology-ga Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka, G/sare Faarax Cali Cartan iyo Saraakiil kale.

items.title: Saraakiisha Sare ee Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka oo Gaaray Gobolka Gedo
items.description: BAARDHEERE – Taliyaha Ciidanka Dhulka Xoogga Dalka Soomaaliyeed, Sareeye Guuto Sahal Cabdullaahi Cumar “Gen. Khaalid”, ayaa maanta gaaray magaalada Baardheere ee gobolka Gedo, halkaas oo uu u tagay kormeer iyo u kuurgelidda xaaladda amni iyo howlaha ay ciidamada ka wadaan gobolka. Taliyaha waxaa socdaalka ku weheliyay Taliyaha Taliska Tababarada iyo Doktriinka Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka Soomaaliyeed, Gen. Axmed Ciise Axmed, Madaxa Hoggaanka War-isgaarsiinta iyo Teknolojiyadda Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka, G/Sare Faarax Cali Cartan, iyo saraakiil kale. Garoonka diyaaradaha ee magaalada Baardheere ayaa waxaa wafdiga ku soo dhaweeyay Taliyaha Guutada 36-aad, Qeybta 43-aad ee Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka Soomaaliyeed, G/Sare Cismaan Sheekh Cabdi Qorax iyo saraakiil kale oo ka tirsan ciidamada. Intii ay socotay soo dhaweynta, Taliyaha Ciidanka Dhulka ayaa salaan sharaf ka qaatay cutubyo ka tirsan Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka Soomaaliyeed. Soo dhaweynta kaddib, Taliyaha ayaa kulan la yeeshay saraakiisha amniga degmada, isagoo ka dhageystay warbixinno la xiriira xaaladda guud ee amniga iyo howlgalada ay ciidamada ka wadaan degmada Baardheere iyo deegaanada ku dhow. Socdaalka Taliyaha Ciidanka Dhulka ayaa salka ku haya u kuurgelidda xaaladda amni ee gobolka Gedo, kormeerka howlaha Ciidanka Xoogga Dalka Soomaaliyeed, dardargelinta howlgalada ka dhanka ah kooxaha argagixisada iyo arrimo kale oo muhiim u ah waajibaadka ciidamada.

items.title: Is the Horn of Africa Becoming the Next Front in the Middle Eastern Power Competition?
items.description: The Red Sea no longer separates the Middle East from Africa. It increasingly connects their security problems. Across the Horn of Africa, ports, trade routes, military partnerships and local conflicts are attracting greater attention from Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Egypt and Türkiye. The Bab el Mandeb sits at the centre of this changing strategic cartograph. It links the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and the Indian Ocean. Recent threats to commercial shipping have made this geography even more valuable. According to the Reuters, In July 2026, Saudi Arabia proposed a multinational maritime defence coalition to protect Red Sea shipping and energy routes. Egypt, Türkiye, Sudan and Djibouti were among its supporters, while the UAE was notably absent from the supporting group. The Red Sea is no longer a dividing line between two regions. It is becoming the strategic bridge between them. Ports sit at the heart of this competition. They are no longer only places where ships load and unload goods. They now carry political and strategic value. The UAE has built a strong commercial presence around Berbera in Somaliland. In 2025, DP World launched a direct shipping service between Jebel Ali and Berbera. The company presents Berbera as an alternative gateway towards landlocked Ethiopia and says it holds a 58.5 percent stake in the port operation as per the DP World. For Somaliland, such investment brings infrastructure, trade and international attention. For the UAE, it provides commercial access near one of the world’s most important maritime corridors. A port can carry containers in peacetime and influence in a crisis. Saudi Arabia views the same maritime space through its own security needs. The renewed Houthi threat to Red Sea shipping in 2026 pushed Riyadh to seek a wider maritime security arrangement. Its proposed coalition would cover the Bab el Mandeb, Gulf of Aden and Red Sea trade routes as mentioned in the Reuters. The UAE’s absence from the initial group of supporters does not by itself prove a Saudi-Emirati contest for the Horn. But it does show that the two Gulf powers do not always approach regional security through the same framework. This matters because their economic and political footprints increasingly reach the African side of the Red Sea. Egypt adds another layer. Its rivalry with Ethiopia has traditionally centred on the Nile and the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam. That rivalry is now becoming connected with maritime access and Red Sea security. Ethiopia remains landlocked and wants reliable access to the sea. Somalia strongly resists arrangements that it believes weaken its sovereignty over Somaliland. Meanwhile, Egypt has deepened its engagement with Somalia and Eritrea. In July 2026, Cairo hosted talks involving Egyptian, Somali and Eritrean officials alongside a senior US envoy. Horn of Africa security was central to the discussions, according to the Egypt State Information Service. A dispute that began around water can morph into a contest over ports, coastlines and regional power. Stay ahead of the geopolitical week. Türkiye demonstrates another side of Middle Eastern involvement. Ankara has built deep political and security relations with Somalia but it also maintains working relations with Ethiopia. This gave Türkiye room to mediate when tensions between Addis Ababa and Mogadishu rose over Ethiopia’s search for sea access. According to the Türkiye Ministry of Foreign Affairs under the Ankara Declaration, Somalia and Ethiopia agreed to respect each other’s sovereignty while pursuing arrangements that could give Ethiopia reliable access to the sea under Somali sovereign authority.Therefore,Türkiye shows that outside involvement does not always deepen rivalry. It can also create diplomatic space. The same geography that invites competition can also create a market for mediation. Sudan shows the darker side of this trend. Its civil war began as a domestic struggle between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces. It has since become increasingly internationalised. A UN fact finding mission reported on September 3, 2026 that foreign weapons, military technology, fighters and logistical networks were helping sustain the conflict. Investigators found reasonable grounds to believe that individuals and entities linked to a transnational network involving the UAE, Chad, Libya and Somalia supplied the RSF with weapons, equipment, logistics, training and personnel. The UAE has repeatedly denied supporting the RSF as per the Reuters. This distinction matters. External support should be presented through verified evidence, not political accusation. But the larger lesson is difficult to miss. When outside powers or networks invest in armed actors instead of institutions, local wars gain foreign lifelines. These developments do not mean that Middle Eastern states created the Horn’s conflicts. Ethiopia’s internal tensions, Somalia’s state building problems, Sudan’s civil war and disputes over Somaliland all have deep local roots. Treating every crisis as a proxy war would deny African actors their own interests and choices. External competition works differently. It can extend existing divisions, change local calculations and give governments or armed actors new sources of money, diplomatic support and strategic importance. This is also why African states should not be described simply as pawns. They have agency. Somalia can use competing partnerships to gain security assistance and diplomatic backing. Ethiopia can bargain for maritime access. Somaliland can use its coastline to attract foreign investment. Djibouti has turned its location into economic and strategic value by hosting several foreign military presences. The Horn is not merely being acted upon. Its governments are also learning to bargain with those who want access to it. The real question is whether that bargaining creates autonomy or dependency. Ports create leverage when African states control the competition. They become pressure points when the competition starts controlling African choices. A government that can work with several partners may gain room to manoeuvre. A government that becomes dependent on a single external patron may lose it. The same distinction applies to security. Foreign support that strengthens national institutions can improve stability. Support that empowers rival factions can make conflict harder to end. Therefore, The Horn of Africa is becoming a front in the Middle Eastern power competition but not in the traditional sense of passive states being divided among outside powers. Something more complicated is happening. The security systems of the Gulf, Red Sea and Horn are beginning to overlap. Saudi Arabia wants secure Red Sea shipping. The UAE has built commercial networks around strategic ports. Egypt sees developments in Ethiopia and the Horn through its own national security concerns. Türkiye combines security partnerships with mediation. African governments, meanwhile, are trying to convert geography into bargaining power. The test will be what this competition leaves behind. If foreign investment produces functioning ports, stronger trade corridors and better African institutions, Horn states may emerge with greater leverage. If it produces rival security blocs, competing armed clients and deeper dependence, the region will increasingly become an arena for struggles designed beyond Africa. The danger is not that Middle Eastern powers have arrived in the Horn. They are already there. The danger begins when African crises become instruments of Middle Eastern competition rather than problems shaped by African solutions.   Sher Ali Ranjha I am Sher Ali Ranjha, and I have received an email to send you a short introduction, inorder to joinModern Diplomacy as an intern. I hold an undergraduate degree in Finance from the American University in Dubai and have a keen interest in international affairs, climate change, and policy research. Middle East & Africa

These developments do not mean that Middle Eastern states created the Horn’s conflicts. Ethiopia’s internal tensions, Somalia’s state building problems, Sudan’s civil war and disputes over Somaliland all have deep local roots. Treating every crisis as a proxy war would deny African actors their own interests and choices. External competition works differently. It can extend existing divisions, change local calculations and give governments or armed actors new sources of money, diplomatic support and strategic importance. This is also why African states should not be described simply as pawns. They have agency. Somalia can use competing partnerships to gain security assistance and diplomatic backing. Ethiopia can bargain for maritime access. Somaliland can use its coastline to attract foreign investment. Djibouti has turned its location into economic and strategic value by hosting several foreign military presences. The Horn is not merely being acted upon. Its governments are also learning to bargain with those who want access to it. The real question is whether that bargaining creates autonomy or dependency. Ports create leverage when African states control the competition. They become pressure points when the competition starts controlling African choices. A government that can work with several partners may gain room to manoeuvre. A government that becomes dependent on a single external patron may lose it. The same distinction applies to security. Foreign support that strengthens national institutions can improve stability. Support that empowers rival factions can make conflict harder to end. Therefore, The Horn of Africa is becoming a front in the Middle Eastern power competition but not in the traditional sense of passive states being divided among outside powers. Something more complicated is happening. The security systems of the Gulf, Red Sea and Horn are beginning to overlap. Saudi Arabia wants secure Red Sea shipping. The UAE has built commercial networks around strategic ports. Egypt sees developments in Ethiopia and the Horn through its own national security concerns. Türkiye combines security partnerships with mediation. African governments, meanwhile, are trying to convert geography into bargaining power. The test will be what this competition leaves behind. If foreign investment produces functioning ports, stronger trade corridors and better African institutions, Horn states may emerge with greater leverage. If it produces rival security blocs, competing armed clients and deeper dependence, the region will increasingly become an arena for struggles designed beyond Africa. The danger is not that Middle Eastern powers have arrived in the Horn. They are already there. The danger begins when African crises become instruments of Middle Eastern competition rather than problems shaped by African solutions.   Sher Ali Ranjha I am Sher Ali Ranjha, and I have received an email to send you a short introduction, inorder to joinModern Diplomacy as an intern. I hold an undergraduate degree in Finance from the American University in Dubai and have a keen interest in international affairs, climate change, and policy research. Middle East & Africa

items.title: Every Institution Has a Turning Point: The Scholar Behind Somaliland’s First Central Bank Strategic Plan
items.description: Professor Eid Ali Ahmed’s quiet contribution to institution-building, strategic planning and the transformation of Somaliland’s financial sector Every institution has a turning point—a moment when it moves from simply performing its daily functions to defining where it wants to go. For the Somaliland Central Bank, one of those defining moments came in 2017 , when it began laying the groundwork for its first formal Strategic Plan, covering 2018–2022 . The article was originally prepared by Ahmed Suleiman, Editor of Dawan , and I translated it into English. It begins: At the centre of that effort was Professor Eid Ali Ahmed , an academic, banking expert and strategic planner who brought his knowledge and international professional experience back to Somaliland and offered it in service of national institution-building. His contribution was not simply to write a document. It was to help an institution articulate its direction, define its priorities, strengthen its leadership, and prepare its people for the work of turning strategy into reality. The Strategic Plan became an important milestone in the institutional development of the Somaliland Central Bank, establishing a five-year framework centred on monetary and financial stability, financial-sector development, institutional strengthening and sustainable economic growth. From Vision to Strategy Professor Eid’s approach reflected the understanding that a central bank cannot operate effectively without a clear institutional vision. The plan sought to strengthen the Bank’s governance, human resources, technology, payment systems, accountability and transparency while laying the groundwork for a more modern and efficient central banking institution. But Professor Eid also emphasized that monetary and financial stability alone could not deliver sustainable prosperity. At the launch of the strategy, he stressed the need to connect financial stability with broader economic reforms, diversification, job creation, poverty reduction and sustainable economic growth. In other words, the Central Bank’s development could not be separated from the development of the wider economy. Building the People Behind the Plan Perhaps one of the most important aspects of Professor Eid’s contribution was that he did not stop at preparing the strategy. A strategic plan is only as strong as the people responsible for implementing it. To address that challenge, Professor Eid provided training to 17 directors of the Central Bank , equipping senior officials with knowledge and skills intended to support the implementation of the new strategy. His work therefore combined strategic planning with training, advisory support and institutional capacity-building. That made his contribution broader than the preparation of a strategic document. He was helping build both the roadmap and the institutional capacity required to follow it. A Historic Certificate of Appreciation The Central Bank formally recognized Professor Eid’s contribution. On 1 November 2017 , he was presented with a certificate of appreciation for his role in preparing the Bank’s first Strategic Plan, covering 2018–2022. The certificate was signed by the then Governor of the Central Bank, Mohamed Abdi Ibrahim . For Professor Eid, the recognition represented more than an individual achievement. It became a historical record of a moment when Somaliland’s central monetary institution was taking an important step toward structured, long-term institutional planning. Remembering the Officials Who Supported the Process Professor Eid has also acknowledged the Somaliland officials who helped facilitate the development of the strategy. Among those he specifically thanked were Mohamed Abdi Ibrahim , then Governor of the Central Bank; Omar Mohamed Yusuf Booh (RIP) , then Deputy Governor; and Abdillahi Hassan Adan , who was Director General of the Central Bank at the time and now serves as Somaliland’s Minister of Finance and Economic Development. Their support, he noted, was important in facilitating the preparation and implementation of the strategic programme. The Banking Industry Welcomes the Strategy The private banking sector also recognized the significance of the plan. Abdihakim Mohamed Ismail , representing Dahabshiil International Bank, praised the strategy and Professor Eid’s contribution, describing the plan as important for strengthening the Central Bank, developing private banking and supporting the broader financial system. He emphasized that the Central Bank is fundamental to guiding the economy and maintaining financial stability. Mohamed Ibrahim , representing Dara-Salaam Bank, similarly praised the plan, highlighting its focus on strengthening the Central Bank, improving regulation of private banks and developing staff capacity. For private financial institutions, the strategy offered something particularly important: a clearer institutional framework for the regulator responsible for overseeing the banking sector. Liban Ismail , representing Premier Bank, described the strategy as modern and aligned with international financial standards. He said it could strengthen the Central Bank and contribute to economic growth, while demonstrating that the institution was preparing itself to fulfil its responsibilities toward the country’s banking sector. Liban referred to the Central Bank as the “mother of banks” , arguing that it should lead the development, guidance and protection of Somaliland’s banking system. “An Institution Without a Plan Cannot Know Where It Is Going” Among those who strongly praised Professor Eid’s contribution was Said Mohamed Elmi , who served as Chairman of the Economic Committee of the Somaliland House of Representatives and previously served as Director of the Central Bank. He emphasized a simple but fundamental principle: an institution without a clear plan cannot know where it is going. For him, the strategic plan gave the Central Bank a clearer sense of direction, vision and ambition. Speaking at the time, Said Mohamed Elmi described 1 November 2017 as a day worthy of special recognition. “Today, 1 November 2017, is a significant day for Somaliland and deserves to be specially remembered, honoured, and recognized. This day marks an important milestone for the Central Bank, because it was the day the Bank acquired a clear institutional identity and a Strategic Plan. For this, I would like to thank Professor Eid Ali Ahmed, who developed that plan.” His words captured the broader significance attached to the strategy: it was not merely another administrative document, but a marker in the evolution of an important national institution. “If We Had Not Had This Plan…” The then Governor of the Central Bank, Mohamed Abdi Ibrahim , was equally emphatic in his appreciation of Professor Eid’s work. He said: “Today, I am extremely pleased with these new programmes. I would like to extend my special thanks to Professor Eid Ali Ahmed, the expert who developed this strategy with great professionalism. I say to him: May Allah reward you, because if we had not had this plan, we would not have been able to achieve our vision and fulfil our goals.” The Governor went further, praising Professor Eid for his dedication to the work. “I would particularly like to thank the expert who devoted himself to this work and accomplished something significant for us. As the saying goes: ‘When you find people, you find wealth.’” He also announced that Professor Eid would support further training aimed at strengthening the knowledge and skills of Central Bank employees. The goal, he explained, was to move through the strategy step by step, translating its ambitions into practical action. A Scholar Who Turned Knowledge into Service Professor Eid Ali Ahmed’s story is ultimately about more than one strategic plan. It is about the role that experienced professionals and scholars can play in building institutions in a country where institutional development requires both vision and expertise. His background in banking, management, strategic planning, institutional development and research gave him a broad perspective on the challenges facing financial institutions. But perhaps more significant was his decision to apply that knowledge directly to Somaliland’s institutional development. Rather than keeping his expertise within academic circles, Professor Eid brought his international experience home and offered it in service of national institutions. His work demonstrated how academic knowledge can be transformed into practical institutional reform. A Legacy Written into Institutional History The 2018–2022 Strategic Plan may have been a five-year document, but the institutional principle behind it was longer-lasting: successful institutions need a clear vision, measurable objectives, capable people and a willingness to plan beyond the immediate moment. Professor Eid’s contribution combined all four. He helped the Central Bank establish a strategic direction, trained senior officials who would participate in implementation, and promoted a broader understanding of what a modern central bank should become. That is why his contribution deserves to be remembered not simply as the preparation of a document, but as part of the continuing story of Somaliland’s institution-building. Institutions are built over time. Strategies provide them with direction. But behind every successful strategy are people willing to contribute their knowledge, experience and vision. For Somaliland’s Central Bank, Professor Eid Ali Ahmed was one of those people.

items.title: Demonstrators accused Turkey and Egypt of involvement in the strike
items.description: Hundreds of Somalis have taken to the streets in several cities across Somalia to protest the airstrike targeting General Mahad Abdirahman Aden, widely known as General Shub, the former Commander of the Somali Custodial Corps and a former member of Somalia’s Federal Parliament. Demonstrators accused Turkey and Egypt of involvement in the strike and other military operations that they allege have resulted in civilian casualties. During the protests, some demonstrators burned the Turkish flag, while others trampled on the Egyptian flag as an expression of their opposition to the two countries’ perceived role in Somalia. The demonstrations reflect growing public anger among participants over foreign military involvement and the civilian impact of ongoing security operations in Somalia.
