items.fullContent: Baidoa – South West State’s Security Minister, Osman Isaaq Mohamed, has called on Kenya to arrest Laftagareen, the region’s former president, and extradite him to Somalia. Multiple Somali outlets reported the demand, made Thursday. The minister was addressing the security crisis in Baidoa after the deadliest clashes the city has seen since March. He accused former President Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed “Laftagareen” of responsibility for recent attacks and bombings in the city. He said Laftagareen must face accountability for the violence. The demand to arrest Laftagareen lands at a tense moment for Somalia’s federal system. Baidoa has become the flashpoint in a months-long power struggle between the federal government and the man who once ran South West State. Last week’s battle for the city was the most serious armed confrontation since that dispute began. As a result, a political rift has hardened into open military conflict, with regional and diplomatic consequences that reach well beyond one city. Minister’s Direct Appeal to Nairobi Minister Mohamed did not soften his language. He said South West authorities want Kenya to detain the former leader and route him back to Somalia through Interpol’s international channels so that he can be held accountable. No Kenyan government official has publicly responded to the request as of this writing. The Battle That Preceded the Ultimatum The minister’s ultimatum came days after Baidoa’s fiercest fighting since March. Fighters loyal to Laftagareen entered the city from two directions before dawn on Monday, Aug. 17, and attacked positions held by federal forces, Reuters reported, citing a resident and a military officer. Laftagareen’s spokesperson, Hassan Mohamed, claimed on Facebook that the former president’s forces had captured Baidoa’s city center and called on federal troops to surrender. That claim could not be independently verified, Reuters noted. Federal forces later said they had driven the attackers out after hours of fighting. “I saw 10 dead people, including four civilians and six soldiers from both groups,” a local elder, Farah Ibrahim, told Reuters. Somalia’s Defence Ministry said its forces killed roughly 30 attackers and described them using a term the government applies to Islamist militants. It accused Laftagareen’s forces of fighting alongside Al-Shabaab and said the attackers used vehicles loaded with explosives, according to Al Jazeera’s report on the ministry’s statement. That casualty figure is the military’s own count and has not been independently verified. The fighting hit a city already under severe strain. A July survey by Médecins Sans Frontières found that one in four children in Baidoa’s displacement camps suffered from severe malnutrition, Reuters reported. Al-Shabaab Ties Alleged as Minister Hardens Stance Minister Mohamed escalated the federal side’s accusations this week. He said fighters loyal to the former president initially looked like aggrieved kinsmen but now show clear links to Al-Shabaab. Those who surrender, he said, would go through the same process used for Al-Shabaab defectors. Neither the minister’s claim nor the Defence Ministry’s account of an Al-Shabaab link has been independently verified. No court has confirmed any of the accusations against Laftagareen or his loyalists. Roots of the Baidoa Crisis Monday’s battle did not emerge from nowhere. It grew out of a political feud that has simmered since March. Laftagareen’s administration severed ties with the federal government that month, following a dispute over elections, constitutional changes, and the distribution of power between Mogadishu and the regional states. Federal forces then seized Baidoa on March 30. Laftagareen resigned as South West president the same day and left for Kenya. He has been based in Nairobi ever since. Meanwhile, forces and officials still loyal to him remained active outside Baidoa. Sporadic clashes and troop movements continued in the months that followed, keeping the standoff alive without a decisive break, until Monday’s assault turned it back into direct military confrontation. Background: Interpol, Extradition, and Precedent Interpol is a policing-cooperation body, not a court, so a “red notice” alone would not resolve the case. Any handover would still require a legal and diplomatic process between Kenya and Somalia, weighing the underlying charges and each country’s extradition rules. Kenya has used Interpol channels against Somalia-linked suspects before: in 2013, Interpol issued a notice at Kenya’s request for a British citizen wanted in connection with explosives charges after the Westgate mall attack in Nairobi. items.title: DF oo ciidamo hor leh ku kordhisay ciidanka Muqdisho
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa kordhisay ciidamada sugaya amniga magaalada Muqdisho, kaddib markii toddobaadkii lasoo dhaafay qaybo ka mid ah caasimadda ay ka dhaceen qaraxyo aan geysan khasaare nafeed oo weyn. Ciidamo dheeraad ah ayaa lagu xoojiyay goobaha lagu baaro gaadiidka ee magaalada, iyadoo ciidamada ammaanku ay baaritaanno ku sameynayaan gawaarida iyo dadka la socda, si looga hortago in waxyaabaha qarxa ama hub lagu soo geliyo magaalada. Sidoo kale, waddooyinka iyo xaafadaha qaar ee Muqdisho ayaa lagu arkayaa ciidamo dheeraad ah oo wada howlgallo baaris ah. Tallaabadan ayaa qeyb ka ah qorshe lagu adkeynayo amniga caasimadda iyo ka hortagga weerarro kale. Ciidamada ammaanka ayaa sidoo kale habeenkii howl-gallo ka sameeya degmooyinka gobolka Banaadir, iyadoo baaritaannada lagu beegsanayo goobo iyo deegaanno ay hay’adaha ammaanku u arkaan inay muhiim u yihiin sugidda amniga. Ilo kala duwan ayaa sheegay in illaa hadda aan si rasmi ah loo shaacin natiijooyinka kasoo baxay howlgalladii habeenkii ay ciidamada ammaanku ka sameeyeen degmooyinka gobolka Banaadir. Dhanka kale, waxaa dib u billowday ka qeyb-galka ciidamada boolis milataaro, kuwaas oo horay qeyb uga ahaa howl-gallada lagu sugayo amniga Muqdisho. Ciidamadan ayaa loo tababaray hawlo u baahan feejignaan iyo awood ciidan oo dheeraad ah. Tallaabooyinka cusub ayaa ku soo beegmaya xilli dowladda federaalku ay xoogga saareyso adkeynta amniga magaalada Muqdisho, iyadoo ciidamada ammaanku ay sare u qaadeen baaritaannada iyo howl-gallada looga hortagayo falalka amni-darrada ah ee ka dhaca caasimadda. The post DF oo ciidamo hor leh ku kordhisay ciidanka Muqdisho appeared first on Caasimada Online .

items.title: Kooxo hubaysan oo calan ka taagay magaalada Marka
items.description: Wararka laga helayo magaalada Marka ee xarunta gobolka Shabeellaha Hoose ayaa sheegaya in kooxo hubaysan oo dhawaan ku dhawaaqay maamul ay ugu magac dareen “Koonfur-bari Soomaaliya” ay gudaha magaalada soo galeen, isla markaana ay halkaasi ka taageen calankooda. Kooxda ayaa la wareegtay inta badan magaalada Marko sida Xarunta maamulka. Kooxdan ayaa hore uga dhawaaqday maamul cusub, iyagoo sheegay in aysan ka tirsanayn Dowlad-goboleedka Koonfur Galbeed Soomaaliya. Sida warbaahinta maxalliga ah hore u baahisay, maamulkaasi waxaa looga dhawaaqay Marka bishii May 2026, balse weli ma haysto aqoonsi rasmi ah oo ka yimid Dowladda Federaalka ama Koonfur Galbeed. Tallaabadan ayaa kusoo beegmaysa xilli ay magaalada Marka iyo guud ahaan Shabeellaha Hoose ka jiraan dhaqdhaqaaqyo siyaasadeed iyo kuwo amni oo xasaasi ah, iyadoo gobolka uu muhiim u yahay amniga Muqdisho iyo isku socodka koonfurta Soomaaliya. Ilaa hadda, ma jiro war rasmi ah oo madax-bannaan oo si cad u xaqiijinaya cidda hubaysan ee magaalada la wareegtay ama xaaladda ay hadda ku sugan yihiin ciidamada dowladda iyo maamulka Koonfur Galbeed.

items.title: Markab Mareykanku Cunaqabateyn Saaray oo ay Afduubteen Burcad-badeed Soomaali ah
items.description: Burcad-badeed Soomaali ah ayaa lagu soo warramayaa inay afduubteen markab shidaal oo ka diiwaangashan Eritrea, kaas oo marayay xeebaha Yemen, iyagoo markii dambe u jiheeyay dhanka xeebaha Puntland. Markabka M.T. Sibu 1 ayaa la sheegay in lix nin oo hubeysan ay qabsadeen Khamiistii, xilli uu ku sugnaa qiyaastii 252 kiiloomitir bariga magaalada Al-Mukalla ee Yemen. Markabka waxaa saarnaa 20 shaqaale ah, oo ay ku jiraan 16 Hindi ah, hal Suuriyaan ah, hal Suudaani ah iyo hal Ciraaqi ah, halka jinsiyadda qofka 20-aad aan la xaqiijin. Sibu 1 ayaa sidoo kale waxaa saaran cunaqabateyn uu Mareykanku horay ugu soo rogay, iyadoo Waaxda Maaliyadda Mareykanka ay ku eedeysay inuu qeyb ka yahay waxa loogu yeero Maraakiib qarsoodi ah oo Iran u adeegsato dhoofinta shidaalka iyo ka dhuumashada cunaqabateynta Mareykanka. Afduubka markabkan ayaa yimid saddex maalmood kadib markii burcad-badeeddu ay gacanta ku dhigeen markabka xamuulka ee Lutuf oo ka dhacay meel ka baxsan xeebaha Soomaaliya. Sida laga soo xigtay xogta la helayo, burcad-badeedda Soomaalida ayaa tan iyo 21-kii Abriil afduubtay lix markab oo ganacsi, taasoo muujineysa soo laabashada weerarrada burcad-badeednimada ee Gacanka Cadmeed iyo Badweynta Hindiya. Maamulka Puntland ayaa sheegay in kooxaha ka dambeeya falalkan aysan ka amar qaadan hay’adaha Puntland, balse aan la shaacin cidda ay yihiin.

items.title: Clashes in Mogadishu’s Tookiyo leave Ten hurt over demolitions
items.description: Nearly ten people were injured on Sunday in Mogadishu’s Yaaqshiid district after clashes broke out between government forces and residents during an operation to demolish homes in the Tookiyo neighbourhood, according to local reports. The confrontation erupted after security forces moved to clear the area, which the federal government claims as state-owned land. Residents, refusing to leave, staged street protests against the operation. The clash is the latest flashpoint in a wider, months-long dispute over land ownership and forced evictions across Mogadishu, where the government’s push to reclaim what it calls public land has repeatedly collided with residents who say they hold legitimate claims to their properties. The recurring unrest underscores how fragile Mogadishu’s urban land governance remains, and how quickly such disputes can turn violent. Witnesses said the operation began without adequate warning, prompting angry residents to confront the demolition team and the troops accompanying it. Images circulating online showed young men with visible injuries being treated at hospitals in the capital. Government officials have not yet issued a detailed public statement on Sunday’s incident, though authorities have previously indicated more broadly that demolitions in Mogadishu are tied to reclaiming land designated for public infrastructure and development projects. The injured were taken to hospitals in Mogadishu, though the exact number of casualties and their conditions have not been officially confirmed. Local sources indicated that tension had been building in Tookiyo for days after residents were informed they would be evicted from the area. This is not the first such incident. Similar demolition operations in other Mogadishu neighbourhoods have sparked protests, allegations of forced eviction, and, in some cases, armed confrontations between rival elements of the security forces themselves, reflecting how contentious the land question has become in the capital. Human rights advocates have repeatedly called on the government to ensure transparency and due process before carrying out demolitions, warning that unannounced evictions risk further displacing already vulnerable, low-income families. No official casualty toll or arrest figures have been released. This is a developing story, and further updates are expected as authorities and community leaders respond. items.title: Sidee loo dilay horjooge Cabdullaahi Odowaa oo muddo dheer ka tirsanaa Al-Shabaab?
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Laba ka tirsan ciidamada Macawiisleyda deegaanka Wargaadhi ayaa galabnimadii Jimcihii deegaanka Tawakal oo qiyaastii shan kiiloomitir u jirata Cali Gaduud ee gobolka Shabeellaha Dhexe ku khaarijiyay horjooge muddo dheer ka tirsanaa kooxda Al-Shabaab, sida ay shaacisay Wasaaradda Gaashaandhigga Soomaaliya. Horjoogahan oo lagu magacaabi jiray Cabdullaahi Maxamuud Odawaa, kuna magacdheeraa (Faadhuud) ayaa 57 jir ahaa, wuxuuna kooxda argagixisada ah ku biiray sannadkii 2009, xilligaas oo uu ku sugnaa deegaanka Cali Gaduud. Faadhuud ayaa kooxda u qaabilsanaa sahminta goobaha ay ka samaystaan fariisimaha qarsoon iyo waddooyinka ay u adeegsadaan abaabulka weerarrada gobolka Shabeellaha Dhexe. Aqoonta uu u lahaa juqraafiga gobolka ayuu u adeegsan jiray hagidda maleeshiyaadka iyo u fududeynta falalka argagixisada ee ka dhanka ah shacabka iyo ciidamada. Wasaaradda ayaa sheegtay in si gaar ah ugu lug lahaa tilmaamidda dhul-kaymeedka ku xeeran Cali Gaduud oo ay ka mid yihiin Juxaay, Warta Dibisamatar, Bacadka Laandheer iyo Quracda Nayleey, halkaas oo uu kooxda u sahmiyay meelo ay ka qotaan godad iyo gabbaadyo qarsoon. Goobahaas ayaa la sheegay inuu u xushay in ay yihiin dhul hawd ah oo ay adag tahay in la gaaro, kana fog shacabka iyo waddooyinka caadiga ah, si maleeshiyaadka kooxda ugu dhuumaaleystaan ugana abaabulaan dhagartooda. Howl-galka lagu khaarijiyay horjoogahan ayaa waxaa fuliyay laba geesi oo ka tirsan ciidamada deegaanka, kuwaas oo xeelad ugu dhowaaday, kaddibna ku dilay hub gacmeed. Wasaaradda Gaashaandhigga ayaa khaarijinta Faadhuud ku tilmaantay mid dhabarjab ku ah shabakadda Shabaab-ka ee sahminta iyo hagidda weerarrada gobolka Shabeellaha Dhexe, gaar ahaan deegaannada Cali Gaduud iyo dhul-kaymeedka ku xeeran. items.title: Madaxweyne Cirro oo qaabilay Fihiima Quuje, shaaciyayna sida uu ku wajahayo Waqooyi Bari
items.description: Hargeysa (Caasimada Online) – Madaxweynaha Somaliland, Cabdiraxmaan Maxamed Cabdillaahi (Cirro) ayaa Madaxtooyada Somaliland ku qaabilay Fahiima Yusuf Quuje, oo dhawaan iska casishay xildhibaanimadii baarlamaanka maamulka Waqooyi Bari. Kulanka waxaa sidoo kale ka qeyb-galay Guddoomiyaha Golaha Wakiillada, Professor Yaasiin X. Maxamuud (Faratoon), General Mahad Cambaashe, Guddoomiyaha Guddiga Nabadda Qaranka, Cabdulqaadir Jirde, wasiirro iyo mas’uuliyiin kale oo ka tirsan xukuumadda Somaliland. items.title: Maxay Hindiya uga shakisan tahay xiriirka xoogeysanaya ee Soomaaliya iyo Pakistan?
items.description: New Delhi (Caasimada Online) – Xiriirka difaaca ee Soomaaliya iyo Pakistan oo si xawli ah u sii xoogeysanaya ayaa indhaha ku soo jeediyey Hindiya, oo si dhow ula socota doorka cusub ee Islamabad ay ka sameysaneyso Geeska Afrika iyo galbeedka Badweynta Hindiya. Arrintan ayaa si gaar ah loo hadal hayaa kadib booqashadii uu bishan Pakistan ku tagay wasiirka gaashaandhigga Soomaaliya Axmed Macallin Fiqi, oo ay wehliyeen saraakiil sare oo ka tirsan ciidamada qalabka sida, oo ay ku jiraan madaxda ciidamada badda iyo cirka. Intii uu joogay Pakistan, Fiqi wuxuu kulamo la yeeshay madaxda ciidamada dhulka, cirka iyo badda ee dalkaas, iyadoo labada dowladood ay isla meel dhigeen in la ballaariyo iskaashiga tababarka ciidamada, la-dagaallanka argagixisada, amniga badda iyo dhismaha awoodda ciidamada Soomaaliya. Booqashadaas ayaa sidoo kale gaartay xarumaha waxbarashada iyo warshadaha difaaca Pakistan, taas oo muujineysa in iskaashigu uusan ku koobneyn tababar ciidan oo keliya. Hindiya ayaa 7-dii Agoosto sheegtay inay “si dhow” ula socoto horumarka xiriirka Soomaaliya iyo Pakistan, xilli New Delhi ay sidoo kale isha ku heyso isbeddellada cusub ee amni ee ka socda Bariga Dhexe, Badda Cas iyo Badweynta Hindiya. Aragtidaas waxaa sii xoojiyey Gurjit Singh, oo hore u ahaa safiirka Hindiya u fadhiya Itoobiya, Jabuuti iyo Midowga Afrika, kana mid ah diblomaasiyiinta Hindiya ee muddo dheer ka shaqeynayey arrimaha Afrika. Singh ayaa maqaal uu dhowaan qoray ku tilmaamay Soomaaliya inay isu beddelayso “xuduud istaraatiiji ah oo cusub” oo Pakistan ay ka sameysaneyso gobolka. Waxa uu xiriirka Muqdisho iyo Islamabad u arkaa mid ka weyn heshiis iskaashi oo caadi ah, isaga oo ku xiraya tartanka awoodaha ee ka socda Badda Cas, Gacanka Cadmeed iyo Badweynta Hindiya. Sababta Somalia muhiim u tahay Soomaaliya waxay ku taallaa meel juqraafi ahaan aad muhiim ugu ah ganacsiga iyo amniga caalamka. Xeebteeda dheer waxay ku fidsan tahay Gacanka Cadmeed iyo Badweynta Hindiya, waxaana waqooyiga dalka ka dhow marin-biyoodka Baabul-Mandab oo isku xira Badweynta Hindiya, Badda Cas iyo Kanaalka Suweys. Marinkan waxaa mara qeyb weyn oo ka mid ah ganacsiga u kala goosha Aasiya, Bariga Dhexe iyo Yurub. Hindiya lafteeda ayaa muddo dheer muhiimad gaar ah siisay ammaanka biyaha Soomaaliya. Ciidamada badda Hindiya waxay tan iyo 2008 howlgallo ka dhan ah burcad-badeedda ka wadeen Gacanka Cadmeed iyo xeebaha Soomaaliya, iyagoo ilaalinayey maraakiibta ganacsiga. Pakistan-na waa quwad ciidan oo muhiim ah oo ku taal Badweynta Hindiya, isla markaana ah dalka ay Hindiya sida weyn ugu loolanto Koonfurta Aasiya. Sidaas darteed, xiriir militari oo waqti dheer dhex mara Pakistan iyo Soomaaliya wuxuu New Delhi ku yeelan karaa macne ka duwan kan Muqdisho. Pakistan waxay xiriirkaas ka heli kartaa saameyn diblomaasiyadeed, xiriirro joogto ah oo dhex mara saraakiisha ciidamada, fursado suuq oo dhinaca qalabka difaaca ah iyo aqoon dheeraad ah oo ku saabsan deegaan badeed istaraatiiji ah. Hase yeeshee, arrintaasi weli kama dhigna in Pakistan ay saldhig ciidan ka dhisaneyso Soomaaliya. Ma jiro saldhig Pakistani Ilaa hadda ma jiro heshiis la shaaciyey oo Pakistan siinaya saldhig militari, deked ay si joogto ah u isticmaalaan ciidamadeeda badda ama ciidamo dagaal oo ay Soomaaliya keento. Waxa la xaqiijiyey waxay ku kooban yihiin tababar, la-dagaallanka argagixisada, iskaashi farsamo, horumarinta hay’adaha ciidamada iyo amniga badda. Si kastaba, baaxadda kulamadii ugu dambeeyey ayaa muujineysa in Pakistan ay raadineyso xiriir difaac oo ka qoto dheer kii hore. Wasiir Fiqi wuxuu la kulmay taliyaha ciidamada badda Pakistan Admiral Naveed Ashraf, waxaana wada-hadallada diiradda lagu saaray ammaanka badda iyo sidii loo xoojin lahaa awoodda ciidamada badda iyo ilaalada xeebaha Soomaaliya. Waxa kale oo uu la kulmay taliyaha ciidamada cirka Pakistan, iyadoo Islamabad ay soo bandhigtay tababar iyo taageero lagu horumarinayo ciidamada cirka Soomaaliya. Waftiga Soomaaliyeed wuxuu sidoo kale booqday Jaamacadda Difaaca Qaranka Pakistan iyo shirkadda dowladda ee Global Industrial & Defence Solutions, oo soo saarta isla markaana suuq-geysa qalabka difaaca. Tallaabooyinkaas ayaa muujinaya in iskaashigu u socdo dhinacyo badan oo ka tirsan ciidamada Soomaaliya. Pakistan oo galbeed u sii jeedda Dhaqdhaqaaqa Pakistan ee Soomaaliya wuxuu sidoo kale ku soo beegmayaa xilli Islamabad ay ballaarineyso doorkeeda amni ee ka baxsan Koonfurta Aasiya. Pakistan waxay xiriir militari oo aad u dhow la leedahay Turkiga iyo Sacuudiga, oo labaduba Soomaaliya dano amni iyo istaraatiiji ah ku leh. Turkiga ayaa Soomaaliya ka leh saldhigga tababarka ciidamada ee TURKSOM, wuxuuna door weyn ka qaataa tababarka ciidanka iyo horumarinta awoodaha difaaca Soomaaliya. Sacuudiga ayaa isna muhiimad gaar ah siinaya ammaanka Badda Cas iyo Baabul-Mandab, oo si toos ah ula xiriira ammaanka iyo ganacsiga boqortooyada. Si kastaba, ma jiro wax caddeynaya in saddexda dal ay Soomaaliya ka dhisayaan isbahaysi militari oo wadajir ah. Waxa muuqda ayaa ah in Pakistan ay hadda xiriir la sameysaneyso goob ay laba ka mid ah saaxiibadeeda ugu dhow horey saameyn ugu lahaayeen. Taasi waa mid ka mid ah sababaha ay Hindiya arrintan u eegayso si ka duwan iskaashi laba geesood ah oo caadi ah. Xisaabta siyaasadeed ee Muqdisho Dowladda Soomaaliya dhankeeda waxay xiriirka Pakistan u arki kartaa qeyb ka mid ah dadaalka ay ku kala ballaarineyso saaxiibada ka caawinaya dib-u-dhiska ciidamada. Soomaaliya waxay weli dagaal kula jirtaa Al-Shabaab, waxayna dooneysaa inay dhisto ciidan awood u leh inuu la wareego masuuliyadaha amni ee muddo dheer ay qaadeen saaxiibada caalamka. Pakistan waxay Soomaaliya siin kartaa tababar, khibrad la-dagaallanka kooxaha hubeysan, aqoon dhinaca ciidamada cirka iyo badda ah iyo qalab difaac oo ka jaban kan dalal badan oo reer galbeed ah. Muqdisho sidoo kale xiriir militari oo xooggan ayay la leedahay Turkiga, Mareykanka iyo dalal kale, iyadoo isku dayaysa inaysan ku tiirsanaan hal saaxiib oo keliya. Xiriirka Soomaaliya iyo Hindiya laftiisa weli waa mid wanaagsan, labada dowladoodna waxay iska kaashadaan arrimo ay ka mid yihiin waxbarashada, caafimaadka iyo ganacsiga. Sidaas darteed, xiriirka Pakistan iyo Soomaaliya si fudud looguma tilmaami karo inuu yahay qeyb cusub oo ka mid ah loolanka Hindiya iyo Pakistan. Hase yeeshee, marka laga eego New Delhi, Pakistan waxay hadda dhiseysaa xiriir militari, mid badeed iyo mid dhinaca warshadaha difaaca ah oo ay la leedahay dal ku yaalla mid ka mid ah meelaha ugu istaraatiijisan Badweynta Hindiya. Pakistan weli saldhig ciidan kuma laha Soomaaliya, mana jirto qorshe noocaas ah oo la shaaciyey. Laakiin xawaaraha iyo baaxadda uu xiriirka labada dal ku socdo ayaa hadda ku filan in Hindiya ay si dhow isha ugu hayso halka uu ku dambeyn karo. items.title: Iiraan oo wada dadaalo lagu yaraynaayo xiisada
items.description: Wasiirka Arrimaha Dibadda Iiraan Abbas Araqchi ayaa taleefanno kala duwan kula hadlay dhiggiisa Cumaan iyo Masar, iyagoo ka wada hadlay xaaladda gobolka iyo dadaallada lagu yareynayo xiisadaha. Wasaaradda Arrimaha Dibadda Iiraan ayaa sheegtay in Araqchi iyo Wasiirka Arrimaha Dibadda Cumaan Badr Busaidi ay ka wada hadleen “xaaladaha ku habboon ee dib loogu bilaabi karo wadaxaajoodyada”, iyo sidoo kale xaaladda la xiriirta maraakiibta isaga kala goosha Marinka Hormuz. Cumaan ayaa bilihii u dambeeyay door muhiim ah ka ciyaaray dhexdhexaadinta wadaxaajoodyada u dhexeeya Iiraan iyo Maraykanka. Wadaxaajoodyada labada dal ayaa hadda hakad ku jira. Wasiirka Arrimaha Dibadda Iiraan ayaa sidoo kale taleefan kula hadlay dhiggiisa Masar, Badr Abdel Ati, iyagoo ka wada hadlay xaaladda Gacanka Faaris iyo Badda Cas, iyo dadaalladii ugu dambeeyay ee diblomaasiyadeed ee lagu yareynayo xiisadaha gobolka. Wadahadalladan ayaa ku soo beegmaya xilli Madaxweynaha Iiraan Masoud Pezzekian uu mar kale carrabka ku adkeeyay baahida loo qabo in la soo afjaro xaaladda “dagaal iyo nabad midna ahayn”, isagoo sheegay in dhibaatooyinka lagu xallin karo wadaxaajood “awood leh, balse caqli iyo garasho ku dhisan.”

items.title: Before the Floodwaters Rise: Turning the October–December 2026 Rainfall Forecast into Early Action Across the Horn of Africa
items.description: By Hussien Mohamed Yusuf and Abdiweli Sulaiman Abdi The Greater Horn of Africa has received an important early warning. The regional climate outlook released in Kigali, Rwanda, on 18 August 2026 indicates an increased likelihood of wetter-than-normal conditions during the October–December 2026 rainy season. Rainfall outlook for the Oct-Dec 2026 rainy season The forecast was released by the IGAD Climate Prediction and Applications Centre (ICPAC), together with the National Meteorological and Hydrological Services of the Greater Horn of Africa and other partners. It provides governments, humanitarian agencies, communities and development partners with valuable time to prepare for potentially heavy and torrential rainfall. The October–December period is one of the most important rainy seasons for the equatorial and southern parts of the Greater Horn of Africa. It contributes up to 70 per cent of annual rainfall in parts of Ethiopia, Kenya and Somalia, and up to 40 per cent in parts of Rwanda, Burundi, Tanzania and Uganda. The performance of this rainy season therefore has major implications for agriculture, livestock, water availability, food security, public health, infrastructure and regional trade. According to the forecast, southern Ethiopia, central and southern Somalia, and north-eastern Kenya have a 90 per cent probability of receiving enhanced rainfall. Seasonal rainfall could exceed 400 millimetres in parts of central and southern Somalia, central Kenya, the Lake Victoria Basin, Burundi, western Rwanda and western Tanzania. The rains are expected to begin early or around the normal time across Somalia, central and eastern Kenya, southern Ethiopia and most parts of Tanzania. At the same time, warmer-than-average temperatures are likely across much of the region, particularly in eastern Kenya, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Djibouti and Somalia. This is not simply a weather update. It is an early warning that should immediately influence government preparedness plans, humanitarian operations, local development decisions and household-level action. Understanding what is driving the expected rainfall The expected rainfall is associated with changes in ocean temperatures that influence weather patterns across the world. El Niño has developed over the Pacific Ocean and is expected to strengthen during the remainder of 2026. At the same time, the Indian Ocean Dipole is expected to enter a positive phase. When these two climate conditions occur together, they often contribute to increased rainfall over the eastern parts of the Greater Horn of Africa. ICPAC has identified 1997 and 2023 as useful historical reference years because wetter-than-normal conditions were experienced across much of the region during the October–December rainy seasons of those years. However, historical comparisons should only provide context for preparedness. They do not mean that the events of 1997 or 2023 will be repeated in exactly the same way in 2026. The current forecast remains the primary source of information for decision-making. A wetter-than-normal forecast also does not mean that every location will experience flooding or that rain will fall continuously throughout the three-month period. Rainfall may vary considerably in timing, intensity and geographical distribution. Some areas may receive prolonged rainfall, while others may experience extremely heavy rain within a few hours or days. Preparedness must therefore consider not only the total amount of rainfall expected during the season but also how quickly it falls, where it falls and whether rivers, soils, drainage systems and infrastructure can safely absorb or carry the water. More rainfall can be both a beneficial and a threat After recurrent droughts in parts of the Horn of Africa, enhanced rainfall could provide much-needed relief. It may replenish dams, reservoirs, shallow wells and groundwater sources. It could regenerate pasture, improve livestock conditions, support crop production and create opportunities for rainwater harvesting. Nevertheless, rainfall only becomes beneficial when it is properly managed. The same rain that fills reservoirs and restores pasture can destroy homes, farms and infrastructure when it falls intensely, reaches saturated land or flows through degraded catchments and blocked drainage channels. Torrential rainfall may cause flash floods in drylands and towns, while sustained rainfall can increase river levels and trigger extensive riverine flooding. Floodwater can sweep away people and livestock, destroy standing crops, damage schools and health facilities, contaminate water sources and cut roads connecting communities to markets and essential services. Stagnant and contaminated water may increase the risk of cholera and other water-borne diseases. Pools of standing water can create breeding grounds for mosquitoes, increasing the risk of malaria and other vector-borne diseases. Health and nutrition services may also be interrupted precisely when affected communities need them most. Pastoral communities may benefit from improved water and pasture but could simultaneously experience livestock diseases, damaged access routes, isolated grazing areas and dangerous river crossings. Farmers may receive sufficient rainfall for crop production but lose their harvests to waterlogging, erosion or flooding if drainage and soil conservation measures are inadequate. Urban settlements face their own serious risks. Rapidly growing towns across the region frequently have inadequate drainage systems, construction in floodplains and waterways, poor solid-waste management and large populations living in informal settlements. Heavy rainfall can quickly overwhelm these areas, leading to loss of life, displacement, property damage and disruption of economic activity. Somalia and neighboring areas require particular attention Somalia and the adjoining lowlands of Ethiopia and Kenya require urgent and coordinated preparedness. Their shared rivers, dryland catchments, cross-border roads and mobile pastoral livelihoods create interconnected risks. Heavy rainfall in the Ethiopian highlands can raise river levels and cause flooding further downstream in Somalia, even when local rainfall in the affected Somali communities is relatively moderate. Preparedness along the Juba and Shabelle rivers must therefore be supported by continuous exchange of information about upstream rainfall, river levels and reservoir conditions between Ethiopia and Somalia. Southern and central Somalia face a combination of riverine and flash-flood risks. Communities living along rivers, seasonal waterways and low-lying areas should receive regular information about changing conditions, safe evacuation routes, temporary shelters and the availability of essential services. The Mandera Triangle, shared by Kenya, Ethiopia and Somalia, also requires close cross-border coordination. Flash floods can damage roads, isolate settlements and disrupt livestock movement, trade, markets and humanitarian access. The few bridges along Jubba river, Tana river and Shabelle that survived during 2023 floods are at risk of being washed away. Furthermore, border communities often depend on services, grazing areas, markets and water sources located across national boundaries. Climate hazards do not recognize political borders. Preparedness must therefore extend beyond individual districts, counties and countries. Cross-border coordination is essential for monitoring hazards, sharing warnings and protecting communities whose lives and livelihoods depend on movement across borders. Turning the forecast into early action The first priority is to translate the regional forecast into detailed and understandable local information. National meteorological and hydrological services should identify the areas most likely to experience heavy rainfall, flash floods, riverine flooding and related hazards. Disaster management authorities, local governments and sector ministries should then translate these forecasts into practical scenarios. They must clearly explain what may happen, where it could happen, who and what may be affected, and which actions should be taken. Seasonal forecasts are useful for advance planning, but they cannot provide every detail required for local operations. Governments, humanitarian organisations and communities must continue following weekly, monthly and shorter-range forecasts. River levels, soil moisture, reservoir conditions and community observations should also be continuously monitored. The second priority is to activate anticipatory action plans and make financing available before disasters occur. Contingency funds, emergency procurement arrangements, cash-transfer systems and agreements between governments and humanitarian partners should be prepared before warning thresholds are reached. Waiting until homes are destroyed, livelihoods are lost and communities are displaced defeats the purpose of early warning. When forecasts and river-level monitoring indicate increasing danger, authorities and partners should be ready to act immediately. Early measures could include providing forecast-based cash assistance to vulnerable households, pre-positioning food and essential supplies, distributing water-treatment materials, preparing temporary shelters, supporting voluntary evacuation and moving equipment and essential stocks away from flood-prone areas. Medicines, mosquito nets, cholera-treatment supplies, livestock vaccines, boats and rescue equipment should be positioned near areas likely to become inaccessible. Communities should know where emergency resources are located and which institution is responsible for providing assistance. Reducing risk before the rains intensify Local authorities should use the remaining preparedness period to clear drainage systems, culverts and waterways. Waste blocking drainage channels must be removed and disposed of safely. Weak river embankments should be inspected and reinforced, while dams and other water-control structures should undergo urgent safety assessments. Water sources, boreholes, latrines and waste-disposal sites should be protected against contamination. Health authorities should strengthen disease surveillance, stock essential medicines, prepare mobile health teams and identify alternative routes for reaching communities if roads become impassable. Road agencies should map locations that are frequently cut off by floods and position machinery, fuel and repair materials nearby. Bridges, crossings and road sections exposed to erosion should be inspected before the rains intensify. Transporters and travellers should receive timely information about unsafe roads and available alternative routes. Agriculture authorities should advise farmers on planting dates, suitable crop varieties, soil conservation and farm drainage. Farmers in flood-prone areas may need assistance to protect seeds, farming equipment, harvested crops and livestock feed. Livestock agencies should increase surveillance for diseases associated with wet conditions, undertake vaccination where appropriate and advise pastoralists on safe grazing areas and livestock movement routes. Fodder should be stored in locations protected from flooding. These measures must be designed carefully. Strengthening an embankment in one location should not simply redirect floodwater towards another community. Clearing drains must be linked to proper waste management. Water-harvesting infrastructure must be constructed and maintained safely to prevent dam failures, erosion and the creation of disease-breeding sites. Evacuation plans must consider children, older people, pregnant women, persons with disabilities and households without transport. Temporary shelters should provide adequate water, sanitation, health services, security, privacy and protection. Anticipatory action is not only about acting quickly. It is about taking the right action early, protecting human dignity and avoiding the creation of new risks. Climate information must reach the people who need it most A climate forecast has little protective value if it remains in GHACOF hall, technical reports, conferences or government offices. Information must reach the people who will decide whether to plant crops, move livestock, reinforce their homes, protect their businesses, change their travel routes or evacuate to highlands when necessary. Warnings should be communicated through multiple trusted channels, including local radio, community meetings, extension workers, health workers, religious leaders, schools, disaster management committees, market associations, mobile-phone alerts, social media and interactive voice services. Messages should be provided in local languages and accessible formats. They must also be repeated and regularly updated. A single announcement at the beginning of the season is not enough, especially when conditions may change rapidly. The message must go beyond saying that wetter-than-normal conditions are expected. Communities need to know the likely local consequences, the areas at greatest risk, the period of greatest concern, the actions they should take, the places they should avoid and where they can obtain assistance. Technical terms such as El Niño and the Indian Ocean Dipole may be useful to scientists, but communities need practical guidance. A warning should tell farmers whether they need to improve field drainage, pastoralists whether a river crossing is unsafe, traders whether an important road may close and families whether they should prepare to evacuate. Communication must also be two-way. Community information about rising rivers, damaged embankments, blocked drains, livestock diseases, unsafe roads and population movements should be incorporated into official monitoring and decision-making. Women, farmers, pastoralists, fishers, transporters, displaced people and persons with disabilities may experience climate hazards differently. Their knowledge and participation can improve the accuracy, practicality and credibility of preparedness measures. The media also have a major public-safety responsibility. Journalists should receive regular briefings from meteorological, hydrological, health and disaster management authorities. Sensational reporting can create unnecessary panic, while vague or inconsistent reporting may encourage complacency. Forecast information should be communicated accurately and accompanied by clear and verified public advisories. Four priorities for the preparedness period First, governments must localize the forecast and map its likely consequences. Regional information should be combined with national and local forecasts, river monitoring, flood-risk maps, infrastructure information and community knowledge. Every district, county, municipality and cross-border cluster should know its main risk areas and priority actions. Second, governments and partners must release early financing and implement practical measures before losses occur. Clearing drainage systems, protecting water sources, strengthening health surveillance, pre-positioning emergency supplies, repairing critical access routes and supporting safe water harvesting can provide benefits even if the most severe rainfall scenario does not occur. Third, authorities must establish strong last-mile communication systems. Warnings should reach communities in languages and formats they understand and should provide clear instructions. Communication must combine radio and mobile technology with community-based engagement, particularly in remote areas and among mobile populations. Fourth, countries must strengthen coordination across sectors and borders. Meteorological and hydrological services, disaster authorities, health agencies, agriculture and livestock departments, water institutions, road agencies, humanitarian organizations, local administrations and the media should participate in regular operational briefings. Upstream and downstream information must be shared rapidly, particularly across the Juba and Shabelle river basins and other cross-border catchments. The value of a forecast lies in the losses it prevents The October–December 2026 rainfall forecast has provided the region with something extremely valuable: time to prepare. Governments and communities do not have to wait for rivers to overflow, roads to disappear or families to be displaced before taking action. The scientific information is available early enough to guide planning, release resources and protect those most at risk. As a regional climate center, ICPAC is expected to continue to provide regional updates, while National Meteorological and Hydrological Services will issue detailed country forecasts and public advisories. Stakeholders must follow these updates because the seasonal outlook will continue to evolve and local hazards may emerge quickly. Preparedness should therefore be treated as a continuous process rather than a one-time response to a seasonal forecast. The forecast is clear enough to justify immediate action but uncertain enough to require regular monitoring. If the region acts early, enhanced rainfall can replenish water resources, support agriculture and restore pastoral livelihoods while the risk of destructive flooding is reduced. If the warning is discussed but not translated into action, the region may once again count losses that timely climate information could have helped prevent. The success of this forecast will not be measured by the accuracy of its maps alone. It will be measured by how quickly the information reaches exposed communities, the decisions it changes, the early measures it triggers and, most importantly, the lives and livelihoods it protects. Hussien Mohamed Yusuf and Abdiweli Sulaiman Abdi ———– Hussein and Abdiweli are climate change adaptation and DRM Experts who have been involved in translating Regional Climate Outlooks into practical actions in the Horn and Southern Africa Regions for many Years, supporting different partners in Africa. items.title: Somalia’s Flag Carrier: Ambition Without the Institutional and Economic Foundation
items.description: Mogadishu (WDN) — Somalia is preparing to revive its long-dormant national airline through a Rent-to-Buy (Lease-to-Own) agreement with LEMA Air Group that would initially provide two Airbus A320 aircraft. Under the arrangement, the government would operate the aircraft under a lease before eventually taking ownership once the agreed payments have been completed. There is very little publicly available information about the contract with LEMA Air Group or the company itself. The plan is being presented as the first major step toward restoring Somali Airlines, which suspended operations in 1991 after the collapse of Somalia’s central government. The government has previously indicated that the national carrier could resume flights in September 2026, although technical preparations and outstanding agreements could push that timeline back. On the surface, the revival of a national airline is an attractive symbol of sovereignty and national recovery. But beneath the symbolism lies a much harder question: Can a government whose fiscal capacity remains heavily dependent on international support sustainably operate a national flag carrier? The Economics Behind the Flag Operating two Airbus A320s is considerably more complicated than acquiring or leasing the aircraft. A national airline must cover aircraft leasing or financing, maintenance, insurance, fuel, crews, airport charges, navigation fees, spare parts, regulatory compliance and ground operations. It must also survive periods of low passenger demand, fuel-price volatility and route competition from established regional carriers. Somalia faces those challenges while still confronting severe security, institutional and fiscal constraints. The government’s dependence on international assistance makes the economics even more difficult. If external partners provide the overwhelming share of public financing, the state has limited fiscal room to absorb sustained losses from a commercial airline. That raises a fundamental question: Who ultimately carries the financial risk if Somali Airlines fails to generate enough revenue? The history of national carriers elsewhere offers a warning. Governments in countries with far larger economies—including South Africa, Nigeria and Australia—have at various times struggled to sustain national airlines without substantial restructuring, public support or repeated financial intervention. Somalia has neither their fiscal depth nor their aviation infrastructure. The proposed revival of Somali Airlines has also triggered questions about the concentration of economic power in Somalia. Among the names increasingly mentioned in discussions about the country’s business landscape is businessman Sheikh Ahmed Nur Ali Jimale. Critics and business observers allege that he has accumulated significant interests across telecommunications, banking, construction, consumer goods, transportation and other strategic sectors. The extensive list of companies and services attributed to his business interests includes Hormuud, Salaam Somali Bank, BECO, Daallo Airlines, EVC Plus, WAAFI, SomGas, Coca-Cola Somalia, TAAJ, Rikaab, and other enterprises. These claims should not be treated as established facts without independent verification of ownership structures, shareholdings and corporate relationships. But the allegations themselves highlight a serious policy question for Somalia: Is the country creating a genuinely competitive private sector, or allowing strategic markets to become increasingly concentrated in the hands of a small number of powerful business groups? That question becomes particularly important if a private commercial actor gains substantial influence over the national airline. The Flag Carrier Dilemma A national airline is different from an ordinary private company. A flag carrier carries the country’s name, represents its sovereignty abroad and can become a strategic instrument for tourism, trade, diaspora connectivity and national integration. But symbolism does not pay for aircraft maintenance. If Somali Airlines is to succeed, it will require professional management, transparent procurement, independent financial oversight, commercially viable routes and a governance structure that prevents political or private interests from capturing the airline. The government must also clarify whether the airline will remain wholly state-owned, whether private investors will eventually acquire shares, and who will be responsible for covering operating losses. Without clear answers, the revival risks becoming another state enterprise whose political importance exceeds its commercial viability. The most important issue may therefore extend beyond the two Airbus aircraft. Somalia needs to demonstrate that major national assets are not being allocated through informal political or commercial networks operating behind the scenes. If powerful business interests are seeking greater influence over aviation, the public deserves transparency about ownership, contracts, financing arrangements, beneficial interests and decision-making structures. The government should publish the full terms of the LEMA Air Group agreement and explain precisely how the lease-to-own arrangement will be financed, what guarantees the state is providing, and what happens if Somali Airlines cannot meet its obligations. A national airline cannot become sustainable through political symbolism alone. The larger economic concern is the possibility that the revival of Somali Airlines could occur alongside increasing concentration in other strategic markets. A functioning economy requires competition. Telecommunications, banking, aviation, energy, transport and other essential sectors should not become dominated by a handful of actors with disproportionate economic and political influence. Somalia’s emerging private sector has played an important role in keeping the economy functioning through decades of state collapse. But that achievement could be undermined if market concentration becomes so extreme that new competitors cannot enter or existing businesses cannot compete on equal terms. The government therefore has a responsibility not simply to revive Somali Airlines, but to ensure that its revival strengthens competition, transparency and consumer choice. The Question Somalia Must Answer There is nothing inherently wrong with Somalia restoring its national airline. In fact, a professionally managed flag carrier could provide significant economic and strategic benefits. But the project must be judged by the same standard applied to any major public investment: Who owns it? Who controls it? Who finances it? Who carries the losses? And who ultimately benefits? Those questions become even more important in a country whose public finances remain heavily reliant on international assistance. The greatest danger would be to create a national airline in name while allowing its financial risks, commercial decisions or strategic assets to fall under the influence of a small circle of politically connected interests. Somali Airlines should become a symbol of national recovery—not another example of economic concentration. The aircraft may be arriving under a lease-to-own agreement, but the real test will be whether Somalia can build an airline governed by transparency, competition and commercial discipline rather than political connections and private monopolies. items.title: Baidoa on Edge as Rival Forces Mobilise
items.description: BAIDOA (Raxanreeb Online) — Tensions are rising in and around Baidoa following reports of significant troop movements to positions on the outskirts of the city, amid an escalating political dispute over the leadership and direction of South West State. Sources in the Bay region say a large contingent of heavily armed forces, reportedly aligned with Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen, has been deployed to areas outside Baidoa. The troops are said to have travelled from Doolow district in the Gedo region. Preliminary reports indicate that the forces are being positioned for possible military operations in areas surrounding Baidoa. However, authorities have not publicly clarified the purpose, scale or duration of the deployment. The reported mobilisation comes at a time of heightened political and security uncertainty, with increased military activity observed around several approaches to the regional capital. Meanwhile, Sheikh Aden Mohamed Nur, commonly known as Aden Madobe, arrived in Baidoa on Saturday and addressed the developing security and political situation. Speaking at a press conference, Aden Madobe said Somali National Army personnel and South West forces under his side would respond firmly to armed groups he accused of supporting Laftagareen. He said the forces would no longer limit their operations to defensive measures and were prepared to launch offensive action against groups he described as an alliance of hostile forces. The statements have added to concerns over a possible escalation as rival sides continue to mobilise forces around Baidoa. The dispute centres on competing claims over the administration and political future of South West State, with both sides trading accusations and presenting their respective forces as legitimate security actors. There has been no independent verification of the number of troops involved in the reported deployments, and no official confirmation has been issued regarding any planned military operation. The situation remains fluid, with residents and observers closely watching developments amid fears that the political confrontation could develop into a wider security crisis. items.title: Somalia in the Trump Era- The Whistle, the Ban, and the Rise of a Generation
items.description: By Ali Haji Warsame A Referee Sent Home, and A Nation Watching In June 2026, Omar Abdulkadir Artan, a 34-year-old referee from Somalia, landed in Miami, USA , with a diplomatic passport and a valid US visa. He was Somalia’s first-ever FIFA World Cup referee and the reigning CAF Men’s Referee of the Year. He had worked for ten years for this moment. However, US border officials pulled him aside, held him for about eleven hours of interrogation, and sent him back to Istanbul, Turkiye, where he had started his journey. The US border security claimed that Mr Artan was denied entry for “vetting concerns.” A US official later claimed he was suspected to have links to “terror organisations”, a claim never proven and firmly denied by Artan. Somalia is one of nearly forty countries on the Trump administration’s travel ban list, and Artan became its most visible victim. He was punished not for anything he did, but for the passport he carried. FIFA, despite all its talk about football uniting the world, did little or nothing at all to help. It simply said host countries decide who enters. So, referee Artan flew home alone, his World Cup dream shuttered before it began, but what happened next said just as much about Somalia and its people as it did about Washington. From Deportation to a Hero’s Welcome Artan’s warm welcome, Mogadishu Referee Artan did not go home quietly. In Mogadishu, he was welcomed like a champion and national hero. The public embraced him, and government officials met him at the airport. Crowds wrapped him in the Somali flag, and thousands packed a stadium just to see him. Many Somalis in the diaspora, over two million, used him as their profile in their social media accounts, and world football figures reacted with him. The whole continent of Africa stood with him, and big world football players backed him. In a country too often known abroad for war and hardship, his return became a moment of pride. He told the crowd he would keep chasing his dream and urged young Somalis to never give up on theirs. He has not shown any signs of remorse or revenge, and he has shown courage, determination, and calmness, which are symbol of self-confidence and integrity. Two months later, UEFA made a bold and clearly political move: it appointed referee Artan to officiate the 2026 UEFA Super Cup between Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa in Salzburg, Austria. On 12 August 2026, he became the first non-European, and the first African, ever to referee a UEFA Super Cup final. Afterwards, he wrote on the match ball that this had become his World Cup. It was a rare moment where European football stood up, quietly but firmly, against an American injustice. It also showed that talent and integrity travel further than any ban. “Garbage”: Harsh Words, and a Somalis Answer Artan’s story did not happen alone. It was part of a wider pattern of harsh language from the Trump administration toward Somalis, a community made up mostly of American citizens: taxpayers, doctors, nurses, business owners, and elected officials. Somalis in Minnesota and in the USA at large have been called “garbage,” accused of “contributing nothing,” and insulted in ways rarely used against any other community, along with claims that Somalia is contributing nothing but poverty and disorder. Statistically, Somali-descents in the US are estimated as 260,000. In the State of Minnesota alone, estimates range from 61,000 to 107,000, with 83,000-84,000 in the Twin Cities. Nationally, only 8.4% are non-citizens (over 90% are citizens). In Minnesota, more than 58% were born in the USA, and above 87% of the foreign-born are naturalised, one of the highest naturalisation rates of any immigrant group in U.S. history. Bruce Corrie, an economist, estimates that Somalis’ economic contribution is around $500M in annual household income, $67M in state/local taxes, and $8B in economic activity supported statewide, even bigger than several Minnesota counties’ economy. True to their culture of wit and resilience, Somalis mostly answered with humour rather than anger. Social media turned the insults into jokes and pride. One popular joke smartly and sarcastically described that Minnesota was promised to them “three thousand years” ago. Alongside the jokes came real pride in Somali doctors, engineers, and community leaders across America. It is a very Somali response: when insulted, laugh, work harder, and let their achievements speak. 1 July: The Diaspora’s Loudest Celebration Yet Fast forward, the same pride was on full display around Somalia’s Independence and Unity Day on 1 July 2026, marking sixty-six years since British Somaliland and Italian Somaliland (then a UN Trust Territory) came together to form the Somali Republic. In London, young Somalis turned Oxford Street and the London Eye into unofficial Somali landmarks for the day. Somali flags were worn as capes, folklore songs and buraanbur filled the streets, and a generation raised in Peckham, Camden and Woolwich chose to be openly and proudly Somali in the heart of a European capital. Similar celebrations took place in Minneapolis, Toronto, Stockholm, and Nairobi. For a diaspora often talked about rather than listened to, 1 July has become a yearly moment to tell their own story. I have personally attended the raising of the Somali flag at the centre of Birmingham, in front of the biggest library in Europe, and it was a moment of joy and pride. What stands out most about the Somali diaspora is how much has survived the journey, the war, the refugee camps, the years of rebuilding a life abroad, and the hostility along the way. Restaurants like Sabiib in West London serve suqaar, canjeero, and meat to Somali elders and curious Londoners alike. Somali-owned shops have built thriving markets around cardamom coffee, honey, and sweet, caramel-style treats in cities like Minneapolis and Columbus. The Somali language is still sung and recited in poetry, still taught to children born thousands of miles from Somalia. A people who temporarily lost a functioning state did not lose their culture. A View from the UK: Strong Abroad, Let Down at Home Having lived and worked among this diaspora in the UK for many years, I have watched Somalis build careers, run successful businesses, and take up posts in local councils, hospitals, schools and universities, all while still sending money home to support families and villages. Their resilience is not accidental, but hard-earned, built in refugee camps, and passed down from parents who lost everything once and refused to lose it again. Yet, this same diaspora has been let down again and again by the political leaders back home in Somalia. While young Somalis abroad were proving themselves on football pitches, in hospitals and in universities, politicians at home spent much of the last two decades arguing over election rules, clan shares and personal power. Elections have been delayed , disputed, and manipulated far more often than they have been fairly held . Corruption still remains widespread, with public money too often diverted away from real services, and Somalia is consistently ranks near the bottom of Transparency International’s Corruption Index. The country still depends heavily on foreign aid rather than its own revenue. Perhaps most damaging of all, Somalia still has no single, fully unified national army to protect the country and safely secure its borders. Security remains split between non-inclusive federal forces, regional forces and international partners, a gap that groups like Al-Shabaab continue to exploit. On top of this, the ongoing tug-of-war between the Federal Government and the Federal Member States over power and resources has eaten up energy that should have gone into building roads, schools and hospitals. The contrast is hard to ignore: young Somalis proving what the country can achieve on the world stage, while leaders at home still cannot agree on how to hold a fair election. The Youth Are the Absolute Majority, and the Real Hope Somalia’s challenges are real and well-known, including, among other things, broken politics, weak institutions, corruption, nepotism, misuse of public resources, aid dependence, a divi ded security sector , and constant friction between federal and regional governments. No one can simply wash these away, but they are not the whole story, and they are not the final word. Somalia is one of the youngest countries on earth. The median age in the country is 16 years, and about 46.% of the population. About seventy percent of its people are under thirty, a generation so large that, measured across a single lifetime, it adds up to well over a billion cumulative weeks of youthful energy still ahead of it. This is not a small group waiting on the sidelines. At home and abroad, the youth are the absolute majority, and they are already showing what is possible: Omar Artan officia ting a UEFA final months after being turned away at a US border; young Hafids from the West who have memorised the entire Qu r’an and compete in international forums. Somali professionals rising in medicine, law, finance, and technology across the Western world; and a growing number of Somali-heritage politicians winning seats from the US, Canada, Finland, the UK, to Sweden. Turning this potential into a stronger Somalia will not happen on its own or overnight. It requires deliberate choices. The Final Word In conclusion, I would like to wrap up this conversation with what is needed to happen, especially in the following four areas which stand out as most urgent: Hold credible, transparent elections on an agreed and everlasting model, so power peacefully changes hands through the ballot box, not through disputes and delay. Build one unified, professional, and all-inclusive Somali national army, selecting the best of the best from federal and regional militia forces under agreed-upon command, to close the security gaps that armed groups exploit. Use the forces stated in the national security architecture, who are conscripted from the whole country. Fight corruption seriously, with independent oversight of public funds, so resources reach schools, hospitals, and roads instead of patronage networks and personal pockets of the politicians. Establish public institutions that ensure transparency and accountability in the Federal Government and Federal Member States, to safeguard and effectively manage the country’s meagre resources. Involve the diaspora directly in nation-building, not just through remittances, but through investment, skills transfer, and real roles in policy and public service. The best guarantee for their survival and contribution is proving our capability to rule ourselves at home. None of this is easy, and none of it will happen overnight, but a country with this many young people, this much talent already proven on the world stage, and this much resilience running through its diaspora has every reason for hope. The task now is for Somalia’s leaders, at home and abroad, to finally build a nation that matches the ambition of its youth. If they do, the achievements we celebrate today- a referee’s whistle in Salzburg, a flag raised on Oxford Street, a young Hafids reciting the Qur’an from memory- will be remembered not as rare exceptions, but as the first signs of what Somalia’s majority generation was always capable of. One popular joke smartly and sarcastically described that Minnesota was promised to them “three thousand years” ago. Alongside the jokes came real pride in Somali doctors, engineers, and community leaders across America. It is a very Somali response: when insulted, laugh, work harder, and let their achievements speak. 1 July: The Diaspora’s Loudest Celebration Yet Fast forward, the same pride was on full display around Somalia’s Independence and Unity Day on 1 July 2026, marking sixty-six years since British Somaliland and Italian Somaliland (then a UN Trust Territory) came together to form the Somali Republic. In London, young Somalis turned Oxford Street and the London Eye into unofficial Somali landmarks for the day. Somali flags were worn as capes, folklore songs and buraanbur filled the streets, and a generation raised in Peckham, Camden and Woolwich chose to be openly and proudly Somali in the heart of a European capital. Similar celebrations took place in Minneapolis, Toronto, Stockholm, and Nairobi. For a diaspora often talked about rather than listened to, 1 July has become a yearly moment to tell their own story. I have personally attended the raising of the Somali flag at the centre of Birmingham, in front of the biggest library in Europe, and it was a moment of joy and pride. What stands out most about the Somali diaspora is how much has survived the journey, the war, the refugee camps, the years of rebuilding a life abroad, and the hostility along the way. Restaurants like Sabiib in West London serve suqaar, canjeero, and meat to Somali elders and curious Londoners alike. Somali-owned shops have built thriving markets around cardamom coffee, honey, and sweet, caramel-style treats in cities like Minneapolis and Columbus. The Somali language is still sung and recited in poetry, still taught to children born thousands of miles from Somalia. A people who temporarily lost a functioning state did not lose their culture. A View from the UK: Strong Abroad, Let Down at Home Having lived and worked among this diaspora in the UK for many years, I have watched Somalis build careers, run successful businesses, and take up posts in local councils, hospitals, schools and universities, all while still sending money home to support families and villages. Their resilience is not accidental, but hard-earned, built in refugee camps, and passed down from parents who lost everything once and refused to lose it again. Yet, this same diaspora has been let down again and again by the political leaders back home in Somalia. While young Somalis abroad were proving themselves on football pitches, in hospitals and in universities, politicians at home spent much of the last two decades arguing over election rules, clan shares and personal power. Elections have been delayed , disputed, and manipulated far more often than they have been fairly held . Corruption still remains widespread, with public money too often diverted away from real services, and Somalia is consistently ranks near the bottom of Transparency International’s Corruption Index. The country still depends heavily on foreign aid rather than its own revenue. Perhaps most damaging of all, Somalia still has no single, fully unified national army to protect the country and safely secure its borders. Security remains split between non-inclusive federal forces, regional forces and international partners, a gap that groups like Al-Shabaab continue to exploit. On top of this, the ongoing tug-of-war between the Federal Government and the Federal Member States over power and resources has eaten up energy that should have gone into building roads, schools and hospitals. The contrast is hard to ignore: young Somalis proving what the country can achieve on the world stage, while leaders at home still cannot agree on how to hold a fair election. The Youth Are the Absolute Majority, and the Real Hope Somalia’s challenges are real and well-known, including, among other things, broken politics, weak institutions, corruption, nepotism, misuse of public resources, aid dependence, a divi ded security sector , and constant friction between federal and regional governments. No one can simply wash these away, but they are not the whole story, and they are not the final word. Somalia is one of the youngest countries on earth. The median age in the country is 16 years, and about 46.% of the population. About seventy percent of its people are under thirty, a generation so large that, measured across a single lifetime, it adds up to well over a billion cumulative weeks of youthful energy still ahead of it. This is not a small group waiting on the sidelines. At home and abroad, the youth are the absolute majority, and they are already showing what is possible: Omar Artan officia ting a UEFA final months after being turned away at a US border; young Hafids from the West who have memorised the entire Qu r’an and compete in international forums. Somali professionals rising in medicine, law, finance, and technology across the Western world; and a growing number of Somali-heritage politicians winning seats from the US, Canada, Finland, the UK, to Sweden. Turning this potential into a stronger Somalia will not happen on its own or overnight. It requires deliberate choices. The Final Word In conclusion, I would like to wrap up this conversation with what is needed to happen, especially in the following four areas which stand out as most urgent: Hold credible, transparent elections on an agreed and everlasting model, so power peacefully changes hands through the ballot box, not through disputes and delay. Build one unified, professional, and all-inclusive Somali national army, selecting the best of the best from federal and regional militia forces under agreed-upon command, to close the security gaps that armed groups exploit. Use the forces stated in the national security architecture, who are conscripted from the whole country. Fight corruption seriously, with independent oversight of public funds, so resources reach schools, hospitals, and roads instead of patronage networks and personal pockets of the politicians. Establish public institutions that ensure transparency and accountability in the Federal Government and Federal Member States, to safeguard and effectively manage the country’s meagre resources. Involve the diaspora directly in nation-building, not just through remittances, but through investment, skills transfer, and real roles in policy and public service. The best guarantee for their survival and contribution is proving our capability to rule ourselves at home. None of this is easy, and none of it will happen overnight, but a country with this many young people, this much talent already proven on the world stage, and this much resilience running through its diaspora has every reason for hope. The task now is for Somalia’s leaders, at home and abroad, to finally build a nation that matches the ambition of its youth. If they do, the achievements we celebrate today- a referee’s whistle in Salzburg, a flag raised on Oxford Street, a young Hafids reciting the Qur’an from memory- will be remembered not as rare exceptions, but as the first signs of what Somalia’s majority generation was always capable of. items.title: Xogta cajiibka ah ee kobaca dhaqaalaha Soomaaliya xilli ay yaraadeen deeqaha dibedda
items.description: Muqdisho (Caasimada Online) – Dowladda Federaalka Soomaaliya ayaa sheegtay in dhaqaalaha dalka uu sanNadkii 2025 kordhay 3.1 boqolkiiba, iyadoo isla xilligaas ay hoos u dhaceen qaar ka mid ah taageeradii iyo deeqihii caalamiga ahaa ee Soomaaliya muddo dheer ku tiirsaneyd. Labadan arrimood oo isku mar dhacay ayaa mudan in si gaar ah loo fahmo, maadaama ay taabanayaan su’aasha ah halka uu dhaqaalaha Soomaaliya u jihaysan yahay iyo in dalka uu si tartiib ah uga gudbi karo ku-tiirsanaanta taageerada dibadda. Maxay 3.1% dhab ahaan ka dhigan tahay? Kobaca 3.1 boqolkiiba ah wuxuu muujinayaa in dhaqaalaha Soomaaliya uu leeyahay awood uu ku sii koro xitaa marka jawiga deeqaha dibadda uu adkaanayo. Hase yeeshee, kobaca GDP-ga iyo kordhinta dakhliga dowladda waa laba arrimood oo kala duwan, waana muhiim inaan la isku khaldin. GDP-gu wuxuu cabbiraa qiimaha guud ee badeecadaha iyo adeegyada dalka lagu soo saaro muddo cayiman. Marka dhaqaaluhu kordho 3.1 boqolkiiba, waxay ka dhigan tahay in wax-soo-saarka guud uu kordhay marka loo eego sanadkii ka horreeyay, balse si toos ah ugama dhigna in dakhliga dowladda uu isla heerkaas ku kordhay. Soomaaliya waxay leedahay dhaqaale ay qayb weyn ku leeyihiin xoolaha, ganacsiga, adeegyada, lacagaha qurbo-joogta iyo dhaqdhaqaaqyada gaarka loo leeyahay. Haddii wax-soo-saarka iyo ganacsigu koraan, waxaa sidoo kale kordhaya fursadda ay dowladdu kaga soo ururin karto canshuuro iyo dakhli gudaha ah. Haddii kobaca dhaqaalaha lagu lammaaniyo nidaam canshuureed oo hagaagaya iyo maamul maaliyadeed oo hufan, dowladda waxay si tartiib ah u yareyn kartaa farqiga u dhexeeya baahideeda dhaqaale iyo lacagaha dibadda laga helo. Si kastaba, Soomaaliya muddo dheer waxay si weyn ugu tiirsaneyd taageerada caalamiga ah. Deeqaha iyo mashaariicda ay maalgelinayaan hay’adaha caalamiga ah iyo dowladaha saaxiibka ah ayaa qayb muhiim ah ka ahaa adeegyada dowladda, horumarinta hay’adaha iyo barnaamijyada bulshada. Marka deeqahaasi yaraadaan, waxaa soo baxaya imtixaanka dhabta ah ee awoodda dhaqaale ee dowladda: ma awoodi doontaa inay kordhiso dakhliga gudaha si ay u buuxiso qayb ka mid ah farqiga ka dhasha maalgelinta dibadda oo yaraata? Haddii jawaabtu noqoto haa, kobaca dhaqaalaha iyo dakhliga gudaha waxay Soomaaliya u noqon karaan laba tiir oo muhiim u ah isku-filnaanshaha dhaqaale. Haddii aysan sidaas noqon, hoos u dhaca deeqaha wuxuu keeni karaa cadaadis ku yimaada adeegyada dowladda iyo miisaaniyadda qaranka. Dakhliga gudaha oo noqon kara furaha Soomaaliya haddii ay rabto inay ka gudubto ku-tiirsanaanta kaalmo shisheeye, waa inay marka hore awood u yeelataa inay si joogto ah u maalgeliso kharashaadka aasaasiga ah ee dowladda. Canshuur-ururinta oo la kordhiyo se macnaheedu ma aha in canshuuraha si aan qorshe lahayn loo kordhiyo. Waxaa muhiim ah in la ballaariyo saldhigga canshuuraha, la yareeyo baxsashada canshuuraha, la diiwaangeliyo ganacsiyada, lana sameeyo nidaam canshuureed oo caddaalad ah. Haddii culayska canshuuraha lagu kordhiyo ganacsatada yar yar iyo dadka danyarta ah oo keliya, iyadoo ganacsiyada waaweyn ama dhaqaalaha aan nidaamsanayn aan si ku filan loo canshuurin, waxay dhaawici kartaa kalsoonida shacabka. Sidaa darteed, dakhli-kordhintu waxay u baahan tahay nidaam ku dhisan caddaalad iyo hufnaan. Dowladdu sidoo kale ma abuuri karto koboc dhaqaale oo waara iyadoo kaligeed shaqeyneysa. Ganacsiga gaarka loo leeyahay ayaa Soomaaliya ka ah mishiinka ugu weyn ee dhaqdhaqaaqa dhaqaale, waxaana dowladda looga baahan yahay inay abuurto jawi ganacsi oo fudud oo la isku halleyn karo. Maalgashiga gudaha iyo kan dibadda, wax-soo-saarka beeraha, xoolaha, kalluumeysiga, adeegyada iyo ganacsiga ayaa dhammaantood ballaarin kara saldhigga canshuuraha. Marka dhaqaalaha rasmiga ahi kordho, dowladda waxay heli kartaa dakhli badan iyadoo aan si xad-dhaaf ah u kordhin heerarka canshuuraha. Sidaas darteed, isku-filnaanshaha dhaqaale wuxuu ka bilaabmaa su’aal muhiim ah: sidee Soomaaliya u abuuri kartaa dhaqaale rasmi ah oo ballaaran oo dowladda iyo shacabka labaduba ka faa’iideystaan? Maamul maaliyadeed oo hufan wuxuu muhiim u yahay in shacabka iyo deeq-bixiyeyaashuba ogaadaan halka ay ku baxayaan lacagaha dowladda. Sidoo kale, wuxuu dowladda ka caawinayaa inay si gudaha ah u hubiso in dakhliga la ururiyo iyo kharashaadka la bixiyo ay leeyihiin raad cad oo la xisaabtami karo. Haddii hufnaanta maaliyadeed ay sii xoogeysato, waxay kordhin kartaa kalsoonida ganacsatada iyo maalgashadayaasha. Qofka maalgashanaya wuxuu u baahan yahay inuu ogaado in nidaamka canshuuraha iyo xisaabaadka dowladda uu yahay mid la fahmi karo oo saadaal laga sameyn karo. Isku-filnaanshaha dhaqaale ma dhow yahay? Halkan ayay tahay in hadalka siyaasadeed laga sooco xaqiiqada dhaqaale. In dhaqaalaha Soomaaliya uu 3.1 boqolkiiba koro waa horumar, laakiin ma ahan caddeyn keligeed ku filan in dalka uu dhowaan ka maarmi doono deeqaha shisheeye. Isku-filnaanshaha dhaqaale wuxuu u baahan yahay dakhli gudaha ah oo joogto ah, awood dowladeed oo canshuur-ururin leh, wax-soo-saar gudaha ah oo kordha, kharash dowladeed oo la xakameeyo iyo hay’ado maaliyadeed oo awood leh. Soomaaliya waxay weli u baahan tahay inay muddo dheer dhisto ilahaas dhaqaale. Sidaa darteed, 3.1 boqolkiiba waa in loo arkaa tallaabo wanaagsan oo ka mid ah geeddi-socod dheer ee aan loo arkin in dhibaatadii ku-tiirsanaanta deeqaha oo xilli hore la xalliyay. Si kastaba, hoos u dhaca deeqaha wuxuu dowladda siin karaa fursad ay ku sameyso isbeddel dhab ah. Marka maalgelinta dibaddu yaraato, waxaa qasab noqon karta in la raadiyo ilo gudaha ah, taasoo dardargelin karta dib-u-habaynta nidaamka canshuuraha iyo maamulka maaliyadda. Tani waxay noqon kartaa fursad haddii si wanaagsan loo maareeyo. Soomaaliya muddo dheer waxay heshay taageero dibadeed, balse caqabadda weyn waxay ahayd sidii taageeradaas loogu beddeli lahaa hay’ado iyo nidaamyo awood u leh inay mustaqbalka iskood u shaqeeyaan. Haddii dakhliga gudaha uu kordho iyadoo dhaqaalaha gaarka loo leeyahay la kobcinayo, waxaa suuragal ah in Soomaaliya ay si tartiib ah u yeelato awood ay ku maalgeliso ciidamadeeda, adeegyada aasaasiga ah iyo hay’adaha dowladda. Caqabadaha weli taagan Kobaca dhaqaalaha Soomaaliya waxaa weli caqabad ku ah amni-darrada, shaqo la’aanta, kaabeyaasha oo xaddidan, wax-soo-saarka gudaha oo hooseeya iyo dhaqaale badan oo aan rasmi ahayn. Haddii aan wax laga qaban arrimahaas, kobaca 3.1 boqolkiiba ah wuxuu noqon karaa mid aan si ku filan u dhalin dakhli dowladeed. Sidoo kale, dowladda waa inay ka taxaddartaa in raadinta dakhliga gudaha aysan culays xad-dhaaf ah saarin ganacsiga. Nidaam canshuureed oo aan caddaalad ahayn wuxuu yareyn karaa maalgashiga, wuxuuna ku qasbi karaa ganacsiyada qaar inay ka fogaadaan nidaamka rasmiga ah. Ugu dambeyn, waxa Soomaaliya hadda u baahan tahay waa inay 3.1% ka dhigato bilowga shaqo adag oo gudaha, halkii ay ka dhigi lahayd guul lagu faano oo keliya. Kobac dhaqaale oo joogto ah, dakhli gudaha oo kordha, maamul maaliyadeed oo hufan iyo maalgashi wax-soo-saar leh ayaa noqon kara waddada Soomaaliya uga gudubto ku-tiirsanaanta deeqaha. Haddii afartaas arrimood si isku xiran loo fuliyo, hoos u dhaca kaalmooyinka caalamiga ah wuxuu noqon karaa caqabad isu beddesha fursad. Haddii kale, kobac dhan 3.1 boqolkiiba ah wuxuu ahaan karaa tiro aan weli si weyn u beddelin awoodda dhaqaale ee dowladda. Haddii aan wax laga qaban arrimahaas, kobaca 3.1 boqolkiiba ah wuxuu noqon karaa mid aan si ku filan u dhalin dakhli dowladeed. Sidoo kale, dowladda waa inay ka taxaddartaa in raadinta dakhliga gudaha aysan culays xad-dhaaf ah saarin ganacsiga. Nidaam canshuureed oo aan caddaalad ahayn wuxuu yareyn karaa maalgashiga, wuxuuna ku qasbi karaa ganacsiyada qaar inay ka fogaadaan nidaamka rasmiga ah. Ugu dambeyn, waxa Soomaaliya hadda u baahan tahay waa inay 3.1% ka dhigato bilowga shaqo adag oo gudaha, halkii ay ka dhigi lahayd guul lagu faano oo keliya. Kobac dhaqaale oo joogto ah, dakhli gudaha oo kordha, maamul maaliyadeed oo hufan iyo maalgashi wax-soo-saar leh ayaa noqon kara waddada Soomaaliya uga gudubto ku-tiirsanaanta deeqaha. Haddii afartaas arrimood si isku xiran loo fuliyo, hoos u dhaca kaalmooyinka caalamiga ah wuxuu noqon karaa caqabad isu beddesha fursad. Haddii kale, kobac dhan 3.1 boqolkiiba ah wuxuu ahaan karaa tiro aan weli si weyn u beddelin awoodda dhaqaale ee dowladda.
